FCC's Justice Farooq and Justice Rizvi will hear cases on the second floor, where IHC's Justice Muhammad Asif and Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro's courts exist.
The cause list for Justice Asif and Justice Soomro, however, has been cancelled for today.

title: Pakistan seeks to boost military collaboration with Jordan, says COAS Munir
text:
Pakistan seeks to boost military collaboration with Jordan, says COAS Munir
King Abdullah witnesses Military exercise at Tilla Field Firing Ranges, lauds Pak Army's professionalism
RAWALPINDI: Jordanian King Abdullah II on Sunday lauded Pakistans military, noting its exceptional training, professionalism, and strong operational preparedness.
He expressed his views during a visit to the Global Industrial and Defence Solutions (GIDS) and Tilla Field Firing Ranges, according to a press release issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR).
King Abdullah was accompanied by Princess Salma and a delegation of Jordanian officials. Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir received the royal guests along with senior military officials.
During the visit, the Jordanian king was given a comprehensive briefing on the structure, capabilities, and product portfolio of GIDS.
The briefing showcased Pakistan's progress in indigenous defence production, technological innovation, and potential avenues for bilateral defence cooperation with Jordan.
The Jordanian monarch later visited the Tilla Field Firing Ranges. Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif also graced the occasion; whereas, Azerbaijan Minister of Defence Industry Vugar Valeh oglu Mustafayev was also amongst the distinguished guests.
King Abdullah and distinguished guests witnessed a joint fire and manoeuvre exercise.
The exercise demonstrated multi-domain operations, including conventional and air firepower, coordinated manoeuvres, and spectrum warfare capabilities supported by multi-purpose drones employed in various configurations and roles.
King Abdullah II appreciated the high standards of training, professionalism, and operational capabilities and preparedness demonstrated by the participating troops and aircrews.
On the occasion, PM Shehbaz expressed Pakistan's deep respect and affection for King Abdullah II and the people of Jordan, noting that the visit reflects the enduring friendship, mutual trust and a shared desire for peace and development.
COAS Munir highlighted the strong military ties between Pakistan and Jordan, emphasising continued cooperation and the shared vision of a stable and peaceful region, the military's media wing said.
During the visit, the Jordanian king conferred the Order of the Military Merit of First Degree upon Field Marshal Munir, recognising his contributions to strengthening bilateral military relations.
The two-day visit of the Jordanian king marks a milestone in reinforcing the historic bonds of fraternity and brotherhood between Pakistan and Jordan.
In a separate event, President Asif Ali Zardari conferred the country's highest civilian award upon King Abdullah, in a special investiture ceremony held at the Aiwan-e-Sadr, for his contribution towards regional and global peace.
The Jordanian king also conferred the Wisam al-Nahdah al-Mursa (Bejewelled Grand Cordon of Al Nahdah, translated as Order of the Renaissance) on President Zardari.

title: Parliament holds exclusive right to amend Constitution: minister
text:
Parliament holds exclusive right to amend Constitution: minister
Chaudhry criticises sections of judiciary, saying Constitution will reflect parliament, not judges
Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry on Sunday defended the federal government, saying only Parliament holds the exclusive right to amend the Constitution, responding to Supreme Court judges' criticism of the 27th Constitutional Amendment.
His statement came after two top court jurists, Mansoor Ali Shah and Athar Minallah, tendered their resignations following the enactment of the 27th Constitutional Amendment earlier this week.
Not only the top court, a Lahore High Court (LHC) judge, Shams Mehmood Mirza, also resigned a day ago, saying he was "not inclined as a matter of principle and in good conscience to continue as a judge" after the 27th Amendment.
The tweaks fine-tuned the structure of the newly established Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), clarified the titles and ranking of the country's top judges, and approved changes to the military command.
On Friday, President Asif Ali Zardari approved Shah and Minallah's resignations.
"Amending the Constitution is Parliament's exclusive right, and it will do so whenever it chooses," he stated while talking to journalists in Faisalabad today.
He stressed that judges "are not a political party" and only take an oath to uphold the Constitution.
Criticising sections of the judiciary, Chaudhry said that the Constitution will reflect the parliament and the people of Pakistan, not judges. He added that the legislature "must be seen as Parliament", arguing that certain actors had "reduced it to a municipal corporation".
He further said that judges' salaries and "every single decision" ultimately came under Parliament's authority.
"These resignations [of judges] are political. They remained partial," the minister said.
The ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz leader said that the country cannot afford any form of chaos or instability at this stage.
"At times, they dismissed prime ministers through suo motu, and at other times they paralysed elected governments," he said.
Chaudhry said it was not the judiciary's role to "oust whomever it wants and install whomever it prefers".
It is noteworthy to mention here that the SC jurists had criticised the 27th Amendment, describing it as a "grave assault on the Constitution of Pakistan".
Shah, in his 13-page resignation letter, called the recent constitutional tweak an assault on the Constitution that dismantles the Supreme Court, compromises judicial independence, and weakens the country's constitutional democracy.
Warning that judicial independence faces "the beginning of the end", he said nations lose their moral compass when justice is constrained.
Justice Minallah, in his resignation letter, rejected the 27th Amendment, saying the Constitution he pledged to defend "no longer exists” and now survives only as a shadow without its spirit.
He wrote that he had warned the chief justice before the amendment's passage, but his concerns were realised amid "silence and inaction". Continuing in office, he said, would betray his oath and dishonour the Constitution's memory.
However, the federal government called the judges' resignations "political speeches" and the latter's allegations "unconstitutional".

title: President honours Jordan's king with Nishan-e-Pakistan
text:
President honours Jordan's king with Nishan-e-Pakistan for global peace efforts
Pakistan recognises King Abdullah II's role in enhancing bilateral ties with its highest civilian award
President Asif Ali Zardari awarded the Nishan-e-Pakistan, Pakistan's highest civilian award, to Jordan's King Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein for promoting regional and global peace, and his role in enchanting bilateral ties.
A special investiture ceremony was held at the Aiwan-e-Sadr (President's House), after President Zardari hosted the Jordanian king for a luncheon, which was also attended by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Army Staff (COAS) Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, state-run PTV reported.
The Jordanian king also conferred the Wisam al-Nahdah al-Mursa (Bejewelled Grand Cordon of Al Nahdah, translated as Order of the Renaissance) on President Zardari.
Jordan's king bestows the award on the heads of state and distinguished dignitaries.
Before the ceremony, the two leaders held a meeting to review regional and international developments, with particular focus on peace and security in the Middle East.
President Zardari and King Abdullah II emphasised the importance of bolstering cooperation at multilateral forums and for humanitarian causes.
The Jordanian king voiced pride in "the deep-rooted ties" between Jordan and Pakistan, saying that Jordan was keen to expand cooperation across various sectors.
During the meeting, the two leaders agreed to maintain close coordination on bilateral, regional and global issues.
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar; Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, Senator Musadik Malik; Secretary of Ministry of Foreign Affairs, as well as the ambassadors of Jordan in Pakistan and Pakistan in Jordan, also attended the meeting.
'Need for two-state solution for Palestine'
During the meeting, President Zardari and the Jordanian king reiterated their strong support for a two-state solution for Palestinians.
The two leaders reaffirmed their principled stance on post-war Gaza, saying that they would reject any plan involving the displacement of Palestinians.
They called for the establishment of an independent and sovereign state of Palestine on pre-June 1967 borders with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital.
Their remarks come as Israeli ministers Israel Katz and Gideon Saar said that their government would not accept the creation of a Palestinian state.
"Israel’s policy is clear: There will be no Palestinian state," Israeli Defence Minister Katz wrote on X earlier in the day.
In a separate post on X, Foreign Minister Saar said Israel "would not agree" to the establishment of a Palestinian state.

title: Karachi braces for water shortfall after Dhabeji power breakdown
text:
Karachi braces for water shortfall after Dhabeji power breakdown
Power breakdown disrupts operations in second phase, affecting major water supply line: KWSC
THATTA: A fresh power breakdown hit the Dhabeji pumping station on Sunday morning, halting operations in the second phase and disrupting a key supply line, the Karachi Water & Sewerage Corporation (KWSC) said.
Karachi may face a shortfall of 100 million gallons of water per day (MGD) due to the closure of the pumps and the affected line, a KWSC spokesperson said, detailing that the fault occurred at 6:35am after a sudden electricity outage hit the second phase.
The metropolis's main water source, the Dhabeji pumping station, relies heavily on stable power, with even short outages causing instant supply disruptions.
According to the spokesperson, the breakdown forced the shutdown of two pumps, resulting in reduced discharge from Line No 5. "The line was directly impacted when power was suspended," the official added.
Water Corporation teams were immediately deployed to the site and are carrying out repairs on an emergency basis.
The Dhabeji system has faced recurring technical issues in recent weeks. "On November 5, the K-III pump house remained non-operational for 36 hours due to a cable fault," the spokesperson concluded.
Frequent breakdowns this year alone have deepened shortages, leaving numerous neighbourhoods struggling with an escalating water crisis.
The facility has suffered persistent technical faults and inadequate maintenance for years, repeatedly undermining its pumping capacity.

title: COAS warns of Pakistan's 'firm response' to any aggression
text:
Field Marshal Munir warns of Pakistan's 'firm response' to any aggression
Army chief calls Pakistan's victory in May conflict with India "Allah's special blessing"
Chief of Army Staff (COAS) Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir on Sunday vowed that Pakistan would respond swiftly to any act of aggression against its sovereignty.
He, while speaking to Daily Jang at a luncheon hosted for Jordan's King Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein at the President's House, raised his finger towards the sky, saying: "I did not lead Pakistan to victory, Allah did."
"It is Allah's special blessing that Pakistan's enemy bit the dust in May. Pakistan's Army is Allah's Army, its soldiers fight in the name of Allah," he added.
The May confrontation between the two neighbouring countries saw Pakistan downing seven Indian fighter jets, including three Rafale aircraft, after India's unprovoked missile strikes on the night of May 5 and 6, which resulted in the martyrdom of several civilians and security personnel.
India's strikes came after a terrorist attack on tourists in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir's Pahalgam area, which resulted in the killing of 28 men.
New Delhi, without providing any concrete evidence, said the attack was backed by Pakistan, which denies its involvement.
Pakistan then targeted over 20 Indian military sites across multiple regions in a large-scale retaliatory strike, named "Operation Bunyan-um-Marsoos".
The war between the two nuclear-armed nations ended on May 10 with a ceasefire agreement brokered by the United States.
Shortly after the war, the federal government formally promoted COAS Munir to field marshal for his leadership during the conflict.
Meanwhile, the army chief reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to peace. He, however, said that the country would respond firmly to any aggression, similar to its response during the May conflict with India.
Field Marshal Munir, recalling verses from the Quran, said that Allah Almighty has promised believers that with faith they can defeat any enemy, regardless of its strength, adding that Pakistan demonstrated this in May.
As the participants of the meeting began congratulating the field marshal, he asked them to pray for Pakistan’s progress.
The army chief then reiterated his unwavering commitment to fulfil his duties "as commanded by Allah".
Field Marshal Munir's remarks came just days after the federal government confirmed that his tenure will restart following his new appointment as Chief of Defence Forces (CDF).
Speaking during a National Assembly session on November 13, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said that the CDF's term would be five years from the date of his appointment.
The bill, passed by both the Senate and NA, to amend the Army Act mentioned that the COAS, concurrently the CDF under Article 243 of the Constitution, "the tenure under this section shall commence from the date of notification of the said office".

title: Judicial commission calls Mir Raza probe an ‘epic failure’
text:
Judicial commission calls Mir Raza probe an ‘epic failure’
A judicial commission declared Karachi businessman Mir Raza Ali's death a murder, not suicide, slamming the police investigation as an "epic failure" and recommending a new joint investigation.
- The "epic failure" of the police investigation.
- Evidence conclusively proving Mir Raza Ali's death was murder.
- Recommendations for a new joint investigation team and police accountability.
A judicial commission investigating the death of Karachi businessman Mir Raza Ali has declared that he was murdered and described the police investigation into the case as an “epic failure”, finding that officers breached every procedure required for the case to withstand judicial scrutiny.
“This case demonstrates an epic failure by the police in their investigation,” the 62-page report said.
“The police breached all required procedures, both knowingly and unknowingly, necessary to withstand judicial scrutiny and a successful prosecution.”
The Sindh cabinet decided on Tuesday to make the report public at a meeting chaired by Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah.
The single-member commission, formed by the provincial government in August, examined 49 witnesses over 15 hearings.
“It was a murder,” the report declared. It said the bullet trajectory, the unusual location of the wound, the absence of blood, the state of the body, acid burns and anaesthesia detected in the blood “all clearly excluded suicide as the cause of death.”
Ali, 25, an Institute of Business Administration graduate who ran a waffle business, went missing on July 28 after leaving his PECHS home. His body was recovered the following morning in Gulistan-i-Jauhar with gunshot wounds. Police initially built the case around suicide, relying on the first post-mortem, but police surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed disputed its findings; the body was exhumed on August 8, and a second post-mortem concluded the death was caused by a gunshot wound to the back. Murder and destruction-of-evidence provisions were later added to the FIR.
The commission described the police handling of the case as “like a rudderless ship, not aware of its destination,” and the investigation as ranging “from negligent to criminally negligent, inexplicable, casual, and unprofessional.” It said dozens of officers — authorised and unauthorized — collected evidence and interrogated crucial persons without documenting their actions, and that senior officers, driven by ego and “tunnel vision,” doubled down on the suicide theory instead of investigating further.
Significantly, the report said an active cover-up in the initial stages “cannot be conclusively ruled out,” noting that senior officers swept clear investigative lapses under the carpet. “The police investigation failed in its most basic duty: to establish the truth,” it concluded.
The commission recommended accepting the family’s request for a joint investigation team headed by DIG Irfan Baloch and including senior representatives of the ISI, the Intelligence Bureau, Pakistan Rangers (Sindh) and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency — calling it the “most viable path” to restore public trust.
It said a significant portion of physical evidence had been compromised, meaning the case could now only be resolved through a rigorous, intelligence-based investigation.
It also proposed a high-level committee, preferably led by the Federal Investigation Agency, to examine whether police officials involved in the probe’s first 10 days violated sections 201, 166(2) and 218 of the Pakistan Penal Code, and to initiate criminal action against those found culpable.
The report further called on police to publicly acknowledge and apologise for their lapses and recommended reforms to investigation protocols, with a three-month timeframe for the exercise.
The chief minister constituted a four-member sub-committee comprising Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar, Local Government Minister Nasir Hussain Shah, Labour Minister Saeed Ghani and the Sindh advocate general to ensure implementation of the report.

title: French riots and looting hit supermarket chain Carrefour
text:
French riots and looting hit supermarket chain Carrefour
- Riots in France force Carrefour to lower profit forecasts, grappling with damaged stores, higher security expenses, and a drop in customer footfall
LONDON: Carrefour is facing an “unprecedented situation” in France due to riots and looting, the supermarket chain’s CEO said on Tuesday, forcing the company to cut its annual profit margin targets as curfews and higher security costs hit its business.
Carrefour said the unrest was hurting consumer confidence that was already weak due to a surge in fuel prices, and is reducing footfall at its stores as the key fourth-quarter trading period begins.
“The direct costs add up to several tens of millions of euros … of stolen or destroyed merchandise, damaged stores, damaged equipment, and then there are also the stores we were forced to close,” Carrefour finance chief Matthieu Malige said on a call with journalists.
France to deploy troops, admits to failures over weekend unrest
“In the weeks to come we will continue to be impacted as some stores have to close earlier due to curfews, and more broadly we think we’re in a new situation marked by deep uncertainty for our customers,” he added.
Malige said 50 Carrefour stores were directly hit by the riots, while many more were closed in anticipation of unrest, including on Sunday and Monday. He declined to give a total number of stores shut.
Costs have increased as stores took measures to protect themselves, including by hiring external security guards, Malige said.

title: France to deploy troops, admits to failures over weekend unrest
text:
France to deploy troops, admits to failures over weekend unrest
- France boosts security with troops for upcoming protests, aiming to restore order after recent widespread urban unrest
PARIS: France will reinforce police with troops and mount a huge security operation for more protests planned on Saturday, the government said on Tuesday, acknowledging failures in its response to last weekend’s violence.
“The deployment next Saturday will be massive,” Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said, adding that the immediate priority was to restore order after rioting and looting swept Paris, Marseille, Lyon and other cities on October 17.
In a sometimes rowdy debate, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the military would be deployed alongside police, while the government pledged to overhaul tactics after widespread criticism that city centres had been left vulnerable.
France wants curfews in some areas after weekend of riots
Targeted curfews help restore calm
Framing the crisis as a choice “between violence and the Republic”, Lecornu blamed the unrest on far-left groups, who in turn have accused the government of underestimating public anger over high living costs and declining public services.
The unrest shocked France because of both its scale and the apparent inability of police to contain it, inflaming tensions ahead of presidential elections next year with candidates from the far right and hard left performing strongly in polls.
Protests in other European countries, including Italy and Albania, have added to concerns that anger over living standards risks spreading around the continent at a time when many nations, including France, are struggling with budget woes.
A night of relative calm in France followed targeted curfews imposed in several areas affected by the turmoil, which the government said had helped reassert control.
In central Paris, police emptied and guarded the Place de la Republique overnight, with a helicopter overhead. In Lille, in the north, where the curfew only applied to minors, officers patrolled the city centre, checking bypassers’ identities.
Tear gas, clashes hit French cities in cost-of-living protests
Marseille mayor Benoit Payan said there would be curfews for minors around the commercial areas hardest hit by the weekend’s riots, starting Tuesday night.
Lecornu acknowledged shortcomings in the state’s response at the weekend, saying there had been intelligence failures, while police deployments had been too static and authorities had decided against cancelling planned police leave.
Nunez apologised for the failings. “I deeply regret what happened. I accept my share of responsibility,” he said.
Suspect arrested for limoges town hall destruction
Parliament is setting up a commission of inquiry to establish the causes of the unrest, while authorities have assigned 200 investigators to identify and track down those involved in the street violence.
Police arrested on Tuesday a man suspected of starting a blaze that destroyed a historic town hall in the central city of Limoges during the rioting. Officials said he had been on a security watch list and belonged to an ultra-left group.
Students and teachers march in France on biggest day of high school protests
Sylvain Maillard, a Renaissance deputy for Paris, told Reuters some apps had become “a walkie-talkie system for rioters and looters”.
Underscoring the broad impact of the crisis, French borrowing costs rose further on Tuesday as investors fretted about the prospect of more unrest, with the yield on benchmark 10-year government bonds touching its highest level in 24 years.
France’s main student union UNEF has called for further protests on Saturday, pledging to maintain pressure on Macron’s government over what it says is a deteriorating and underfunded education system. “We carry on,” it said on social media.
Separately, groups identifying themselves as “Gilets Jaunes” (Yellow Vests) called for protest actions over rising fuel costs.
The yellow vest movement, largely inactive in recent years, sprang up in 2018 during Macron’s first term over plans to raise petrol taxes. Traffic blockades continued for months until the government made costly concessions it can ill afford now.
Italy faces new form of unrest, minister says
Northern Italian cities, including the financial capital Milan, were also hit by riots last weekend.
Though not on the scale seen in France, the unrest nonetheless jolted Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s government, which was expected to introduce new security measures at a cabinet meeting on Tuesday.
Defence Minister Guido Crosetto described the disturbances as a form of “hybrid warfare” conducted through social media platforms such as TikTok, YouTube and other online networks.
“The events in Milan and elsewhere in Italy are fundamentally different from those seen in other eras,” Crosetto wrote on X. “The West has yet to realise this or take any meaningful action in response.”
In Milan’s central Corso Vittorio Emanuele II, sportswear retailer On and a Levi’s store that were targeted during the unrest had reopened on Tuesday but remained boarded up. Luxury stores had restored merchandise to window displays after temporarily removing it for security reasons.
In Albania, protesters were expected to take to the streets of Tirana for a seventh consecutive day against the government of Prime Minister Edi Rama.

title: UEFA demands answers from FIFA over Infantino presidency
text:
UEFA demands answers from FIFA over Infantino presidency
- UEFA challenges FIFA President Infantino, demanding urgent transparency and answers on his governance ahead of his reelection bid
UEFA has sent a letter to FIFA seeking answers by November 2 about Gianni Infantino’s presidency, including questions over the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) project and the FIFA Peace Prize.
European soccer’s governing body UEFA has led calls for Infantino to resign since he proposed the now-abandoned FFE project, which involved creating a company to run the commercial interests of FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, and selling a minority stake to private investors.
The 56-year-old, who is up for reelection next year, apologised to the FIFA Council last week and told attendees to submit any questions they had about his governance in writing so he could answer them at the next meeting on December 16.
However, UEFA General Secretary Theodore Theodoridis wrote to his FIFA counterpart Mattias Grafstrom on Monday seeking a swift response to 42 questions covering 12 topics.
Infantino promises further FIFA support for African football
“These questions require answers now,” Theodoridis wrote.
“They cannot be deferred until the next meeting of the FIFA Council - nor can future governance reforms substitute for scrutiny of decisions already taken and accountability for them…
“We expect FIFA to provide the transparency required by its own governing body and to respond fully within the above deadline.”
Reuters has seen a copy of the letter.
“The FIFA Governance Regulations state that Council meetings and their associated documentation are confidential,” a spokesperson for world soccer’s governing body FIFA said on Tuesday.
“While FIFA intends to reply to questions submitted by its Council members it has no intention of breaching confidentiality by commenting on internal communication and/or documentation to media.
Gianni Infantino backs proposal for federation payments from FIFA
“FIFA considers respect for these Regulations to be a function of respect for the Council itself and for its individual members. FIFA will always maintain this respect and will not be drawn into any exchange with any third parties that undermines this.”
UEFA did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Infantino will stand for reelection in March 2027, with a November 18 deadline looming for potential candidates to submit their nominations.

title: Opposition leader ordered to pay Rs3mn to Punjab minister in defamation case
text:
Opposition leader ordered to pay Rs3mn to Punjab minister in defamation case
- Case was filed before Lahore Defamation Tribunal over remarks made by Moeen Qureshi during a television programme
Punjab Minister Azma Bokhari won a Rs3 million defamation case against opposition leader Moeen Riaz Qureshi for false allegations made during a TV program, as he failed to provide evidence.
- Specific false allegations made by Moeen Riaz Qureshi.
- Tribunal's finding that Qureshi failed to substantiate claims.
- The Rs84 million damages initially sought by Bokhari.
Punjab Minister for Information and Culture Azma Bokhari won a defamation case against provincial assembly’s opposition leader Moeen Riaz Qureshi, with the Lahore Defamation Tribunal ordering him to pay Rs3 million in damages to the minister, a statement from the Directorate General Public Relations (DGPR) said on Tuesday.
As per the details, Bokhari had filed a defamation suit seeking Rs84 million in damages against Moeen Riaz Qureshi under the Defamation Act. The case was filed before the Lahore Defamation Tribunal over remarks made by Moeen Qureshi during a television programme.
In his remarks, Moeen Qureshi had alleged that Bokhari arranged for 150 to 200 paid individuals to enter the Punjab Assembly during the visit of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi. He had also alleged that journalists who questioned KP CM were paid employees of Azma Bokhari.
Bokhari rejected the allegations as “entirely false, fabricated and a malicious” attempt to damage her reputation, subsequently initiating legal proceedings against Moeen Qureshi.
According to the tribunal, Moeen Qureshi himself acknowledged that he had made the statements in the television programme. The tribunal further observed that he had failed to produce evidence substantiating the allegations. His counsel also failed to establish, through their arguments, that Bokhari’s claim was unfounded.
The tribunal issued its short order in the case, while the detailed judgment will be announced later.
‘Right to disagree is the strength of democracy’
In his reaction to the verdict, the opposition leader said: “My voice cannot be suppressed through damages, and the voice I raise in support of public rights, the supremacy of the Constitution and Imran Khan cannot be silenced.
“This verdict ordering me to pay damages raises serious questions about freedom of expression and democratic values. If speaking up for the rights of the people and demanding answers from those in power becomes such a grave offence that an attempt is made to impose damages worth millions of rupees, then this is not merely an issue concerning one individual, but one that affects democracy as a whole and the right to dissent.
“Remember, the right to disagree is the strength of democracy, not its weakness. Attempting to respond to criticism through damages cannot prove a viewpoint wrong,” he wrote in a post on X.

title: China says US DeepSeek ban disregards Xi-Trump consensus
text:
China says US DeepSeek ban disregards Xi-Trump consensus
- Beijing condemns the US order banning its DeepSeek AI from federal agencies, calling for an immediate reversal of the restrictive measures
BEIJING: China’s commerce ministry on Tuesday criticised a US government order banning Chinese AI model DeepSeek from federal agency IT systems, saying it harmed Chinese firms’ interests and disregarded understandings reached by the countries’ leaders.
In a statement, the ministry urged the US to “immediately correct wrong practices … and revoke relevant discriminatory restrictive measures”, adding that Beijing would closely monitor developments and “take all necessary measures” to safeguard its interests.
The US Homeland Security Department on Monday ordered the removal of DeepSeek products and third-party services using the Chinese AI model from civilian federal agency IT systems. It also barred agencies from acquiring DeepSeek products or third-party services developed using the model.
US banning Chinese AI DeepSeek from government agency IT systems
DHS said DeepSeek models pose “multiple threat vectors” and raised concerns that their use could result in the transfer of sensitive data to China if used by US government employees or vendors.
Beijing is “strongly dissatisfied and firmly opposes” the order, the commerce ministry said.
China hopes the US will implement the consensus reached by the two leaders, work with China “in the same direction” and make full use of the China-US artificial intelligence dialogue mechanism, it added.

title: Amazon to recruit over 300,000 workers for holiday season in first hiring jump in three years
text:
Amazon to recruit over 300,000 workers for holiday season in first hiring jump in three years
- Preparing for a massive holiday surge, Amazon plans to add over 300,000 new workers across the US, a significant increase in seasonal recruitment
Amazon said on Tuesday it plans to hire more than 300,000 workers for the US holiday season, marking the first increase in recruitment for the period in three years as the online retailer prepares for a surge in orders.
Amazon, which employed 250,000 workers during the season for the past three years, said it was hiring for seasonal, part-time and full-time roles across its US core operations for the period.
US holiday sales growth is expected to accelerate 4.2% from a year earlier to more than $1 trillion this year, the National Retail Federation forecast last week.
Starting next year, seasonal employees who work at least 30 hours per week will receive healthcare benefits offered to regular full-time employees, Amazon said.
Amazon makes fresh job cuts, mainly in retail division
Last week, retailer Walmart expanded healthcare benefits for its workforce, as surging healthcare expenses pressure Americans who are already facing rising costs of living.
Amazon, which announced a small number of layoffs in its retail division earlier this month, said it would pay full-time employees a minimum of $20 per hour, with average pay reaching nearly $24, while average hourly wages for seasonal employees will be $20.

title: Rubio to encourage India's Reliance to produce, refine more Venezuelan oil
text:
Rubio to encourage India's Reliance to produce, refine more Venezuelan oil
- Rubio's India trip aims to boost Venezuelan oil refining by Reliance and finalize a US-India trade deal, following a key sanction waiver
MUMBAI: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio plans to encourage India’s Reliance Industries to refine more Venezuelan crude at its local refineries and potentially begin producing oil in the South American country, he told reporters in Mumbai on Tuesday.
Rubio landed in India’s sweltering financial capital days after President Donald Trump waived potential sanctions on the world’s top buyers of Russian oil, a list that includes India. The move is likely to help pave the way for a trade deal between New Delhi and Washington, but has been panned by US lawmakers, who complain that the Trump administration has been far too soft on Moscow.
During the two-day visit to Mumbai and Jamnagar in the western part of the country, Rubio is slated to meet government and business leaders, including Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar and billionaire Mukesh Ambani, chairman of Reliance Industries, which operates the world’s largest refining complex.
Marco Rubio kicks off India visit with trade deal, Russian oil on agenda
“We will talk about (refining more Venezuelan crude) tomorrow with Reliance…They have done so in the past, and I think as more and more of Venezuelan oil comes online, that is something they can do,” Rubio told reporters.
Reliance’s two massive refineries at the Jamnagar complex, with a combined capacity of about 1.4 million barrels per day of crude oil, are able to process the ultra-heavy crudes coming out of Venezuela, some of which have a sludge-like consistency. As Venezuela’s oil production has increased following the Trump administration’s capture of former Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro in January, Reliance has emerged as a significant importer of the nation’s crude.
Asked whether he would discuss the possibility of Reliance itself producing oil with Venezuela, Rubio said the matter had been discussed in the past, and that the matter would come up again. While Reliance is a major refiner of Venezuelan crude, it is not active inside the South American country.
“We are going to go see what the holdup is and what opportunities exist…this is a company that has had a presence in Venezuela in the past, and whose refining capabilities are substantial,” he said.
New Delhi, Washington close in on trade deal
Rubio’s visit comes as Trump removed one potential stumbling block to a trade deal between the countries last Friday when he waived potential tariffs that would have punished New Delhi for its extensive purchases of Russian crude oil.
Legislation signed by Trump in September authorizes the administration to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top five importers of Russian oil, which would include India, which stands at number two on that list after China.
Trump’s decision to waive all substantive provisions of that bill has upset both Democrats and Republicans who have pushed him to up economic pressure on Moscow for its war with Ukraine.
Rubio has said the effort to finalize a trade deal was a factor in the decision to waive those tariffs, and a comprehensive trade deal is almost complete, raising the possibility that it could be signed during his visit.
He said the Trump administration was entering a 60-day review period, during which it would consider which new tariffs, if any, to impose.
While the Trump administration has in the past pressed India to cut Russian oil imports, the US signed a deal with Russia last week to import diesel in a bid to cut domestic fuel prices before the midterm elections, making it unclear to what extent that remains a foreign policy priority.
“Every country has a complex set of factors that they have to take into account,” Rubio told reporters on Monday when asked about India’s Russian oil purchases.
India imports more than 85% of its crude oil requirements to help power its fast-growing economy.
Rubio’s India visit follows a trip to the Uzbekistan city of Samarkand, where he met Central Asian political and business leaders.

title: Energy and industrial stocks drag Sri Lankan shares lower
text:
Energy and industrial stocks drag Sri Lankan shares lower
- CSE All-Share index settled 0.38% lower at 19,983.78 points
Sri Lankan shares closed lower on Tuesday, dragged by energy and industrial stocks.
The CSE All-Share index settled 0.38% lower at 19,983.78 points.
Serendib Land PLC and LAUGFS Gas PLC were the top percentage losers, down 12.5% and 10.4%, respectively.
Trading volume on the index fell to 20.9 million shares from 33.6 million shares in the previous session.
Turnover, however, rose to 741.4 million Sri Lankan rupees ($2.23 million) from 680.3 million rupees in the previous session, according to exchange data.
Foreign investors were net sellers, offloading stocks worth 81.2 million rupees; domestic investors were net buyers, purchasing shares worth 720 million rupees, the data showed.

title: Most Gulf bourses in red after Houthis claim attacks on Saudi energy, airport sites
text:
Most Gulf bourses in red after Houthis claim attacks on Saudi energy, airport sites
- Saudi Arabia’s benchmark index dropped 1.7%
Most Gulf stock markets closed lower on Tuesday after Yemen’s Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military targets on Monday, while Egypt’s index bucked the trend after parliament delayed a vote on authorising military support for Riyadh.
The group said it hit an Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield, and the Riyadh and Abha airports.
Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the claims and Reuters could not independently verify them.
Saudi air travel is already under severe strain with more than 45% of departures from the kingdom’s airports cancelled since October 8, according to aviation analytics firm Cirium.
Saudi Arabia’s benchmark index dropped 1.7%, dragged down by a 4.7% slide in Saudi Arabian Mining Company and a 1.2% decrease in oil giant Saudi Aramco.
Saudi Arabia, rocked by deadly attacks in recent weeks as the Middle East conflict widens, postponed its flagship investment conference on Monday until next year, organizers said.
Separately, a Houthi attack on a training camp for government security forces in Yemen’s Shabwa province killed 58 people and injured more than 200 on Monday.
In Qatar, the index dipped 0.4% to 8,598, its lowest level in over six years, with Qatar National Bank — the Gulf’s biggest lender — retreating 0.7%.
GCC stocks came under pressure as traders kept a cautious eye on geopolitical developments. The absence of diplomatic progress is fueling doubts over any quick de-escalation or improvement in regional security, and the uncertainty could keep risk appetite subdued in the near term, said Ranim Turfa, head of research & market analysis MENA at Tickmill.
“At the same time, economic resilience and robust business activity could limit the declines in some markets.”
Meanwhile, Brent crude futures rose to $111.75 a barrel, the highest since May, and as of 1120 GMT were trading at $111.20, up $1.65 or 1.5%.
Dubai’s main share index eased 0.3%, with sharia-compliant lender Dubai Islamic Bank losing 0.7%.
The Abu Dhabi index , however, bucked the trend to close 0.5% higher.
Outside the Gulf, Egypt’s blue-chip index advanced 1.9%, as most of its constituents were in positive territory including Talaat Moustafa Group Holding , which was up 4.2%.
Egypt’s parliament has delayed until October 26 a vote on allowing the armed forces to back Saudi Arabia if asked, prolonging debate over a deeper role in the conflict with Yemen’s Houthis.

title: Pakistan army chief arrives in Tehran for talks with senior Iranian officials
text:
Pakistan army chief arrives in Tehran for talks with senior Iranian officials
- Visit comes a day after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to mediating between Washington and Tehran
Pakistan's army chief visited Tehran for ongoing mediation efforts between Iran and the US, aiming to de-escalate tensions and facilitate a negotiated settlement despite previous agreements faltering.
- Pakistan's ongoing mediation between Iran and the US.
- The faltering Islamabad Memorandum peace agreement.
- Efforts to reopen the strategic Strait of Hormuz.
Field Marshal Asim Munir arrived in Tehran on Tuesday with a delegation of Pakistani officials to meet senior Iranian officials, Iran’s semi-official Mehr news agency reported.
The visit is the latest in a series of trips to the Iranian capital by the chief of army staff and chief of defence forces as part of Pakistan’s ongoing mediation between Iran and the United States.
On August 24, Field Marshal Munir visited Tehran alongside Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi for talks focused on regional de-escalation, breaking the military stalemate and exploring a negotiated settlement.
Islamabad’s mediation had produced an interim peace agreement, the Islamabad Memorandum, signed in June, but the accord quickly faltered amid renewed fighting between Iran and the US.
The visit comes a day after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to mediating between Washington and Tehran, telling the Global Security Forum in Doha that Islamabad “never gave up” on the peace efforts despite difficult moments during the conflict.
Naqvi credited Field Marshal Munir with a “remarkable role” in bringing the two sides closer, and recalled the June 18 signing of the 14-point Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding and the subsequent Lake Lucerne Summit in Switzerland, organised jointly by Pakistan and Qatar.

title: Ronaldo let Man United down, says club's former boss Ten Hag
text:
Ronaldo let Man United down, says club's former boss Ten Hag
- Erik ten Hag claims Cristiano Ronaldo's lack of fitness 'let the team down' at Man Utd, forcing the manager to make a 'rational decision'
Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has blamed Cristiano Ronaldo’s lack of fitness and preparation for the forward’s struggles during his second stint at the club, saying the Portugal international “let the team down.”
Ronaldo won three Premier League titles under Alex Ferguson before leaving United for Real Madrid in 2009, and returned to Old Trafford in 2021.
But under Dutchman Ten Hag, Ronaldo struggled in the 2022-23 season, scoring once in 10 league appearances before leaving the club in November 2022.
“He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him,” Ten Hag told The Athletic in an interview published on Tuesday.
Reuters has contacted Ronaldo’s representatives for comment.
Manchester United expects higher fiscal 2027 revenue on Champions League boost
Ten Hag, who guided United to a third-place league finish in 2022-23, said he had confronted Ronaldo about the player’s performance.
“Many times I say, ‘Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score.’ He was not capable to do this,” said Ten Hag, who was sacked by United in 2024.
“It’s the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he’s exhausted. But he couldn’t. He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn’t prepare himself.”
Ronaldo joined Saudi club Al-Nassr in December 2022 and scored 14 league goals in 16 appearances before the end of the season.
Man City found guilty on all but one of 115 charges, reports say
“Obviously, he’s one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and keep the players I admire in,” said Ten Hag.
Ronaldo, Portugal’s all-time leading scorer with 146 goals, was handed a 30-day ban by the country’s football federation on Monday after he left the national team camp following a rift with coach Jorge Jesus.
The 41-year-old forward is expected to play for Al-Nassr in a Saudi Pro League game later on Tuesday. He is 19 goals short of scoring 1,000 in his career.

title: Turkiye submits Pakistan-Saudi defence pact to parliament for ratification, sources say
text:
Turkiye submits Pakistan-Saudi defence pact to parliament for ratification, sources say
- A new defence pact between Pakistan, Turkiye, and Saudi Arabia is moving towards ratification, creating a united front
Turkiye is ratifying a defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, to strengthen mutual defence against threats like Houthi attacks, involving military support and intelligence sharing.
- The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement's terms and implications.
- Turkiye's expected contributions to Saudi Arabia's defence.
- Parliamentary ratification process for the defence pact.
ANKARA: Turkiye has submitted a defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia to parliament for ratification, three parliamentary sources said on Tuesday, moving NATO’s second-largest army closer to a formal mutual defence pledge with Riyadh as it faces Houthi attacks.
The three countries signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in August, under which an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all. A joint statement issued when they signed the deal did not specify what each country had committed to.
At an emergency meeting of the alliance in Riyadh earlier this month, they agreed to ensure the “rapid deployment” of military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia.
Turkiye, which has a robust defence industry, has condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, expressed willingness to help meet Riyadh’s military technology needs and agreed to join a Saudi-led coalition to ensure navigational safety in the Red Sea.
Parliamentary ratification is required for Turkiye to formally approve the agreement.
Saudi Arabia thwarts Houthi ballistic missiles, Yemen’s Saudi-led coalition says
Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmus, currently visiting Kyrgyzstan, will refer the agreement to parliament’s foreign affairs commission upon his return, two of the sources said. The contents and details of the agreement are expected to become public once it is submitted to the commission.
The commission could debate the agreement as early as Friday, another source said.
A Turkish official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said Turkiye’s own contribution was expected to belimited to military equipment, intelligence sharing and weapons systems, adding that no other form of deployment had taken place under the alliance so far.
Asked how Turkiye could help Saudi Arabia defend against attacks by Yemen’s Houthis, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said that the Makkah Agreement was not an “offensive agreement,” adding that Turkiye would not send troops to another country to carry out attacks on its territory.

title: Apple commits up to $100 million for US titanium in domestic manufacturing push
text:
Apple commits up to $100 million for US titanium in domestic manufacturing push
- Apple boosts US manufacturing with a $100M titanium deal for new iPhones, including its first foldable, strengthening domestic supply chains
Apple said on Tuesday it has committed to purchasing up to $100 million of titanium over three years from a Pennsylvania-based company as part of the iPhone maker’s push to expand manufacturing in the United States.
The purchase agreement with Perryman Company, part of Apple’s American Manufacturing Program, covers titanium for various products, including its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo.
Perryman will melt, forge and roll titanium with at least 80% recycled content at its site in Houston, Pennsylvania.
Apple is also expanding its partnership with Delaware-based Qnity Electronics to cover production of films for the new variable-aperture camera system in the iPhone 18 Pro.
Nearly 100 components in the iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro are produced by American companies, drawn from suppliers in more than a dozen states, Apple said.
Apple to host ‘Pro and tell’ event on October 28 in LA
TSMC’s Arizona plant will produce more than 100 million chips for Apple in 2026, while Corning’s Kentucky facility will make all cover glass for iPhones and Apple Watches sold worldwide by the end of the year.
Apple launched the American Manufacturing Program last year as part of its $600-billion, four-year commitment to US manufacturing.
In August, Apple opened an Advanced Manufacturing Center in Houston, Texas, in the same facility that builds its AI servers and will begin making Mac minis this year.

title: Britain says it will carry out defensive air missions over Saudi Arabia
text:
Britain says it will carry out defensive air missions over Saudi Arabia
- UK sends RAF Typhoons to Saudi Arabia for defensive missions, bolstering protection against Houthi aerial assaults on key areas
LONDON: Britain will fly Royal Air Force Typhoon fighter jets on defensive missions to help protect Saudi cities and critical national infrastructure from Houthi aerial attacks, the Ministry of Defence said on Tuesday.
The ministry said the aircraft would operate only in a defensive role and would not conduct offensive strikes against the Houthis, whose attacks Britain says threaten regional stability and risk disrupting energy supplies and trade routes.
“The continuing attacks from the Houthis on our ally Saudi Arabia are absolutely despicable. The targeting of the airport in Riyadh in particular shows the lengths the Houthis are going to escalate the situation in the region,” defence minister Wes Streeting said in a statement.
Yemen’s Houthis vow more attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities after Aramco HQ hit
“That’s why today I have approved further UK military support. RAF Typhoons will fly defensive air missions to help protect Saudi airspace from drones and missiles.”
The additional support follows a request from Saudi Arabia’s government, which Prime Minister Andy Burnham said earlier this month Britain was prepared to consider.
Yemen govt forces say advancing against Houthis around key waterway
Britain will also deploy an Atlas A400M transport aircraft and military advisers, expanding assistance announced in September which included an RAF Voyager air-to-air refuelling aircraft but not fighter jets.
Houthi attacks against Saudi oil facilities and other infrastructure have intensified in recent weeks as the conflict in Yemen has escalated.
Inside Yemen, authorities said a Houthi strike on Monday against a training camp for Yemen government security forces killed 58 people.

title: Israeli fire kills four people in Gaza, medics say
text:
Israeli fire kills four people in Gaza, medics say
- At least four Palestinians, including a couple, died in Gaza as Israeli strikes and gunfire continued, challenging the year-old ceasefire
CAIRO: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least four Palestinians, including a married couple and a 17-year-old, in separate incidents in the Gaza Strip on Tuesday, health officials said.
Medics said an Israeli airstrike killed Akram Yassin and his wife Dina Abu Baker in an apartment in Gaza City.
The Israeli military said it struck a fighters in the area, without giving further details.
In Khan Younis, in the south, medics said a 17-year-old boy was killed by Israeli gunfire near the Qizan Al-Najar neighbourhood, while another was killed by Israeli gunfire in the Zeitoun suburb east of Gaza City, taking Tuesday’s death toll to at least four.
The Israeli military did not immediately comment on either of the two gunfire incidents.
Israeli strike kills five, including four women, in Gaza, health officials say
Palestinians inspected the aftermath of the strike on the apartment in Gaza City before gathering for the couple’s funeral.
“We’re supposed to be in a ceasefire period, but honestly, we are not seeing a ceasefire or anything. The war is still going on, assassinations are continuing, and the shelling has not stopped,” said Mahmoud Yassin, whose brother was killed.
Israel, which says the Hamas group has been rearming and launching attacks in violation of the ceasefire, has stepped up strikes on the group in recent weeks.
Hamas has denied trying to carry out attacks or rebuild its arsenal and accuses Israel of undermining the Gaza peace deal.
The ceasefire, brokered by the US a year ago, calls for the eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made towards implementing a deal to end the conflict that includes terms for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops.
Gaza health officials have said at least 1,500 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli fire since the ceasefire. Israel says four of its soldiers have been killed by Hamas in Gaza over the same period.

title: CCP greenlights Lotte Chemical Pakistan’s stake acquisition in Engro Polymer & Chemicals
text:
CCP greenlights Lotte Chemical Pakistan’s stake acquisition in Engro Polymer & Chemicals
- The assessment found that LCPL does not operate in any of the identified relevant markets
The Competition Commission of Pakistan approved Lotte Chemical's acquisition of shares in Engro Polymer. The assessment found no significant impact on market competition due to no operational overlap.
- CCP's approval of the share acquisition.
- Products manufactured by Lotte Chemical and Engro Polymer.
- Market assessment for PVC, caustic soda, and hydrogen peroxide.
The Competition Commission of Pakistan (CCP) has approved the proposed acquisition of a shareholding in Engro Polymer & Chemicals Limited (EPCL) by Lotte Chemical Pakistan Limited (LCPL) from Engro Corporation Limited, following a Phase-I competition assessment under the Competition Act, 2010, read a statement on Tuesday.
LCPL is a public limited company engaged in the manufacture and supply of Purified Terephthalic Acid (PTA) in Pakistan. PTA is primarily used as a raw material in the production of polyester and polyethylene terephthalate (PET). EPCL, the target company, manufactures and supplies Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC), caustic soda, hydrogen peroxide and other chlor-alkali products.
Back in March, Lotte Chemical Pakistan Limited announced its intention to acquire shares and control of EPCL.
For its competition assessment, CCP identified PVC, caustic soda and hydrogen peroxide as the relevant product markets, with Pakistan constituting the relevant geographic market.
The assessment found that LCPL does not operate in any of the identified relevant markets.
Furthermore, neither LCPL nor any of its associated, affiliated or group companies purchases products from EPCL, read the statement. The proposed transaction therefore gives rise to neither a horizontal nor a vertical overlap between the merging parties.
In the PVC market, EPCL is the sole domestic manufacturer, while imports provide an important competitive constraint. In the markets for caustic soda and hydrogen peroxide, EPCL holds comparatively lower market shares and competes with other market participants.
CCP further observed that the proposed acquisition entails a change in the ownership and control of EPCL without, in itself, increasing the target company’s production capacity, sales or output. The transaction is therefore not expected to increase market concentration, create barriers to entry or materially enhance the market power of either party.
Based on its Phase-I assessment, the regulator concluded that the proposed transaction is unlikely to substantially lessen competition or create or strengthen a dominant position in any of the relevant markets. The transaction has accordingly been authorised under Section 31(1)(d)(i) of the Competition Act, 2010.

title: Swiatek loses last chance to qualify for WTA Finals after withdrawing from Ningbo
text:
Swiatek loses last chance to qualify for WTA Finals after withdrawing from Ningbo
- Thigh injury forces Iga Swiatek to withdraw from the Ningbo Open, effectively ending her direct qualification hopes for the WTA Finals.
Iga Swiatek is set to miss the season-ending WTA Finals after the six-time Grand Slam champion withdrew from the Ningbo Open in China with a thigh injury on Tuesday.
The Pole, who has played at every edition of the Finals since 2021 and won the event in 2023, had to reach at least the quarter-finals in Ningbo to have any chance of displacing Czech Karolina Muchova in the last qualifying place.
Swiatek was hampered by the injury in her 7-5 6-1 loss to compatriot Maja Chwalinska in the Wuhan Open semi-finals last week. She has won only one tournament this year and failed to advance beyond the quarters at any of the four Grand Slams.
Injured Swiatek goes down fighting in Wuhan Open semi-final
“After careful consideration, I’ve decided to withdraw from the tournament,” the 25-year-old said in a statement posted on the Ningbo Open’s social media.
“I’ve been experiencing an ongoing problem with my left thigh over the past weeks and I feel that giving myself the time to rest and recover is the right decision.”
Muchova, who is not competing at the WTA 500 tournament in China, can still be overtaken by Marta Kostyuk. The Ukrainian has to make up 815 points at the Ningbo event and next week’s Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo.
While Swiatek is unable to qualify directly for the November 8-15 WTA Finals in Indian Wells, California, she could go to the event as one of two alternates.

title: Rupee registers gain against US dollar
text:
Rupee registers gain against US dollar
- Currency settles at 276.87 against the greenback
The Pakistani Rupee gained marginally against the US Dollar in the interbank market, closing at 276.87, amidst a churning US dollar and rising oil prices due to Middle East tensions.
- PKR's marginal gain against the US dollar.
- Global currency market trends and European political instability.
- Impact of rising oil prices and Middle East tensions.
- Interbank and open market rates for major currencies.
The Pakistani rupee continued its marginal gains against the US dollar, appreciating 0.01% in the interbank market on Tuesday.
The local unit closed the day at 276.87, a gain of Re0.03 against the greenback.
On Monday, the Pakistani rupee settled at 276.90 against the dollar.
Internationally, the US dollar churned at the start of trading in Asia on Tuesday as a tepid recovery in investor confidence bolstered higher-yielding currencies, but growing political risk in Europe continued to test traders’ nerves.
The euro was steady at $1.1216, while the British pound rose 0.1% to $1.3308.
The Australian dollar was up 0.1% at $0.6986, while its New Zealand counterpart nudged 0.1% higher to $0.5668.
Against the yen, the US dollar was flat at 158.56 yen ahead of an auction of 20-year Japanese government bonds.
French authorities set curfews in several cities on Monday after nationwide anti-government protests plunged President Emmanuel Macron’s final months in office into turmoil.
In Italy, the government said it will dispatch 500 troops after two days of unrest.
The spread between French and German 10-year government bonds widened 9.9 basis points on Monday to 147.3 basis points. The yield on the US 10-year Treasury bond was flat at 5.131%.
The US dollar index, which measures the greenback’s strength against six currencies, ended two days of loss on Monday, rising 0.2% to 101.98.
Oil prices, a key indicator of currency parity, advanced on Tuesday, with Brent reaching a five-month high, as traders priced in a geopolitical risk premium from Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf.
Yemen’s Houthis said on Monday they launched several attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military targets, such as an Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield, Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport, and Abha airport.
Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the Houthi claims and Reuters could not independently verify them.
Brent crude futures rose to $111.75 a barrel, the highest since May, and as of 1120 GMT were trading at $111.20, up $1.65 or 1.5%.
