France in recent days has seen some of the worst unrest in years as huge protests over the cost of living and underfunded public services descended into riots and looting.
Trump himself has struggled to make goods and services more affordable in the United States.
The rally comes as Republicans face defensive political terrain in historically conservative regions, pressured by voter frustrations over economic conditions, inflation, and policy challenges.

title: Beluga whale Cyprus dies in California months after leaving Ontario's Marineland
text:
Beluga whale Cyprus dies in California months after leaving Ontario's Marineland
The aquarium said a full necropsy would be conducted to determine the cause of death
A nine-year-old beluga whale rescued from the now-closed Marineland in Ontario has died at SeaWorld San Diego, becoming the latest animal to die following a mass relocation.
The whale, named Cyprus, arrived at the California aquarium on August 22 and had reportedly been adjusting well to his new surroundings.
However, SeaWorld said Cyprus stopped eating on Friday, and an ultrasound revealed that his intestinal tract was not functioning normally.
The aquarium said a full necropsy would be conducted to determine the cause of death.
Cyprus was among 30 belugas and four dolphins transferred from Marineland in Niagara Falls after the facility said it could no longer afford to care for its remaining animals.
His death follows several others involving animals relocated from the Canadian park.
Earlier this month, Shedd Aquarium in Chicago confirmed the death of Caspian, a 27-year-old female beluga. Two other belugas, Peekachu and Rain, also died at the aquarium.
A beluga named Jelly Bean and a dolphin named Echo died after being transferred to Oceanogràfic Valencia in Spain.
SeaWorld said its two remaining rescued belugas were in stable condition and continued to receive close monitoring.
“As we have indicated, this process will take a considerable amount of time. Our commitment to the health, well-being and care of these belugas, like every animal we rescue, continues,” SeaWorld said in a Facebook post on Sunday.

title: Australian employers using AI to track workers without their knowledge, report warns
text:
Australian employers using AI to track workers without their knowledge, report warns
The report highlighted cases including a fast-food chain allegedly using cameras in changing rooms
Australian employers are increasingly using AI and surveillance technology to monitor workers, raising concerns about employee privacy and workplace rights.
According to The Guardian, a new report from the University of Technology Sydney's Human Technology Institute warns that companies are tracking employees through CCTV cameras, keystroke monitoring, office access cards and workplace messaging platforms.
The report highlighted cases including a fast-food chain allegedly using cameras in changing rooms to prevent staff from using their phones.
Another case involved a supermarket cashier receiving a final written warning after an AI system detected an error rate of just 0.18 percent, roughly one mistake every 533 items scanned.
Researchers also raised concerns about Microsoft Teams, which can automatically update employees' office locations when they connect to workplace Wi-Fi.
A March 2026 survey found that only nine percent of Australians knew monitoring was happening in their own workplace.
The institute is calling for stronger workplace privacy laws, including new rules requiring employers to justify surveillance and consult employees.
The report also recommends banning surveillance technologies that pose unacceptable risks to employees' rights.

title: UK hits back at Hegseth after he questions NATO allies' sacrifices in Afghanistan
text:
UK hits back at Hegseth after he questions NATO allies' sacrifices in Afghanistan
Hegseth claimed during a speech on Saturday that only a handful of countries were involved in actual fighting
Downing Street has criticised US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth for suggesting that most NATO allies did not take part in combat operations during the Afghanistan war.
According to The Guardian, Hegseth claimed during a speech on Saturday that only a handful of countries were involved in actual fighting, despite dozens contributing troops to the mission.
He recalled joking that the NATO-led International Security Assistance Force (ISAF) stood for “I Saw Americans Fighting”.
The remarks sparked criticism from the British government, which highlighted the sacrifices made by UK and allied forces.
“Frankly, the facts speak for themselves when it comes to the UK’s and Nato’s contribution to Afghanistan. And it is wrong to diminish their role,” a Downing Street spokesperson said.
More than 450 British military personnel died during the conflict, alongside troops from over 30 other countries.
The criticism follows similar remarks made by US President Donald Trump earlier this year, when he suggested NATO troops had avoided frontline fighting in Afghanistan.
Meanwhile, Downing Street also reaffirmed Britain's support for Ukraine amid growing tensions between Washington and Kyiv..
“Our support for Ukraine is unwavering,” the spokesperson said.

title: US Supreme Court refuses to restore plea deals for three alleged 9/11 conspirators
text:
US Supreme Court refuses to restore plea deals for three alleged 9/11 conspirators
The court on Monday declined appeals from Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, Mustafa al Hawsawi and Walid Bin ‘Attash
The US Supreme Court has refused to restore plea agreements for three men accused of planning the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, allowing the possibility of the death penalty to remain.
According to CNN, the court on Monday declined appeals from Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, Mustafa al Hawsawi and Walid Bin ‘Attash.
The decision leaves in place a previous appeals court ruling that former Defence Secretary Lloyd Austin had the authority to cancel their plea agreements.
The deals, announced in 2024 after more than two years of negotiations, would have required the defendants to plead guilty in exchange for avoiding the death penalty.
They would also have faced public sentencing hearings where survivors and victims' families could question them.
However, Austin cancelled the agreements, arguing that such an important decision “should rest with me.”
The move followed criticism from some groups representing families of those killed in the attacks.
The Supreme Court's decision means the cases will return to military courts, where proceedings have faced years of delays.
Legal disputes over torture at CIA detention facilities and whether evidence obtained through torture can be used in court have complicated the trials.

title: ICE agents accused of using force against US citizen in Long Beach
text:
ICE agents accused of using force against US citizen in Long Beach
Long Beach police said ICE agents also requested assistance following reports of vehicle vandalism
A US citizen was injured during an encounter with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents in Long Beach, California, on Saturday, officials said.
According to CNN, Ricardo Gonzalez, a former city employee, had called 911 alongside other residents to report concerns about unmarked vehicles.
Long Beach police said ICE agents also requested assistance following reports of vehicle vandalism and a person needing medical attention.
When officers arrived, they found Gonzalez handcuffed and bleeding while detained by federal agents. Police also reported a disturbance involving a large group.
Long Beach Mayor Rex Richardson said Gonzalez had contacted emergency services as the situation escalated.
“When the police arrived, we know that he was detained. He was on a curb. He was injured,” Richardson told CNN.
Gonzalez's daughter alleged in an online fundraiser that an unmarked vehicle believed to be driven by federal agents struck him while he rode an electric bicycle.
Witness Sherman Austin separately alleged that agents used a Taser, broke Gonzalez's arm and restrained him on the ground. These allegations have not been independently established.
Video recorded by Austin showed Gonzalez pleading for medical help while handcuffed.
Local police took Gonzalez to a fire station, where his handcuffs were removed, before paramedics transported him to hospital.

title: Trump is using presidency to make himself richer, say majority Americans in new poll
text:
Trump is using presidency to make himself richer, say majority Americans in new poll
Sixty-six percent percent of Americans think Trump is using the presidency for personal financial gain
A majority of Americans believe US President Donald Trump is using his position to enrich himself, according to a new poll released ahead of November's midterm elections.
The Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos survey found that 66 percent of Americans think Trump is using the presidency for personal financial gain.
The findings also show that 34 percent of Republicans share this view, an increase of 12 percentage points since September last year.
Meanwhile, Trump's approval rating has fallen to 33 percent, marking a new low as Republicans prepare for crucial congressional elections.
The poll also highlights growing financial concerns among Americans.
Nearly half of respondents, 48 percent, said they were financially worse off than when Trump returned to the White House in 2025.
According to The Washington Post, this is the highest proportion expressing such concerns about a president since the polling series began in 1986.
The survey also found widespread concerns about democratic freedoms under Trump's administration.
Around 67 percent of respondents said Trump was not committed to protecting press freedom, while 61 percent questioned his commitment to free and fair elections.

title: Helen Haines, former nurse turned Australian MP critically injured in suspected attack
text:
Helen Haines, former nurse turned Australian MP critically injured in suspected attack
Helen Haines has represented the rural electorate of Indi, north of Melbourne, since 2019
Australian MP Helen Haines is in critical condition after being struck by a car outside her office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on Monday.
According to The Independent, police are treating the incident as a targeted attack and have arrested a 43-year-old man.
Haines, 65, was reportedly unloading her car when a white Toyota Land Cruiser struck her. She was airlifted to hospital with serious injuries.
Police said a knife was found inside the vehicle, but the motive remains unknown.
Haines is an independent Australian politician who has represented the rural electorate of Indi, north of Melbourne, since 2019.
A former nurse, midwife and academic, she spent three decades working in rural healthcare before entering politics.
She made history in 2019 by becoming the first independent politician to succeed another independent in the same Australian parliamentary seat.
Haines was re-elected in 2022 and 2025 and has campaigned on regional healthcare, housing, climate change and government transparency.
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese praised Haines following the attack.
"She's just a thoroughly decent, respectful human being who is a delight to work with, and her presence in the Parliament adds to it."
Her family thanked bystanders, medical workers and police for their assistance.

title: Meta admits mistaken suspension of 'No Kings' Instagram account, cites Claude AI glitch
text:
Meta admits mistaken suspension of 'No Kings' Instagram account, cites Claude AI glitch
Meta says Anthropic’s Claude AI triggered mistaken suspension of 'No Kings' Instagram account
Meta has issued a formal apology after its automated security systems mistakenly suspended the Instagram account of the No Kings Coalition during nationwide protests.
Demonstrators gathered at thousands of events across the United States on Saturday decrying President Donald Trump's aggressive deportation efforts, war in Iran and other policies in the third round of the "No Kings" rallies.
The company explained that the disruption was triggered when a tool linked to Anthropic's Claude AI read profile posts and hashtags at roughly four times the speed of normal human browsing, creating intense bursts of activity that closely resembled automated bot or spam traffic.
The sudden algorithmic shutdown temporarily locked organizers out of the page during a critical window of rallies and early-voting initiatives across multiple states.
The Instagram account used by organizers and attendees, however, was offline for more than an hour. And Meta spokesman Andy Stone wrote in a post on X that it took longer to fix problems with organizers' access to the accounts.
Stone said network security systems detected the use of a Claude tool reading profiles, posts, and hashtags, with the rate sharply increasing in intense bursts on October 17.
"These abrupt, high-volume, sequential requests in a short period resembled automated bot traffic rather than an ordinary human browsing our systems. This activity caused our automated protections to incorrectly take the No Kings Instagram account offline," he said.
Although public access was restored relatively quickly following an automated review, administrators experienced extended login delays.
Organizers strongly criticized the platform for the suppression during a major mobilization effort, highlighting how vital social media channels are for communicating with supporters.

title: Playing loud music in public transport in UK can lead to £100 fines under new crackdown
text:
Playing loud music in public transport in UK can lead to £100 fines under new crackdown
British transport authorities can issue fines up to £100 for bus nuisances like loud audio, vaping, and littering under new government-approved rules
The UK government has launched a nationwide crackdown and awareness campaign aimed at tackling antisocial behavior, noise, and everyday nuisances on public transport.
Under the initiative—highlighted by a new rail campaign titled "Share the journey, not the noise"—passengers are strongly urged to use headphones rather than playing music or videos out loud on speaker.
Alongside the campaign, local transport authorities in England have been granted powers to issue fixed penalty notices of up to £100 for bus-related nuisance behaviors such as loud audio, vaping, and littering, subject to local rules approved by the Transport Secretary.
On the rail network, individuals who refuse to comply with requests to turn off loud media risk being removed at the next station and facing prosecution with fines scaling up to £1,000 under existing railway bylaws.
To protect frontline workers, bus drivers will not be tasked with enforcement; instead, authorized transport safety officers and police will handle infractions using a structured three-step approach involving engagement, explanation, and eventual enforcement if compliance is refused.

title: French PM calls for partial curfews as nationwide riots and protests escalate
text:
French PM calls for partial curfews as nationwide riots and protests escalate
French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has announced localized curfews following a weekend of violent nationwide protests, widespread looting, and clashes that left nearly 2,400 arrested
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has instructed local authorities to implement "local and partial" curfews in response to severe nationwide unrest, rioting, and widespread looting.
The measures follow a weekend of violent demonstrations and student protests—driven by cost-of-living pressures and economic anxieties—that spilled over into widespread clashes, the ransacking of an estimated 2,000 shops, and damage to public buildings.
Nuñez-whose offer to resign was rejected by French President Emmanuel Macron - said there was a "lack of anticipation" from officers
The disorder began last month with students protesting over school conditions, but have since escalated to take in a broader range of concerns
Lecornu says the movement is being led by "ultra-left radical groups" hoping to "create chaos" before the 2027 French presidential elections
More than half a million people took to the streets on Saturday. On Sunday, more than 350 arrests were made in Paris alone, with at least five shops looted
While giving regional prefects and municipalities the power to enforce targeted restrictions starting Monday evening, the Prime Minister emphasized that the curfews would be strictly localized. He explicitly ruled out imposing a blanket curfew over the entire city of Paris.
As reported by the Guardian, nearly 2,400 people have been arrested and close to 1,000 police officers injured since the worst of the clashes began.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez acknowledged that authorities experienced a "lack of anticipation" and that security forces momentarily lost control in major cities.
Nuñez offered his resignation, which President Emmanuel Macron rejected, instead tasking him with overhauling operational security methods.
While prioritizing localized curfews for now, Prime Minister Lecornu noted that the government remains prepared to declare a broader state of emergency if the violence continues to escalate.

title: Could Putin, Trump and Xi meet to discuss Ukraine? Kremlin responds
text:
Could Putin, Trump and Xi meet to discuss Ukraine? Kremlin responds
Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit is scheduled for November 18–19 in Shenzhen
The Kremlin on Monday raised the possibility of holding a trilateral meeting of Putin with US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping next month on the sidelines of the APEC summit in China.
The response from Russia comes after the Wall Street Journal reported that Putin floated the idea of holding such talks with Trump and Xi for making a Moscow-favorable deal on the Ukraine to end the conflict.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov responded, “"Given that all three heads of state may potentially take part in the summit in China, the subject of such a hypothetical meeting was indeed raised.”
“It was raised, but no specific proposals or agreements were discussed or put forward by anyone, either regarding the meeting itself or the possible agenda and content of that meeting.”
Peskov also admired the US efforts in holding peace talks aimed at resolving this conflict. Speaking about the involvement of Ukraine in the potential meeting, Peskov said it is impossible to reach a final settlement without the involvement of someone from Kyiv who is prepared to take responsibility.
Earlier this morning, Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, shared the US stance over this summit.
"There's been talks of a meeting. I don't know whether it's been finalized, but the president has been clear. He'd like the war in Ukraine and Russia to end,” Rubio said.
However, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha slammed the idea of such a summit.
"A trilateral meeting between the leaders of Ukraine, the US, and Russia could help end the war sooner. A trilateral meeting between the leaders of Russia, China, and the US would do only the opposite: encourage Putin to continue this war," he said on X.
Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit is scheduled for November 18–19 in Shenzhen.

title: Putin approves major Russian government reshuffle following parliamentary elections
text:
Putin approves major Russian government reshuffle following parliamentary elections
The changes come as Russia seeks new drivers of economic growth to navigate a rising budget deficit, higher taxes, and elevated interest rates
Russian President Vladimir Putin has approved a major government cabinet reshuffle proposed by Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin, following recent parliamentary elections that secured a historic majority for the ruling United Russia party.
Analysts have characterized the changes as a reinforcement of the government’s fiscal leadership, driven by the need to find new sources of growth, manage a rising budget deficit, and navigate high interest rates and increased tax burdens.
According to Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, the personnel changes were greenlit during discussions addressing key social and economic priorities.
The shakeup arrives as Moscow faces mounting economic headwinds including a widening budget deficit, high interest rates, elevated tax burdens, and an urgent need to uncover new sources of growth.
Major role shifts and key appointments:
The structural adjustments heavily reinforce the administration's fiscal leadership.
Long-serving Finance Minister Anton Siluanov has been appointed to take on additional responsibilities as a deputy prime minister, maintaining his financial portfolio while elevating his policy role.
Additionally, transportation Minister Andrei Nikitin has been nominated as a deputy prime minister to manage the development of the national transport sector, succeeding Vitaly Savelyev.
In another notable shift, longtime chief of government staff Dmitry Grigorenko transitioned out of his post, with Prime Minister Mishustin nominating First Deputy Finance Minister Irina Okladnikova to step into the role.
If confirmed by lawmakers, Okladnikova will make history as the first woman to serve as chief of government staff.
The newly proposed appointments have been submitted to the State Duma for formal legislative approval.

title: Ukraine performs world's first drone soldier evacuation from the frontline
text:
Ukraine performs world's first drone soldier evacuation from the frontline
The rescue occurred shortly after Ukraine began front-line testing of StarGate
Ukraine has achieved a milestone by performing the world’s first drone soldier evacuation.
In a latest development, Ukrainian forces evacuated a wounded soldier from the front line using a heavy aerial drone, claiming it as a world-first operation of its kind.
Ukraine’s 92nd Assault Brigade announced the mission on October 19 via its Unmanned Ground Systems Company's official Telegram channel. The operation was a collaborative effort involving personnel from 92nd Assault Brigade, 30th Mechanized Brigade, 14th Mechanized Brigade, 10th Army Corps and Gurzuf Defence.
Napalm, a squad commander and programmer with the 92nd Brigade’s unmanned ground systems company stated that “This is a historic event, at least for our unit.”
A wounded infantryman from the 30th Mechanized Brigade could not be evacuated using standard unmanned ground vehicles due to intense Russian drone activity and heavy mining.
To bypass these hazards, soldiers modified a Ukrainian-made Gurzuf Defence heavy hexacopter, originally designed as a bomber, to carry the wounded soldier. Gurzuf Defence provided the drone free of charge.
Working closely with the manufacturer, they implemented technical solutions to ensure stability in flight while carrying human weight, following preliminary test flights at Gurzuf facilities.
Gurzuf Defence supplied the heavy hexacopter free of charge for the evacuation operation.
The rescue occurred shortly after Ukraine began front-line testing of StarGate, a purpose-built medical evacuation drone developed by SkyFall for the 475th Separate Assault Regiment.
The StarGate drone can carry up to 150 kg on a medical stretcher, has a one-way range of 15 km, is expected to cost at least $50,000 per system, and has a production target of up to 1,000 units per month by the end of 2026.

title: Global food inflation set to accelerate into 2027 as supply shocks mount
text:
Global food inflation set to accelerate into 2027 as supply shocks mount
Driven by Red Sea shipping disruptions, costly fertilizers, and El Niño droughts, agricultural markets face a prolonged squeeze
Recent report shows, global food markets face mounting price pressures as a compounding wave of geopolitical conflicts, extreme weather, and logistical bottlenecks threaten to drive up the cost of living globally through late 2026 and into 2027.
According to the World Bank, food prices in the September quarter outpaced headline inflation in 22% of the 150 countries it analyzed, up from 14% in the previous quarter.
The United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in a basket of internationally traded commodities, averaged 136 points in September, the highest reading since November 2022.
Rising prices heighten the risk of social unrest and could prompt governments that are key suppliers to impose export bans, further exacerbating shortages.
In Indonesia, rice prices have already jumped to record highs amid forecasts of delayed rains, while the cost of bread in Egypt has risen by a quarter and sugar prices in India hit an all-time high as the weakest monsoon in over a decade curbed production.
"All this has put considerable pressure on the system," said Maximo Torero, chief economist at the FAO.
"We will see a bigger impact towards the end of the year, at the beginning of next year and potentially throughout next year."
The world's poorest consumers are being hit the hardest as food prices rise sharply in low- and middle-income countries across the Middle East, North Africa and Asia, where food accounts for a larger share of household spending.
As reported, wheat prices have spiked over 30% this year, while rice prices in major Asian exporting nations have jumped 10% to 13% despite large underlying inventories. Staple items like sugar, onions, and cooking oils are hitting record highs in key markets.
Furthermore, ongoing Red Sea shipping diversions, Black Sea grain corridor attacks, and rising oil prices have pushed freight rates up by roughly 50% on vital global routes, squeezing shipping margins and delivery timelines.
Lingering El Niño weather patterns, combined with soaring fertilizer and fuel costs driven by regional conflicts, are also severely straining agricultural production yields worldwide.
According to World Bank data, food inflation is also outpacing general headline inflation in nearly a quarter of tracked countries, heavily squeezing vulnerable consumers and heightening risks of social unrest.

title: Putin proposes Trump-Xi summit on Ukraine deal, Rubio shares US stance
text:
Putin proposes Trump-Xi summit on Ukraine deal, Rubio shares US stance
Potential trilateral talks will take place on the sidelines of the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit
Russian president Vladimir Putin has proposed a trilateral talks with US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping to discuss a peace deal on the Ukraine conflict.
According to the Wall Street Journal citing sources privy to the matter, the proposed summit is meant to favour Moscow in drafting the peace plan. As per the source, the idea of holding a summit was floated during Putin’s telephone call with Trump on October 9 that ended with a diesel deal between the two countries.
According to the report, the Kremlin has proposed holding the trilateral talks on the sidelines of the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which is scheduled for November 18–19 in Shenzhen.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed the possibility of such a meeting. “There is no clear understanding yet regarding the meeting itself or its potential agenda, although all three parties acknowledge the hypothetical possibility of such a meeting taking place,” he told the Wall Street Journal.
Although no response has come from either the White House or Xi’s office. But a senior US official told the media outlet that Trump had not agreed to such a summit but “he could be receptive to the idea.”
Putin’s proposal comes as the international community is witnessing the warming ties between Washington and Moscow marked by the diesel deal and suspension of Russia sanctions.
Soon after the proposal, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio responded that Ukraine and Russia should be focused on ending the war between them.
Speaking about the possibility of a trilateral summit, Rubio said, "There's been talks of a meeting. I don't know whether it's been finalized, but the president has been clear. He'd like the war in Ukraine and Russia to end."
"We see nothing good coming from this war. We see a lot of downside to it, including the very real risk of escalation and spread of this thing.., Rubio added.

title: France: Macron rejects interior minister Nunez resignation after nationwide riots
text:
France: Macron rejects interior minister Nunez resignation after nationwide riots
President Emmanuel Macron rejected Interior Minister Nuñez's resignation after the October 17 riots, demanding transparency over security planning failures
French President Emmanuel Macron has officially declined Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez's offer to resign following the severe, nationwide riots and widespread civil unrest that swept across Paris, France.
Beyond the capital, violence erupted in cities like Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, and Limoges—where a historic 19th-century town hall was largely destroyed by a deliberately set fire.
President Emmanuel Macron and top government officials condemned the extreme violence as "unacceptable," deploying heavy security forces using tear gas and water cannons to restore order.
The Elysée Palace stated that keeping Nuñez in office is essential to maintaining an unbroken chain of command within the police and security forces during an active national crisis.
While rejecting the resignation, President Macron explicitly criticized planning and intelligence "failures" that allowed the demonstrations to erupt into widespread arson, looting, and clashes.
As reported, the widespread protest has been sparked by public anger over rising living costs, faltering public services and also the state of schools.
In response, Macron has ordered Nuñez to rapidly implement new operational methods and security frameworks to better handle looters and ensure full transparency regarding the security lapses that preceded the weekend's violence.
As reported, nationwide demonstrations erupted into riots on Saturday, October 17, with a town hall torched, shops pillaged and buildings covered in graffiti as violent groups clashed with police in cities.
More clashes also broke out in Paris and Marseille on Sunday, where riot police intervened to prevent attempts to ransack businesses.

title: Trump explains why he put Russia sanctions on hold
text:
Trump explains why he put Russia sanctions on hold
On Friday President Trump signed an executive order for suspension of Russia sanctions
President Donald Trump defended his move of suspending Russia sanctions two days before the law would take into effect on Sunday.
On Friday, Trump signed an executive order to exempt Russia from the US-related sanctions and tariffs, citing that his move is in the US national interests.
The sudden backtracking ignited a backlash from various lawmakers who blasted the Trump administration for giving Putin leverage in war with Ukraine and undermining efforts to pressurize Moscow.
In his recent Truth Social Post, Trump explained the reason why he eased Russia sanctions. According to the president, the decision to suspend several Russian sanctions is aimed at keeping Moscow at the negotiating table.
He wrote, “"I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine,” adding that he didn't want to "do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table".
Zelenskyy responded to the act of Trump being sided with Vladimir Putin as a “historic mistake,” meanwhile Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev called sanctions waiver an “important and truly historic moment.”
In his post, Trump also slammed the Ukrainian president for not wanting to end this war. He also said Zelensky "doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did.”
According to the president, if he would, he could have made a better deal two years ago than he can now.
In the past few weeks, the relations between Washington and Kyiv have hit rock bottom as Trump called for electing a new president as Zelensky is incapable of making a deal with us.
US’ pivot to Moscow camp also drew fierce remarks from Zelenskyy who felt betrayed by the Trump administration as Trump made a diesel deal with Russia last week.

title: Trump says Zelensky 'doesn't want to end this war' after Ukraine attacks Russia
text:
Trump says Zelensky 'doesn't want to end this war' after Ukraine attacks Russia
Trump accused Zelensky of obstructing efforts to negotiate peace with Moscow
US President Donald Trump has sharply criticised Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky after Ukraine launched a major drone attack on Russia, targeting key energy infrastructure.
According to CNN, Ukraine carried out one of its largest drone attacks this year overnight on Saturday, striking the St Petersburg Oil Terminal despite Trump's calls to stop attacks on Russian energy facilities.
Russia's defence ministry claimed it intercepted 1,015 Ukrainian drone and reported one death and five injuries.
Trump accused Zelensky of obstructing efforts to negotiate peace with Moscow.
In a Truth Social post on Sunday, Trump claimed Zelensky “doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did.”
He said he did not want to push Russia away from negotiations, insisting progress was being made towards ending the conflict.
However, Zelensky warned that Washington siding with Moscow would be a “historic mistake.”
Ukraine's president also accused Russia of continuing attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure despite Trump's announcement of an energy ceasefire.
Ukrainian authorities reported 11 deaths and nearly 50 injuries from Russian missile and drone strikes over 24 hours.
Meanwhile, Zelensky raised concerns about restrictions on Ukrainian access to Starlink and temporary interruptions to US intelligence sharing.
Despite growing tensions, Zelensky said he remained in contact with US officials, including Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, to pursue peace negotiations.

title: US indicts California woman accused of spying on Taiwan president's son for China
text:
US indicts California woman accused of spying on Taiwan president's son for China
Wanying Zhang, 34, also known as Heather, faces charges of conspiracy and acting as an unregistered foreign agent
A California woman has been indicted on charges of allegedly spying for China on the son of Taiwan's president, according to US federal prosecutors.
NBC News reported that Wanying Zhang, 34, also known as Heather, faces charges of conspiracy and acting as an unregistered foreign agent.
Teh indictment, filed on October 9 in California, alleges Zhang conducted surveillance outside the president's son's home near Seattle between June and September 2025.
Prosecutors claim she photographed and filmed the property, collected vehicle registration details and shared the information with a suspected Chinese government handler.
Zhang allegedly travelled from California to the Seattle area to monitor the unidentified individual.
Authorities also claim she visited China in August 2025 to meet a government official.
Her lawyer, Craig Harbaugh, has rejected the allegations, describing Zhang as a mother of two who lives with her family in Irvine, California.
“The government’s theory — she’s been a sleeper agent for the last 10 years, working as a real estate agent, raising her family and will choose to go to China and abandon her work, her family and her home — it’s not supported,” Harbaugh said during an October 7 court hearing.
A federal judge ordered Zhang to remain in custody after prosecutors raised concerns she could flee.
She is scheduled to appear in court on Friday and could face up to 15 years in prison if convicted.

title: Chris Nanos mocked for Halloween video as Nancy Guthrie remains missing
text:
Chris Nanos mocked for Halloween video as Nancy Guthrie remains missing
Chris Nanos, however, reiterated previously that the department remains dedicated to the Nancy Guthrie case
Since the disappearance of Nancy Guthrie, the person who has arguably got the most spotlight among the section of authorities who have been investigating the case was Chris Nanos.
The sheriff of the Arizona Department was perceived by a quarter for botching the investigation of the abduction of anchor Savannah Guthrie.
Now, he was featured in a 90-second video promoting PAW Patrol, an animated series, as Chase, a German Shepherd character in the show.
Posing as Chase, Nanos appeared with dog-like ears and a nose painted to resemble a dog.
The video was an effort by the sheriff's department to promote the Halloween event set for October 24.
The slogan linked to the Paw Patrol, which said, "Good thing no county is too big or dog too small," was used by Nanos.
But in response, some users found the zany Halloween video inappropriate because Guthrie remained missing.
According to the Daily Mail, the Pima County Sheriff's Department turned off the comment section. Still, the netizens kept mocking the video.
In addition, the sheriff's department earlier stated that the ransom note said to be associated with Guthrie's disappearance was not credible.
Guthrie, however, has remained missing since Feb. 1.

title: Driver released after deadly Wichita soccer crash leaves two dead and 10 injured
text:
Driver released after deadly Wichita soccer crash leaves two dead and 10 injured
The incident happened around 3:25 PM on Saturday at Stryker Sports Complex, where children were playing football
Two people were killed, including one child, after a pickup truck drove onto a youth football field in Wichita, Kansas, injuring 10 others.
According to CNN, the incident happened around 3:25 PM on Saturday at Stryker Sports Complex, where children were playing football as families watched nearby.
Police identified the victims as Cole Adrian, six, and Nicholas Schafer, 35.
The injured included five children, with victims ranging in age from five to 68. Police said none of the injuries appeared life-threatening.
The driver, a 34-year-old woman, was released pending toxicology tests and a mechanical examination of her vehicle. No charges have been filed.
Two of her children were inside the pickup, while another was playing on a different field.
Emergency crews arrived to find bystanders already helping injured victims.
Police have interviewed more than 30 witnesses and are seeking additional video footage to determine how the truck entered the field.
Wichita Mayor Lily Wu expressed condolences to the victims' families.
“My heart breaks for the families who have lost loved ones, especially the family grieving the loss of a child,” she said.
All events at Stryker Sports Complex have been cancelled until further notice.

title: Andy Burnham targets 'headphone dodgers' with new £100 bus fines
text:
Andy Burnham targets 'headphone dodgers' with new £100 bus fines
Under the Bus Services Act, authorities can introduce and enforce rules against loud music, vaping and littering
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has announced a nationwide crackdown on passengers who play loud music or videos without headphones on public transport.
The new campaign targets so-called “headphone dodgers”, with local transport authorities being advised to issue fines of up to £100 for nuisance behaviour on buses.
Under the Bus Services Act, authorities can introduce and enforce rules against loud music, vaping and littering.
“We’ve all been on the train when someone starts blasting music or videos from their phone. It gets on your nerves and can quickly spoil the journey,” he said.
The government will also launch a poster campaign with the slogan “share the carriage, not the noise”, encouraging passengers to use headphones and avoid speakerphone calls.
Transport safety officers and police will be responsible for enforcement, rather than bus drivers.
Train operators already have powers to impose fines of up to £1,000 for similar behaviour.
The announcement follows growing public frustration over noise on buses and trains, with surveys showing strong support for tougher penalties.

title: Amazon deforestation drops to lowest level since 1988 as Brazil election looms
text:
Amazon deforestation drops to lowest level since 1988 as Brazil election looms
Environmental campaigners warned that the election could determine whether Brazil continues protecting its forests
Deforestation in Brazil's Amazon rainforest has fallen to its lowest level since records began in 1988, according to new government data released ahead of a crucial presidential election.
The Guardian reported that forest destruction dropped by 41.8 percent over the past year to 3,335 square kilometres, beating the previous record low.
Data from Brazil's National Institute for Space Research also shows deforestation has declined by 71.2 percent since 2022, before President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva took office.
Stronger environmental enforcement and increased funding for conservation agencies have helped reduce forest clearance.
However, the rainforest's future remains uncertain ahead of Brazil's October 25 presidential run-off between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro.
Lula has prioritised environmental protection, while Bolsonaro has attracted support from agricultural and mining interests seeking greater access to natural resources.
Under Jair Bolsonaro's previous administration, Amazon deforestation increased by 59.5 percent.
Environmental campaigners warned that the election could determine whether Brazil continues protecting its forests.
Marcio Astrini, executive secretary of the Climate Observatory, said, according to The Guardian: “The figure makes it clear that putting an end to forest destruction in Brazil is entirely possible.”

title: Alberta separation unlikely as new poll reveals strong support for staying in Canada
text:
Alberta separation unlikely as new poll reveals strong support for staying in Canada
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith has urged voters to support the referendum's first nine questions
Alberta's push towards separation from Canada appears unlikely to succeed, with a new poll showing most residents oppose taking the next step towards independence.
An Ipsos survey conducted for Global News found that 70 percent of Albertans plan to vote against beginning the legal process for a binding separation referendum on Monday.
Only 23 percent support proceeding with that process, an increase of three percentage points from September.
Support was highest among men, people aged 35 to 54 and residents living outside Calgary and Edmonton.
The survey questioned 801 Albertans between October 13 and 16.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith has urged voters to support the referendum's first nine questions, which focus on immigration and constitutional issues.
She argues that approving those proposals would strengthen Alberta's position in negotiations with Ottawa.

title: Obama says Ilhan Omar deportation threat could set dangerous precedent for Americans
text:
Obama says Ilhan Omar deportation threat could set dangerous precedent for Americans
Obama criticised the Trump administration on Sunday following an investigation into Omar's citizenship
Former US President Barack Obama has condemned comments by Donald Trump's border czar, Tom Homan, suggesting Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar could lose her American citizenship and face deportation.
According to The Guardian, Obama criticised the Trump administration on Sunday following an investigation into Omar's citizenship and a federal raid on her Minnesota home.
Homan was asked during a Fox News interview whether authorities could strip Omar of her citizenship and deport her.
“Of course”, he replied, explaining that citizenship can be revoked if someone lied during the naturalisation process.
Obama accused the administration of targeting an elected official for criticising the president.
He warned that “the full weight of the federal government is being brought down on a law-abiding elected official because she has dared to criticize the president.”
Omar, who was born in Somalia, became a US citizen in 2000 after arriving in America as a refugee. Obama urged Americans across political parties to defend Omar's rights.
Federal investigators are examining whether immigration laws were violated when she obtained citizenship.
Omar has denied wrongdoing, while her lawyers say there is no legitimate evidence supporting the allegations.
The investigation comes weeks before November's midterm elections, when Omar is seeking re-election.

title: Four Canadian soldiers killed in Wainwright fire as Mark Carney orders flags lowered
text:
Four Canadian soldiers killed in Wainwright fire as Mark Carney orders flags lowered
The fire broke out on Saturday during combat training involving approximately 84 soldiers
Four Canadian soldiers have been killed and 39 people hospitalised after a fast-moving fire swept through CFB Wainwright, a military training base in Alberta.
According to The Guardian, the fire broke out on Saturday during combat training involving approximately 84 soldiers. At least 19 people remain in critical condition.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney described the incident as “one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime”.
The military identified those killed as Sergeant Morgan Wong and Privates Shaun Farrell, Aidan Goulding and Hayden Lykkemark.
Major General Wade Rutland said a grass fire spread rapidly after strong winds suddenly changed direction, pushing flames towards soldiers conducting simulated combat exercises.
“The fire was a kilometre away when the wind shifted. That is not normal for a fire to move a kilometre in 36 seconds,” he said.
Emergency crews and military personnel responded as hospitals in Wainwright and Edmonton struggled with the number of injured soldiers.
Carney ordered flags on federal buildings to fly at half-mast and requested a detailed report into the tragedy.
The cause of the fire remains under investigation, with the RCMP involved.
CFB Wainwright is one of Canada's busiest military training facilities, used to prepare soldiers for combat operations.

title: Macron empowers local authorities to ban gatherings amid protests
text:
Macron empowers local authorities to ban gatherings amid protests
Macron, in his speech, also took a hardline view against the rowdy protestors
French President Emmanuel Macron announced France would ban certain public gatherings in coordination with mayors of French cities in the wake of deadly protests in Paris.
The measure was announced during the president's earlier national address on Sunday.
In his speech, Macron further stated that the youth of France are "expressing great anguish and concern about the future. We need to pay heed to what they are saying, and we must not minimise the hardships that they are facing."
Regarding the rowdy protestors, the French president said, "Those who tried to bring down the Republic will pay the price."
Meanwhile, local authorities and mayors can handle the banning of some public gatherings and implement it wherever they see fit.

title: Trump reacts to violent unrest in France, blames immigration
text:
Trump reacts to violent unrest in France, blames immigration
Trump has said that France ought to seal its borders in response to escalating violence across the country
US President Donald Trump reportedly blamed immigration for the flurry of instability shaking France in a Truth Social post on Sunday, following weeks of protests over rising living costs and deteriorating public services that erupted into widespread turmoil across major cities.
Trump wrote accusing immigrants from distinct cultural backgrounds undermining the state’s ability, “ France is burning”.
“The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country, he continued.”
His remarks followed one of France’s most destructive unrests in recent days as demonstrations erupted into rioting on Saturday with government buildings set ablaze, stores looted and demonstrators scuffling with law enforcement.
French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu also denounced the destruction and said the government would not be daunted by those responsible. He blamed the violence on the far-left criminals, warning against efforts to capitalize on the turmoil for partisan advantage leading up to next year’s presidential election.
The demonstrations mobilized hundreds of participants nationwide. Furthermore, French President Emmanuel Macron also condemned the attacks, pledging to bring to justice those responsible for the destruction.

title: EU condemns West Bank settler attacks targeting European diplomats
text:
EU condemns West Bank settler attacks targeting European diplomats
Amid rising tensions in the West Bank, Brussels demands accountability following assaults on international officials and local communities
The European Union has strongly condemned a series of violent attacks by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank, which notably targeted a delegation of visiting European diplomats and a French mayor.
"We take positive note of statements by several Israeli representatives who condemned the attacks but we expect full accountability as well as effective measures to prevent continued acts of violence and violent harassment, including during the ongoing olive harvest season, as well as against journalists," the EU spokesperson said.
The condemnation follows an incident in the West Bank village of Taybeh, where masked settlers confronted and attacked vehicles carrying European officials and local activists who were observing conditions during the sensitive olive harvest season.
Belgian Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot also highlighted the assaults, which targeted Palestinian civilians alongside the international delegation.
While acknowledging that several Israeli representatives have spoken out against the violence, the EU foreign policy spokesperson emphasized that rhetoric must be matched by action.
The bloc is demanding full accountability for the perpetrators and effective measures from Israeli authorities to halt ongoing harassment against Palestinians, journalists, and international workers in the region.

title: France protests turn violent: Over 1,800 arrested amid nationwide clashes and looting as riots devastate Paris streets
text:
France protests turn violent: Over 1,800 arrested amid nationwide clashes and looting as riots devastate Paris streets
Around 550,000 people took to the streets across France to protest rising costs and declining public services
France counts cost of worst unrest in years to the wreckage of one of its most violent days of unrest in years after protests over high prices and public services left one demonstrator dead, hundreds of police injured and nearly 2000 people arrested.
Nationwide demonstrations erupted into riots on Saturday, with a town hall torched, shops ransacked, and buildings covered in graffiti as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country.
Mass demonstrations across France—sparked by widespread anger over inflation, the rising cost of living, and high school conditions—degenerated into severe nationwide rioting and violence.
Authorities reported that over 1,800 people have been arrested nationwide following intensive clashes with police, arson attacks, and widespread looting.
Major thoroughfares, particularly in Paris (such as along Boulevard Magenta), were left heavily damaged with smashed storefronts, burned-out vehicles, and debris-littered streets.
Organized groups targeted boutiques, banks, and department stores.
As reported, by the Guardian, French interior minister Laurent Nunez in a post on X, said “the Republic will not yield” as more than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters have been injured in the demonstrations.
“The material damage is considerable,” Nunez added, pointing to damaged shops.
He blamed thousands of “far-left” protesters along with “criminals who looted and ransacked” buildings across France.
“The Republic will yield nothing to those who seek to impose disorder and violence,” he said.
Beyond the capital, violence erupted in cities like Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, and Limoges—where a historic 19th-century town hall was largely destroyed by a deliberately set fire.
President Emmanuel Macron and top government officials condemned the extreme violence as "unacceptable," deploying heavy security forces using tear gas and water cannons to restore order.

title: Pope Leo outlines major gradual return to duties in first event since cancer surgery
text:
Pope Leo outlines major gradual return to duties in first event since cancer surgery
Pope Leo hails crowds at the Vatican in first event since cancer surgery
On Sunday, Pope Leo pledged to ease back into his routine as the leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics as he welcomed crowds in St. Peter’s Square during his first public event in his early recovery phase for lung cancer following surgery five days ago.
The 71-year-old pontiff had undergone an operation on Tuesday to remove the lower lobe of his right lung, igniting debate about how his illness may change his 17-month papacy.
While looking down with a soft smile from the Vatican's Apostolic Palace as he spoke to pilgrims below firmly, he thanked people across the world for their prayers and stated he was not ready to return to his usual routine.
Leo said in a statement: “Having overcome this dedicated phase, I will not gradually resume my activities, always with the help of God and your prayers.”
The pope who was released from Rome’s Gemelli hospital on Saturday approached the palace window unassisted and held his regularly scheduled weekly midday session. Furthermore, he also implored pilgrims beneath leaden skies to set aside self-serving devotion and serve God without compromise.

title: Trump-Zelensky clash sparks urgent fears over future US support for Ukraine
text:
Trump-Zelensky clash sparks urgent fears over future US support for Ukraine
As public tensions mount over shifting policy stances, Ukraine faces heightened vulnerabilities in defense coordination and technology access
Political tensions between Washington and Kyiv have escalated sharply, casting a heavy shadow over the future of American military and intelligence backing for Ukraine.
The friction intensified following a series of public clashes between U.S. President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, driven by disagreements over energy infrastructure strikes, recent U.S. executive actions pausing certain sanctions packages, and a controversial diesel deal.
Fears among Ukrainian and European officials have grown following temporary disruptions to military-grade satellite communication infrastructure (such as Starshield) and warnings from U.S. officials regarding potential reductions in critical intelligence sharing.
While Washington maintains that key communication channels and intelligence links remain under review with Secretary of State Marco Rubio pointing to a 60-day window to evaluate broader economic and diplomatic impacts—the unfolding dynamic has left Kyiv facing heightened vulnerabilities as it prepares for ongoing defense operations.
The widening rift has sparked concerns that Trump and Zelenskiy's tumultuous relationship could lead to even worse outcomes for Kyiv.
As per Reuters, Trump could yet restrict the supply of weapons to Ukraine, follow through on threats to stop sharing battlefield intelligence, or strike more economic deals with Moscow.

title: China targets solar supply chain with new export restrictions on key technologies
text:
China targets solar supply chain with new export restrictions on key technologies
China proposes strict export controls on 12 advanced solar technologies to protect its dominant green-energy supply chain
China's Ministry of Commerce has proposed a new set of export controls targeting 12 advanced solar-manufacturing technologies and core equipment, citing national security and strategic interests.
The ministry released a statement on Friday that it proposed the photovoltaic technologies to China's export-control list, adding that greater oversight is needed because solar technologies are increasingly being used in sensitive areas like aerospace and national defense.
The sweeping proposal is part of a broader regulatory overhaul spanning 40 key technologies—including artificial intelligence and biopharmaceuticals—designed to protect Beijing’s dominant technological edge in the renewable energy sector as countries like the U.S. and India ramp up domestic manufacturing.
Next-Gen solar cells targeted:
The draft splits the targeted solar technologies into two tiers: items facing complete export prohibitions and those requiring strict export licensing/restrictions.
Manufacturing know-how for cutting-edge perovskite and perovskite-silicon tandem cells (which boast high efficiency rates) face strict export bans.
The restrictions cover advanced production methods for ultra-thin silicon wafers (70 µm or less), large-scale fluidized-bed polysilicon manufacturing processes, and high-efficiency cell tech like TOPCon and xBC variants.
Because China controls a vast majority of the global solar supply chain, the proposed measures threaten to complicate international expansion plans, raise capital expenditure costs for western clean energy projects, and shift equipment supply dynamics.
The draft is currently open for public consultation through mid-November, with interim pre-export registration measures enacted in the interim.

title: Rubio leads US delegation to Central Asia to expand trade and strategic influence
text:
Rubio leads US delegation to Central Asia to expand trade and strategic influence
Secretary of State Marco Rubio kicked off a high-stakes tour of Central Asia and India to deepen economic ties and counter regional rivals
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio embarked on a high-profile diplomatic tour to Central Asia and India, leading a major business delegation to deepen commercial ties and counterbalance the influence of Russia and China.
The top US diplomat is scheduled to land in Samarkand on Sunday to meet with leaders from the C5+1, a grouping that brings together the United States and the Muslim-majority post-Soviet states of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan.
Rubio traveled to Samarkand to participate in ministerial talks with Central Asian leaders, focusing heavily on commercial diplomacy, energy cooperation, and expanding access to critical rare earth mineral resources.
Accompanied by more than 200 business executives, the push aims to establish lasting American economic and corporate footprints along strategic regional corridors.
Following Uzbekistan, Rubio headed to Mumbai and Jamnagar to meet with corporate leaders—including a focus on infrastructure and energy investments—to advance ongoing bilateral trade discussions.
While Rubio steers a commercial and strategic offensive in Central and South Asia, other U.S. special envoys and officials continue managing critical developments across traditional foreign policy hot spots.
US officials have portrayed resource-rich Central Asia — the region between China, Russia and Iran — as worthy of more attention than it received from US President Donald Trump's predecessors.
Trump hosted C5 leaders at the White House last November, when Kazakhstan agreed to join the Abraham Accords, a series of agreements under which Muslim-majority countries have normalized or deepened relations with Israel.
Separately, Trump met with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev at the United Nations General Assembly last September.
Regional politics aside, the trip fits an emerging pattern in which Rubio often visits regions not at the center of the news cycle, while leaving some more fraught foreign-policy portfolios to other Trump aides, including special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and Vice President JD Vance.
More than 200 business executives will accompany Rubio to Uzbekistan, the State Department said.
The Central Asian diplomat said the Trump administration has focused its commercial efforts on expanding access to the area's rare earth mineral resources.
After Uzbekistan, Rubio will visit the Indian cities of Mumbai and Jamnagar to meet with business leaders, including Reliance Industries, Chairman Mukesh Ambani, who earned the Trump administration's favor earlier in the year by backing a new refinery in Texas.
As reported, the trip is due to wrap up on Thursday, October 22, 2026.
Rubio's previous foreign trip, in early October, took him to Greece, Portugal and Iceland.

title: Vietnam signs free trade agreement with EFTA nations including Switzerland and Norway
text:
Vietnam signs free trade agreement with EFTA nations including Switzerland and Norway
Vietnam signs a landmark free-trade agreement with EFTA nations, slashing tariffs on industrial goods, seafood, and key agricultural products
Vietnam has officially signed a comprehensive free-trade agreement with the EFTA (European Free Trade Association) bloc including Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein.
As reported, key highlights of the agreement include tariff elimination, agriculture access, trade investment and boost.
EFTA countries will eliminate import tariffs on industrial and seafood products originating from Vietnam immediately upon implementation.
Vietnam's trade ministry said it signed the deal in Hanoi with the European Free Trade Association members.
According to the Norwegian government, around half of Norway's exports to Vietnam will be tariff-free when the agreement enters into force, with more than 98% to be tariff-free within seven years.
Long-stalled free-trade talks were relaunched last year amid global tensions over US tariffs. Negotiations concluded in July.
Trade ministry said the Southeast Asian country mainly exports seafood, footwear, textiles, machinery and equipment, electronics and components to the EFTA market and imports industrial machinery and equipment, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and raw materials for production.
Meanwhile, Vietnam will gradually reduce or eliminate tariffs on products from EFTA nations over an 11-year transition period.
Select agricultural goods—including cheese, coffee, and chocolate—will gain duty-free access to Vietnam under a phased transition timeline.
The ministry said, bilateral trade between Vietnam and the EFTA bloc has grown steadily, reaching roughly €4.8 billion.
The pact aims to streamline customs, open up investment protections in non-service sectors like manufacturing, mining, and agriculture and foster deeper tech and economic cooperation.

title: Lindsay Clancy lawyer criticised for outing lone holdout juror
text:
Lindsay Clancy lawyer criticised for outing lone holdout juror
Lindsay Clancy's lawyer also asked the court to open an inquiry into the lone holdout juror
In the trial of Lindsay Clancy, the spotlight on a particular juror becomes strikingly important when his identity is revealed in the wake of him becoming the only one holding the mom-of-three criminally responsible.
His name is Michael Desronvil.
With his stance becoming public, he earned admiration and triggered the wrath of critics.
Recently, after multiple interviews, he appeared for his first televised interview.
In the spotlight, Naema Rahmani, a former federal prosecutor, told NewsNation that Clancy lawyer Kevin Reddington made a mistake by publicly identifying him as one of the jurors who disagreed with fellow jurors.
“I don’t think Reddington should have outed him," he shared.
However, Rahmani argued Desronvil interviews are doing the opposite of maintaining his privacy.
"But if you wanted to maintain his privacy, now he’s doing a media tour. That’s not going to help."
By speaking, Rahmani believes Desronvil — who in the press is popular for being the lone holdout juror — is attracting attention onto himself by speaking out.
“To some folks, Lindsay Clancy supporters, he’s a villain; to others, he’s really a hero of sorts. So I think he’s bringing on some of the attention to himself,” he said.
The former federal prosecutor, then, focused on Reddington. His view is plain: do not outvote the jury who disagreed with other jurors.
“Although I have been critical of Reddington. I know he’s advocating for his clients. But if you believe in our jury system, leave the guy alone. Move on to the next trial."
Clancy's next hearing date is on Nov. 2.

title: OpenAI seek to raise $30 billion at $1.4 trillion valuation ahead of Anthropic IPO
text:
OpenAI seek to raise $30 billion at $1.4 trillion valuation ahead of Anthropic IPO
To lock in a staggering private valuation before its rival's public market debut, the AI giant is pushing to close a massive funding round ahead of Anthropic IPO
OpenAI is rushing to close a massive $30 billion funding round—targeting a valuation north of $1.4 trillion—to lock in its private valuation before rival Anthropic hits the public markets.
By securing capital before Anthropic’s anticipated public debut, OpenAI aims to set its own valuation terms.
As reported, Anthropic's upcoming financial disclosures (via its confidential S-1 filing) will give Wall Street a transparent look into frontier AI financials, which could invite intense scrutiny and direct comparisons for OpenAI.
Sam Altman's AI firm has been pitching investors on an annualized revenue run-rate between $50 billion and $70 billion, though the race highlights mounting pressure as both firms scale up infrastructure and compute spending ahead of their expected public offerings.
The rapid timetable reflects, in part, a desire to get ahead of Anthropic as the two frontier labs are increasingly tapping in to a similar investor base.
Experts weighs if OpenAI wants to capitalize on its recent revenue growth after launching new models.
OpenAI is pitching investors on growth that accelerated after the launch of its GPT-6 Astra model, saying it had reached $50 billion in annualized revenue and expecting that figure to rise to $70 billion by year-end.
The AI platform has also cut prices on its cheaper models, which it said has boosted usage, and told investors it can further lower the price of AI models.
Though there is high demand for the shares of both companies, investors face the challenge of evaluating and allocating capital to two complexes, competing offerings within days or weeks of each other.
Some investor’s view OpenAI’s financing push as an effort to lock in capital from funds that might otherwise devote more of their resources to Anthropic’s IPO.

title: Supreme Court rejects Google challenge to patent office review policy: Here's why
text:
Supreme Court rejects Google challenge to patent office review policy: Here's why
By declining to hear the appeal, the high court preserves a controversial rule that restricts administrative challenges to older patents.
The U.S. Supreme Court has declined to hear an appeal from Alphabet Inc.’s Google, leaving in place a federal patent office policy that restricts administrative reviews for older patents.
Core Dispute:
The dispute stemmed from a software patent infringement case involving developer which accused Google of infringing upon its server technology.
The legal battle centered around a software patent infringement dispute between Google and a developer named VirtaMove, which accused Google of infringing on its server software technology.
Google's stance:
In response, Google sought to challenge the validity of the patent through the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB), an administrative tribunal housed within the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office.
However, the agency declined to initiate the review by applying its "settled expectations" practice, a framework under which the board more frequently rejects petitions to review patents that have been active for more than six years.
The patent office argues that older patents have built up "settled expectations" for their owners in the marketplace, making them less appropriate for administrative cancellation procedures.
In response, Google argued in its Supreme Court appeal that the patent office exceeded its statutory authority by imposing artificial time restrictions that were never established by Congress.
By refusing to hear the case, the Supreme Court left lower-court rulings intact without issuing a detailed opinion.
Broader context:
Previously, Lower courtsrejected Google's challenge, and with the Supreme Court opting not to intervene, the policy remains active, dealing a notable setback to major technology companies that routinely rely on these administrative procedures to contest questionable patents.
For tech giants like Google, Apple, and others—who frequently rely on PTAB reviews to invalidate overly broad or suspect software and hardware patents—this decision is a notable blow.
It solidifies the patent office's power to gatekeep administrative challenges, leaving tech firms with fewer avenues to clear out older patents they are accused of infringing.

title: Netflix faces scrutiny over user engagement ahead of Q3 report
text:
Netflix faces scrutiny over user engagement ahead of Q3 report
Facing mounting pressure over plateauing viewing hours and rising domestic churn, the streaming giant heads into high-stakes financial results
As Netflix prepares to report its third-quarter earnings, investors are focusing on slowing user engagement, rising domestic churn and intensifying competition for viewers’ attention.
According to a Nielsen report, the streaming giant faces a fundamental shift in entertainment consumption as lower-cost, creator-led videos increasingly compete with premium scripted content.
YouTube, the leading streaming platform in the US by viewing share, commands nearly twice Netflix’s viewing time, underscoring the growing challenge from digital video competitors.
Analysts warn that slowing viewing hours and intensifying competition could test Netflix’s growth narrative. Ted Sarandos, the company’s co-CEO, recently acknowledged that Netflix “is not growing as fast as I want us to,” while suggesting that live programming could provide an opportunity to accelerate growth.
Market data also points to pressure on viewing time per member compared with previous years, partly reflecting a lighter content slate and competition for consumer attention.
Meanwhile, research firm Apptopia reported that Netflix’s US user churn rose 16.6% year over year in the third quarter, roughly twice the pace recorded in each of the previous three quarters.
Downloads across the US and Canada also fell 20%, pointing to potential challenges in attracting and retaining users.
Netflix has also taken steps to strengthen its cost discipline. The company cut about 6% of its workforce, a move that eMarketer analyst Ross Benes said reflected the streaming industry’s broader shift toward profitability.
Separately, the company underwent a content leadership change, with longtime content head Bela Bajaria leaving and former Disney executive Peter Rice taking over.
With subscriber growth maturing, investors are expected to scrutinize Netflix’s advertising-tier monetization and cost-management strategy for signs that these measures can offset slowing engagement and support profit margins.
According to data compiled by LSEG, Netflix is forecast to post its slowest third-quarter revenue growth in three years, with sales expected to rise 11.8% to $12.87 billion.
The results, due Tuesday, will offer investors a clearer picture of whether the company can sustain growth amid rising churn, shifting viewing habits and mounting competitive pressure.

title: Meta and Tesla are set to report earnings next week: What to know
text:
Meta and Tesla are set to report earnings next week: What to know
Meta and Tesla are set to report earnings in the coming week
Meta and Tesla are scheduled to announce earnings next week in the wake of a weekly market report showing a high market sensitivity.
According to reports, seventy S&P companies are reporting this week with FactSet data revealing that about 45 S&P 500 companies have reported to date.
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite dropped last week as traders moved away from technology stocks-a shift triggered by apprehensions about rising debt levels from AI funding.
On Wednesday, Meta Platforms will report earnings after the market closes and hold a conference call. The LSEG data shows that analysts project Meta’s earnings per share to have surged 460% compared with a year earlier.
This marks Meta's first quarterly results since launching the AI agent Muse on September 8. Notably, Meta shares have surged more than 25% since the release, though investors are seeking evidence of how Muse will affect Meta’s earnings.
LSEG data shows analysts expect to drop Tesla’s earnings to 14.5% compared to the same period last year.
On the contrary, analysts expect Tesla’s revenue to have dropped by 1% over the same period. Wolfe Research estimates Tesla’s earnings fell short of consensus estimates in what the firm calls a tough quarter for automobile stocks.
Tesla’s third-quarter deliveries slumped 2% from a year earlier but surpassed estimates. Bespoke Investment Group data shows Tesla missed analysts’ earnings estimates in two of the last four quarters, respectively.

title: SpaceX sets Q3 2026 earnings release date: What to know
text:
SpaceX sets Q3 2026 earnings release date: What to know
SpaceX set to release its Q3 2026 financial and operational results
SpaceX will reportedly post its third-quarter 2026 post-close operational and financial report after the market close on Tuesday, October 20, while hosting a live audio-only webcast at 3:30 p.m. CT on the same day.
According to a release on SpaceX’s investor site from the company today, the webcast and archived recording will be accessible via its investor relations site where pre-registration is open, and the event will also be livestreamed on X by SpaceX.
This marks one of the first earnings reports since SpaceX went public with shares that began trading on June 12 on the Nasdaq under the ticker SPCX following a $135 per share IPO.
The company’s initial report in August showed $7.8 billion in second-quarter revenue and a net loss of $541 million. Meanwhile, market reactions show positive expectations but with a careful, watchful eye on potential risks.
Nonetheless, the release does not speak or what the webcast will cover beyond the significant results. Tesla reports has already opened its question box for its October.21 earnings call so this is a hectic two days for Elon’s companies.

title: Hyundai to recall nearly 100,000 US vehicles over fire risk from overheating
text:
Hyundai to recall nearly 100,000 US vehicles over fire risk from overheating
Hyundai recalls over 95,000 US vehicles over a seat motor defect that poses a fire risk even when parked
Hyundai to recall nearly 100,000 vehicles over safety risks.
The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) announced a recall for 94,622 vehicles distributed by Hyundai Motor America due to a serious fire risk.
The defect stems from front power seat motors that can overheat if a power seat control switch becomes stuck.
As reported, the electrical malfunction can cause the motors to continuously draw power, creating a fire hazard that can happen whether the vehicle is actively being driven or parked and turned off.
The recall specifically affects certain 2015–2016 Hyundai Genesis and 2017–2020 Genesis G80 models.
Because an official repair remedy is still actively being developed by the manufacturer, the U.S. NHTSA and Hyundai are advising owners to park their vehicles outdoors and away from structures or other cars until the fix is completed.
The core issue or defect:
The front power seat motors may overheat due to a stuck power seat control switch, which can result in a fire while parked or driving.
The risk revolves around the overheating, that creates a significant fire hazard that can occur whether the vehicle is actively being driven or parked even when the ignition is turned off.
The auto safety regulator said the recall remedy is currently being developed.
Because a fix isn't immediately available, NHTSA and Hyundai are strongly advising owners to park their vehicles outdoors and away from structures or other cars to mitigate potential property damage or safety hazards if a fire occurs.
Affected owners will receive notification letters detailing when they can bring their vehicles in for service once the remedy is finalized.

title: Will Tesla and SpaceX merge? Barclays expects announcement ahead of December meeting
text:
Will Tesla and SpaceX merge? Barclays expects announcement ahead of December meeting
A merger between Tesla and SpaceX could be announced ahead of the carmaker’s annual shareholder meeting
According to Barclays analysts, a potential merger between Tesla and Elon Musk’s SpaceX could be announced before the electric vehicle manufacturer’s 2026 annual shareholder meeting with the consolidated entity viewed as a way to consolidate control over Musk’s artificial intelligence ambitions.
While a merger could generate financial efficiencies, Barclays believes its greater value would come from integrating companies, their artificial intelligence companies, and infrastructure investments. The analyst warned that an investment too close to the shareholder meeting could imperil the approval process.
A statement from Barclays reads: “While it is possible that a merger announcement could be delayed until late October or even early November, we believe such a timing could make it more difficult to approve the transaction at the annual shareholder meeting.”
Barclays said a potential Tesla-SpaceX combination had become the mainstream expectation among investors. The bank identified shareholder voting as a substantial bottleneck with investors in both companies required to vote on a potential transaction. Primarily, the potential merger would bring together two businesses that have deepened their AI integration even though their primary core activities remain different.
Artificial intelligence is poised to become SpaceX’s largest source of revenue during 2026, according to Bloomberg Intelligence models. Barclays believes that the combination would allow Musk to integrate AI development more closely across computing infrastructure and client operation.
Nonetheless, Barclays anticipates the timing of any announcement will be influenced by the December shareholder meeting though neither company has confirmed a binding agreement for a transaction.

title: GSK eyes over 1,200 Belgian job cuts in cost-saving drive
text:
GSK eyes over 1,200 Belgian job cuts in cost-saving drive
Aiming to save £1.9 billion by 2029, the drugmaker GSK has initiated a collective dismissal procedure affecting sites in Wavre, Rixensart and Gembloux
British pharmaceutical giant GSK has announced plans to cut up to 1,217 permanent jobs across its sites in Belgium as part of a sweeping three-year global restructuring programme.
CEO Luke Miels had launched the effort in July as part of a broader push to speed up drug development and reassure investors that GSK can manage an approaching patent cliff for its blockbuster HIV drug dolutegravir.
Globally, GSK had 66,841 employees at the end of last year.
According to its annual report, the proposed cuts would affect some of its more than 8,000 employees at sites in Rixensart, Wavre and Gembloux, though factory workers would be spared.
Changes include simplifying the company's research, manufacturing and support operations, including through increased use of digital tools and more automation.
