Meanwhile, Belgian labor unions have been formally notified under collective-dismissal procedures, prompting local government officials to monitor the situation closely to ensure impacted workers receive adequate support.
GSK said it will remain the country's largest biopharmaceutical sector employer and that Belgium will continue to produce the majority of its vaccines.
Shares in the company were up 2.6% at 1430 GMT, in line with broader sector gains.
First reported by local media, the cost-efficiency drive aims to slash annual overhead by £1.9 billion ($2.5 billion) by 2029.
GSK boss Luke Miels is pivoting capital toward high-priority drug pipelines and late-stage vaccine research to offset an impending patent cliff.

title: Netflix slashes 1,000 jobs: What’s behind the cuts?
text:
Netflix slashes 1,000 jobs: What’s behind the cuts?
Netflix is cutting a significant number of jobs, in its biggest round of layoffs in years
Netflix is reportedly eliminating about 1,000 jobs from its global workforce as the streaming company re-evaluates its workforce needs while seeking new ways to retain users.
According to the Wall Street Journal, the cuts are one of the company’s largest since 2022, and were announced to employees today by Co-Chief Executive Greg Peters and Ted Sara Sarandos. Notably, the majority of the layoffs will impact the product, technology, legal and human resources departments.
Netflix has been diversifying its content strategy beyond on-demand films and television adding live events, sports, video podcasts and content from YouTube creators.
It has also sought content distribution networks and joint packaging deals with rival streaming platforms.
The company has maintained a steady renewal hold on subscribers with the US cancellation rate at just over 2%, though Netflix shares have lost more than 40% over the past year, shifting its focus toward maintaining momentum and meeting shareholder demands.
The executives wrote in an email to staff, “Our mission -- to entertain the world -- is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources.”
Netflix is preparing to report its quarterly results next week. The co-CEOs told employees the business is positioned to achieve its full-year revenue and earnings targets.

title: Anthropic to reveal new revenue figures as AI financial race heats up
text:
Anthropic to reveal new revenue figures as AI financial race heats up
Anthropic to disclose financials for the first time at a meeting with personal investors on Wednesday
In a recent update, Anthropic reportedly plans to reveal its third-quarter financials for the first time at a meeting with potential investors on Wednesday as the artificial intelligence powerhouse is set to stage the largest initial public offering in history.
The recent meetings come as revenue numbers from the AI giants have shown to exert an outsized influence on broader markets.
At present, it remains uncertain if Anthropic will report aggregate partner revenue but the numbers this week will provide investors more corporate finance context as they look to value the company ahead of an IPO.
Further it will help Anthropic senior executives and bankers assess investor sentiment and evaluate the market response to the updated financials. Anthropic filed confidentiality with the Securities and Exchange Commission this year but has not made its S-1 financials public. According to Reuters, the company will list in November with major plans but could not confirm a listing date.
Anthropic will also be going public amid rising interest rates that are rattling sections of the AI sector. In addition, market conditions are one of the massive factors in Anthropic’s upcoming IPO and bankers are keenly monitoring market demand for growth and AI equities.

title: HSBC to phase out fixed-pay allowances by 2028 in major compensation overhaul
text:
HSBC to phase out fixed-pay allowances by 2028 in major compensation overhaul
HSBC will phase out fixed-pay allowances by 2028, pivoting to a bonus-heavy remuneration model following the UK's removal of the banker bonus cap
HSBC Holdings Plc has announced plans to phase out fixed-pay allowances (FPAs) for staff starting in January 2028, marking a significant shift toward a Wall Street-style remuneration framework.
According to an internal memo, the upcoming transition is enabled by regulatory changes in the United Kingdom that removed the historical 2-to-1 cap on variable-to-fixed pay.
Originally implemented to comply with post-crisis EU restrictions, fixed-pay allowances were used to supplement base salaries.
Under the new model, HSBC will eliminate these allowances while keeping base salaries untouched, allowing a greater proportion of total compensation to be paid through performance-linked bonuses.
Bank executives noted that the strategic pivot aims to strengthen competitiveness, align payouts with individual performance, and enhance the firm's ability to attract and retain top talent.
HSBC said base salaries would not be reduced and its approach to total compensation would not change.
Staff affected by the move may have more of their compensation paid through variable pay, such as bonuses.
"As a global bank, adapting our approach in this way strengthens our ability to pay for performance, better differentiate, attract the best talent, and recognize those who deliver the best outcomes for our customers, clients and stakeholders," an HSBC spokesperson said.
HSBC has been reshaping its business under CEO Georges Elhedery, who took the role in September 2024, merging some businesses and splitting its structure into four main units.

title: TotalEnergies expands US renewable venture with KKR in $1.2B solar portfolio deal
text:
TotalEnergies expands US renewable venture with KKR in $1.2B solar portfolio deal
TotalEnergies expands its US clean energy venture with KKR, adding a 700 MW solar portfolio across Texas and Ohio valued at $1.2 billion
TotalEnergies said on Monday it is expanding its joint venture with KKR in the United States with an additional renewable’s portfolio.
French energy giant has announced an expansion of its U.S. renewable energy joint venture with global investment firm KKR, incorporating an additional 700-megawatt (MW) solar portfolio valued at $1.2 billion.
The deal covers three utility-scale solar assets in Texas and Ohio, adding 700 megawatts to the joint venture the companies created in 2025 that currently holds 1.4 gigawatts.
Electricity from the assets situated in Texas and Ohio, with commercial operations expected to launch by the first quarter of 2027.
The oil and diesel supplying group will retain operational responsibility for the new facilities, with the generated power either secured via pre-existing third-party contracts or actively marketed through its integrated portfolio.
For KKR, the investment deepens its exposure to high-demand North American clean infrastructure as utility firms race to meet surging commercial and industrial electrification loads.
The move underscores TotalEnergies' ongoing strategy to leverage private equity backing to accelerate capital turnover while expanding its footprint in key deregulated U.S. power markets.
Transaction completion is slated for later this year, subject to customary closing conditions.

title: Australian telecom shares tumble as SpaceX moves closer to direct-to-cell market
text:
Australian telecom shares tumble as SpaceX moves closer to direct-to-cell market
Regional carrier shares tumble across Australia and New Zealand as investors reprice long-term satellite competition risks following a multi-billion-dollar spectrum acquisition.
Major telecommunications stocks across Australia and New Zealand fell sharply on Monday, echoing a global sell-off triggered by fears that SpaceX's expansion into direct-to-device mobile services could challenge traditional telecom operators.
Australia's Telstra dropped 2.5% to a six-week low, while TPG Telecom fell 4.9%, its steepest daily decline since early June.
New Zealand's Spark lost 1.8%, while smaller regional players, including Superloop and Aussie Broadband, also declined.
The sell-off followed SpaceX's agreement last week to acquire a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio in the United States, strengthening Starlink Mobile's direct-to-cell capabilities and bringing Elon Musk's satellite venture closer to competing with established wireless carriers.
Low-band frequencies travel longer distances and penetrate buildings more effectively than higher-frequency airwaves, potentially allowing satellite-based services to challenge traditional mobile networks.
The deal has raised concerns among investors in the US and Europe about growing competition from satellite-based mobile services.
"Investors fear the U.S. is just the first market, and that incumbents' biggest advantage, coverage, is losing its value," said David Tuckwell, CIO at ETF Shares in Sydney.

title: World Bank in crisis aid talks with dozens of nations amid global shocks
text:
World Bank in crisis aid talks with dozens of nations amid global shocks
With global markets facing intense shocks from Middle East conflicts and rising borrowing costs, President Ajay Banga confirms active discussions with up to 40 nations
The World Bank is engaged in active discussions with dozens of countries regarding potential crisis aid to help developing economies navigate severe energy shocks and price spikes.
As reported by Reuters, the World Bank's president Ajay Banga said is in discussions with 30 to 40 countries about potential crisis aid to help them manage energy shocks and price increases triggered by the war in the Middle East, its president.
Banga stressed the global economy had proven fairly resilient, in part due to big AI investments and adjustments in supply and demand for oil, which meant that few countries had sought the initial issues in crisis funds that the World Bank had made available when the war began in late February.
"There is pressure, and so I think maybe over the coming months, more countries will come for some slice of that first $50 to $60 billion."
World Bank President Ajay Banga said the institution initially made $25 billion available for crisis financing but could mobilise as much as $100 billion if economic conditions worsen.
Many developing countries are already struggling with heavy debt repayments while higher diesel and fertiliser prices threaten transport costs, food production and household budgets.
Banga did not identify all the countries seeking assistance, but Reuters reports that capital flows to Africa have increased, with Nigeria among major recipients of World Bank-supported private investment.
The discussions come ahead of the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, where energy prices, debt and slowing economic growth are expected to dominate talks.
World Bank President announced that while the global economy has shown unexpected resilience—partly cushioned by major technology investments and supply adjustments mounting geopolitical tensions and volatile energy costs continue to threaten vulnerable nations.
Speaking ahead of joint international financial meetings, Banga noted that many governments are currently opting to retool existing project portfolios rather than immediately tapping specialized emergency windows.
However, the institution remains prepared to deploy substantial financing if economic conditions deteriorate further.
The ongoing talks also focus heavily on tackling soaring public debt levels that have constrained fiscal space across the developing world.
The World Bank and the International Monetary Fund are concurrently advancing initiatives—including debt-for-development swaps and portfolio-backed guarantees—to help emerging markets restructure high-priced legacy debt into sustainable funding for education, healthcare, and infrastructure.
Officials stress that agile, proactive policy responses will be critical as nations grapple with the compounding pressures of regional conflicts, shifting commodity markets, and tightening global liquidity.

title: Deutsche Bank chief explains why German election results alarm foreign investors
text:
Deutsche Bank chief explains why German election results alarm foreign investors
Christian Sewing urged the German government to intensify structural reforms to ease employment protections
On Sunday, the head of Germany’s largest bank warned that a withdrawal of international capital could be triggered by last month’s state election results where parties on the political extremes gained ground.
Primarily, the AfD which wants to restrict immigration and send asylum seekers home secured some of its unprecedented victory in eastern Germany last month. At the same time, The Left Party at the same time achieved a sweep in the Berlin city state election committing to the expropriation of real estate portfolios.
In this connection, Christian Sewing, chief executive of Deutsche Bank said: “ You can't expect a foreign investor to immediately draw a distinction between a state government and Germany as a whole,”
“It's seen as Germany as a whole and I think that from an investor's point of view, that's understandable.”
The AfD has been accused by economists of creating a hostile economic environment that deters vital talent and foreign capital. Meanwhile, The Left Party vowed to tackle Berlin’s rising housing costs by confiscating the holdings of large residential property companies.
Sewing stated, “ Whether it's Saxony-Anhalt with the AfD or what is happening here in Berlin it is anything but conducive to economic growth..”

title: China orders development of national blockchain network in economic blueprint: Here’s why
text:
China orders development of national blockchain network in economic blueprint: Here’s why
China is planning a national blockchain network as part of its significant new economic plan
Beijing is reportedly moving to centralize blockchain infrastructure under state control as an integral component of a broader digital economy strategy.
The initiative appears to be part of a broader campaign to expand digital infrastructure under government direction. At present, details regarding the network’s precise boundaries and timeline are omitted from early reports.
China has long differentiated between blockchain technology and cryptocurrency. Beijing banned cryptocurrency trading and mining years ago but now officials have promoted blockchain as a key tool for data management, supply chain tracking and government services.
The latest report underscored that a national blockchain network under government oversight would allow Chinese authorities to control data flows. This system would stand in stark contrast to public and permissionless blockchains used for Bitcoin and Ethereum.
The significant move comes as China continues to develop its central bank digital currency, yuan. Blockchain infrastructure projects are primarily discussed by Chinese officials though the digital yuan itself does not rely on an open blockchain in the way decentralized cryptocurrencies do.
Cryptocurrency markets have historically had a muted reaction to Chinese blockchain infrastructure announcements since such projects are typically insulated from public crypto trading and token markets. Nonetheless, investors particularly operating in the Chinese market may watch for further crucial details on strategic network development.

title: Tesla renames 'full self-driving' to 'assisted driving' in Europe: What to know
text:
Tesla renames 'full self-driving' to 'assisted driving' in Europe: What to know
European regulators flagged Tesla's old name as misleading because the system demands constant supervision, keeping drivers fully responsible.
Tesla has quietly rebranded its controversial "Full Self-Driving" (FSD) software package to "Assisted Driving" across several European markets as the automaker ramps up efforts to secure regulatory approval from European safety authorities.
EAs reported, EV-maker Tesla has started calling its "Full Self-Driving" feature "Tesla Assisted Driving" on its European websites, dropping a name regulators have said was misleading, as CEO Elon Musk pushes for EU-wide approval for the software.
The rebrand comes after Germany said on Tuesday Tesla had offered to switch to the new name.
Musk has described the self-driving technology as key to the company's future growth.
Tesla's FSD page for Slovakia now redirects to a "Tesla Assisted Driving" page, as do pages in other European countries such as Germany, Spain and the Netherlands. The US site still refers to it as "Full Self-Driving (Supervised)."
A Reuters report published this week detailed how Tesla mounted a campaign to win approval for FSD in Europe, including encouraging owners and supporters to lobby national regulators for faster approvals.
Several regulators have said the old name is misleading because the system requires constant supervision and drivers remain legally responsible.
According to documents, a Norwegian Tesla owner in November also asked the Norwegian Public Roads Administration whether Tesla's changes to how it described FSD addressed concerns about the name.
Eight EU countries already allow the system, with Slovakia expecting to become the ninth within days.
An EU-wide vote has been pushed from October to at least December, with countries like France conducting additional testing.
By shifting the nomenclature to "Assisted Driving", aligning more closely with standard Level 2 driver-assistance classifications, Tesla aims to clear the compliance hurdles needed to legally roll out its advanced driver-assistance features on European roads.

title: US sanctions ICC hours after former judge wins Nobel Prize: What to know
text:
US sanctions ICC hours after former judge wins Nobel Prize: What to know
US impose fresh sanctions on unaccountable International criminal court
On Friday, US President Donald Trump's administration reportedly imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court hours after one of its former magistrates was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, setting Washington on a diplomatic trajectory toward conflict with European allies.
The administration has long been hostile to the court and imposed sanctions on judges. Recent moves would take it a step further by potentially punishing companies.
Navi Pillay is the South American jurist who won the Nobel Peace Prize for her work in international crime justice and served as a judge on the ICC’s Appeals Chamber from 2003-2008.
In this connection, Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated in a statement: “ President Trump will never allow the International Criminal Court to prosecute Americans,
“That is why, today, the United States is sanctioning the International Criminal Court. We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling its ability to operate.”
The prize committee asserted it had sought to issue a reminder at a time when judges and institutions of international law are under political attack. US sanctions commonly bar all US-based companies from any work with a sanctioned organization which implies a collective, intentional refusal to deal with an organization or country.
Trump earlier instituted restricted measures against tribunal personnel on court officials during his first term which were nullified under President Joe Biden. Rubio said in a statement that the United States had delayed its sanctions hoping that the ICC and the countries party to its founding Rome Statue would address US concerns.

title: Trump holds millions in Meta stock: What to know
text:
Trump holds millions in Meta stock: What to know
Trump’s investment brought up to $25 million of Meta in August marking the portfolio’s most significant acquisition of the month
In a major update, Meta Platforms shares rose more than 1% after President Donald Trump’s recent financial reporting revealed he had purchased as much as $25 million in stock before a market correction.
According to a newly released 18-page financial statement, Trump revealed more than 500 securities transactions in August including the Meta purchase and a substantial investment in SpaceX debt. The CNBC analysis showed that the 517 purchases and sales had an aggregated reported value of between $74.3 million and $273.3 million.
As federal rules emphasize reporting assets within structured categories, purchases totaled at least $44.2 million and sales at least $30.1 million.
The 18-page filing primarily shows Trump’s portfolio maintained a high velocity of capital deployment even as trading slowed compared to June and July when he revealed more than 1,000 transactions in each of the months. The largest transaction occurred on August 21 with the purchase of between $2 million and $25 million in Meta shares amid a broader portfolio restructuring that day.
Trump signed a National Security Presidential memorandum calling for the US to support more than 1,000 launches and yearly returns by 2030.
SpaceX is a central Pentagon contractor and NASA launch provider putting it in a strategic position to capitalize on policies aimed at expanding the US commercial launch market.
The new filing does not reveal the size of Trump’s investments because federal disclosures report transactions in value ranges. Crucially, Trump’s account also continued in purchasing municipal debt, a pattern that has emerged repeatedly in his disclosures.
The August filing includes holdings linked to state and local government, schools, hospitals and other public entities.

title: Amazon announces 1,000 corporate job cuts, primarily targeting retail division
text:
Amazon announces 1,000 corporate job cuts, primarily targeting retail division
Latest workforce reductions hit core stores unit as E-commerce giant continues streamlining structure
Following a wave of recent job cuts worldwide, Amazon has eliminated fewer than 1,000 corporate roles, with the majority of the reductions concentrated within its core Stores retail division.
The layoffs to its retail unit coincide with one of Amazon's biggest shopping days, which it calls Prime Big Deal Days.
The promotion started on Tuesday and runs through Wednesday, offering varying discounts.
The targeted cuts impacted various units across the global e-commerce infrastructure—including customer service, marketplace support, and selling partner services spanning the US, UK, and India.
An Amazon spokesperson confirmed the move, noting that the adjustments are designed to realign the company's operational structure with its key business priorities.
Founder and executive chairman Jeff Bezos recently attributed ongoing corporate workforce adjustments to rapid pandemic-era expansion, stating that the company significantly overhired to manage unprecedented spikes in online consumer demand.
The cuts are the latest in a series of small reductions since a larger round of 30,000 job cuts that began last year and continued into January.
Some affected employees reached out to Reuters and shared posts from internal Slack channels about the news.

title: Coupang files lawsuits to contest record $462 million South Korean data breach penalties
text:
Coupang files lawsuits to contest record $462 million South Korean data breach penalties
E-Commerce giant challenges regulators over massive fines tied to historic customer information leak
E-commerce giant Coupang has filed administrative lawsuits challenging South Korean regulatory penalties stemming from a massive data breach
Coupang said on Thursday it has filed two administrative lawsuits against 620 billion won ($462.75 million) in fines imposed by South Korea's government over a data breach.
Reuters report, E-Commerce giant challenges regulators over massive fines tied to historic customer information leak.
The fines levied by South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission, follow an investigation into a security lapse that exposed personal account data affecting tens of millions of users.
As reported, regulators cited inadequate access controls and delayed reporting windows as primary justifications for the record-breaking financial penalty.
Coupang’s legal challenge argues that the enforcement actions and calculations are disproportionate, maintaining that the company implemented swift protective measures following the discovery of the breach.

title: Google and Unity partner on new AI game creation platform
text:
Google and Unity partner on new AI game creation platform
Playground is an experimental gaming platform that lets you create your own games with a codeless experience
Google and Unity have reportedly announced a joint partnership for a new integrated gaming platform this year engineered to redefine the next era of gaming.
This initiative will put game creation in the hands of millions of new creators by bringing together the power of Google AI, the reach of Google's top-tier gaming portfolio with over a billion users and the elite development capabilities of Unity.
The partnership unites Google’s pioneering research with Unity’s industry-leading engine technology to develop new creation tools. It features creation tools anyone can pick up, AI designed for interactive play and a platform that is built for community-focused features.
Google and Unity will introduce an enriched creative environment called Unity Spark built on Playground. The partnership includes Google's ecosystem distribution through Google’s consumer network across its platforms. Notably, the system integrates with Google Play Games profiles to support social gaming infrastructure.
Playground is accessible at playground.google.com for users to test the platform’s capabilities. Furthermore, the press release included forward-looking information subject to contingencies, underlining that the actual results could differ from expectations. Unity further stated it does not seek to update cautionary statements regarding future projections.

title: Sources reveal truth behind French brand Lacoste CEO getting fired ahead of Paris runway show
text:
Sources reveal truth behind French brand Lacoste CEO getting fired ahead of Paris runway show
Following a brief tenure aimed at moving the brand upmarket, former chief executive Éric Vallat has been dismissed, with parent company head Thierry Guibert resuming the role
In a major update, French luxury lifestyle brand Lacoste quietly dismissed Chief Executive Éric Vallat just days before its latest runway show in Paris.
Vallat, the former head of Rémy Cointreau who took the helm in mid-2025, was tasked with steering the crocodile-logo brand further upmarket and cutting back on low-margin wholesale.
Following his brief tenure, parent company Maus Frères has reinstated former chief executive Thierry Guibert to resume the role.
A spokesperson for the company confirmed the departure, noting that Lacoste will press forward with its long-term strategy on "robust fundamentals" without disclosing specific reasons for the sudden split.
Sources close to the matter indicated that the unlisted brand's overall financial performance was not behind the ouster.
As reported by Reuters, Thierry Guibert, who led Lacoste for a decade prior to Vallat's appointment and serves as head of Swiss parent company Maus Frères, will immediately step back in to reclaim the chief executive role.
Guibert is also the head of Maus Freres, Lacoste's Swiss parent company.
Other sources familiar with Vallat's ouster said the performance of the unlisted brand, which aims to reach €4 billion in annual sales by 2028-2030, was not the reason for his departure.

title: Canadian rents hit three-year September low after 24 months of declines
text:
Canadian rents hit three-year September low after 24 months of declines
The average asking rent for residential properties fell to $2,034 in September, down 4.2 percent from the same month last year
Average asking rents in Canada have fallen for the 24th consecutive month, marking two full years of declines in one of the country’s longest recent rental market downturns.
The average asking rent for residential properties fell to $2,034 in September, down 4.2 percent from the same month last year, according to a report from Rentals.ca and Urbanation cited by Global News.
That was the lowest average asking rent recorded for September since 2022. Rents are now 9.2 percent below their record high of $2,202 reached in May 2024.
“Two straight years of falling rents is the longest downturn the Canadian rental market has seen in recent history,” Urbanation president Shaun Hildebrand said.
Hildebrand said an oversupply of rental properties in major markets including Toronto and Vancouver has been a key factor behind the decline.
Condo rents recorded the biggest annual drop, falling 7.8 percent to an average of $2,052. Studio condo rents declined 9.6 percent.
Rents for secondary units, including houses and townhomes, dropped 7.4 percent to $2,016.
Purpose-built rental properties recorded a smaller decline, falling 2.7 percent to an average of $2,036.
However, Hildebrand said rents in Toronto and Vancouver have been trending higher over the past six months as more renters return to the market.

title: Google under fire in £1 billion UK case over app store charges
text:
Google under fire in £1 billion UK case over app store charges
Google was accused of antitrust violations for levying excessive commissions on app developers
Google’s £1 billion lawsuit in the UK over allegations that its app store fees are unfairly high began in London on Tuesday, as the case adds to the escalating pressure on Big Tech companies and their business practices.
The case was brought primarily on behalf of around 20 million consumers who bought apps through Google’s Play Store or paid for in-app purchases and subscriptions between 2015 and this July- the latest brought against Big Tech.
Meanwhile, consumer protection lawyer Liz Coll says Google used its dominant position to charge commissions of up to 30% on purchases of applications through its Play Store.
They argue that app developers passed those inflated charges directly down to consumers citing as an example that when Google sold YouTube Premium through Apple’s App Store it decided to pass along the commission it was charged.
The trial at London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal mirrors similar actions against Apple and Sony over their Apple Store and PlayStation store. Furthermore, Coll’s case comes following years of regulatory scrutiny and legal disputes over Google’s app store practices including a protracted struggle with Fortnite maker Epic Games whose London lawsuit was due to be heard alongside Coll’s.

title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pulled in $18 Million last Year, IPO filing shows
text:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pulled in $18 Million last Year, IPO filing shows
The package leans heavily on equity components, including stock and options, alongside an annual salary that was recently doubled to $1.4 million
Anthropic Chief Executive Dario Amodei pulled in total compensation of $18 million last year.
According to the artificial intelligence startup’s newly unveiled initial public offering prospectus, the figures place the Claude developer's chief executive squarely in the middle of the tech industry pack, trailing top earners at legacy giants while outstripping standard executive baselines.
The package leans heavily on equity components, including stock and options, alongside an annual salary.
Amodei's pay last year puts him above CEOs at Alphabet, and Amazon, but behind those at Oracle and Nvidia.
Dario Amodei and his sister, Anthropic President Daniela Amodei, each had their annual salaries doubled this past July to $1.4 million.
Stock and options awards made up the bulk of their packages in 2025, with Daniela Amodei receiving a total of $16.4 million last year.
Anthropic's board this year granted the pair the promise of further equity in the form of restricted stock units, which promise a future payout if certain conditions are met.
Some of that is tied to their remaining at the company, and some of it is tied to the IPO.
The financial disclosures arrive as Anthropic lays the groundwork for a massive public market debut that could value the AI lab in the multi-trillion-dollar range.
Despite the eye-catching compensation figures, the filing also highlights that Amodei and his fellow co-founders have formally pledged to dedicate a vast majority of their personal equity holdings to philanthropic causes.
According to Reuters, Anthropic is preparing for an IPO as early as this fall that could value it at more than $2 trillion.

title: X faces pressure to reject Turkey’s broad requests to block accounts
text:
X faces pressure to reject Turkey’s broad requests to block accounts
The groups urged X to carefully examine blocking requests from Turkish authorities
On Tuesday, journalism groups called on social platform X not to comply with government takedown orders directed at journalists and media outlets in Turkey that occur outside the course of regular judicial proceedings.
In a joint declaration, the International Federation of Journalists, the European Federation of Journalists and the Turkish Journalists Union reported a surge in access limitations and said X was reportedly complying with demands that lacked adequate judicial oversight.
The groups urged X to scrutinize blocking requests by Turkish authorities to ensure they are supported by independent and clear court decisions and to rebuff overbroad or excessive requests while increasing transparency regarding limitations.
Further requests from administrative authorities, law enforcement agencies and other public bodies should not automatically constitute sufficient grounds to block access to journalists’ or media organization accounts without due process, as reported by the Reuters.
Furthermore, according to the Freedom of Expression Association, courts are verified for only 115 of the 1,270 X accounts whose access was restricted in Turkey in September while the grounds remain undisclosed for blocking the remaining 1,155 accounts.

title: Euro plunges to 17-month low as France debt and Spain election fuel uncertainty
text:
Euro plunges to 17-month low as France debt and Spain election fuel uncertainty
The euro has also weakened against the British pound, falling to about 85p
The euro fell to its lowest level against the US dollar in 17 months on Monday as concerns over France’s growing public debt and a sharp government bond sell-off shook markets.
The European currency dropped as much as 0.9 percent during trading, extending four consecutive weeks of declines against the dollar. One euro is now worth about US$1.12.
Pressure has increased as investors focus on France’s public finances. The yield on the country’s benchmark 10-year government bonds is approaching 5 percent, a multi-decade high that means the French government faces significantly higher borrowing costs.
Higher bond yields can also feed through to consumers by increasing borrowing costs for products such as fixed-rate mortgages and other loans.
Political uncertainty elsewhere in Europe is adding to market volatility. Spain called a snap election on Monday, raising further questions about the outlook for the eurozone.
The euro has also weakened against the British pound, falling to about 85p.
The latest decline puts the euro at its weakest level against the US dollar since May 2025, with concerns over government debt and political uncertainty weighing on the currency.

title: OPEC+ agrees to keep November oil targets steady amid market uncertainty
text:
OPEC+ agrees to keep November oil targets steady amid market uncertainty
An agreement has been reached in principle to maintain oil output targets for this November
OPEC+ has reportedly agreed in principle to keep its November oil production targets unchanged ahead of the group’s meeting scheduled for Sunday. According to reports, Gulf OPEC+ producers have been operating well below target due to ongoing export bottlenecks caused by the US-Israeli war with Iran with exports fluctuating at 60-80% of normal levels in recent months.
The geopolitical tensions have also delayed the productivity evaluation review essential for reviewing members; 2027 output quotas because they have clouded future production outlooks.
A source close to the talks said that the OPEC+ group including the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies including Russia concurred in theory to maintain baseline objectives.
OPEC+ has been raising output targets for much of the year 2026 following years of production cuts but most of the increases stayed on paper due to the Middle East conflict.
According to OPEC data, the seven core OPEC+ members’ output reached 25 million barrels per day in August, though it was still roughly 5 million bpd below prewar levels in February. There are almost 25 million bpd of output cuts in place covering most members but a workload assessment is needed to determine how to allocate rises and structural adjustments and any changes to output are unlikely before 2027. Furthermore, the group’s seven core members meeting on Sunday include Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman.

title: Meta’s AI data centers: What to know about its major tax strategy
text:
Meta’s AI data centers: What to know about its major tax strategy
Meta is exploiting a lucrative tax break intended to support research
In a major update, the AI data centers are not disturbing their neighbors with screeching noise and using up large amounts of power and water, they are also enabling corporate entities to save billions of dollars on their federal tax bill.
According to the New York Times, Meta is classifying its immense multi-billion dollar data center construction projects as pilot models originally designed to assist businesses experimenting in potentially risky research and experimentation.
Meta has been capitalizing the loophole for two years now, saving $2 billion in 2024. The company saved almost $4 billion according to its 2025 annual report making it the largest known recipient of the credit to date among public companies.
The exploit is part of a growing and disturbing trend in which the AI industry is already aggressively accounting for inflated revenues and creative accounting while operating in a regulatory vacuum, fueling concerns over a possible AI bubble that experts fear is about to burst, leaving the market highly unstable and on the brink of collapse.
Nonetheless, Meta is trying to fudge the numbers to avoid paying taxes which could fuel the raging controversy over the AI industry’s attempts to justify its enormous data centre buildouts.

title: Tesla’s Cybercab faces a tough test after rocky Austin debut: Here's why
text:
Tesla’s Cybercab faces a tough test after rocky Austin debut: Here's why
Tesla’s Cybercab has grown to a major presence in Austin units but faces a first-responder safety concerns
Tesla’s Cybercab faced significant challenges during its first month of operations in Austin, fueling concerns over the vehicle’s early performance and rollout.
The unusual driverless vehicle with no steering wheel, pedals or outside door handles has received polarized feedback from paying passengers who shared videos and posts online after the launch on September 3.
On Friday, Tesla announced a positive third-quarter delivery surprise lifting the stock almost 5% but the company still had 2% annual contractions in shipments.
In addition to technical difficulties, the company is navigating compliance challenges that may delay its scaling efforts. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration initiated a compliance review after the Cybercab launch to ensure the vehicles adhere to mandatory safety codes.
Notably, no major safety breaches or impacts have been reported in Austin involving a Cybercab since the commercial debt. However, first responders have raised apprehensions about managing the Cybercab’s lack of manual driving controls and its unique doors.
In this connection, Austin Fire Captain Matt McElearney told CNBC in an interview that while Tesla claims to provide precise, necessary instructions and constraints and gave first responders comprehensive guidance on how to deal with Cybercab and Model Y Robotaxi vehicles in a variety of events.
Furthermore, analysts at Cantor highlighted the potential of the opportunity stating, “Management previously said that once production ramps, it expects Cybercab to ultimately be the largest volume vehicle in its lineup.”

title: Trump pushes South Korea on Alaska LNG deal: Why Seoul is hesitant
text:
Trump pushes South Korea on Alaska LNG deal: Why Seoul is hesitant
Trump’s push for major investment in Alaska's liquefied natural gas is renewing emphasis on the project
South Korea is adopting a conservative approach to the long-planned Alaska liquefied natural gas project despite Donald Trump advertising it as part of a significant $200 billion investment package in the US.
On Wednesday, Trump said that the two countries had decided to collaborate on the $50 billion project but South Korean President Lee Jae Myung pushed back, adding that South Korea’s engagement could be contingent upon its economic viability and statutory adherence.
According to the Alaska Gasline Development Corporation, the Alaska LNG project seeks to transport liquefied natural gas across an 800-mile pipeline from Prudhoe Bay on Alaska’s North Slope to an LNG facility in the south.
Head of business intelligence for Asia Pacific at Poten&Partner, Kit Ling Wong said: “The economics of Alaska LNG is expensive given the long pipeline versus other LNG projects.”
“It will not be the cheapest supply for South Korea.”
Shipping LnG from Niskiski to South Korea would take seven to nine days compared to around 20 to 30 days from the US Gulf Coast. However, for South Korean buyers, the significant question is whether the shorter route can touch down into a competitive LNG price with alternatives such as LNG Canada, the US Gulf Coast, Kpler’s Katayama said.
South Korea also has to weigh its geopolitical and economic ties with the US against the project’s financial viability. The ultimate test will be the total acquisition cost of Alaska LNG after accounting for pipeline, financing, liquefaction, taxation and shipping costs for the majority of South Korean buyers and investors.
Nonetheless, additional US government support, including tax incentives and financial assistance would also be significant along with opportunities for South Korean companies to participate in the project’s construction and engineering, moving beyond the role of traditional LNG consumers.

title: AI boom could trigger severe market shocks, Bank of England warns
text:
AI boom could trigger severe market shocks, Bank of England warns
Governor Andrew Bailey cautions that massive capital inflows and debt accumulation in the technology sector could amplify losses across global markets if productivity gains falter
Bank of England (BoE) warns that artificial intelligence (AI) could trigger financial market shocks and the UK needs to be prepared for them.
BoE's Governor said that the AI investment boom carries the risk of sparking wider financial market shocks if corporate earnings expectations or productivity gains fall short, Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey warned.
Speaking on systemic financial risks, Bailey noted that massive capital inflows into AI have pushed asset prices sharply higher, increasingly intertwining technology spending with core financial markets.
Andrew Bailey said the central bank is watching the huge amounts of money being invested in AI "very carefully" and cautioned that "not everybody always wins".
The money that has been spent on and loaned to AI firms over the last few years in the hope of large returns is causing markets to value some of them as multi-trillion dollar businesses.
Asked if he believed an AI bubble could burst, Bailey said: "You could see some correction of asset prices at some point."
As reported by BBC, the company saif that the risks and benefits of AI could be for the UK economy. Bailey said he believed the technology has "great potential to strengthen growth in our economies", adding that this was something the country needed.
"But it also brings with it substantial risks and so we have to be on top of both of those."
One such risk is what happens if the big bets being made on AI don't pay off.
The central bank's Financial Policy Committee highlighted that a significant portion of AI-related expansion is being fueled by rapidly growing debt and high leverage, raising the danger that a sudden shift in investor sentiment could amplify losses across global equities and credit.
While central bank officials emphasized that institutions must remain vigilant and prepared for potential volatility, the warning underscores rising international anxiety over structural bottlenecks, high valuations, and the broader economic fallout should the current tech rally face an abrupt correction.

title: US inflation rises less than expected: What to know
text:
US inflation rises less than expected: What to know
July’s headline and core PCE inflation rates were also revised down by 30 basis points
US inflation increased more slowly than expected in August which could lead financial markets to further diminish the likelihood of another rate hike from the Federal Reserve next month.
On Wednesday, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysts said that economists had forecast the PCE price index rising 0.4% after a past reported 0.2% gain in July.
The inflation has now advanced 2.6% after subsequently decreasing by a revised 3.4% in July. The BEA revised its framework for software and hardware deflation, portfolio management fees and legal services in the PCE price index, revising the inflation data going back to 2021.
Excluding the fluctuating components, the PCE Price Index climbed 0.2% over the months after a revised 0.1% rise in July. The so-called core PCE was initially reported to have increased 0.2% in July. Core PCE primarily inflation increased 3.0% year-on-year August after an adjusted increase of 3.3% in the 12 months through July.
The Fed this month increased bank borrowing costs to the 3.75%-4.00 range, marking the first rate hike in three years. The odds of an October rate hike were reduced by New York Fed President John Willaims’ comments on Tuesday that there is no immediate necessity to proceed.
Furthermore, financial markets priced in a roughly 51.5% ahead of further policy restrictions next month down from 70% on Monday.

title: OpenAI’s revenue run rate nears $70 billion: What to know
text:
OpenAI’s revenue run rate nears $70 billion: What to know
The startup annualized revenue run rate has risen since the beginning of the third quarter in July
In a recent update, OpenAI’s annualized revenue run rate has increased by more than 70% since the start of the third quarter- a move that underscores the accelerated monetization of its developer network.
It has been observed that these staggering figures arrived just as the industry braced for impact while OpenAI’s chief rival Anthropic hastened its transition to public trading. Separately, Anthropic’s annualized run rate also crossed $65 billion by the end of July.
At present, no date has been confirmed for an OpenAI IPO compelling the disclosure of audited financial statements with eliminating costs that currently obscure its true margins.
Nonetheless, investors in Microsoft, Oracle and the broader semiconductor ecosystems saw these public debuts as significant test cases; though a high public valuation for either AI labs would validate the monumental capital expenditure currently driving the sector and could further fleet acceleration across AI infrastructure equities.
Earlier, the company also clarified that the historical data disclosures appearing in updated protocols were implemented over a month ago. OpenAI also said that an internal security review revealed that its models bypassed boundaries meant to segregate them from the internet.

title: Canada’s economy records zero growth in July as key sectors decline
text:
Canada’s economy records zero growth in July as key sectors decline
Real gross domestic product was essentially unchanged during the month, despite gains in the construction and utilities sectors
Canada’s economy recorded essentially no growth in July, losing momentum at the beginning of the third quarter, Statistics Canada said Tuesday.
Real gross domestic product was essentially unchanged during the month, despite gains in the construction and utilities sectors.
Construction activity rose 1.3 percent in July, marking its fourth consecutive monthly increase following a difficult start to the year.
The utilities sector also recorded its strongest monthly growth of the year, driven by a surge in electricity generation, transmission and distribution.
However, those gains were offset by declines across several parts of the economy. Manufacturing contracted during the month, while mining, quarrying and oil and gas extraction also fell.
Retail and wholesale trade were among the other sectors that recorded declines in July.
This comes after a stronger second quarter for the Canadian economy as Statistics Canada previously estimated that GDP grew at an annualised rate of 3.3 percent during the April-to-June period.
Early estimates suggest economic growth could regain some momentum in August, with Statistics Canada currently projecting GDP to increase by 0.2 percent.

title: UK diesel price hits all-time high amid Middle East supply crunch, RAC warns
text:
UK diesel price hits all-time high amid Middle East supply crunch, RAC warns
Average pump prices cross 199p per litre as geopolitical conflicts strain global fuel supplies and spike consumer costs
The average price of diesel in the UK has surged to a record-breaking high of 199.18p per litre, eclipsing previous peaks set in 2022.
According to the RAC, ongoing Middle East conflicts and global refining constraints are heavily driving up costs for motorists and freight operators alike.
As reported, the sharp escalation is driven primarily by intense geopolitical conflicts and tightening global oil supplies.
Analysts note that ongoing military escalations in the Middle East and supply disruptions affecting major refining hubs have sent crude benchmarks soaring.
Automotive and logistics organizations have warned that the fallout extends far beyond individual motorists. Because commercial freight, delivery vans, and heavy goods vehicles rely heavily on diesel, the soaring fuel costs are expected to cascade through supply chains, adding inflationary pressure to consumer goods and retail prices nationwide.
Experts caution that unless global oil prices experience a sustained downturn over multiple weeks, pump prices will remain stubbornly near the 200p threshold.
Fuel prices are one of the key drivers of UK inflation, which hit a five-month high in August, adding pressure on consumers who are grappling with a protracted cost-of-living crisis.
The price high on Monday eclipsed the previous highest price of 199.09 pence in June 2022, during the acute energy market shock in the aftermath of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
"Only a sustained lower oil price over several weeks, not days — will lead to cheaper prices at the pumps ... the government could take steps to ease the burden on drivers by lowering fuel duty further or reducing VAT," Williams said.

title: Meta’s Muse AI agent gets new tools for small businesses: What to know
text:
Meta’s Muse AI agent gets new tools for small businesses: What to know
Meta launches Muse for small businesses, pushing beyond the consumer AI market
Meta Platforms is reportedly expanding its AI agent Muse to small businesses by implementing software integrations with tools such as Shopify, QuickBooks, Stripe and Canva-a significant move to help them run their businesses and find new customers as the Facebook-parent reduces its reliance on ad revenue.
The primary motive behind Muse for Small Business is to connect Instagram professional account analytics, Facebook Pages and Meta ad accounts with tools including Asana, Box, Dropbox, Figma, Klaviyo, Notion, Slack and Zoom.
The company said that Muse is now capable of being integrated or unified with a company’s brand storefront, books and customer records.
Muse will not publish content or send messages or make purchases without a user’s approval. Most importantly, Muse is free for most users while a subscription plan will be available for users seeking additional features.
In this connection, Meta said in the blog post, “Small businesses have been growing on our apps for nearly two decades.”
“They told us they’re short on hours, not ideas. So we built Muse for Small Business to help get work done with the tools they already use.”
Muse launched this month is a personal AI agent designed to complete crucial tasks including shopping, travel booking, emailing and proxy payments. Nonetheless, the app has reached the top of the rankings in the US and Canada in recent weeks with market intelligence firm Sensor Tower recording factual data of about 2.8 million downloads in its first two weeks.

title: China weighs allowing ByteDance, Alibaba to purchase new Nvidia RTX Pro 5500 chips
text:
China weighs allowing ByteDance, Alibaba to purchase new Nvidia RTX Pro 5500 chips
Beijing signals it may allow tech giants like ByteDance and Alibaba to buy Nvidia's new workstation graphics chips, easing prior import curbs
China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology has asked major domestic tech firms—including ByteDance and Alibaba—to report their purchasing plans for Nvidia's newly unveiled RTX Pro 5500 workstation chip.
As the global race for artificial intelligence supremacy intensifies, tech giants in China are facing a massive potential turning point.
With local domestic chips struggling to match high-end Western processing demands, Beijing is reportedly rethinking its rigid hardware strategy.
"US firms continue to be restricted by a combination of outdated US export controls, which cover gaming products released nearly a half a decade ago, and China's own limits on US imports," an Nvidia spokesperson said, when asked to comment on the report.
According to The Information, reports, Chinese regulators are weighing a major policy shift that could soon allow tech powerhouses like ByteDance and Alibaba to acquire Nvidia's advanced workstation graphics chips.
As reported, the State regulators have signaled an intent to approve these procurement requests, marking a potential easing of Beijing's strict domestic limits on U.S. hardware imports as local AI compute demands outpace what domestic suppliers like Huawei can provide.
Built on Nvidia’s advanced Blackwell architecture, industry executives expect the RTX Pro 5500 chip to cleverly bypass stringent U.S. export restrictions, offering a massive relief valve for Chinese cloud and AI giants hungry for high-end processing power.

title: Why Bill Gates is calling for stronger AI rules amid growing safety concerns
text:
Why Bill Gates is calling for stronger AI rules amid growing safety concerns
‘AI requires safeguards that go beyond self-regulation, says Bill Gates’
In an interview broadcast Sunday, Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates said that AI requires statutory oversight that goes beyond self-regulation-particularly calling on Congress to pass federal legislation requiring protective barriers.
Gates said in a taped interview on NBC’s, “ You need law enforcement and the politicians to get into the discussion about what safeguards and monitoring look like.”
A sudden wave of support for federal intervention popped up after OpenAI said in July that an autonomous AI agent went rogue during a security test and hacked into another company evading human oversight. Gates joined that refrain saying that the government must be involved.
According to Gates, he wants to meet Trump to discuss AI, staying, “I hope that, given my life's work in the field, my saying how unique and different this is and how concerned I am will add to what he's hearing from other people.”
As reported by Axios, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has a dinner planned for Sunday with President Trump at the White House. Although warnings about AI risks are not new but gained fresh priority this month after researchers in leading AI labs assigned a schedule and likelihood to each risk.
In this connection, former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon warned that AI could kill us by the end of the decade, fueling US lawmakers to call for new rules to govern the technology.
In a memo released in August, Gates defined AI as a technology carrying great importance and leaving a lasting mark on the future. He further argued that AI will either be the greatest equalizer or the worst source of injustice.
Gates said the government and political parties must collaborate immediately to establish guardrails for AI development.
Some policymakers have proposed requiring a kill switch that would allow federal authorities to halt AI models with Gates adding that he is not opposed to a kill switch though he noted that it would be ineffective if other precautions are also omitted. In addition, the US and China agreed to launch key AI dialogues after Xi Jinping’s recent visit to Washington.

title: Meta’s Muse agent targets one of the economy’s most profitable sectors: Key details to know
text:
Meta’s Muse agent targets one of the economy’s most profitable sectors: Key details to know
The Muse agent is undermining the financial stability of bank’s most profitable revenue streams
The Meta Muse AI agent is capitalizing on a high-growth area of the economy as the company explores new ways for artificial intelligence to manage workflow automation and coordinate tasks between external partners and end-users.
With the rollout of Meta Muse this month-an AI agent that can handle tasks across many areas of personal life, it became clear that subscription bloat was an easy target. Muse can help consumers identify and terminate a subscription, even though subscription management services have existed for years.
Muse primarily brings that capability into a broader personal assistant streamlining subscription tracking.
Neale Mahoney, an economics professor at Stanford University and director of the Institute for Economic Policy Research said: “ We found that when people are forced to decide, they are about four times more likely to cancel, citing data from his 2025 American Economic Review paper “Selling Subscriptions.”
The AI personal agent addressing this facet of consumer behavior carries profound theoretical implications far beyond subscription management and influences mission-critical transaction processing within the core financial services that banks take for granted.
Subscription companies are dealing with high customer turnover with the Mastercard report showing that the average monthly churn rate- the percentage of subscribers who cancel or fail to renew in a given month has reached 20%. More than half of US subscription businesses reported that at least 10% of their subscriber base was inactive with some customers remaining subscribed without actively using the service.
A 2026 State of Subscriptions Report analyzing 76 million unique subscribers across more than 2,200 businesses found that the use of pause before cancel options surged by 337% with three out of four customers who paused and eventually returned.
Nonetheless, whether it is AI or the consumer taking action, people stop paying for something that is no longer wanted in order to spend money elsewhere is good for markets, and it is good for high-demand enterprises that are making products that people actually want.
“When people are trapped in subscriptions they don’t want or can’t get out of, market forces are limited, and companies don’t have the incentives to have a high-quality product at a low price. They can just rely on a locked-in install base, said Mahoney, an economics professor at Stanford University.”

title: Andy Burnham refuses to back Heathrow’s third runway
text:
Andy Burnham refuses to back Heathrow’s third runway
Burnham refuses to say whether he supports third runway at Heathrow
In the latest update, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has declined to confirm his support for a third runway at Heathrow after it emerged that the expansion of the London airport could be delayed by up to four years.
On Sunday, he opposed the project with Laura Kuenssberg, “I think principally it is a matter for London and Londoners.”
“I think we ought to hear the voices of people there first. It's not right for me to just jump straight in on the back of the consultation, he continued.”
Burnham, being Manchester's mayor, had been opposed to the project due to apprehension that it would delay investment in transport of the North..
The project’s projected cost of £33bn has sparked fierce local and environmental backlash from local residents as well as the Mayor of London Sadiq Khan.
Primarily, a third runway would mean demolishing hundreds of homes, diverting rivers and rerouting a section of the M25 motorway through a tunnel.
It is roughly calculated it would create 100,000 jobs and provide a major boost to the UK economy. It has been observed that the number of flights from the site is capped at 480,000 a year and could rise up to 720,000 a day on average.
Heathrow this weekend also acknowledged that meeting the original deadline would be difficult to achieve without further steps to streamline the entire planning process. Furthermore, the Department for Transport said the timeline had always been aspiring and asserted it would continue to work with stakeholders who are moving expeditiously on the matter.

title: US, China agree to $30 billion tariff cuts; Launch 'Super Intelligence' AI dialogue
text:
US, China agree to $30 billion tariff cuts; Launch 'Super Intelligence' AI dialogue
Washington and Beijing agree to slash tariffs on $30 billion of goods and establish a formal 'super intelligence' AI dialogue during Xi's US visit
Following Chinese President Xi Jinping’s high-profile three-day state visit to Washington, the United States and China have reached an eight-point consensus, securing a reciprocal trade agreement and establishing formal bilateral frameworks for advanced technology.
The $30 Billion Tariff Package: Both superpowers agreed to reciprocal, favorable tariff reductions on $30 billion of non-sensitive goods in each direction.
US exports favored: Agricultural products, seafood, wood, cosmetics, and medical devices while Chinese imports favored: Small appliances, toys, holiday decorations, and child car seats.
The two nations agreed to launch a dedicated bilateral dialogue addressing the risks and benefits of advanced AI technologies, with the first round of talks scheduled for November. Notably, the White House confirmed that both sides agreed to formally adopt the term "super intelligence" instead of artificial intelligence for upcoming official discussions.
Washington and Beijing will establish a direct emergency communication channel specifically designed to handle and resolve AI-related incidents.
As part of the broader economic outcomes, the agreement builds on an extension of the existing trade truce (the Busan Agreement) and includes commitments for China to import 10 million metric tons of US coal annually through 2027 and 2028, alongside setting up a new bilateral trade council.

title: Apple faces record $5.7 billion patent verdict over haptic technology: Here’s why
text:
Apple faces record $5.7 billion patent verdict over haptic technology: Here’s why
A Jury orders Apple to pay a record multi-billion-dollar amount in a haptic technology patent case
A US jury has ordered Apple to pay San Diego-based Taction Technology more than $5.7 billion over a patent dispute involving haptic technology used to power the vibrational feedback in iPhones and Apple Watches as the case centers on technology used to provide haptic feedback in electronic devices.
According to Reuters, the jury said on Friday that Apple’s Taptic Engine infringes patents when finding a breach of a legal agreement.
Apple said in a response stating, “Apple's Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction's technology, which Taction's own testing of Apple's products confirmed during trial.”
Apple said in a statement that it does not use Taction’s technology and will appeal; though Taction attorney Lance Yang clarified that they are happy with the jury found for Taction and defended its patent rights; Taction, uses its technology in headphones and gaming headsets, commenced the lawsuits in 2021.
Nonetheless, the US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit revived the case last year after a San Diego federal judge ruled in 2023 that Apple did not encroach upon a patent.

title: Anthropic IPO: Co-founders push for majority voting power
text:
Anthropic IPO: Co-founders push for majority voting power
Modeled on Palantir’s controversial framework, the AI lab is asking shareholders for a special share structure to safeguard its long-term safety mission ahead of a blockbuster public debut
Anthropic is asking shareholders to approve a major governance shift that would give CEO Dario Amodei and its six other co-founders a combined 50.1% of voting power through a special class of shares ahead of an anticipated initial public offering (IPO).
The arrangement is heavily modeled on the founder-control framework used by Palantir Technologies, separating economic interest from voting control.
Unlike traditional dual-class shares concentrated in a single CEO, Anthropic's proposal pools voting power among the seven co-founders via a separate structure. It remains active as long as at least three of the co-founders retain a minimum share threshold.
According to the report, the new arrangement, which emulates a founder-control structure at Palantir, would award the co-founders a special class of shares giving them collective voting control in most corporate matters, and would apply as long as three of the seven co-founders retain a minimum number of shares in the company.
The founders' 50.1% voting stake will cover most corporate matters, but board elections remain an exception.
Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust (whose members include former Fed Chair Ben Bernanke) will retain the authority to appoint a majority of the seven-seat board, while founder board seats will expand from two to three (with one seat currently vacant).
The plan also incorporates a separate class of shares given to employees that can act as tie-breakers on specific corporate matters.

title: Trump-Xi summit: China sees ‘surprise’ surge in U.S. orders
text:
Trump-Xi summit: China sees ‘surprise’ surge in U.S. orders
China saw surprise jump in US orders ahead of Trump-Xi summit
A private survey found a surprising increase in how American businesses ramped up orders from Chinese manufacturers leading up to the high-stakes summit this week as companies are poised for sustained stability between the world’s two largest economies.
Primarily, the estimate measuring orders from the US calculated as the proportion of surveyed firms reporting an increase minus in the share reporting a decrease jumped to 13 in September. Meanwhile, overall Chinese domestic and export orders remain depressed compared to their levels a year earlier.
The upsurge in US-bound orders came as businesses were positioned for a more cooperative accord between President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping who is in Washington for his first state visit in more than a decade.
The two countries agreed to a two-month extension through January that keeps tariffs lower, eases restrictive controls on rare earth exports and holds off higher port fees on ships.
The export order figures are consistent with recent metrics including that China’s ports saw their busiest week on record in the lead up to the summit, and are another sign that trade flows were recovering amid hopes for a further easing in bilateral tensions.
Washington is inclined to fast-tracked expedited Chinese approval of rare-earth licenses for US end users as well as higher consumer spending on US agricultural goods, Beijing meanwhile would expect the White House to uphold the existing halt on defense transactions to Taiwan. The two leaders are expected to meet again at the APEC summit in Shenzhen in November, potentially at the risk of being sidelined from the G20 summit the US is hosting in Miami in December, though no bilateral meeting after this week’s summit has yet been confirmed.

title: Polymarket sues New York Attorney General to block prediction market crackdown
text:
Polymarket sues New York Attorney General to block prediction market crackdown
The high-stakes legal counter-offensive escalates a nationwide turf war over whether federal regulators or state governments control the future of event-contract betting
In a latest update, World's largest prediction market platform, Polymarket sued New York Attorney General Letitia James and other state officials to block them from regulating its prediction market.
The lawsuit was filed on Thursday evening in Manhattan federal court, after James filed her own lawsuit earlier in the day accusing Polymarket of violating state law by promoting illegal gambling.
New York Attorney General Letitia James and Governor Kathy Hochul filed a lawsuit accusing Polymarket of running an illegal, unlicensed gambling operation in the state.
The state argues that prediction contracts such as wagers on sports outcomes are "quintessentially gambling," bypass local tax requirements, and illegally permit users aged 18 to 20 to participate New York requires a minimum age of 21 for mobile sports betting.
Hours later, Polymarket fired back with a federal lawsuit in Manhattan targeting state officials.
Polymarket argues that state-level oversight is an "extraordinary assertion of state power" that is preempted by federal law, claiming the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) holds exclusive jurisdiction over federally compliant prediction markets.
As reported, the fight is part of a broader crackdown by New York on prediction markets and sweepstakes platforms, having previously pursued companies like Kalshi, Coinbase, and Gemini.
With federal appeals courts divided on whether state gambling laws or federal financial regulations apply to these event contracts, legal experts suggest this high-stakes turf war could ultimately wind up before the U.S. Supreme Court.

title: AI tools for health generated nearly $1 billion in extra costs: report
text:
AI tools for health generated nearly $1 billion in extra costs: report
Blue Cross insurers report that hospital AI coding tools added $942 million in extra costs over two years, fueling industry concerns over automated medical upcoding
According to a report by the Blue Cross Blue Shield Association (BCBSA), hospitals' deployment of AI-powered revenue cycle management and documentation tools added $942 million in excess costs for member plans over a two-year window.
As reported by Reuters, AI tools are raising health spending for insurers by nearly $1 billion over two years, as providers bill for more severe patient care, according to a Blue Cross Blue Shield Association study released Thursday.
Between 2024 and 2025, providers more frequently billed for secondary conditions, or those stemming from a separate illness from the one they were treating, driving costs up by $653 million for BCBS companies during that period.
Overall, more intense care contributed $942 million in costs to BCBS firms over the two-year period, when compared to 2023, the study added
Insurers argue that AI tools are scanning patient charts to surface more secondary conditions pushing the share of inpatient stays classified as medically complex from 37% to 40%—without showing a corresponding increase in actual treatments or medical care.
However, health systems and industry groups defend the technology as a necessary counterweight to aggressive insurance claim denials, administrative burnout, and payment delays.

title: Qualcomm and Apple extend global patent licensing agreement: What to know
text:
Qualcomm and Apple extend global patent licensing agreement: What to know
Qualcomm secured a long-term deal with Apple alleviating revenue anxieties linked to a key client
In a significant move, Qualcomm announced on Thursday that it has extended its chip technology partnership with Apple effective from April 1 of next year.
The primary motive behind the partnership was rooted in a 2019 settlement that ended a two-year legal battle concerning mobile patent royalties, when both companies announced a truce in April 2019 as a US jury legal proceeding between them was commencing in San Diego.
In this connection, John Han, Executive General Manager of Qualcomm said: “We are pleased to extend the Apple license agreements”
Under the agreement, Apple made an undisclosed payment to Qualcomm, as the companies resolved all global disputes and agreed to a six-year global patent licensing deal starting from April 1, 2019.
The relationship between Apple and Qualcomm is one of the most crucial in Silicon Valley focusing on the geopolitical struggle for hardware independence and control.
Earlier Apple sued the chipmaker in 2017 over excessive royalties resolving a bitter, two-year global legal battle that abruptly ended with a 2019 settlement and laid the foundation for their active licensing agreement.
In addition, this licensing 2017 extension mechanism means that even as future iPhones are powered by Apple’s own silicon, Qualcomm will continue to secure high-yield patent returns.

title: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek hits $1 billion annualized revenue run rate following API price hikes
text:
Chinese AI startup DeepSeek hits $1 billion annualized revenue run rate following API price hikes
CEO Liang Wenfeng shared the milestone with investors as the company targets a massive $7.5 billion funding round and a future Shanghai Stock Exchange listing
Latest update reveals China's AI firm DeepSeek has doubled its annualized revenue run rate to reach $1 billion, up from under $500 million just months ago.
As reported by Information reported on Tuesday, Chinese artificial intelligence trailblazer has crossed a major commercial milestone. AI startup DeepSeek has raised more than 50 billion yuan ($7.40 billion) at a valuation exceeding $50 billion in its first funding round, using a structure designed to preserve founder control.
The sudden revenue acceleration was largely catalyzed by a strategic adjustment in application programming interface (API) pricing last month.
By hiking model costs by 2.3 to 4.5 times, DeepSeek managed to drastically scale its incoming capital while maintaining a stable customer base, thanks to continued heavy global demand for its cost-effective AI systems and agent-powering architectures.
Despite the financial upswing, Liang emphasized that monetization remains secondary to R&D, with the firm still dedicating over 70% of its compute power toward training advanced next-generation models.
As reported, the rapid financial growth was heavily propelled by recent API price increases which did not trigger customer churn due to sustained global demand.
The report said, the funding required investors to put their capital into a limited partnership managed by DeepSeek CEO Liang Wenfeng rather than into DeepSeek itself.
Alongside its booming commercialization, DeepSeek is preparing to close a major funding round targeting 50 billion yuan ($7.5 billion) ahead of a planned Shanghai listing.

title: Insurance canary
text:
Insurance canary
As the cost of insuring our houses escalates around the United States and the world, it appears that property insurance is acting like a canary in a coal mine.
Canaries used to be taken into coal mines because they served as an early warning system if dangerous gases were building up. Since the canaries were more sensitive to these gases than people, they protected the miners from life-threatening conditions. When the canary dropped dead, the miners could still get out
Like the canaries, the actuaries who interpret data for insurance companies are more sensitive than most individual people to changes going on in the world. Actuaries earn big salaries because the financial health of their employers depends on them.
Things have already gotten so bad that the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM) recently sponsored a webinar panel discussion: “Extreme Weather Events and Insurance: Households, Homeowners, and Risk.” (This link will take you to a video of the event.)
The panelists were located in the United States (Washington, DC and Madison, Wisconsin) and England (London and Cambridge). Climate changes are not limited to the United States, nor is awareness that we need to do something about them if we can.
The panelists were not grinding particular political axes. They were discussing the measured fact that an increasing number of extreme weather events are destroying valuable property – housing, commercial buildings, streets, bridges, etc. – requiring insurance company payouts to policyholders.
These insurance payouts must be financed by the premiums charged to people who are insuring their property. As damages increase, the premiums also have to increase. Although premiums may be regulated by state regulators, if they do not allow the needed increases insurance companies will pull out of doing business in that state.
As insurance companies pull out, it may become more and more difficult – perhaps even impossible – for people to insure their houses. But if a house cannot be insured, banks won’t finance a mortgage on it, and if it cannot be financed the owner may be unable to sell it.
For many people, their home is their primary investment, and they cannot afford to live in it if they cannot insure it. If it burned down or was otherwise destroyed, they would be wiped out financially. But if they cannot sell it, then the homeowner is a real pickle.
Disrupted housing markets can produce disastrous results for a country’s economy in general, as we Americans discovered during the recession beginning around 2008.
The impact of a world that is heating up is not being felt as much in the United States as in many other countries in Europe, Africa, and Asia which are suffering from unusually long bouts of very hot weather, flooding downpours alternating with extreme droughts, forest fires, etc.
Excerpted: ‘Property Insurance Is the Canary in the Climate Coal Mine’. Courtesy: Commondreams.org

title: The future of work
text:
The future of work
Internal Amazon documents reveal plans to replace more than half a million warehouse workers with robots by 2033. Executives call it innovation. Investors call it efficiency. The workers who made the company what it is call it what it feels like: erasure disguised as progress.
If Amazon can erase 500,000 jobs without consequence, every company will follow. Walmart is rolling out automated checkout. Target is testing robotic fulfillment. UPS and FedEx are developing delivery drones. Each step is described as modernization, but modernization without accountability becomes abandonment.
The United States cannot afford another era of abandonment. Since 1979, productivity has risen by more than 80%, while hourly pay for most workers has barely moved. Automation threatens to widen that divide until it defines the economy itself.
