title: Disaster management cooperation: Dar, Tajik PM highlight potential
text:
ISLAMABAD: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar called on the Prime Minister of Tajikistan, Qohir Rasulzoda, in Dushanbe on Monday, highlighting Pakistan’s disaster management expertise and highlighting the potential for bilateral cooperation through the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA).
The DPM/FM thanked the PM for the warm hospitality extended to him and his delegation and appreciated the arrangements for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Council of Heads of Government (CHG) meeting. He also congratulated Tajikistan on the 35th anniversary of its independence, a DPM’s Office news release said.
The two leaders reviewed bilateral relations and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation in trade, investment, energy, connectivity, defence and culture, as well as promoting people-to-people exchanges. They also underscored the importance of cooperation on climate change and water security.
They also exchanged views on regional developments. The DPM/FM reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to working closely with Tajikistan to promote regional peace and deeper economic integration.

title: Master Plan Lahore Division 2050: LDA, EPA host hearing to evaluate environmental dimensions
text:
LAHORE: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) and the Punjab Environment Protection Agency (EPA) on Monday hosted a public hearing to evaluate the environmental dimensions of the ‘Master Plan Lahore Division 2050’.
The session addressed critical urban and ecological challenges, aiming to refine the 2050 vision by integrating citizen feedback and expert recommendations. The event was attended by Sharjeel Hafeez Wattoo, Additional Director General (Operations) of the EPA, and the Chief Metropolitan Planner of the LDA.
On this occasion, the Chief Metropolitan Planner and the consultants briefed participants on the necessity and significance of the Master Plan 2050, assuring them that suggestions regarding environmental pollution raised during the public hearing would be reviewed, while Fauzia Akram, a Director at the Punjab Environment Protection Agency, provided a briefing on issues such as smog and environmental pollution.
Kamil Khan Mumtaz, a renowned architect and member of the ‘Lahore Bachao Tehreek’, explained the various stages of the Master Plan. He noted that the Master Plan is being developed with the ongoing global environmental crisis in mind, with the primary objective of fostering a ‘prosperous Lahore’ that serves as a ‘hub of civilisation’.
During the public hearing, the international consultancy firm Dar Al-Handasah and Asian Consultant Engineering, both involved in the Lahore Master Plan, delivered presentations. Representatives from Dar Al-Handasah stated that the Master Plan is being formulated with due consideration for Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA). The plan addresses concerns such as environmental pollution, smog, the haphazard expansion of industry, and various socio-economic challenges. It focuses on key urban requirements, including public transport, road infrastructure, housing, agriculture, healthcare facilities, landscaping, educational institutions, industrial development, and sewage systems.
The Master Plan covers the Lahore Division. Various urban amenities in Lahore, Sheikhupura, Kasur, and Nankana have been reviewed. The master plan incorporates input from citizens, as well as proposals and recommendations from the Environment Department. It accounts for projected future population growth, urban sprawl, and housing requirements. Planning is being conducted with a focus on urban amenities, public transportation, and the needs of commuters and pedestrians.
Moreover, the master plan for the Lahore Division also encompasses provisions for cultural spaces, parks, greenery, sewerage systems, and water infrastructure. The construction of high-rise buildings, including both commercial and residential properties, will be encouraged. It further integrates planning for areas under the jurisdiction of RUDA, CBD, the Cantonment, and DHA. Efforts are underway, in collaboration with developers and other stakeholders, to address issues related to environmental pollution.
Environmental experts Aleem Butt and Rafay Alam briefed the participants on the causes of environmental pollution and potential remedial measures. A large number of stakeholders, consultants, citizens, and students participated in the public hearing. At the conclusion of the seminar, the consultants addressed questions raised by the citizens and students.

title: Forced loadshedding: ‘New grid stations, additional power transformers needed in Hyderabad’
text:
HYDERABAD: According to the HESCO spokesperson, Member of the National Assembly and Member of the Standing Committee on Energy, Syed Waseem Hussain, while speaking during a meeting held at the HESCO Conference Hall about the electricity transmission system, the elimination of forced loadshedding and improved electricity supply to consumers, said that new grid stations, additional power transformers and a dual-source 500 kV system are needed to eliminate forced loadshedding in Hyderabad and ensure a better and more stable electricity supply for domestic, commercial, industrial and agricultural consumers.
He said that providing better electricity is their objective and that establishing new grid stations and new 11 kV feeders is essential to further improve the electricity transmission system. Additional power transformers should be installed at the NGC Jamshoro Grid Station, while a dual-source 500 kV system is urgently needed to ensure an uninterrupted electricity supply. In addition, a 500 kV grid station should be established in Nawabshah.
He said that he would discuss these matters with the responsible officials of the National Grid Company (NGC). He would also approach the Managing Director and other concerned officials regarding the installation of additional power transformers at the 500 kV grid station in Jamshoro, so that forced load-shedding can be eliminated throughout Hyderabad, Sanghar and Mirpur Khas.
He further emphasized that effective measures should be taken to eliminate forced load-shedding in Hyderabad through the 630 kV AC/DC grid station at Matiari, ensuring a better and more stable electricity supply for domestic, commercial, industrial and agricultural consumers.
On this occasion, HESCO Chief Executive Officer Faizullah Dahri said that HESCO management is taking practical measures to provide better facilities to consumers, improve electricity supply and provide them with relief.
Transferring 79 HESCO 11 kV general feeders to zero-load-shedding status is an important achievement, enabling consumers in the relevant areas to receive uninterrupted electricity. This achievement is the result of the collective efforts of HESCO officers, engineers, field staff and other relevant teams.
The Chief Executive Officer further said that HESCO management’s foremost priority is to ensure a better and more reliable electricity supply to consumers, resolve their problems and further improve the organization’s performance.

title: CPPs’ matters: Work to launch investigations is complete: NAB
text:
ISLAMABAD: National Accountability Bureau (NAB) Chairman Lieutenant General Nazir Ahmed Butt (Retd) said on Monday that the bureau had completed preparatory work to launch investigations into matters relating to captive power plants (CPPs), with the results expected to emerge early next year.
“The NAB has taken notice of irregularities in the power sector and will initiate cases at the federal and provincial levels,” he said during a media briefing on the bureau’s recoveries during the first quarter of 2026.
He said the bureau had finalised preparations for initiating cases relating to CPPs, adding the results of the investigations were expected early next year.
Responding to a question about money laundering, he said some countries that lectured Pakistan on democracy had questionable records of their own. He alleged that these countries had granted undeclared amnesties in cases involving money laundering.
He said around 147,000 Pakistani children were studying at universities abroad, adding that relevant institutions in those countries were not responding to Pakistan’s requests for information.
Without naming any institution, he said three countries with large Pakistani populations were not cooperating with Pakistan.
“The countries where money laundering hubs exist have enacted stronger secrecy laws,” he said, adding that Pakistan generally followed international laws more strictly than necessary.
Butt said that NAB has attached properties of worth Rs 180 billion in connection with money laundering cases with the direction of the court.
To another question, he said that NAB was also conducting an investigation regarding matters related to the government but so far not released its details to the media.
The NAB chairman said that Interpol has issued red notices against Bahria Town owner Malik Riaz. “If Malik Riaz wants to return, he is welcome to come back and face the cases against him.”
He said the bureau has received 60 percent complaints regarding private businessmen, 18 percent against bureaucrats and only 4.5 per cent of complaints regarding politicians during the past.
The Chairman NAB said that action against irregularities in mines and minerals, as well as the Auqaf department, has also been included in the NAB’s future plan.
Amjad Aulakh, Director General (DG) NAB operations, briefed the media about the anti-graft recoveries in the third quarter of 2026. He said that NAB sustained initiatives have resulted into recoveries of Rs 9.2 trillion in the third quarter of 2026. The year 2026, so far, has witnessed an aggregate recovery of valuable state lands and other assets worth Rs 14.6 trillion, he said.
He said that the bureau has recovered land, measuring 235,622 Kanals (29,453 acres) worth Rs 6.78 trillion, of Pakistan Railways. Furthermore, NAB has recovered 866,299 acres land of provincial departments, including Forest, Revenue & Highways, valued at Rs 2.395 trillion. “This has marked a total recovery of State assets worth Rs 9.18 trillion in the third quarter of 2026,” he said.
DG operation said that NAB Sukkur has recovered 51.41 acres land of provincial revenue department worth Rs 1.14 billion and Pakistan Railways land measuring 179,072 kanals worth Rs 5.06 trillion located in the vicinity of prime urban areas of Karachi Division. NAB Balochistan further moved on the front of locating unmutated/ misappropriated lands of forest department and recovered 811,967 acres worth Rs 1.71 trillion, he said.
Aulakh said that NAB Multan recovered 43,028 acres of provincial revenue, forest and highway departments’ land worth Rs 102.97 billion and Pakistan Railways land measuring 49,426 kanals worth Rs 1.56 trillion. NAB Lahore has recovered highly valuable provincial state land measuring 4,380 acres worth Rs 563.07 billion and 7,124 kanals of Pakistan Railways land worth Rs 156.10 billion, he said.
He said that NAB Khyber Pakhtunkhwa recovered Forest and Revenue Departments’ land measuring 6,872 acres worth Rs 16.16 billion NAB Islamabad and Rawalpindi and NAB Khyber Pakhtunkhwa recovered Rs 2.22 billion in terms of plea bargain in cases of Bahria Town and Kohistan scandal.
He said the bureau has stepped into a transformation phase by adopting an AI based Investigation regime named as “NAB EYE” to minimize human discretion / error and expedite the processes. Further, in the instant quarter, Pakistan Anti-Corruption Academy (PACA) has imparted trainings through three Specialized Courses, one Capacity Building Course, one Workshop, one Learning Program and one Promotional Course.

title: UNHCR appoints Noriko as new Representative in Pakistan
text:
ISLAMABAD: UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency, has appointed Ms. Noriko Takagi, as its new Representative in Pakistan, who arrived here to take up her responsibilities, succeeding Ms. Philippa Candler.
Ms. Takagi brings nearly three decades of experience in humanitarian and protection responses, programme management and partnership-building across Asia, Africa and Europe, including at UNHCR Headquarters in Geneva.
Before her appointment in Pakistan, Takagi served as UNHCR Representative in Myanmar from 2023 to 2026. Her previous assignments include Senior Programme Coordinator at UNHCR’s Regional Bureau in Bangkok, Deputy Representative in Myanmar and Senior Regional Programme Officer in Budapest.
She has also held field positions in Tanzania and Nepal. Before joining UNHCR in 1997, she worked with development organizations in Uganda.
“I am very excited to take up my new role in Pakistan and look forward to working closely with the Government and UNHCR’s partners to support refugees and asylum-seekers. Together, I am confident we will continue with our steadfast efforts to address their protection needs and help them find solutions for a better future,” said Ms. Takagi.

title: Diplomacy only solution for resolving Pak-Afghan tensions: Masood
text:
ISLAMABAD: Former AJK president and former ambassador Masood Ahmed Khan on Monday stressed that diplomacy remains the only viable solution to resolve the ongoing tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan, urging Islamabad to prioritise diplomatic engagement to address outstanding disputes.
Masood Khan, President of the Centre for Law and Security (CLAS) and TMUC, was speaking during a lecture organised by the Institute of Cost and Management Accountants of Pakistan (ICMA), where he discussed Pakistan-Afghanistan relations, the country’s economic potential and the evolving role of public diplomacy.
He said Pakistan had historically extended support to millions of Afghan refugees but had faced hostile policies from the Afghan government in return. He emphasised that diplomatic engagement remained essential to resolving existing differences and improving bilateral relations.
Khan said the government was making serious efforts to improve diplomatic ties with Afghanistan. He also referred to reports that the National Defence University had invited the Afghan ambassador to Pakistan, describing diplomatic engagement as an important avenue for addressing bilateral challenges.
Highlighting Pakistan’s economic potential, the former ambassador referred to a World Bank report indicating that the country had the potential to become the world’s 10th-largest economy. He said this reflected the scale of opportunities available to Pakistan if its economic potential was effectively realised.
He also highlighted the potential role of Zakat in poverty alleviation, observing that nationwide enforcement of a 2.5 percent Zakat system could help address poverty.
Speaking about public diplomacy, Khan said technological advancements and the widespread use of digital communication platforms had transformed traditional diplomatic practices. Platforms such as WhatsApp and other social media networks had enabled diplomats to communicate directly with their counterparts abroad, changing the way international engagement was conducted.
He noted that Pakistan’s population of approximately 250 million included around 210 million mobile phone users and 160 million broadband subscribers. This extensive digital connectivity, he said, had transformed society and increased the influence of social media on decision-making.
In the evolving environment of public diplomacy, every individual mattered in shaping global engagement and influencing perceptions, he added.
Khan also stressed the need for agricultural reforms, calling for more effective utilisation of foreign direct investment to strengthen the sector and support economic growth.
He underscored Pakistan’s longstanding role at the United Nations and its engagement at the level of the UN secretary-general, describing the country as an important player in regional and international affairs.
“Pakistan is one of the most consequential states in West Asia,” he said, highlighting its substantial economic potential. He added that as Washington sought more diversified supply and value chains across Eurasia, Pakistan should be viewed as a developing hub for trade, energy, transport and broader regional connectivity.
Former diplomat said Washington had publicly acknowledged Pakistan’s contributions to promoting peace across South and Central Asia.
He further noted that Pakistan had enjoyed the confidence of both Washington and Tehran in efforts to broker a ceasefire, facilitate direct talks and secure a memorandum of understanding providing a framework for negotiations.
Although the process had not progressed further, Pakistan continued to pursue all available avenues to bring the war to an end, he added.
ICMA President Muhammad Yasin and Ghulam Mustafa Qazi also spoke on the occasion.

title: Australia, NZ dollars firm as French fallout pressures euro
text:
Australia, NZ dollars firm as French fallout pressures euro
- The Aussie was flat at $0.6977, having risen 0.5% overnight and away from a recent 15-week trough of $0.68945
SYDNEY: The Australian and New Zealand dollars held firm on Tuesday helped by gains on European currencies following riots in France, while investors awaited developments on domestic interest rates.
The Aussie was flat at $0.6977, having risen 0.5% overnight and away from a recent 15-week trough of $0.68945.
Near-term resistance comes in at $0.6993 and $0.7015. It also bounced on the euro, sterling and the Swiss franc as political concerns hit bonds across the continent.
The kiwi dollar stood at $0.5665, after edging up 0.1% overnight.
Major support lies at the recent 17-month low of $0.5566, with resistance at $0.5675 and $0.5750.
The next domestic hurdle for the Aussie will be an appearance by Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser on Wednesday where he is likely to field questions about the chance of a fifth hike in rates this year.
Speaking on Monday, the RBA’s head of financial markets acknowledged that the labour market might be loosening a little faster than expected, but also highlighted the importance of third-quarter consumer price data due on October 28.
Analysts see a risk core inflation could rise a hefty 1.0% in the quarter to keep the annual pace at 3.6% and well above the RBA’s target range of 2% to 3%.
Indeed, analysts at Westpac think core inflation could also rise by a chunky 0.9% this quarter, putting annual inflation at 3.5% compared to the RBA’s forecast of 3.3%.
Central bank officials will have an opportunity to respond live to the Q3 numbers as Governor Michele Bullock and her team are appearing before lawmakers on the same day and at almost the same time.
Markets imply a one-in-three chance of a hike in the 4.60% cash rate in November, rising to 56% for December.
Also on October 28, the Reserve Bank of New Zealand will announce whether it is lifting rates for a third time this year, with investors pricing in an 89% probability of a quarter-point move to 3.0%.
Markets also imply rates could reach 3.75% or more next year, far above the RBNZ’s own projection of 3.20%.

title: Australian shares head for worst day in nearly three weeks as miners, banks slide
text:
Australian shares head for worst day in nearly three weeks as miners, banks slide
- The S&P/ASX 200 index fell 1.1% to 8,752.80
Australian shares fell more than 1% on Tuesday and were on track for their biggest drop in nearly three weeks, as financials and commodity-linked stocks overshadowed gains in tech shares, while National Australia Bank unveiled a major restructuring plan.
The S&P/ASX 200 index fell 1.1% to 8,752.80 by 2327 GMT, heading for its worst session since October 1.
The benchmark closed 0.4% higher on Monday. Selling was broad-based in miners and banks, with softer commodity prices hurting miners and energy firms and National Australia Bank’s restructuring programme adding pressure to lenders.
National Australia Bank said it would cut up to 2,500 jobs, or about 6% of its workforce, in 2027 to simplify its operations as the country’s top business lender grapples with a more challenging outlook for credit growth.
Its shares gave up early gains to trade 1.9% lower, tracking weakness in the sector.
Financials dropped 1.3%, with Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Westpac and ANZ down between 1.2% and 1.6%.
Miners slid 2%, with BHP falling as much as 2.4% after the world’s largest listed miner reported weaker-than-expected first-quarter copper production, hurt by disruptions at its Escondida mine in Chile. Both Rio Tinto and Fortescue declined more than 1%.
Gold miners fell 2.3% after bullion prices closed lower overnight.
Energy stocks slid as much as 1.6%, marking their biggest intraday drop since October 1, after Brent crude edged lower.
Woodside and Santos fell 0.9% and 1.2%, respectively. Bucking the trend, technology stocks advanced as much as 2% to a one-week high after their Wall Street peers closed higher overnight.
Xero and WiseTech Global rose more than 2.3% each.
New Zealand’s benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index was nearly flat at 13,650.72.
Investors were focused on third-quarter inflation data, due later this week, for clues on the central bank’s policy path.
Markets are pricing in an 89% probability of a third rate increase this year at the central bank’s October 28 meeting.

title: Japan's 20-year bond yield falls sharply after strong auction
text:
Japan's 20-year bond yield falls sharply after strong auction
- The 20-year JGB yield fell as much as 6 basis points (bps) to 3.71%
TOKYO: Japan’s 20-year government bond yield fell sharply on Tuesday after a strong auction for the bonds with the same maturity lifted sentiment.
The 20-year JGB yield fell as much as 6 basis points (bps) to 3.71%, its lowest level since September 9, after the auction outcome was announced.
Yields move inversely to bond prices.
The auction received bids worth 5.84 times the amount sold, higher than a ratio of 4.01 times at the previous auction last month.
“The strong auction outcome suggests that many investors expect a rebound in the bond market, as they turned to risk off after the mass protest in France and the sell-off of CoreWeave stocks and bonds,” said Katsutoshi Inadome, senior strategist at Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset Management.
The 30-year yield fell 1.5 bps to 3.970%.
The benchmark 10-year JGB yield rose 1.5 bps to 2.920%‑Reuters

title: ABB says data centre business booming, Q3 figures in line with forecasts
text:
ABB says data centre business booming, Q3 figures in line with forecasts
- Revenue meanwhile rose 14% to $9.70 billion, slightly below forecasts of $9.74 billion in a company gathered consensus
ZURICH: ABB is continuing to see a boom in spending on data centres used to power artificial intelligence, the engineering group said on Tuesday, as it reported its latest earnings.
The Swiss company said its operational earnings before interest, tax and amortisation jumped 24% to $2.03 billion in the three months to the end of September, slightly ahead of analyst forecasts for $2.0 billion.
Revenue meanwhile rose 14% to $9.70 billion, slightly below forecasts of $9.74 billion in a company gathered consensus.
ABB, which makes electrification and automation products used by factories, ships and ports, has been seeing strong demand for products like power distribution and cooling systems used in data centres.
A surge in spending on AI and data centres is propping up the global economy, helping it withstand the energy shock from the Middle East war, the IMF said last week, although it said a reassessment of efficiency gains from adopting the technology could dent investment.
ABB beats forecasts with Q2 earnings and announces biggest-ever acquisition
During the third quarter ABB said it had seen a triple digit increase in orders for data centre products, continuing the trend it saw during the second quarter.

title: South Korean shares fall nearly 3% as AI concerns hit chipmakers
text:
South Korean shares fall nearly 3% as AI concerns hit chipmakers
- The benchmark KOSPI was down 170.63 points, or 2.96%, at 5,597.38
SEOUL: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
South Korean shares slumped nearly 3% on Tuesday as chipmakers dropped on concerns over AI investment, while political instability in France dampened risk appetite across global financial markets.
The benchmark KOSPI was down 170.63 points, or 2.96%, at 5,597.38 as of 0132 GMT, after rebounding for two consecutive sessions from a recent six-month low.
“Although it is confirmed that recent losses in AI chip stocks were excessive in the short term, credit risks of AI investments have not been resolved,” said Seo Sang-young, an analyst at Mirae Asset Securities.
French markets tumbled on Monday, with bonds, Paris-listed stocks and even the euro falling after widespread protests across France underscored difficulties the government faces in reducing its large deficit.
The turmoil in the euro zone’s second-largest economy has also been partly responsible for keeping the European equities stuck within a narrow range over the past month.
“It is difficult to determine the sustainability of the recent rebound amid pressure from Europe’s financial instability and higher bond yields,” Seo said.
South Korean chipmaker Samsung Electronics fell 1.61% on Tuesday, while peer SK Hynix lost 4.62%.
AI infrastructure company Elice Group opened 16% below its IPO price in its market debut, reflecting broader concerns over AI investment.
Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution slid 2.08%, while Hyundai Motor and sister automaker Kia Corp were down 3.37% and 3.02%, respectively.
Steelmaker POSCO Holdings shed 2.23%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics fell 0.63%. Of the total 913 traded issues, only 95 shares advanced, while 803 declined.

title: UniCredit to buy back securities-services unit from Societe Generale, document shows
text:
UniCredit to buy back securities-services unit from Societe Generale, document shows
- Societe Generale bought UniCredit’s securities services unit in 2006
MILAN: Italy’s second-biggest bank, UniCredit, has signed an agreement to repurchase its securities-services business from French peer Societe Generale , according to a union document seen by Reuters on Monday.
The unit, which looks after investors’ securities and handles related administrative services, has 54 staff in Milan and Turin, according to the document, which did not provide any financial details of the agreement.
Societe Generale bought UniCredit’s securities services unit in 2006, striking a long-term partnership to handle those services for the Italian bank.
The supply contract was last renewed in 2017 until 2026.
UniCredit is seeking to bring in-house activities it deems strategic, and the transaction is part of that effort, the document said.
Handling the securities itself will reduce the need for an external supplier and improve use of the business’ data, UniCredit and Societe Generale did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

title: “Uzbekistan Airways” to increase Tashkent–Islamabad flights operation to three weekly flights
text:
Uzbekistan Airways, the national airline of Uzbekistan, will increase the frequency of its flights between Tashkent and Islamabad from twice to three times a week from October 26, aiming to strengthen air connectivity and boost tourism, trade and cultural ties between Uzbekistan and Pakistan.
“Uzbekistan Airways” to increase Tashkent–Islamabad flights operation to three weekly flights
By: Shams Abbasi
ISLAMABAD, Oct 20 (APP):Uzbekistan Airways, the national airline of Uzbekistan, will increase the frequency of its flights between Tashkent and Islamabad from twice to three times a week from October 26, aiming to strengthen air connectivity and boost tourism, trade and cultural ties between Uzbekistan and Pakistan.
Currently, the airline operates flights on the Tashkent–Islamabad–Tashkent route twice a week, on Tuesdays and Saturdays. Under the revised schedule, flights will operate on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.
The additional service is expected to provide greater convenience for tourists, business travellers and transit passengers, offering more flexibility in travel planning and creating new opportunities for closer bilateral cooperation.
The enhanced air connectivity is also expected to encourage more Pakistani tourists to visit Uzbekistan, promote pilgrimage tourism and showcase the country’s rich historical and cultural heritage.
Improved flight connections will facilitate travel to Samarkand, Bukhara and Khiva, three of Uzbekistan’s prominent historic cities associated with the ancient Great Silk Road. The increased frequency will also strengthen Tashkent’s role as a regional transport hub, providing travellers with more opportunities to explore other Central Asian destinations.
Tourism exchanges between the two countries have shown considerable potential for growth. More than 20,000 Pakistani tourists visited Uzbekistan in 2025, while nearly 20,000 visited during the first nine months of the current year.
The rising number of visitors highlights growing interest in Uzbekistan as a tourism destination and underscores opportunities for further expanding people-to-people contacts and tourism cooperation between the two countries.
Currently, eight scheduled flights operate between Uzbekistan and Pakistan each week. These include four flights on the Tashkent–Lahore route and two on the Tashkent–Islamabad route, alongside services connecting Tashkent with Karachi.
With the introduction of the additional Islamabad service, the total number of scheduled weekly flights between the two countries will rise to nine.
The increased flight frequency is expected to further strengthen bilateral transport links, facilitate two-way tourism, support business travel and contribute to broader trade, economic, cultural and humanitarian cooperation between Uzbekistan and Pakistan.

Pakistan, US discuss trade agreement, market access, investment cooperation
ISLAMABAD, Oct 20 (APP):Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan on Tuesday held a meeting with United States Chargé d’Affaires Natalie A. Baker and discussed strengthening bilateral economic relations, accelerating ongoing trade agreement negotiations, expanding market access and exploring new opportunities for cooperation in agriculture, minerals, technology and investment.
Rana Ihsaan Afzal Khan, Coordinator to the Prime Minister on Commerce and Industries, Secretary Commerce Jawad Paul and senior officials of the Ministry of Commerce also attended the meeting, said a news release.
Welcoming the US delegation, the minister underscored Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening its longstanding economic partnership with the United States, highlighting the potential to expand bilateral trade through enhanced market access, greater private-sector engagement and investment in emerging sectors.
Jam Kamal highlighted Pakistan’s efforts to diversify its export markets and strengthen international commercial partnerships despite prevailing regional and global economic challenges.
He said deeper economic engagement with the US could create new opportunities for businesses, enhance industrial competitiveness and contribute to sustainable economic growth.
Both sides reviewed progress on the ongoing Pakistan–U.S. bilateral reciprocal trade agreement negotiations and expressed their commitment to advancing discussions towards a mutually beneficial outcome.
Secretary Commerce Jawad Paul informed the meeting that substantial progress had been achieved on several important provisions of the proposed agreement while a few technical points need to be discussed with the USTR.
The meeting also discussed market access opportunities for Pakistani agricultural products, particularly mangoes and dates. Jawad Paul stressed the need to expedite the visit of relevant U.S. inspection teams for mango export arrangements and sought progress on the pending market access process for Pakistani dates.
He said that greater access to the U.S. market would create valuable export opportunities, particularly for growers and businesses in Balochistan.
The U.S. delegation welcomed the discussion and indicated its willingness to follow up with the relevant American authorities on these matters.
Both sides also explored opportunities to increase agricultural trade, particularly U.S. exports of cotton and soybeans to Pakistan. The Secretary Commerce highlighted the importance of competitive pricing and trade financing in facilitating greater imports from the United States.
Discussions also covered possible financing arrangements and closer coordination with relevant trade institutions and industry associations.
Jam Kamal underlined Pakistan’s significant potential in agriculture, food processing, livestock and value-added production, encouraging US companies to explore investment opportunities in modern agricultural machinery, food processing technologies, cold-chain infrastructure and improved farming practices.
He invited American businesses and agricultural organizations to participate in FoodAg 2026, scheduled to be held in Karachi from November 23 to 26, saying the exhibition would provide an important platform to connect international buyers and investors with Pakistan’s growing agricultural and food-processing industries.
The U.S. Chargé d’Affaires appreciated Pakistan’s efforts to promote agricultural trade and expressed interest in facilitating greater engagement between American agricultural technology companies and Pakistani businesses.
Highlighting Balochistan’s economic potential, Jam Kamal identified dates, olive oil and other agricultural products as promising areas for value addition and export development.
He said international cooperation could help improve processing facilities, product quality, packaging and access to global markets, while creating opportunities for small enterprises, farmers and women entrepreneurs.
Minerals and mining also featured prominently in the discussions, with both sides exploring opportunities for investment, technical cooperation, skills development and responsible resource development.
The U.S. delegation conveyed continued interest in strengthening cooperation in Pakistan’s mineral sector, including opportunities for American companies to contribute technical expertise, investment and commercial partnerships.
The minister also highlighted the industrial potential of Hub, Balochistan, noting its strategic proximity to Karachi and opportunities for investment in manufacturing, industrial infrastructure and special economic zones. He welcomed the existing presence of American companies in Pakistan and encouraged further private-sector investment.
During the discussion on regional trade connectivity, Secretary Commerce highlighted challenges arising from disruptions to traditional land trade routes, particularly those connecting Pakistan with Afghanistan and Central Asian markets.
He observed that uninterrupted regional connectivity, predictable trade arrangements and efficient logistics were essential for sustaining export growth and maintaining long-term commercial relationships.
The minister emphasized that Pakistan remained committed to strengthening its economic resilience, improving the business environment and expanding trade opportunities while taking into consideration broader regional developments.
Both sides acknowledged the importance of continued institutional dialogue, stronger business-to-business contacts and practical cooperation in promoting shared economic interests.
Jam Kamal reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to developing a forward-looking economic partnership with the United States, based on mutual respect, shared opportunities and sustainable commercial growth.
U.S. Chargé d’Affaires appreciated the constructive discussions and reiterated the United States’ interest in expanding economic engagement with Pakistan, particularly in trade, agriculture, technology and investment.
Both sides agreed to maintain close coordination to advance ongoing trade negotiations, address market access issues and explore new opportunities for mutually beneficial economic cooperation.

Petroleum prices determined on seven-day average: Ali Pervaiz Malik
ISLAMABAD, Oct 20 (APP):Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik on Tuesday said petroleum prices were determined on the basis of a seven-day average under a transparent formula.
Responding to a calling attention notice regarding the daily determination of petroleum prices instead of the fortnightly mechanism, the minister said the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) set prices according to the seven-day average. He added that the authority had also published the formula on its website.
Referring to the previous practice of revising petroleum prices every 14 days, Ali Pervaiz Malik said prices had earlier been revised annually and later on a monthly basis.
He said Pakistan imported all its oil requirements, while volatility in international markets made it necessary for the government to ensure an uninterrupted supply chain and prevent profiteering and hoarding.
The minister said keeping domestic petroleum prices close to international market rates helped ensure that changes in global prices were reflected in local prices. This approach also helped maintain the security of the supply chain, he added.
He said the trend in international oil prices became clearer after three to four days, indicating whether prices were rising or falling. The existing pricing mechanism helped improve fuel availability at petrol pumps and reduce difficulties faced by consumers, he added.
Ali Pervaiz Malik said the government had adopted the seven-day average mechanism to address supply-related problems and ensure the availability of petroleum products.
The minister also informed the House that, at the prime minister’s request, refineries had once again reduced their gross refining margins. He said a cap of $38 had been imposed on the crack margin.
He said the measure had led to a reduction of Rs7.69 per litre in the price of high-speed diesel the previous day, while petrol prices had also witnessed a considerable decrease.

title: Pakistan’s twin deficit falls to 2.6pc of GDP, says Aurangzeb
text:
ISLAMABAD, Oct 20 (APP):Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb on Tuesday said Pakistan’s twin deficit had declined from a cumulative 12.5 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to 2.6 percent, reflecting progress in macroeconomic stabilization and fiscal consolidation. Addressing a two-day high-level workshop on “Reforms for a Modern and Growth-Friendly Tax System in Pakistan”, the minister said that the country had achieved a 22-year low fiscal deficit in …
Pakistan’s twin deficit falls to 2.6pc of GDP, says Aurangzeb
ISLAMABAD, Oct 20 (APP):Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb on Tuesday said Pakistan’s twin deficit had declined from a cumulative 12.5 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to 2.6 percent, reflecting progress in macroeconomic stabilization and fiscal consolidation.
Addressing a two-day high-level workshop on “Reforms for a Modern and Growth-Friendly Tax System in Pakistan”, the minister said that the country had achieved a 22-year low fiscal deficit in the last fiscal year and recorded primary surpluses for three consecutive years.
The event was organized by the Ministry of Finance and the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which bring together senior government officials, representatives of the IMF and World Bank, international tax experts, academics and private-sector leaders to discuss priorities for modernizing Pakistan’s tax system and strengthening its contribution to sustainable economic growth.
Speaking on the occasion. Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb said that the Federal Board of Revenue’s (FBR) tax-to-GDP ratio had increased from 8.8 percent to 10.3 percent, while tax revenues had risen by 40 percent over the last two fiscal years.
The minister attributed the improvement to stronger enforcement measures and new tax policy initiatives, explaining that 0.9 percentage points of the 1.5-percentage-point increase in the tax-to-GDP ratio over the last two and a half years had come from enforcement, while 0.6 percentage points resulted from new policy measures.
The government would further strengthen enforcement, curb revenue leakages and broaden the tax base to improve revenue mobilization, he added.
The minister highlighted the ongoing FBR transformation program, covering human resources, processes and technology, which he said was being led by the prime minister and monitored through weekly reviews.
He said that the taxation reforms remained a critical component of the government’s broader structural reform agenda, alongside reforms in the energy sector, state-owned enterprises (SOEs), privatization, public finance, pensions and tariffs.
Emphasizing the need to move from economic stabilization towards growth, Aurangzeb said Pakistan’s economy had recovered from a contraction of 0.3 percent and returned to a positive growth trajectory.
However, he stressed that the country needed sustainable, export-led growth rather than liquidity-driven, consumption-based expansion, which had contributed to boom-and-bust cycles in the past.
“We will not let that repeat,” he said, underscoring the government’s commitment to ensuring that future growth was sustainable and supported by stronger economic fundamentals.
The finance minister also pointed to improvements in the country’s external position, saying foreign exchange reserves had recovered from a level equivalent to around two weeks of import cover to more than three months, reaching a record high.
He said the quality of reserves was as important as their volume, noting that the recent improvement had not been accompanied by a comparable increase in external debt.
Aurangzeb said Pakistan’s external debt stock had increased by around $4 billion over the preceding four years, compared with an annual increase of $6 billion to $7 billion during the 2015–2022 period, when external liabilities had risen from around $55 billion to more than $100 billion.
He said the government would continue designing tax policies around economic value and competitiveness rather than focusing solely on meeting revenue targets.
Referring to the previous budget, he said the government had undertaken recalibrations relating to exports and export-oriented industries and would build on these measures to support export-led growth.
The minister identified broadening the tax base, simplifying the taxation code and ensuring policy predictability and continuity as key priorities for the ongoing reform process.
He said frequent and unexpected tax changes could undermine private-sector investment, stressing that businesses needed a predictable policy environment to support long-term planning and economic expansion.
Aurangzeb identified political consensus, stronger institutions, improved taxpayer trust and clear communication as essential enablers of successful tax reforms.
He said cooperation between the federal and provincial governments was particularly important, while rebuilding trust and credibility in the tax authority was necessary to improve compliance and strengthen the relationship between taxpayers and the state.
The minister acknowledged the need for better communication to demonstrate progress on structural reforms and explain the measures being taken to increase revenue collection and improve its quality.
He expressed the hope that discussions during the conference would help assess progress on ongoing reforms and develop a roadmap for advancing from stabilization to sustainable economic growth.
He said effective tax policy design and administration would remain critical to strengthening the private sector’s role in economic development and ensuring durable economic stability.
Addressing the workshop Jihad Azour, Director of the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) Middle East and Central Asia Department urged to pursue broad-based, fair and predictable tax reforms to sustain macroeconomic stability, boost private investment and achieve stronger, more inclusive economic growth.
“Pakistan had made significant progress in restoring macroeconomic stability, rebuilding confidence, strengthening external buffers and supporting a gradual economic recovery despite repeated shocks and global uncertainty”, he remarked.
He credited Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, his colleagues in the government, the prime minister and parliament for the progress, saying the next challenge was to translate stabilization gains into stronger and more sustainable economic growth.
“The next milestone is to turn the stabilization into stronger and more durable growth,” Azour said, emphasizing the need to move beyond recurring adjustment cycles towards a more competitive, investment-friendly and inclusive economy.
He said the government’s reform agenda, supported by the IMF through its Extended Fund Facility (EFF), aimed to raise productivity, strengthen the private sector and create better economic opportunities for Pakistan’s younger generations.
Referring to the IMF’s Regional Economic Outlook, he said stronger policy frameworks and buffers had helped countries cushion external shocks, but inflationary pressures, fiscal constraints and financing needs were becoming increasingly evident.
He said a stronger, broader, fairer and more predictable tax system could improve fiscal sustainability while reducing distortions that discourage investment, productivity, business expansion and formal job creation.
Azour outlined four key themes for the workshop including credibility, growth, fairness and implementation, adding that Pakistan needed to preserve its hard-won stabilization gains by continuing to meet fiscal and external objectives, strengthening resilience and ensuring that reforms were sustained and firmly embedded in institutions.
He particularly stressed the importance of coordination between the federal government and provincial authorities, alongside engagement with the private sector and civil society.
Tax policy and tax administration, he said, must advance together, noting that a simpler policy framework makes administration easier, while effective administration lends credibility to policy reforms.
Azour urged participants to use the workshop to move beyond broad principles and identify practical policy measures, implementation priorities and follow-up mechanisms. He said policymakers needed to carefully assess the trade-offs involved in broadening the tax base without undermining economic recovery, simplifying the system while safeguarding revenues, coordinating federal and provincial responsibilities, and using technology without eroding public trust.
Highlighting the importance of collaboration, Azour said the workshop brought together policymakers, tax administrators, experts, private-sector representatives, provincial officials and development partners whose combined perspectives could help shape a coherent reform roadmap.
Concluding his remarks, he said Pakistan’s recent stabilization gains had created an opportunity that needed to be reinforced through transformative reforms. “Tax reform is at the heart of it and this workshop could be the catalyst moment in this journey,” he said, expressing hope for constructive discussions and practical outcomes from the two-day event.

title: All resources to be utilised to redress business community’s concerns: Governor Punjab
text:
Punjab Governor Sardar Saleem Haider Khan on Monday said that all available resources would be utilized to redress concerns and issues of the business community.
All resources to be utilised to redress business community’s concerns: Governor Punjab
FAISALABAD, Oct 19 (APP):Punjab Governor Sardar Saleem Haider Khan on Monday said that all available resources would be utilized to redress concerns and issues of the business community.
Addressing a meeting at Faisalabad Chamber of Commerce & Industry (FCCI), he said that Faisalabad played a significant role in Pakistan’s exports and deserved modern infrastructure, business-friendly facilities and development projects capable of expanding industrial activity, attracting investment and creating new economic opportunities.
Recognizing the challenges confronting local entrepreneurs, he said that high taxes, expensive electricity and gas, and elevated interest rates were increasing production costs and making it difficult for Pakistani manufacturers to compete effectively in international markets.
He stressed the need to broaden tax base instead of imposing additional burdens on existing taxpayers. He said that the salaried class and businesses already contributing taxes were under considerable financial pressure. A fairer taxation system required bringing more people and businesses into the tax net, he added.
He said that energy prices needed to become more affordable and stable to enable industrialists to plan their operations, control production costs and expand their businesses.
He assured the business community that its legitimate demands would be conveyed to President Asif Ali Zardari for early redressal of their genuine problems.
He also announced that efforts would be made to arrange a meeting between the leadership and representatives of business community so that their concerns could be discussed at the highest level.
Emphasizing the importance of promoting Pakistani products internationally, the Punjab governor said that goods manufactured in the country should be clearly identified as “Made in Pakistan” to strengthen national brand and improve export reputation of the country.
He observed that several products originating in Pakistan were exported without a clear indication of their Pakistani origin, limiting opportunities to promote industrial capabilities and manufacturing standards of the country in international markets.
He urged the businessmen to give greater attention to establish a distinct identity for locally manufactured products.
The Governor Punjab also called for strong institutional links between universities and industrial sector, saying that academic research and technical expertise should be aligned with practical needs of businesses.
He said that he would direct vice-chancellors of universities to establish dedicated committees for liaison with industry and appoint focal persons to maintain regular communication with business organizations. Such collaboration would help businesses benefit from modern technology, research, innovation and skilled human resources while enabling universities to orient their academic and research activities towards industrial requirements, he added.
He announced that the initiative would begin with FCCI and his office would also appoint a focal person during next week to establish an effective mechanism for addressing industrialists’ concerns and proposals.
He said that he believed in delivering results rather than limiting commitments to verbal assurances. His office would facilitate the resolution of legitimate business issues instead of creating unnecessary hurdles and practical progress would be pursued without delay, he added.
He also announced the establishment of a “Textile Circular City” in Faisalabad and described the proposed circular city as an important initiative for the industrial hub. Practical steps should be taken to translate the announcement into reality, opening new avenues for economic growth of the city, he added.
During interaction, the killing of prominent businessman Rehan Ashraf was also discussed and the Governor Punjab called for the immediate arrest of those involved in the murder, saying the suspects should be apprehended within the next few hours. He stressed that those responsible for such crimes must be brought to justice to ensure relief for the bereaved family and maintain a sense of security among citizens.

title: Colourful ceremony marks opening of Asian Masters Weightlifting Championship
text:
The Marka-e-Haq 2nd Asian Masters Weightlifting Championship and World Masters Grand Prix 2026 opened at Liaquat Gymnasium, Pakistan Sports Complex, on Tuesday with a lively and colourful opening ceremony attended by athletes, officials, dignitaries, participants and fans from several countries.
Colourful ceremony marks opening of Asian Masters Weightlifting Championship
Muhammad Shafique Raja
ISLAMABAD, Oct 20 (APP):The Marka-e-Haq 2nd Asian Masters Weightlifting Championship and World Masters Grand Prix 2026 opened at Liaquat Gymnasium, Pakistan Sports Complex, on Tuesday with a lively and colourful opening ceremony attended by athletes, officials, dignitaries, participants and fans from several countries.
The vibrant ceremony featured a warm welcome for the participating delegations, while the participants and fans enjoyed the festive atmosphere and the spirit of international sports.
Parliamentary Secretary for Inter-Provincial Coordination Kiran Imran Dar, who was the chief guest welcomed the participating delegations and congratulated Pakistan Masters Weightlifting Association (PMWA) President Arshad Khan Turk for organising the international event.
“Pakistan is delighted to welcome all the participating athletes and officials. I congratulate Arshad Khan Turk for his commitment and hard work in making this international championship possible. Organising an event of this scale requires dedication, perseverance and a strong belief in the power of sports to bring people together,” she said.
Dar extended a special welcome to the Indian delegation and expressed hope that its members would return home with pleasant memories of their stay in Pakistan.
“I especially welcome our Indian guests and hope they will experience the warmth and hospitality of the Pakistani people. I want them to return to their country with sweet memories and share with their fellow citizens how warmly and wholeheartedly the people of Pakistan welcome their guests,” she said.
She said sporting events could build bridges between nations, promote mutual understanding and strengthen people-to-people contacts beyond political and geographical boundaries.
Secretary of the Ministry of Inter-Provincial Coordination Mohyuddin Ahmad Wani also welcomed the delegations and said the championship would strengthen sporting ties among participating countries.
“We are pleased to welcome all the athletes, officials and distinguished guests to Islamabad. We hope you will enjoy Pakistan’s hospitality and take back wonderful memories of your visit. Such international gatherings provide an excellent opportunity to develop friendships and strengthen sporting relations among participating countries,” he said.
Wani said the competition would showcase the strength, determination and experience of masters weightlifters.
“I am confident that spectators will witness exciting competitions during the championship. Masters athletes are an inspiration because they demonstrate that commitment to fitness, discipline and competitive sport can continue throughout life. I wish all the participants the very best and hope they enjoy a memorable and successful competition,” he added.
PMWA President Arshad Khan Turk said organising the championship had required extensive planning, coordination and sustained effort.
“Organising this championship has been a challenging undertaking, requiring sustained effort, coordination and determination. Bringing international athletes and officials together in Pakistan is a significant achievement, and I am grateful to everyone who supported us in making this event possible,” he said.
He described the championship as a watershed moment for weightlifting in Pakistan, saying it would enhance international engagement, raise the profile of masters weightlifting and encourage greater participation in the sport.
“I consider this championship a watershed moment for the development of weightlifting in Pakistan. It is not merely a competition; it is an opportunity to demonstrate our organisational capacity, strengthen international sporting relations and encourage a new generation to embrace weightlifting and physical fitness,” Arshad Khan Turk added.
Organised by the PMWA in collaboration with the Pakistan Sports Board, the championship will continue until October 25 and feature around 250 masters weightlifters from 21 participating countries.

text:
Muhammad Shafique Raja ISLAMABAD, Oct 19 (APP):Pakistan will host around 250 athletes from 21 countries at the Marka-e-Haq 2nd Asian Masters Weightlifting Championship and World Masters Grand Prix 2026, scheduled to begin at Liaquat Gymnasium, Pakistan Sports Complex on Tuesday. The six-day international event, running from October 20 to 25, is being organised by the Pakistan Masters Weightlifting Association (PMWA) in collaboration with Pakistan Sports Board (PSB), bringing together masters …
Pakistan to host Asian Masters Weightlifting Championship, World Masters Grand Prix from Tuesday
Muhammad Shafique Raja
ISLAMABAD, Oct 19 (APP):Pakistan will host around 250 athletes from 21 countries at the Marka-e-Haq 2nd Asian Masters Weightlifting Championship and World Masters Grand Prix 2026, scheduled to begin at Liaquat Gymnasium, Pakistan Sports Complex on Tuesday.
The six-day international event, running from October 20 to 25, is being organised by the Pakistan Masters Weightlifting Association (PMWA) in collaboration with Pakistan Sports Board (PSB), bringing together masters weightlifters and senior international sports officials in the federal capital.
The participating countries include Pakistan, Iran, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Singapore, the United Kingdom, Cyprus, Azerbaijan, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Belarus, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, Serbia, Ecuador and Egypt.
PMWA President Arshad Khan told APP that the championship was an important step towards promoting masters weightlifting in Pakistan and strengthening the country’s links with the international sporting community.
“Hosting the 2nd Asian Masters Weightlifting Championship and World Masters Grand Prix 2026 is a proud moment for Pakistan. With around 250 athletes expected from 21 countries, the event will provide an important platform to promote masters weightlifting and strengthen Pakistan’s links with the international sporting community,” he said.
He said the initiative also reflected the potential of international sporting competitions to contribute to the country’s sports economy.
Pakistan Sports Board conceived the idea of holding such international events last year to promote the sports economy.
Arshad said that the championship could create opportunities for sports tourism, hospitality and related sectors while showcasing Pakistan as a host of international sporting events.
“This championship is not just about weightlifting; it is also about creating opportunities for sports tourism, hospitality and other related sectors while showcasing Pakistan as a capable host of international sporting events,” he said.
The event will help strengthen sporting relations among participating countries and encourage people of different age groups to remain physically active through masters sports.
International weightlifting figures likely to attend the event include Asian Weightlifting Federation President Al Mana Mohamed Yousef, Saudi Arabian Weightlifting Federation President and AWF General Secretary Mohammed Ahmed Al Harbi, Denise Offermann, the chairperson of international weightlifting, and Asian Masters Weightlifting Association
President Mohammad Kabiri.
The opening ceremony will be held at 12:30 pm on Tuesday at Liaquat Gymnasium, Pakistan Sports Complex, Islamabad.
Expressing optimism about the future, Arshad Khan said, “We hope this championship will mark the beginning of many more international competitions in Pakistan. Our aim is to promote masters sports, encourage people to remain physically active throughout their lives and create a sustainable environment for the growth of the sports economy.”

Pakistan-China hockey ties gain momentum as Guangdong team arrives
ISLAMABAD, Oct 19 (APP):China’s Guangdong men’s hockey team arrived in Pakistan on Monday for a 13-day tour that includes matches against leading departmental sides and a Pakistan under-18 team, offering domestic players valuable exposure to international competition.
Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF) officials welcomed the visiting delegation upon arrival, presenting team members with traditional flower garlands and bouquets.
The tour features meatures matches against MPCL, Pakistan Army, Pakistan Navy, Pakistan Customs, Pakistan Rangers and Pakistan Police, as well as a fixture against a Pakistan under-18 side in Gojra.
Guangdong will begin its competitive engagements against MPCL at MPCL Hockey Stadium in Rawalpindi on Tuesday, followed by a match against Pakistan Army on Wednesday at GHQ Stadium, Rawalpindi.
After a rest day, the Chinese side will face Pakistan Navy at Naseer Bunda Hockey Stadium in Islamabad on October 23.
The team will then travel to Lahore to play Pakistan Customs at DHA Hockey Stadium on October 25, before taking on Pakistan Rangers at the Sports Complex in Narowal on October 26.
Following another rest day on October 27, Guangdong will meet the Pakistan under-18 side at National Hockey Stadium in Gojra on October 28. The visitors will play their final match against Pakistan Police at DHA Hockey Stadium, Lahore, on October 29, before departing Pakistan on October 30.
The tour will give Pakistan’s leading departmental sides an opportunity to assess their match readiness against international opposition, while allowing coaches to evaluate tactical discipline, defensive organisation and attacking efficiency.
The fixture against the under-18 side in Gojra will expose emerging players to a different style of hockey and help identify promising talent and areas for improvement ahead of future competitions.
The matches will help strengthen hockey ties between Pakistan and China and support efforts to revive the national game through regular international competitions.

title: England team arrives in Pakistan for ODI Tri-Series
text:
The England cricket team has arrived in Pakistan to participate in the One Day International (ODI) Tri-Series.
England team arrives in Pakistan for ODI Tri-Series
ISLAMABAD, Oct 16 (APP): The England cricket team has arrived in Pakistan to participate in the One Day International (ODI) Tri-Series.
The team arrived at its local hotel from Islamabad International Airport, where officials of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) received and welcomed the visiting side, said a statement issued here.
The tri-series, featuring Pakistan, England, and Sri Lanka, will be played from October 18 to 31.
The England team will hold a practice session on Saturday, at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium.
The opening match of the tri-series will be played between Pakistan and Sri Lanka on October 18 at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium.
Pakistan and England will face each other on October 20 at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium.
The matches of the tri-series will be played in Rawalpindi and Lahore, while the final will be held on October 31 at the Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore.

W-15 World Tennis Women’s Championships continues

text:

PFF confirms final 14-member squad FOR FIFA U15 World Cup, Festival

The young Shaheens will depart for Baku from Islamabad on October 20, said a press release.

title: Ahsan offers Narowal Sports City as training centre for national hockey team
text:
Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal on Thursday called for concerted efforts to revive Pakistan’s hockey glory through youth engagement, private sector support and modern training facilities.
Ahsan offers Narowal Sports City as training centre for national hockey team
ISLAMABAD, Oct 15 (APP):Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal on Thursday called for concerted efforts to revive Pakistan’s hockey glory through youth engagement, private sector support and modern training facilities.
Addressing a signing ceremony marking a partnership between the Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF) and Vital Group to promote youth engagement and strengthen their association with the national hockey team, the minister said Pakistan had immense potential to regain its prominent position in international hockey.
Describing hockey as a symbol of national identity, he said talented young players should be encouraged to carry forward the legacy of Pakistan’s golden era and raise the national flag high at international competitions.
The minister underscored the importance of private sector patronage in promoting sports and supporting athletes, saying financial security would enable players to focus entirely on their performance rather than personal expenses.
“A player’s primary concern should be how to score the next goal rather than how to meet personal expenses,” he said.
Ahsan Iqbal stressed that excellence in modern sports required more than talent and physical ability, highlighting the growing role of sports science, technology and data-driven performance analysis.
Physical fitness, mental resilience, discipline and sustained concentration were also essential for success at the international level, he added.
Referring to leading athletes worldwide, he said their achievements were built on consistent practice, discipline and an unwavering focus on performance.
The minister also highlighted the vision behind establishing the National Sports City in Narowal, saying it offered international-standard infrastructure for 14 sports at one location to provide athletes with modern training facilities.
He offered the National Sports City in Narowal as a permanent training centre for the Pakistan national hockey team, reaffirming the government’s commitment to providing players with a conducive environment to improve their performance.
Describing the PHF-Vital Group partnership as an important step towards strengthening hockey and engaging young people in sports, Ahsan Iqbal expressed confidence that sustained collaboration among sports institutions, the private sector and young talent would help Pakistan rebuild its hockey legacy and restore its standing in international competitions.

title: From street cricket to state-of-the-art arenas: Islamabad’s sporting transformation
text:
Abdul Samad Tariq ISLAMABAD, Oct 18 (APP):For children turning neighborhood streets into cricket grounds, students seeking affordable sports facilities and young athletes striving to develop their talent, the Capital Development Authority’s (CDA) planned Rs952 million multi-sport arenas could open new avenues for recreation, training and competition across Islamabad. The projects reflect the authority’s efforts to expand the capital’s sports infrastructure and bring modern recreational facilities closer to residents. By developing …
From street cricket to state-of-the-art arenas: Islamabad’s sporting transformation
Abdul Samad Tariq
ISLAMABAD, Oct 18 (APP):For children turning neighborhood streets into cricket grounds, students seeking affordable sports facilities and young athletes striving to develop their talent, the Capital Development Authority’s (CDA) planned Rs952 million multi-sport arenas could open new avenues for recreation, training and competition across Islamabad.
The projects reflect the authority’s efforts to expand the capital’s sports infrastructure and bring modern recreational facilities closer to residents.
By developing complexes at three locations, the CDA aims to create more opportunities for people to participate in sports, pursue healthy lifestyles and develop their athletic potential.
The authority plans to establish multi-sport complexes in D-12/1, G-11/3 Markaz and F-8 Markaz. The proposed facilities include indoor swimming pools, gyms, futsal courts, cricket practice cages, padel courts, basketball facilities and multipurpose sports halls, offering a range of activities for sports enthusiasts and aspiring athletes.
The projects could also reduce the need for residents to travel across the city in search of suitable venues. For families, students and amateur players, access to facilities within their communities could make regular participation in sports more convenient.
A CDA spokesperson told APP that operational arrangements would be finalized after construction was completed and the facilities became operational. The authority has yet to announce the fee structure, concessions for students and registered sports clubs, or whether the complexes would be managed directly or through private operators.
These arrangements will be important in determining how residents use the facilities and how effectively the investment supports grassroots sports. Affordable memberships, transparent booking procedures and designated training sessions could help attract a wider range of users.
Existing facilities illustrate the range of costs involved in organized sports. Membership packages at the Pakistan Sports Complex, operated by the Pakistan Sports Board, have included registration charges ranging from Rs5,000 to Rs30,000 and monthly fees of Rs1,500 to Rs5,000, depending on the sport and package.
Commercial padel courts have reportedly charged around Rs2,000 an hour, while booking charges for some CDA-managed cricket grounds have reached approximately Rs15,000 a day for matches.
These rates vary by venue and booking category and do not indicate what the new complexes will charge. The proposed arenas will have their own operational requirements, including staffing, maintenance, utilities and safety arrangements, which will influence their long-term management.
A sports club owner, speaking on condition of anonymity said the new facilities could provide valuable training opportunities for local clubs if booking charges remained manageable.
“New multi-sport arenas sound good on paper, but if they end up with high membership or hourly rates, grassroots clubs will still be locked out,” the owner said, calling for subsidized training slots for registered clubs and youth academies.
The proposed complexes could also widen opportunities for girls and women to participate in physical activity. Convenient timings, reasonable fees, suitable facilities and effective safety arrangements would help make regular sports participation more accessible.
A female student said affordable facilities could encourage more girls to take part in sports, provided the venues offered convenient timings and a safe environment.
“Many girls would like to take part in sports, but access to suitable facilities, the cost of regular sessions and family commitments can become barriers. If these arenas offer affordable rates, convenient timings and appropriate facilities for women, more girls could benefit,” she said.
Residents have also welcomed the prospect of having sports facilities closer to their homes. Murad Khan, a resident of D-12, said the complex planned for his sector could provide local residents with a convenient alternative to travelling across the city or paying private-club rates, provided the facilities remained affordable.
According to available project details, the D-12/1 complex will cover approximately 4.2 acres at an estimated cost of Rs327 million.
The G-11/3 facility will occupy around 3.5 acres and cost Rs317 million, while the F-8 Markaz complex will cover about 3.2 acres at an estimated cost of Rs307 million to Rs308 million. The combined estimates amount to approximately Rs951 million to Rs952 million, making confirmation of the final approved allocation important.
The projects are to be financed through CDA resources and awarded through open competitive bidding. Construction is expected to take about a year after work begins, according to the project information available for this report.
Once completed, the complexes will require regular maintenance, trained staff, proper sanitation and effective safety procedures, particularly for swimming pools and specialized sports facilities.
Sustainable management will be essential to maintaining service standards while ensuring that the venues remain useful to local communities.
Student concessions, group booking options and designated training slots for registered clubs could further expand participation. Clear information about membership fees, opening hours and booking procedures would also help residents plan their use of the facilities.
The investment offers an opportunity to strengthen Islamabad’s recreational infrastructure while creating spaces for young people to develop their skills, build confidence and engage in healthy competition.
With effective management and accessible arrangements, the proposed arenas could become active community hubs that support grassroots sports and encourage a more physically active population.
Ultimately, the value of million investment will extend beyond the construction of courts, pools and sports halls. Its lasting contribution will depend on how effectively these facilities serve Islamabad’s residents and help nurture the next generation of sporting talent.

title: Peshawar school tragedy: When a mother’s morning kiss became a final goodbye
text:
Fakhar-e-Alam Peshawar , Oct 18 (APP)::Every morning, mothers send their children to school with a kiss, a prayer and the hope of seeing them return with stories of lessons learned and dreams taking shape. But for the families of 34 children killed in the collapse of Alkhair School in Peshawar’s Dir Colony, one ordinary Thursday morning shattered that promise forever. Among those who never returned home was 11-year-old Sanan Asad, …
Peshawar school tragedy: When a mother’s morning kiss became a final goodbye
Fakhar-e-Alam
Peshawar , Oct 18 (APP)::Every morning, mothers send their children to school with a kiss, a prayer and the hope of seeing them return with stories of lessons learned and dreams taking shape. But for the families of 34 children killed in the collapse of Alkhair School in Peshawar’s Dir Colony, one ordinary Thursday morning shattered that promise forever.
Among those who never returned home was 11-year-old Sanan Asad, whose dream of becoming a police officer ended beneath the rubble of a three-storey building that collapsed at around 8:45 a.m.
His schoolbag, books and uniform remain painful reminders of a future that will never unfold, while his mother struggles to comprehend the loss of a son she expected to see again within hours.
“Sanan was a very obedient son. I would call him just once in the morning for school and he would immediately say, ‘Okay, Mama,’” she told APP, tears rolling down her face. “He always dreamed of becoming a police officer and watched police movies that motivated him.”
The tragedy also claimed the lives of four of Sanan’s cousins: seven-year-olds Mubasshir Naeem, Amir Mangal and Haleema Haleem and eight-year-old Romaisa Ismail.
Their uncle, Tauseef Ahmad, rushed to the school after receiving news of the collapse. As he approached the building, he heard children crying beneath the rubble.
“I suddenly saw Sanan’s body being recovered by the rescue officials from the debris,” he recalled.
At the family hujra, relatives and neighbors now gather to offer condolences following the funeral prayers and Qul for the five children.
Yet their words cannot fill the silence that has descended on a home once alive with children’s laughter.
“The children who would laugh and scream, who would say, ‘We need this thing, I am going to school tomorrow,’ and ‘It is late and the school van arrives’ they are no longer alive,” Tauseef said.
“Their voices and their talk have ended forever.”
He recalled opening his window at night and finding the entire neighborhood unusually quiet. For Sanan’ s mother, ordinary household moments have become unbearable reminders of her loss.
Beyond the grief, the collapse has raised urgent questions about the safety of educational institutions across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
An initial police investigation identified the building’s age and poor construction quality as major factors. The preliminary report submitted by SSP Operations to the Capital City Police Officer, Peshawar, intensified concerns about structural inspections and enforcement of building standards.
Professor Dr Ibrahim Khan, former director of education, said the children had barely begun their lives.
“They had dreams in their eyes. Their parents sent them to school in the hope that education would give them a better future. Sadly, they went to school to receive education, not to lose their lives,” he told APP.
Questioning whether repeated incidents could continue to be treated as isolated accidents, he cited figures suggesting nearly 300 children had died in similar incidents over three years.
He questioned whether education officials were fulfilling their responsibilities to inspect school buildings, ensure children’ s safety and enforce the law, stressing that negligence and abuse of authority must have consequences where established.
Following the tragedy, the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Elementary and Secondary Education Department ordered immediate safety assessments, prioritizing schools identified as potentially dangerous through complaints, media reports and other credible sources.
Authorities have been directed to suspend classes immediately in buildings declared unsafe and relocate students to nearby schools or other secure locations. Classes may resume only after necessary repairs and certification by the relevant technical authority.
Districts have also been instructed to submit reports covering inspections, unsafe buildings, relocation arrangements and corrective measures by noon on October 21.
Education Adviser Dr Syed Amir Abdullah said a province-wide review had been launched. Private schools are to be assessed through district authorities, while unsafe public-school buildings will be repaired, vacated or closed as necessary.
The government has also announced financial assistance for bereaved families. Deputy Commissioner Peshawar Afaq Wazir distributed compensation cheques worth Rs21 million among families of the deceased children on the directives of Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi.
Families who traveled to their native districts for the burials will receive assistance upon their return, officials said.
The deputy commissioner also confirmed that the school owner had been arrested and an FIR registered.
For families like Sanan’ s, however, no compensation can measure the value of a child.
No cheque can restore a son who dreamed of wearing a police uniform and no official statement can bring back the laughter that once filled their home.
Pakistan has witnessed too many tragedies in which children have paid the ultimate price for negligence and failures of oversight.
Condolences are offered, inquiries ordered and promises made, but grieving parents must live with their loss long after public attention fades.
The Dir Colony tragedy must therefore become a turning point. Every public and private school in the province needs a credible structural safety assessment, verifiable safety certification and regular inspections.
Where negligence or criminal misconduct is established, accountability must follow without political or administrative pressure.
Sanan, Mubasshir, Amir, Haleema and Romaisa will never return to their classrooms. Their deaths must not become another statistic forgotten with time. Behind every inspection report is a child’s life, and behind every school gate is a parent’s trust.
