The decisions were taken at a Sindh cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah at the CM House in Karachi, according to a spokesperson.
The cabinet approved a series of reforms to the Sindh Public Service Commission (SPSC), including changes to the age limit, the number of attempts permitted and the minimum qualifying marks for the CCE.
Under the approved changes, candidates will be allowed to appear in the competitive examination up to five times instead of the existing three attempts. The upper age limit for appearing in the examination has also been raised by three years, from 30 to 33 years.
The provincial cabinet further approved reducing the minimum qualifying marks for CCE 2026 from 40% to 33%.
In another decision, the cabinet approved the introduction of computerised testing for examinations comprising a single paper, the spokesperson said.
During the meeting, CM Shah also briefed the cabinet on his recent visit to China, the spokesperson said.
The meeting also discussed 29 agenda items relating to various provincial departments, according to the chief minister's spokesperson.
Provincial ministers, advisers, special assistants, the chief secretary and other senior officials attended the meeting.

title: Govt urges opposition to hold talks on terrorism, advises PTI to come out of 'social media influence'
text:
Published October 20, 2026
Prime Minister's Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah on Tuesday urged the opposition to set aside its other demands and sit down with the government to discuss counterterrorism.
"Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is ready to invite all stakeholders to discuss this [terrorism]," he said while speaking during a Senate session.
Pakistan is facing the problem of terrorism, he said, adding that the Zarb-e-Azb operation had been launched through consensus.
He said the government was willing to hold talks with the opposition on the issue and called on opposition parties to reconsider their positions.
Sanaullah also referred to his interactions with Senate Opposition Leader Raja Nasir Abbas, saying he had suggested that Abbas meet the prime minister or visit the National Assembly speaker's office.
According to the senior PML-N leader, Abbas declined the suggestions, saying he would not meet the prime minister and did not recognise the speaker.
Comparing the cooperation of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan governments, he said that the latter was fully cooperating with the armed forces and the federal government.
Sanaullah said that the now-dysfunctional KP chief minister Sohail Afridi had repeatedly said he would not allow an operation in the province.
Separately, Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said that an 11-member consultative committee was working under the leadership of KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi.
Chaudhry blamed Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) stance for the decision to take emergency measures in KP, saying the move was taken due to the party's "Stubbornness".
The minister pledged that infiltration from Afghanistan would also be controlled effectively, saying any nexus between terrorists and elements hostile to Pakistan was unacceptable.
He said the federal government's efforts during negotiations with PTI had been aimed at reaching agreement on counterterrorism.
"Without effective cooperation at the provincial level, it was practically impossible to combat terrorism," Chaudhry said, alleging that the KP government had refused to cooperate with the federal government on its policy concerning Afghanistan.
Meanwhile, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said that voices within PTI were emerging in favour of pursuing politics rather than confrontation.
"If PTI engages in politics, it will have a lot of space," he said while speaking to Geo News at the Parliament House.
According to Asif, the Imran Khan-founded party would benefit if its leadership moved beyond the influence of social media.
Asked about remarks by other PML-N leaders concerning Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, Asif said he could not comment on their statements.
He added that he had criticised Fazl's strong remarks from a political perspective.

title: Pakistan, Qatar agree to deepen internal security cooperation
text:
Published October 20, 2026
Pakistan and Qatar have agreed to strengthen their security partnership and expand bilateral cooperation in internal security, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of Interior on Tuesday.
The two sides held detailed discussions on expanding cooperation in areas related to internal security, the ministry said in the statement.
Both ministers reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation between their respective interior ministries and agreed to enhance their partnership in internal security.
Naqvi said Pakistan and Qatar were working together for regional peace and stability, reaffirming Islamabad's commitment to working with Doha on matters of mutual interest, particularly those related to internal security and regional stability.
The Qatari interior minister said his country attached great importance to its relations with Pakistan.
The meeting took place a day after Naqvi addressed the 8th Global Security Forum in Doha, where he said Pakistan and Qatar had worked together to promote regional peace and stability.
Addressing the Global Security Forum in Doha on Monday, Naqvi said Pakistan had made every possible effort to bring Washington and Tehran to the negotiating table. He added that there were moments when tensions escalated sharply, but Islamabad did not give up its efforts.
His remarks come amid mounting regional tensions, as Yemen’s internationally recognised government forces continue to fight Houthi rebels, who are also targeting Saudi Arabia.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that Tehran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days remained on the table, but progress depended on Washington's response to Iran's conditions.
Against this backdrop, Naqvi praised Qatar's diplomatic efforts to mediate between the United States and Iran, saying Islamabad and Doha had worked together to prevent further escalation in the region.
"Peace cannot be achieved in a single meeting. It requires patience, trust and continuous efforts," Naqvi said, underscoring the need for sustained diplomatic engagement to resolve conflicts.

title: CDF Munir set to visit Tehran today amid stalled US-Iran talks: report
text:
Published October 20, 2026
Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff (COAS) Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir is due to visit Tehran on Tuesday (today), Reuters reported, citing a Pakistani official and Iranian media.
Pakistan has played a key mediating role between the US and Iran this year.
The scheduled visit follows earlier talks between CDF Munir and Iranian leaders in the summer that focused on measures to prevent further escalation, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and an expedited termination of the conflict.
Pakistan has taken on a mediator role in negotiations between Iran and the US aimed at ending the war which began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February.
The visit comes amid mounting regional tensions, as Yemen’s internationally recognised government forces continue to fight Houthi rebels, who are targeting Saudi Arabia.
A day earlier, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said achieving peace between the United States and Iran requires patience, trust and sustained efforts, stressing that lasting peace cannot be secured in a single meeting.
Addressing the Global Security Forum in Doha on Monday, Naqvi said Pakistan had made every possible effort to bring Washington and Tehran to the negotiating table. He added that there were moments when tensions escalated sharply, but Islamabad did not give up its efforts.
Efforts to revive US-Iran dialogue remain stalled, with both sides at odds over the terms for resuming negotiations.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that Tehran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days remained on the table, but progress depended on Washington's response to Iran's conditions.
Iran's demands include lifting the US blockade on its ports, easing sanctions on its oil exports and ending hostilities across regional fronts, while Washington wants Iran's nuclear programme addressed as a priority.
Against this backdrop, Naqvi praised Qatar's diplomatic efforts to mediate between the United States and Iran, saying Islamabad and Doha had worked together to prevent further escalation in the region.

title: PHC seeks AG's response on PTI petitions against KP emergency measures
text:
Published October 20, 2026
PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Tuesday issued a notice to the attorney general on Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) petitions challenging governor's rule and the imposition of an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
A two-member bench comprising Justice Ijaz Anwar and Justice Faheem Wali presided over the hearing on petitions filed by PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan and Advocate Salman Khan, asking the court to declare the measures unconstitutional and set them aside.
The Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N)-led federal government imposed a governor's role and emergency in KP, ruled by the Imran Khan-founded party since 2013, on October 11.
The federal government cited rising terrorism incidents and the provincial government's lack of support for counterterrorism operations as the reasons for the move.
KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi took charge of running the province on behalf of the federal government, assisted by an 11-member technocratic KP Advisory Council.
The PTI chairman and Advocate Salman Khan later filed separate petitions against the measures at the PHC, asking the court to declare the measures unconstitutional and set them aside.
During today's hearing, the PTI chief said that governor's rule and the emergency had been imposed on the same day, alongside the formation of an advisory council and the transfer of 38 deputy commissioners.
The PTI chairman further alleged that 12 of the party's members of the National Assembly and 13 members of the provincial assembly had been abducted.
"Our offices have been demolished, and plaques marking the inauguration of development projects have been broken," he said, alleging that his party was being treated differently from others.
Prior to Barrister Gohar, the petitioners' counsel argued that an emergency could be imposed in the event of war or external interference.
"There is neither war nor external aggression here," the lawyer told the court.
The counsel argued that the provincial government had the authority to take measures to tackle terrorism, saying terrorism had reached its peak in the past, but an emergency was not imposed then.
The lawyer further contended that Article 234 of the Constitution could be invoked only when a provincial government ceased to function.
The counsel maintained that the provincial assembly and government had continued functioning and that there had been no breakdown of the Constitution.
After hearing the arguments, Justice Anwar said the court would issue a notice to the Attorney General's Office and seek its response.
The court subsequently issued the notice and adjourned the hearing until 10 November.
Separately, the court sought responses from the government and relevant authorities on petitions seeking the recovery of now-dysfunctional KP chief minister Sohail Afridi, Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati and PTI provincial president Junaid Akbar.
During a hearing on a petition filed for the recovery of Afridi, Justice Arshad Ali issued notices to the provincial government, police and relevant officials, directing them to submit their response within two days.
A two-member bench comprising Justice Arshad Ali and Justice Farah Jamshed heard the petitions regarding the recovery of Swati and Akbar.
The court issued notices to the government, the KP inspector general of police and other relevant authorities, seeking their responses to the petitions within 10 days.

title: Multan employer arrested for allegedly chasing, running over 15-year-old orphan
text:
Published October 20, 2026
MULTAN: A 15-year-old boy was allegedly chased and run over by a man in a car at a private housing society in Multan after leaving work at the suspect’s house, police said, adding that the suspect had been arrested and a murder case registered.
The victim, identified as Waseem, lived at an orphanage run by a non-governmental organisation (NGO). Multan City Police Officer Akhtar Farooq said the orphanage administration had sent him to the suspect, identified as Tauqeer, seven days earlier to learn a trade.
Tauqeer, who undertook electrical work at various buildings, was teaching the boy to become an electrician, the police officer said.
According to police, the boy left the work, prompting the suspect to pursue him in his car. CCTV footage reportedly shows the teenager running away before the car strikes him.
Police said initial investigations had found no evidence that the boy had committed theft.
Police have detained some members of the orphanage administration for questioning as part of the investigation.
Farooq said children from the orphanage had previously been sent to the suspect for vocational training. Investigators are examining the circumstances in which Waseem was sent to work with him and the events leading to his death.
The murder case was registered with the police as complainant, the city police officer said.
Waseem was originally from Muzaffargarh. His body was taken there by his uncle and maternal uncle after the incident.
His funeral prayer was held in the village of Daultpur and he was buried in the local ancestral graveyard. Only close relatives and orphanage officials attended the funeral, according to the available reports.
The funeral was held promptly because of the condition of the body, the reports said.
Police said the investigation was continuing.
Sharing details, Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari said Waseem had been living at the Dar-ul-Khuda orphanage for six years before being handed over to contractor Tauqeer a week ago to learn electrical work.
She said Waseem was mistreated at the workplace on November 19 and fled. Tauqeer and his associate Amjad allegedly chased him in a car for around one kilometre before running him over, killing him.
Bokhari said Tauqeer had been arrested and the vehicle seized, while police were conducting raids in Faisalabad to arrest Amjad.
“Women and children are Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif’s red line. Such crimes will not be tolerated under any circumstances in Punjab,” she said.
FIR No. 990/2026 has been registered under Sections 302 and 34 of the Pakistan Penal Code, with police as the complainant. The arrested suspect has been remanded for five days, she added.
The minister said the prosecution was working with police to build a strong case, while Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz was personally overseeing the matter and had directed authorities to ensure justice “at all costs”.
Bokhari said the SP Cantt had met Waseem’s family in Muzaffargarh, assured them of assistance and provided financial support.

title: Senate passes bill letting ex-lawmakers keep blue passports without serving full term
text:
Published October 20, 2026
ISLAMABAD: The Senate on Monday approved a bill allowing former lawmakers to retain their official blue passports even if they served only part of a parliamentary term, while a separate proposal to extend the privilege to their dependent children under 28 was withdrawn following opposition from treasury members.
According to the details, the approved amendment to the Passports Act, 1974, would cover former members of the National Assembly (NA) and Senate who took the oath of office but left before completing a full term.
The measure, however, must still clear the NA before it can become law.
Official blue passports are issued to designated constitutional office-holders, government and judicial officials, senior bureaucrats and their eligible dependents. They provide visa-free access to 55 countries, including 22 in Europe, according to the report.
Both bills were moved by Senator Abdul Qadir. The approved legislation proposes inserting a new Section 3-A into the Passports Act, allowing a former parliamentarian to retain and use a gratis official passport after leaving office, whether they served a full term or completed only the remainder of another member’s tenure.
Under the existing rules, National Assembly members become eligible for blue passports after taking the oath, while senators must complete their six-year term to qualify. The amendment seeks to remove that disparity by allowing former lawmakers from either House to retain their official passports even if they leave office before completing a full term.
The proposed provision states that “a retired parliamentarian who has taken oath as a Member of the National Assembly (MNA) or the Senate, whether for a full term or for the remainder of the term of another member, shall, on such terms and conditions as may be prescribed, be entitled to retain and use the gratis official (blue) passport issued to him or her after ceasing to hold office”.
The change would cover lawmakers who leave the NA before completing five years or the Senate before completing six years. Under the existing Passport Rules 2021, former parliamentarians qualify for blue passports if they have served at least one full term in either House.
The bill’s statement of objects and reasons says the amendment “brings parity with the privileges available to other high-ranking officials and ensures uniform treatment of persons who have served the state at the highest level”.
The Senate also withdrew a separate bill proposing blue passports for former lawmakers’ spouses and dependent children under 28 after treasury members opposed the measure.
The proposed amendment to Section 12 of the Members of Parliament (Salaries and Allowances) Act, 1974, stated that “an ex-member, the spouse of the ex-member and the dependent children of the ex-member below the age of 28 years shall be entitled to a gratis official (blue) passport”.
The proposal had been approved by the relevant Senate committee in July, drawing criticism over the extension of an official travel privilege to family members. Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry had subsequently said steps would be taken to ensure the documents were used for “only official duties” abroad and issued for limited periods in most cases.
Addressing the Senate on Monday, Chaudhry said the number of official blue passports issued in Pakistan had fallen from 75,000 to 45,000 after European countries and Canada raised concerns. He said around 30,000 unnecessary or inactive passports had been cancelled.
“Security and dignity of passport is a matter of the dignity of people of Pakistan,” he said, adding that Pakistan had agreements with other countries concerning blue and red passports.
Chaudhry said the government had no objection to parliamentarians receiving blue passports but was concerned about extending the facility to their families. A large number of such passports, he said, could make other countries reluctant to offer visa-free access.
He also said the government would soon introduce legislation to withdraw the blue-passport facility available to children of retired bureaucrats.
Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar called for tighter regulation, stressing that official passports were intended for government business.
“Let children make their own careers; respect is not built through blue passports,” he said.
Tarar also called for the removal of the six-year service requirement for senators to qualify for official passports, arguing that the rules should be consistent across both Houses. NA members become eligible after taking the oath, whereas senators must complete their full six-year term. Under the existing arrangement, a senator who resigns shortly before the end of the term may lose eligibility.
PML-N Senator Abid Sher Ali, meanwhile, criticised the requirement for parliamentarians to obtain a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the interior ministry before being issued blue passports. He said the condition had not previously applied and described it as a breach of privilege.
“Are we dacoits or terrorists that we need NOCs?” he said, announcing plans to move a privilege motion.
The Senate also saw a confrontation between opposition and treasury members over the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP).
Leader of the Opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas denounced the measures as an “assault on the people’s mandate”.
“You robbed the people’s votes. Your own minister said the system has collapsed,” he said, referring to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s earlier remarks that the country’s governance system required a reset.
Speaking at the Pakistan Economic Summit in July, Naqvi had said the existing “system” had “collapsed” and was fundamentally incapable of resolving the country’s problems.
Abbas described the measures in KP as “sheer oppression” and said they could have been avoided. He also warned the government against pushing people to the wall.
“You snatched the mandate from Bengalis, and they separated. You have still not learned,” he said.
The opposition leader also called for a parliamentary briefing on Yemen, recalling that Parliament had passed a resolution in 2015 against Pakistan becoming part of the conflict. He said he had written to the prime minister and foreign minister, urging them to pursue mediation rather than involvement in the war.
“This is a sensitive issue. Countries are economically devastated, and we are going to be part of another war,” he said.
Responding to the criticism, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry defended the measures, saying the president had imposed emergency and governor's rule under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, and the Senate and the National Assembly subsequently ratified them.
“All steps have been taken in the interest of peace, stability and national interest,” Chaudhry said.
The bills will now follow separate paths, with the blue-passport amendment requiring approval from the National Assembly before it can become law. The Senate debate also saw opposition criticism of the governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and calls for Pakistan to pursue mediation over the conflict in Yemen.

title: NAB summons KP lawmaker, four others in suspected corruption inquiry
text:
Published October 20, 2026
PESHAWAR: The National Accountability Bureau (NAB) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has issued five notices in an inquiry into alleged assets beyond known sources of income and suspected corruption involving provincial lawmaker Dr Amjad Ali and others, directing him to appear before the bureau in Peshawar today (Tuesday).
Ali, a member of the provincial assembly and special assistant to the chief minister on housing, has been asked to appear at NAB’s Hayatabad office in Peshawar. The bureau said it had initiated the inquiry after receiving a complaint.
Besides Ali, NAB has summoned four people — Bacha Syed, Muhammad Arif Shah, Siraj Ahmad and Naveed Ahmad — as witnesses. They have been directed to appear before the bureau between October 20 and 22.
The bureau has sought property records from various housing societies, including details of allotments, ownership and payments. It has also asked the Accountant General of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to provide records of Ali’s salary, allowances, benefits and travel expenses.
In its summons, NAB warned that failure to comply with the notices could lead to legal action.
The inquiry comes against the backdrop of earlier court proceedings involving Ali. In March 2026, the Peshawar High Court directed NAB not to harass him in connection with an assets case and disposed of his writ petition.
During the hearing, Ali’s counsel, Bashir Wazir, told a two-member bench that his client had already provided records relating to his assets to the bureau. He argued that NAB had issued another notice despite earlier court directions restricting repeated summonses, which he said amounted to harassment.
NAB special prosecutor Arbab Kaleemullah told the court that no call-up notice had been issued to Ali himself at that time. Instead, a female relative and a close associate had been summoned as witnesses.
The prosecutor said certain assets held in their names allegedly belonged to Ali but had not been declared.
The bench, comprising Justice Syed Arshad Ali and Justice Qazi Jawad Ehsanullah, directed NAB to proceed strictly in accordance with the law and refrain from harassing the petitioner. It also observed that Ali could file an appropriate application if he felt he was being harassed.

title: IBA Karachi, AKU, Habib University join hands to advance AI-driven teaching, learning
text:
Published October 19, 2026
The Institute of Business Administration (IBA) Karachi, Aga Khan University and Habib University (HU) have joined hands to advance AI-driven teaching and learning through academic collaboration and innovation.
IBA Karachi, in collaboration with AKU and HU, hosted the Annual Teaching and Learning Symposium 2026 at IBA's Main Campus.
Themed "AI in Pedagogy", the symposium brought together academic leaders, educators, researchers and teaching professionals from Karachi, across Pakistan and internationally to explore the opportunities and challenges artificial intelligence presents for higher education.
In her welcome remarks, IBA Karachi Office of Academic Quality and Excellence Director and Conference Chair Dr Sana Tauseef emphasised the importance of institutional collaboration in addressing AI's impact on education and acknowledged the leadership of all three universities.
AKU Institute for Educational Development Dean Dr Farid Panjwani described the symposium as a significant milestone in advancing teaching and learning through collective efforts.
A leadership panel, titled "Teaching for Today and Tomorrow: What Should Universities Stop, Start, and Continue in the AI Era," was moderated by IBA Karachi Executive Director Dr S Akbar Zaidi.
It featured AKU President Dr Sulaiman Shahabuddin; Habib University President Wasif Rizvi, Durbeen CEO Salma Aslam, and Beaconhouse National University Vice Chancellor Dr Moeed W Yusuf.
A key highlight of the symposium was the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between IBA Karachi, AKU and HU, reaffirming the three institutions' shared commitment to academic collaboration and innovation in teaching and learning.
The keynote address, titled "Critical Thinking and Agency in the Age of AI: Time to Re-think Higher Education?", was delivered by Norway's University of Oslo Professor Dr Fazilat Siddiq.
She highlighted the importance of critical thinking, learner agency, and technological, pedagogical and content knowledge in higher education.
The symposium also featured interactive sessions, an EdTech Innovation Showcase, Visual Voices and a student performance.
The event concluded with an awards ceremony and closing remarks by AKU Quality, Teaching and Learning Vice Provost Dr Jane Rarieya and HU Vice President for Academic Affairs Dr Mohammad Shahid Shaikh, who reaffirmed the importance of academic collaboration in advancing higher education.

title: CDF Munir, new Saudi envoy stress stronger defence ties, strategic coordination
text:
Published October 19, 2026
ISLAMABAD: Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff (COAS) Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir and Saudi Arabia's newly appointed ambassador to Pakistan Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy have stressed the need to strengthen defence collaboration and strategic coordination between the two countries.
The two held a meeting at the General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi on Monday, where they discussed matters of mutual interest and regional security dynamics, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.
Both sides expressed satisfaction over progress made under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), underscoring the importance of strengthening defence cooperation and institutional linkages.
Field Marshal Munir congratulated Albugamy on his appointment and expressed confidence that his tenure would further strengthen the longstanding ties between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.
The military's media wing said the relationship between Islamabad and Riyadh is rooted in shared faith, mutual trust and strategic partnership.
The meeting comes a day after ISPR Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said the MJDA's collective deterrence could come into play if diplomatic efforts failed and the regional crisis escalated into military conflict.
In an interview with Independent Arabia on Sunday, the top military spokesperson described the alliance as defensive in nature and said it was not directed against any particular country.
He warned that a failure to reach a negotiated outcome could lead to military confrontation, stressing that expanding the conflict in the Middle East was not in the interest of any country.
The ISPR chief also called for regional states to resolve their differences through dialogue rather than fighting one another.
He said Saudi Arabia's sovereignty and territorial integrity remained a foremost priority for Pakistan, adding that protecting Islam's two holiest sites was equally important.
Lt Gen Chaudhry said Pakistan's position had been conveyed through the country's political and military leadership.
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the MJDA on August 7 during the Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence. Under the agreement, an armed attack against any one of the three signatories is to be regarded as an attack against all three, establishing a mutual-defence commitment.
The ISPR chief said the agreement had advanced significantly in a short period and reflected the combined thinking of the three countries. He also emphasised that the Makkah alliance aimed to promote regional peace, stability and security.

title: US-Iran peace efforts require patience, trust and continuous engagement: security czar
text:
Published October 19, 2026
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has said achieving peace between the United States and Iran requires patience, trust and sustained efforts, stressing that lasting peace cannot be secured in a single meeting.
Addressing the Global Security Forum in Doha on Monday, Naqvi said Pakistan had made every possible effort to bring Washington and Tehran to the negotiating table. He added that there were moments when tensions escalated sharply, but Islamabad did not give up its efforts.
His remarks come amid mounting regional tensions, as Yemen’s internationally recognised government forces continue to fight Houthi rebels, who are also targeting Saudi Arabia.
The kingdom reported intercepting four drones on Saturday, followed by further interceptions on Sunday, amid repeated Houthi attacks.
Meanwhile, efforts to revive US-Iran dialogue remain stalled, with both sides at odds over the terms for resuming negotiations.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that Tehran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days remained on the table, but progress depended on Washington's response to Iran's conditions.
Iran's demands include lifting the US blockade on its ports, easing sanctions on its oil exports and ending hostilities across regional fronts, while Washington wants Iran's nuclear programme addressed as a priority.
Against this backdrop, Naqvi praised Qatar's diplomatic efforts to mediate between the United States and Iran, saying Islamabad and Doha had worked together to prevent further escalation in the region.
"Peace cannot be achieved in a single meeting. It requires patience, trust and continuous efforts," Naqvi said, underscoring the need for sustained diplomatic engagement to resolve conflicts.
The interior minister also said Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani had worked for more than 16 hours without a break during the Swiss peace talks.
Naqvi cited the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), involving Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, as an example of Islamabad's commitment to regional security, emphasising that the pact was intended to promote peace rather than war.
The security czar's statement came a day after Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry warned that the MJDA's collective deterrence could come into play if negotiations failed and the regional crisis escalated into military conflict.
In an interview with Independent Arabia aired on Sunday, he described the alliance as defensive in nature and said it was not directed against any particular country.
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the MJDA on August 7 during the Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence.
Under the agreement, an armed attack against any one of the three signatories is to be regarded as an attack against all three, establishing a mutual-defence commitment among the countries.

title: PM Shehbaz vows to promote quality education through AI initiatives
text:
Published October 19, 2026
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday said the government would provide all possible resources and facilities to Daanish schools, reaffirming its commitment to ensuring quality education and creating new opportunities for students, teachers and the younger generation across the country through artificial intelligence (AI).
Addressing a memorandum of understanding (MoU) signing ceremony between the Ministry of Education and Gauth AI, the prime minister termed the agreement a significant step towards expanding educational opportunities and welcomed the provision of free subscriptions by the technology company.
He said the first 4,000 subscriptions being gifted by Gauth to Pakistan would help students and teachers benefit from modern educational tools. Of these, 1,000 subscriptions would be allocated to teachers associated with the government’s Daanish schools initiative.
The prime minister said the government had provided all possible facilities to students, adding that Daanish schools were a magnificent educational institution offering free education.
“There is no dearth of resources, and the government will provide all possible resources to the Daanish schools,” he said, reiterating the government’s resolve to support the institutions and their students.
Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja said the initiative reflected the prime minister’s vision of promoting information technology-led development and improving the education sector through modern digital solutions.
She said TikTok had made its AI technology available for Pakistan, while the paid versions of Gauth AI were being launched in Pakistan, making it the first country after the United States to receive this facility.
Regional Director of Global Public Policy at ByteDance Ltd Maria Kohan said technology had the potential to inspire creativity, unlock opportunities and transform lives, particularly in the field of education.
She said ByteDance had already been contributing to educational awareness through TikTok, adding that its dedicated STEM feed, launched in Pakistan in partnership with the Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication and the Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training, was helping young people explore educational content in new ways.
She said the launch of Gauth in Pakistan marked another step in the company’s commitment to supporting education through technology.
Gauth is an AI-powered study platform designed to make learning easier, more interactive and accessible. It offers step-by-step explanations, personalised AI tutoring and interactive study tools to help students understand concepts rather than merely find answers.
She said Gauth was already serving more than 200 million users globally and the company was pleased to bring the platform to Pakistan’s young people.
She said the subscriptions would provide access to AI-powered tools to support teaching and improve students’ learning experiences.
In addition, Gauth would provide 180 free subscriptions for local students, she added.

title: Karachi temperature expected to remain above normal in November: Met Office
text:
Published October 19, 2026
KARACHI: Hot and dry weather is expected to persist in Karachi until Friday, with the intensity of the heat likely to remain high and temperatures potentially reaching 38°C during the period, the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) said in a statement on Monday.
According to the Met Office, temperatures in the city may rise to 38°C by Friday, while the mercury is expected to settle between 34°C and 36°C after Friday, indicating that daytime temperatures will remain relatively high even as the weather pattern changes.
The department said cooler nights had already begun in Karachi, with night-time temperatures expected to fall to around 22°C in the coming days, although the overall temperature pattern is likely to remain warmer than normal.
The PMD also forecast above-normal temperatures in Karachi during November, saying daytime temperatures could range between 33°C and 35°C, while night-time readings are expected to remain between 19°C and 22°C throughout the month.
The normal daytime temperature for Karachi in November is 32.6°C, while the usual night-time temperature is 17.7°C. The forecast suggests that both daytime and night-time temperatures may remain above these monthly averages.

title: DPM Dar arrives in Tajikistan to lead Pakistan's delegation at SCO moot
text:
Published October 19, 2026
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar arrived in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, to lead Pakistan’s delegation at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Council of Heads of Government meeting, scheduled for October 19–20.
Upon arrival, DPM Dar was received by Tajikistan’s Minister of Energy and Water Resources, Daler Juma, who is also co-chair of the Pakistan–Tajikistan Joint Commission, the Foreign Office (FO) said in a statement on Monday.
Pakistan’s Ambassador to Tajikistan, Irfan Ahmed, and the country’s National Coordinator for the SCO, Khalil Hashmi, along with senior Tajik government officials, were also present to receive him.
Besides participating in the proceedings of the meeting, DPM Dar will meet Tajikistan’s leadership and his counterparts from SCO member states on the sidelines of the summit, a statement from the Foreign Office said.
Dar will lead Pakistan’s delegation to the meeting at the invitation of Tajikistan Prime Minister Qohir Rasulzoda.
The prime ministers of Belarus, China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan, along with the vice president of Iran and India’s external affairs minister, will represent their respective countries at the CHG meeting.
The Council of Heads of Government is the SCO’s second-highest decision-making institution and provides guidance on a range of areas, including the economy, finance, trade, connectivity, commerce, socio-economic cooperation and the organisation’s budgetary matters.
The meeting will also adopt a joint communique, statements and important decisions.
During his visit, Dar will call on the president and prime minister of Tajikistan. He will also hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from SCO member states on the sidelines of the CHG meeting, the FO added.
Meanwhile, DPM Dar met Tajikistan Prime Minister Qohir Rasulzoda as the two leaders reviewed bilateral relations and reaffirmed commitment to further strengthening cooperation in multiple sectors.
In a post on X, the FO spokesperson said that the Tajik prime minister appreciated Pakistan’s mediation efforts in the US-Iran conflict.
The DPM reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to working closely with Tajikistan to promote peace and advance regional economic integration.
DPM Dar and the Tajik premier reviewed bilateral relations and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation in trade, investment, energy, connectivity, defence and culture, as well as promoting people-to-people exchanges.
They also underscored the importance of cooperation on climate change and water security.
Highlighting Pakistan’s expertise in disaster management, the deputy prime minister underscored the potential for cooperation with Tajikistan through the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA).

title: Pakistan may review military help to Yemen if requested, says ISPR chief amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
text:
Published October 19, 2026
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has said Pakistan may “evaluate” any request for direct military support from Yemen’s internationally recognised government, as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia continue.
"I think not in my knowledge that there has been any formal request. If there is any request, then that is for the government of Pakistan to evaluate that and respond to that," he said in an interview with Independent Arabia on Sunday, when asked whether Yemen's government had sought support from Pakistan.
The ISPR chief warned that the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement's (MJDA) collective deterrence could come into play if negotiations fail and military confrontation follows in the Middle East.
"If we are unable to come to a negotiated outcome and we turn into a military conflict, then this instrument of collective deterrence of the Makkah alliance will definitely come into play, as it is coming into play," Lt Gen Chaudhry said.
The MJDA between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye advanced significantly in a short period, he said, adding that the pact represented the combined thinking of the three countries.
The regional powers signed the MJDA on August 7 during the Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence. Under the pact, an armed attack against any one of the three countries would be regarded as an attack against all three.
Lt Gen Chaudhry said that Saudi Arabia's sovereignty and territorial integrity remained a foremost priority for Pakistan, adding that the protection of Islam's two holiest sites was equally important.
Reiterating that Pakistan's position was clear and unequivocal, he said that Islamabad's message had already been conveyed through the country's political and military leadership.
The military spokesperson's remarks come as fighting between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis, who control the capital Sanaa and much of the north, has escalated in recent weeks, becoming another front in the US-Israeli war on Iran.
The Houthis have in recent days attacked Riyadh's international airport, Makkah and Madina amid renewed fighting in the region.
The group's advances also threaten the strategic Bab el-Mandeb oil shipping route, following the collapse of a truce.
According to Lt Gen Chaudhry, the Houthi attacks on Islam's holiest sites had caused deep grief and anger among the public and the political and military leadership.
On the regional security situation, Lt Gen Chaudhry warned that escalating military tensions would benefit no country, saying that expanding the military conflict in the Middle East was not in anyone's interest and stressed the need to reach a negotiated settlement.
He said the MJDA's leadership and course of action were clear, emphasising that it had no aggressive intentions and was not directed against any particular country.
Lt Gen Chaudhry also called for unity among Muslims, saying countries in the region needed to work towards resolving their differences rather than fighting one another.
He reiterated that the Makkah alliance aimed to promote peace, stability and security across the region, adding that disputes should be resolved through negotiations rather than military escalation.
— With additional input from Reuters.

title: Dead phone, drained account: How biometric fraud caught two MNAs
text:
Published October 19, 2026
On January 12, when Farhan Chishti landed at Islamabad airport in the afternoon, the MQM MNA’s phone was dead. He could neither call nor receive a message. He thought there might be a network failure, but when it did not restore for many hours, he went to a service centre of the cellular company to report the problem.
There he learnt that a duplicate SIM, which he had never requested, had been issued against his number, disabling his original connection. Staff told him it had been issued in Karachi’s Malir area. Disabling it was possible only from the company’s headquarters, which was closed for the day and would reopen in the morning, he was told.
By then, the damage was already underway. The person holding his number had registered Chishti for online banking, although he had never used electronic channels. The same person raised his withdrawal limit, set the password “Saeen Sarkar,” and moved Rs1.5 million out of his account to that of one Sakina Bibi, herself a victim whose account had been opened without her knowledge, and to other accounts opened in the names of women in South Punjab and Sindh.
Chishti complained to the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA). Investigators questioned the owner of the point of sale in Khokhrapar (Malir), who said a man had approached him claiming his mother, who needed a duplicate SIM, was too weak to leave the car, and asked for the biometric device to take her thumbprint there. How they obtained Chishti’s thumbprint remains unexplained. The man who used the duplicate SIM was from Nawabshah.
Investigators believe bad actors harvest biometrics in bulk from leaked data or from places where fingerprints are not mandatory for routine services, then load them onto software and misuse them.
The case went to the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA), which fined the cellular company Rs77.8 million. The company argued that a third party had deceived the retailer. The PTA rejected this, citing Regulation 4(4) of the Subscribers Regulations, under which any SIM sold by any means is the operator’s sole responsibility. It found failures in monitoring, said the company’s later remedial steps did not cure the initial lapse, and noted that similar violations keep surfacing despite repeated instructions.
Chishti is not alone. Another MNA, Shaharyar Mahar, lost Rs2 million in another episode. Karachi businessman Sunny Kumar also fell victim. A duplicate SIM was issued in his name on September 29, 2025, at a retail outlet in Dhabeji, Thatta. Incidentally, Kumar and Chishti are customers of the same cellular company. As much as Rs8.5 million was taken from Kumar’s account.
The investigation into the case revealed an insider at the bank. A branch service officer in Mardan had viewed Kumar’s account before the SIM was issued. The same officer had accessed around 30 accounts, after which funds were withdrawn or restrictions applied, with suspected fraud of about Rs25 million.
He first said he was helping a friend with a balance inquiry, then admitted sharing customers’ details with that friend, saying he was under pressure. Phone records showed him also seeking customer data from an employee of another bank, and offering payment to a Nadra employee, who later refused to provide the information.
A PTA order in this case imposed the same Rs77.8 million fine in Kumar’s case. Kumar recovered his money from the bank. A source privy to the details said a similar pattern, including the involvement of bank insiders, was observed in the other two cases, but the investigation did not proceed because the complainants were keen only on recovering their stolen funds. This is not limited to these three cases. Such incidents have also occurred in other provinces as well.
While the telecom company was penalised in both cases, the only action against the banks was an order to return the victims’ money.
Originally published in The News

title: France to impose new curfews where necessary: PM
text:
Published October 20, 2026
PARIS: France will impose new curfews in areas where needed on Tuesday, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said, adding that the measures introduced in several cities the previous day had "helped keep the night calm".
France was rocked on Saturday by some of its worst rioting in recent years, just six months before the country elects a successor to President Emmanuel Macron.
Accused of failing to anticipate and contain the street violence, the government has pledged to restore order, and had announced partial curfews in Paris and some other cities on Monday.
"Targeted curfews have contributed to calm overnight," Lecornu wrote on X.
"Tonight new curfews will be decided where the situation requires it. These decisions will be made on the ground, by the prefects, in coordination with the mayors," he said.
Police confirmed the night had passed without major incidents across France.
Several cities, including Paris, the southwestern city of Bordeaux and Nice on the French Riviera, introduced partial curfews on Monday in response to urban unrest that followed weeks of student demonstrations over poor learning conditions in high schools.
While some restrictions, such as those in Paris, initially applied only for the night from Monday to Tuesday, others, particularly in Bordeaux and Nice, were set to remain in force for several days.
During the night, a helicopter flew over the French capital's Place de la Republique, one of the epicentres of the unrest, sweeping a powerful searchlight across the square to monitor compliance with the curfew.
In Lyon, despite a ban on demonstrations, around 500 people gathered on Monday evening outside the tourism office that was set on fire, to show support for shopkeepers affected by looting, according to organisers.
The word "LYON" had been spelled out on the ground with candles.
A banner hung on a fence nearby read "Anti-Rioters Lyon" and "Doucet Resign", referring to Green mayor Gregory Doucet, an AFP journalist said.
Under pressure, the government scheduled another series of emergency meetings on Tuesday, including talks involving representatives of major social media platforms.
Finance Minister Roland Lescure pledged support measures for shopkeepers and craftspeople.
Patrick Martin, the head of France's Medef business lobby group, on Tuesday accused the state of having "failed" during the urban unrest that hit at least 3,000 businesses, according to preliminary estimates.

title: Rubio kicks off India visit with trade deal, Russian oil on agenda
text:
Published October 20, 2026
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in India on Tuesday, days after President Donald Trump delayed tariffs on US imports from the world's largest democracy as the two countries seek to finalise a trade deal.
During his two-day visit to the western cities of Mumbai and Jamnagar, Rubio is set to meet government and business leaders.
These include Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar and billionaire Mukesh Ambani, chairman of Reliance Industries, which runs the world's largest refining complex at Jamnagar.
Rubio landed in the financial capital of Mumbai, where he will meet Jaishankar later in the day.
In recent days, Rubio and other officials have said a comprehensive trade deal between the two nations is almost complete, raising the possibility that it could be signed during his visit.
Trump removed one potential stumbling block last Friday when he waived potential tariffs that would have punished New Delhi for the nation's extensive Russian crude oil purchases.
Under legislation signed by Trump in September, the administration is authorised to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top five importers of Russian oil, which would include India, which is number two on that list after China.
Trump's decision to waive all substantive provisions of that bill has upset both Democrats and Republicans who have pushed him to up economic pressure on Moscow for its war with Ukraine.
Rubio has said in recent days that the effort to finalise a trade deal was a factor in the decision to waive those tariffs. He also said that India has been diversifying its import mix away from Russian crude, even as it still buys millions of barrels of Russian oil every day.
He said the administration was entering a 60-day review period, during which it would consider which new tariffs, if any, to enact.
"You've got countries like India, for example, that have voluntarily diversified their energy portfolio, but are still getting a substantial amount of energy from Russia because it's hard to pivot from one day to the next," Rubio said on Sunday. "But they're also an important ally and partner of the United States."
While the Trump administration has in the past pressed India to cut Russian oil imports, the US signed a deal with Russia last week to import diesel to bring down domestic fuel prices before the midterm elections, making it unclear to what extent that remains a foreign policy priority.
"Every country has a complex set of factors that they have to take into account," Rubio told reporters on Monday when asked about India's Russian oil purchases. "Geography is real. For some countries, it's very difficult to acquire energy from alternative sources."
India imports more than 85% of its crude oil requirements to help power its fast-growing economy.
Rubio is slated to fly into Mumbai from Samarkand, Uzbekistan, where he was meeting with Central Asian political and business leaders.

title: Declared dead: Indian voters fight to get back on electoral rolls
text:
Published October 20, 2026
Kamta Prasad has been shuttling between government offices in Delhi trying to prove he is not dead.
The 53-year-old tailor is among 130 million names removed from India's electoral rolls under a voter roll revision that has sparked mass protests and posed the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.
The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has led to removals for reasons ranging from "logical discrepancies" to people being recorded as dead, leaving many such as Prasad struggling to get more than just their voting status restored.
He has had to forgo his daily wage of 250 rupees ($2.63) that supports his family of four to scurry around the city to reverse the error.
"I panicked when I heard about it," said Prasad, who is among 4.2 million Delhi voters struck off the list, according to the draft rolls published by the poll body on August 31. "Since then I've been going everywhere to prove that I'm alive."
The deletions have triggered a political storm, with opposition parties and youth groups staging near-daily protests in New Delhi and elsewhere, which have been met with force by the police.
They allege Election Commission chief Gyanesh Kumar manipulated the revision to benefit Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party, a charge denied by both the commission and the BJP.
According to Rajendra Kumar, a volunteer with non-profit Jan Sarokar, about 2,000 of the roughly 9,000 voters in Prasad's block were struck off after the revision, classified as absent, shifted, deceased or registered elsewhere.
Prasad is the only person in this block who has been declared dead but several similar cases have been reported by local media across the country.
The Election Commission has said it was removing duplicate, deceased, shifted and otherwise ineligible voters and that anyone excluded in error can file claims, submit supporting documents and pursue appeals before the rolls are finalised.
For voters such as Prasad, however, exclusion leads to a bureaucratic maze, and depending on the circumstances they may have to provide proof of life, establish residency, correct alleged discrepancies or submit fresh documentation.
That involves repeated visits to election offices, hearings before electoral officials and multiple rounds of appeals, with some spending weeks or months trying to restore their names.
"I told them I voted in the last assembly and general elections and have been voting for 35 years, but nobody listens," Prasad said.
India's Election Commission did not reply to a request for comment for this story.
Following weeks of protests, the Election Commission ordered fresh verification in some states, including Delhi, and Prasad said officials had assured him his name would be restored.
Kamal Lal, a 38-year-old private school teacher in Delhi, was marked as "shifted" even though he still lives in a settlement beneath a flyover with dozens of other families.
"It is very disappointing that we have been voting in this country and now our names have been cut because we do not have land papers or a water bill," he said.
Lal said he first learned of his exclusion in September and has since approached election officials, attended hearings and filed multiple reinstatement applications.
For some excluded voters, the remedy offered by officials has brought little comfort: rather than restoring their previous registrations, they were advised to apply afresh as new voters.
For poorer voters, fears run even deeper.
"Now local election officials are asking us to register as new voters, and my husband is strongly opposed to that because he has voted in the last few elections," said 39-year-old Mamta, who does not use a surname.
"I am worried that if our names are not restored to the list, I could lose access to subsidised ration and other government welfare schemes."

title: Trump approval hits record low as Democrats open 12-point lead ahead of midterms
text:
Published October 20, 2026
US President Donald Trump's approval rating fell to a record low as Americans worried about high gasoline prices and appeared ready to punish his Republican Party in the November 3 congressional elections, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that closed on Monday.
Some 31% of Americans approve of Trump's performance in office, down a percentage point from two weeks earlier and the lowest level in either of his presidential terms, the four-day poll showed.
Asked which party they would vote for if the congressional elections were held today in what is known as a "generic ballot" question, some 47% of registered voters in the nationwide poll picked Democrats and 35% chose Republicans.
The 12-point Democratic advantage was the widest over the current election cycle and could bolster Democratic hopes of seizing control of the US House of Representatives and the US Senate.
For Republicans, losing control of either chamber could complicate Trump's agenda in the last two years of his term.
Generic ballot polls are national polls that provide an overall view of which party poll respondents want to see in charge in Congress. 
While these polls provide a view of national public sentiment, they do not capture all the nuances of the state-by-state and district-by-district contests that determine control of the Senate and House, contests in which Republicans hold some structural advantages.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll two weeks earlier showed Democrats leading Republicans by 7 points, 44% to 37%.
Much of the drop in support for Republican congressional candidates was due to a larger share of women saying they would pick Democrats.
Some 50% of female voters said they would vote Democratic, compared to 32% eyeing Republican candidates. Men also favoured Democrats, but by a smaller margin.
Trump's popularity has suffered since he ordered military strikes on Iran in February alongside US ally Israel.
The war triggered a surge in gasoline prices, hitting household finances. Some 68% of Americans disapprove of Trump's handling of the economy, including 37% of self-identified Republicans.
Voters in the poll picked Democrats over Republicans as the better stewards of the economy, by 40% to 33%.
The survey, which was conducted online, gathered responses from 1,679 US adults, including 1,279 registered voters.
The poll's results had a margin of error of 2 percentage points for all respondents and 3 percentage points for registered voters.

title: At least 14 dead in Colombia mine collapse, highlighting risks of unregulated mining
text:
Published October 20, 2026
At least 14 people were killed and seven others injured after an illegal gold mine collapsed in southwestern Colombia, prompting renewed calls for improved safety standards and action to regulate small-scale mining, authorities said on Monday.
The collapse occurred in a rural area of Santa Bárbara de Iscuandé municipality in Nariño province. Search and rescue operations have been completed, Nariño Governor Luis Alfonso Escobar said, according to Reuters.
The governor urged the national government, the National Mining Agency and the Ministry of Mines and Energy to accelerate efforts to bring informal and small-scale miners into the formal sector, arguing that improved regulation could help strengthen working conditions and safety standards.
The disaster prompted an emergency response in the remote area. Colombia’s Ombudsman’s Office called for the deployment of the necessary personnel and equipment, including military air support to rescue and evacuate injured people.
It also urged authorities to activate the hospital network, consider sending the Benkos Biojó hospital ship from Guapi, and ensure the identification and dignified handling of victims’ remains.
In its October 19 statement, the Ombudsman’s Office warned that the presence of illegal armed groups in the area could hinder emergency operations and called for safe access for rescue teams and humanitarian workers. The statement was issued while the number of victims was still being confirmed.
The latest incident follows another deadly mining accident in Nariño in August, when 13 people died in Policarpa municipality, according to Reuters.
The repeated disasters have highlighted the risks faced by workers at informal mining sites, where safety infrastructure and oversight can be inadequate.
Illegal and unregulated gold mining remains a significant challenge in Colombia.
A government report published by the Ministry of Mines and Energy in October, in collaboration with the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, identified 118,410 hectares of land showing evidence of alluvial gold mining in 2025.
Of that area, 75% was associated with illicit or unauthorised operations.
The report also found that 85.6% of municipalities where such mining was identified had a presence of at least one illegal armed group.
The national figures illustrate the scale of the challenge facing authorities, although they do not establish the precise operating conditions or circumstances that caused the latest collapse.
The government faces pressure to improve oversight and bring informal miners into the legal system while addressing the dangers associated with unregulated mining in remote communities.

title: Indian court extends custody of 'Cockroach' movement leaders, says local media
text:
Published October 19, 2026
Activists detained at Delhi's Jantar Mantar protest site.
An Indian court said on Monday that two "Cockroach" movement leaders would stay in prison for two more days, local media reported, after they were detained last week for demonstrating at a historic protest venue in violation of a ban.
Cockroach Janta Party leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were among 14 people who scaled barricades on Tuesday to enter the Jantar Mantar observatory, a day after it was removed from a list of designated protest sites.
They unfurled the Indian flag and chanted slogans demanding the chief election commissioner's resignation before police detained them, with a court later sending them to prison for five days.
On Monday evening, a local court extended their judicial custody by two days after Delhi Police requested more time to question them, local media reported.
Delhi Police did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
"This is an absolute mockery of the judicial system," the group's legal head, Ratna Singh, told reporters outside the court, adding they would challenge the order in a higher court.
The youth-led CJP, opposition parties and left-wing student organisations have held near-daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter lists that they say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party.
The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol, while the BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, student leaders and several of their supporters were also detained on Friday as hundreds poured into central Delhi for a protest in support of Das and Ranka.
The 'Cockroach' movement has emerged as one of the biggest political challenges to Modi and his BJP in his 12 years in power.
A weeks-long sit-in by the group and its supporters earlier this year forced the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over exam paper leaks.
The latest demonstrations erupted after the Indian Express newspaper reported that Kumar's two deputies had raised concerns internally about voter list changes, registration procedures and digital systems.
The 130 million names that were removed from voter lists starting last year — equivalent to more than the population of Japan — included 28 million people who have died, 63 million who have relocated and 30 million who could not be traced, according to the Election Commission.

title: French Prime Minister calls for partial curfews after weekend riots
text:
Published October 19, 2026
French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said on Monday he had asked local authorities to impose partial curfews this evening following violent protests across the nation during the weekend.
Lecornu told reporters he was "fully resolved to restoring public order" and that if declaring a state of emergency was deemed necessary "we could do so", but added that at this stage partial curfews seemed "more appropriate".
He did not say which cities would impose partial curfews nor what form they would take, although he excluded imposing a full curfew on the whole of Paris.
"These curfews must be local and partial. It is out of the question to put all of Paris under curfew."
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez also told reporters during the same press conference there were no plans to cancel on Tuesday evening's Paris Saint Germain versus Barcelona soccer match.
The mayors of France's biggest cities on Monday demanded answers from the government to what they called a lack of preparation by security forces as the country licked its wounds from a weekend of rioting and looting.
The protests followed weeks of student demonstrations with occasional bouts of street violence, rocking the country six months ahead of its next presidential election and increasing pressures over a weak economy and surging debt.

title: Deadly fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright claims lives, injures others
text:
Published October 19, 2026
Flames that killed four Canadian soldiers and left 19 people in critical condition began with a smouldering grass fire that quickly grew in an Alberta base's training area where personnel were carrying out exercises, officials said on Sunday.
Officials said 39 people were in hospitals as a result of the fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, which Prime Minister Mark Carney described as one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's military on home soil.
Winds up to 96 kilometres (60 miles) per hour fed the blaze, which began around 4 p.m. MDT (2200 GMT) on Saturday. But they were below 50 km per hour leading up to the fire, Major General Wade Rutland told reporters at a news conference.
He described the sudden high winds and resulting spread of the fire as an "uncommon, rapid" event in which the flames advanced 1 km in 30 to 60 seconds.
"I’ve certainly never seen anything like it," said Rutland, commander of 1st Canadian Division, which is based in Edmonton, about 210 km west of the military site.
Officials identified the dead as Sergeant Morgan Wong, Private Shaun Farrell, Private Aidan Goulding and Private Hayden Lykkemark.
"The nation is in mourning for those brave members of our Armed Forces whom we have lost," Carney said Sunday, adding that he had ordered flags on federal buildings across the country to be lowered to half-staff to honour the victims.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said many of the injured will require "weeks and months" of specialised, intensive medical care.
When the fire began, Rutland said, 85 soldiers from the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry, were in "high-intensity" combat training using live munitions at the base, which is located in a prairie setting. The soldiers were preparing for deployment to Latvia, where Canadian forces currently have their largest international military operation.
Rutland said the incident remains under investigation and declined to speculate on what caused the grass fire. Officials do not believe the region's extensive oil and gas infrastructure had anything to do with the incident, he said. He also ruled out "outside interference."
CFB Wainwright had 1,310 military and civilian personnel stationed there as of 2021, according to census data. The base houses the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, which runs training scenarios and exercises for the army. Carney said those affected in Saturday's fire came from military bases across the country.
Military and civilian firefighters fought the fire through the night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable," Carney said.
Twenty-two ground ambulances and eight air ambulances responded to the scene, Smith said. Patients are being treated in Edmonton, Wainwright, Calgary and Red Deer.
Military search and rescue technicians also parachuted into the site, Rutland said.
Health staff in Edmonton said a "code orange," or mass-casualty event, was declared to coordinate the medical response for patients being transported from Wainwright.
The town of Wainwright, with a population of about 6,600, is just north of the base.
The municipality posted on social media that the fire had crossed the base fence into the nearby district but no evacuation orders had been issued. It said on Sunday that the fire is not expected to spread beyond its current boundaries.

title: Egypt pledges active support for Saudi Arabia as its parliament weighs military authorisation
text:
Published October 19, 2026
Regional military power Egypt is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability, the presidency said on Sunday, potentially raising the stakes in the Middle East war as Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis intensify their attacks on the kingdom.
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi requested an urgent parliament session to authorise the military, one of the Arab world's largest, to help defend its Gulf Arab ally if the kingdom requested its support.
A parliamentary vote had been expected on Sunday, but discussions were due to continue on Monday, two lawmakers and local media reports said.
Fighting between the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government and the Houthis, who control the capital Sanaa and much of the north, has escalated in recent weeks, becoming another front in the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Any Egyptian military backing for Saudi Arabia could mark a major escalation in the wider Iran war, which has threatened global energy supplies and sent oil prices soaring since the US and Israel attacked the Islamic Republic in late February.
Hours after an announcement on further discussions by the parliament, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said in a post on X that he discussed regional developments and the importance of de-escalation during a phone call with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan.
The Houthis have in recent days attacked Riyadh's international airport and the state oil company Saudi Aramco, amid renewed fighting with Saudi-backed forces.
The Houthi advances threaten the strategic Bab el-Mandeb oil shipping route, following the collapse of a truce.
"Egypt will provide Saudi Arabia with all necessary and possible forms of support to defend its security and stability, protect its resources, territorial integrity and Islamic holy sites," the Egyptian presidency said in a statement.
The statement followed a meeting of Egypt's National Defence Council chaired by Sisi and attended by the parliamentary speaker, the prime minister and the army chief.
Sisi said in a speech on Saturday that Egypt would act in accordance with guidance from Saudi King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, who visited Sisi on September 15, after fighting in Yemen reignited.
If Egypt weighs in, it could face attacks by the Houthis, ragtag mountain fighters who have emerged as a deadly force of tens of thousands and whose missiles and drones threaten the region.
Arab countries, especially Gulf states hosting US bases, have faced repeated attacks by Iran and its allies, including the Houthis and pro-Iranian militias in Iraq, during the conflict.
Egypt's Mediterranean port of Damietta came under a drone attack in July with no group claiming responsibility. Egypt has not blamed any party for the attack but said it was taking necessary measures to protect the country's national security.
Egypt and Saudi Arabia are close strategic and economic partners. Saudi Arabia and other oil-rich Gulf states, including the United Arab Emirates, provided Egypt with billions of dollars in aid, central-bank deposits and investments after the military ouster of Islamist President Mohamed Morsi in 2013. Sisi became president a year later.
Egypt had previously joined the Saudi-led coalition that intervened in Yemen in 2015 to support the government against the Houthis, but played a limited combat role in the civil war.
Riyadh has turned to regional allies and Pakistan after it sought US President Donald Trump's help to fight the Houthis. Trump did not agree to US strikes, sources told Reuters last month. Washington instead offered targeting assistance and intelligence-sharing.
Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman visited Abu Dhabi on Sunday and met with UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, with talks focusing on regional security, according to the Emirati state news agency.
The talks followed a visit to Riyadh last month by UAE Vice President Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the first trip by a senior UAE official to the kingdom since a deep rift emerged between the two Gulf powers last year.

title: France rocked by more riots as Macron vows tough security overhaul after mass arrests
text:
Published October 19, 2026
French President Emmanuel Macron has condemned what he called “unbridled” violence as fresh clashes and looting erupted in Paris and other cities, a day after nearly 2,400 people were arrested and almost 1,000 police officers and gendarmes were injured in some of the country's worst urban unrest in years.
In an address to the nation on Sunday, Macron vowed to strengthen security and review the police response but stopped short of announcing drastic measures such as a state of emergency or curfew.
“Tonight, we all feel anger and shame,” Macron said, distinguishing between protesters with “legitimate demands” and those who “destroyed, smashed, and looted”.
“Those who have destroyed must pay,” he said, vowing the government would be “uncompromising” towards “agitators from ultra-left fringe groups, joined by numerous delinquents” who had “unleashed unbridled violence in our cities”.
AFP journalists reported that police fired tear gas and stun grenades at hundreds of people gathered in a Paris square on Sunday following social media calls for a gathering that authorities said had not been approved.
Protesters hurled bottles and rocks at police, who made several arrests. Shops were also looted around Place de la République, where specialist anti-riot police were deployed for a second consecutive day.
Violence also erupted in the southeastern city of Lyon, where police thwarted attempts by young people to smash the windows of a luxury clothing store.
The unrest comes just months before a presidential election in which centrist Macron cannot stand for re-election, while Marine Le Pen, the far-right National Rally party's presidential candidate, is riding high in the polls.
Le Pen said the unrest showed that Macron's administration was “running on fumes, exhausted and disoriented”. Her top lieutenant, Jordan Bardella, described Macron's speech as a “lamentable” address that showed the authorities had “nothing more to say” to France.
Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of the hard-left France Unbowed party and also a presidential contender, urged Macron to respond to protesters' demands, saying young people “need this episode to reach a positive conclusion”.
Macron said “our country deserves a fine presidential election”, marked by debates “with the parties, rather than in the streets with violence”.
Saturday's protests brought together trade unions, the anti-Macron Yellow Vests movement that shook the early years of his presidency, and school students who had been protesting for weeks. They voiced anger over the cost of living and young people's prospects.
As images of French town halls burning and shops being looted made headlines around the world, US President Donald Trump weighed in, blaming immigration for the unrest.
“France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country,” Trump said in a social media post.
Macron vowed that senior officials would “make decisions in coordination with mayors to protect our cities, public buildings, and businesses”.
“Seeing the streets of our cities ransacked in this way is unbearable,” he said, pledging support for businesses affected by the unrest.
He also promised “full transparency” over the security forces' response to the protests, following criticism that police preparations had been inadequate.
Some opposition politicians have already called for Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez to be dismissed.
Macron said he had asked Nuñez to “draw all necessary lessons”, particularly regarding intelligence gathering and anticipating unrest, adding that he expected “clear answers”.
“It's like we had a war,” 78-year-old Paris resident Mehmet Ozeden told AFP, as burnt-out street barricades from Saturday's protests remained visible.
In the city of Limoges, a fire destroyed the 19th-century town hall. Local prefect Maurice Barate told news channel LCI that the blaze had been deliberately set by “a wild horde”.
In Lyon, a tourist office in the city centre was set ablaze during the protests, amid multiple clashes and incidents of looting.
A 17-year-old boy had his right hand blown off by a crowd-control grenade in the southern city of Saint-Étienne. In Mulhouse, a 17-year-old girl lost an eye, according to prosecutors.

title: Tensions flare again in Paris as France counts cost of worst unrest in years
text:
Published October 18, 2026
Fresh clashes broke out in Paris on Sunday a day after France suffered one of its worst days of unrest in years, with protests over high prices leaving one demonstrator dead, thousands arrested and shops across the country looted or damaged.
Nationwide demonstrations erupted into riots on Saturday, with a town hall torched, shops ransacked, and buildings covered in graffiti as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country.
