One protester died after suffering a cardiac arrest during demonstrations in Paris. Police made more than 2,000 arrests across France, while more than 600 officers were injured, the interior minister said.
"It's like a war zone here," said Dutch entrepreneur Tije De Boer, who had come to Paris with his children to visit a friend and said the protests forced him to evacuate his hotel at Place de la Republique, a trouble hotspot on Saturday.
Police again fired tear gas towards protesters at Place de la Republique and bikes were set on fire on Sunday afternoon, a sign that tensions had not fully subsided in the capital.
More than half a million people joined marches in scores of cities on Saturday, marking the convergence of a month-long student movement with broader social discontent against rising living costs and declining public services.
President Emmanuel Macron will address the nation at 8 p.m. local time (1800 GMT) on Sunday, his office said.
Saturday's unrest laid bare the deep anger at Macron, who leaves office in 2027 after a decade in power that has increasingly become defined by social discontent, a weak economy and ballooning debt.
The government has blamed the violence on hard-left and ultra-left groups, as well as criminals who it said instigated the looting.
French far-right leader Jordan Bardella said France had been "humiliated" and called on Macron to step down.
"What we are paying for is decades of laxity, a loss of authority, and the moral, psychological, and material disarmament of our internal security forces," he said as he was visiting a police station in Paris.
While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully, violent fringe groups targeted public buildings, looted luxury boutiques and supermarkets, and attacked police vehicles and officers.
A massive clean-up operation began in cities from Lille in the north to Marseille in the south and Strasbourg in the east to Bordeaux in the southwest, where a masked mob invaded the residence of the local prefect.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said several hundred shops had been damaged on Saturday.
In Limoges, southwestern France, Mayor Guillaume Guerin denounced the chaos after the city's 143-year-old town hall was set ablaze and largely destroyed in an arson attack on Saturday, drawing comparisons to the 2019 fire that devastated Paris's Notre-Dame Cathedral.
"There was a clear, premeditated intention to burn down the town hall, and the people inside feared for their lives," Guerin told Reuters. He threatened to resign if the city did not receive the funds needed to repair the town hall.
The unrest has increased pressure on President Macron and his government ahead of a presidential election due next year. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu blamed the unrest on the "ultra-left" and criminals.
Economy Minister Roland Lescure pledged support on Sunday for business owners who suffered losses. "Those who break things will pay, repair the damage and be held accountable for their intention to sow chaos," Lescure said in a statement.
Bordeaux Mayor Thomas Cazenave said up to 100 stores had been looted in his city, while Marseille Mayor Benoit Payan announced emergency financial aid to support those businesses impacted by the violence.
French retailer Carrefour's CEO Alexandre Bompard told French broadcaster BFMTV that 50 of the company's shops had been damaged, including 20 that were looted, with losses from the damage running into the tens of millions of euros.
The protests began last month over school conditions and teacher shortages in working-class suburbs, before broadening into a movement against inequality, public spending cuts and the rising cost of living.

title: Trump paused Russia sanctions to 'analyse' impact on global economy: Rubio
text:
Published October 18, 2026
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday that President Donald Trump's waiver of sweeping sanctions and tariffs on Russia would be a 60-day pause to "analyse" their impact on the global economy.
"The president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the US economy," Rubio said, noting that the economic restrictions involved a number of countries, not just Russia.
He said various conflicts were impacting global energy prices, including the US war on Iran and attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen's Houthis.
"These conflicts around the world are starting to crash into each other, and they're having an impact not just on global oil and diesel prices, but on economies as well, Rubio said.
Trump said late Saturday his decision would benefit the US, though it was unclear if he had actually made up his mind on the matter.
"We'll figure it out, and you'll figure it out," he said. "It's a very good decision, and it's going to be a decision that's good for the country, and I think good for the world."
US lawmakers on both sides of the political aisle have sharply criticised Trump after he signed an executive order Friday that waived sweeping sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia — measures adopted by Congress last month.
The law passed in September, and signed by Trump, included sanctions targeting Russian officials, oligarchs and financial institutions, and provided Trump with the authority to impose sanctions on major buyers of Russian oil and gas.
The idea was to cut off sources of funding to supporters of Russian President Vladimir Putin, as well as his war on Ukraine.
But late Friday, two days before the law was due to take effect, Trump exempted Russia from those economic restrictions.
"Beyond irresponsible," Republican Senator Thom Tillis, a frequent Trump critic who will leave office in January, said in a post on X.
"If the President wants to actually bring down energy prices, he can do it by solving the Iran problem, not by doing a solid for Vladimir Putin."
Ted Cruz, a senior Republican senator from Texas, called the move "a mistake" in comments aired on Fox News.
Trump's executive order came after he struck a deal with Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin to allow exports of Russian diesel in exchange for the easing of sanctions.
The impact of steep diesel price hikes due to the Iran war are beginning to filter into the US economy, and cost of living worries are top of mind for voters ahead of key midterm elections next month.
Polls show Trump's Republicans are likely to receive a drubbing at the polls.
"The diesel that Putin was going to sell, they were (going to) make it available to the global market one way or the other. The only difference is how much of it the United States was going to get," Rubio said, underscoring the importance of the vital fuel powering US road hauling, agriculture and construction.
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said he feared the United States would lift more sanctions on Russia and that Trump's action "rewards" Putin.

title: 'Never seen anything like it': Mass looting grips Paris
text:
'Never seen anything like it': Mass looting grips Paris
Looters in Paris poured into stores across capital, clearing shelves of cigarettes, sunglasses, clothes, jewellery and food
Updated Sunday Oct 18 2026
Smashing shop windows and snatching boxes of goods, looters in Paris poured into stores across the capital on Saturday, facing no resistance from authorities as nationwide protests degenerated into violence.
Crowds of masked men wearing black hoodies yanked at metal store shutters until they gave way, clearing shelves of cigarettes, sunglasses, clothes, jewellery and food.
The violence erupted as hundreds of thousands of demonstrators gathered across the country to denounce the cost of living, following weeks of student protests and stoking political uncertainty six months before France's presidential election.
AFP journalists saw looters emerging from a supermarket carrying bags stuffed with cakes, fruit juice and alcohol.
From a small jewellery shop across the street, they took antique clocks. On a street corner, entire display racks of sunglasses vanished.
Inside the shops, they searched for the cash register, smashing it onto the floor, sometimes only to discover it was empty.
Perched on a pavement terrace with a colleague, a 38-year-old art teacher who gave her name as Alma said she had "never seen anything like it".
The pair, who had joined an unsuccessful march earlier in the day to reach the French president's residence, the Elysee Palace, said nonetheless that they "understand" the revolt.
The violence began on the sidelines of marches in the capital and other cities that the interior ministry said were attended by 550,000 people.
The CGT union, which took part, said 800,000 people participated.
Police used tear gas and water cannon against protesters who threw projectiles and aimed fireworks.
'Deep anger'
French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu, who slammed the "violence of extreme intensity", said late Saturday that 1,200 people had been arrested and 150 police officers hurt.
Paris mayor Emmanuel Gregoire said whole streets "have been devastated" in the capital, making a distinction between the "fundamental" right to protest and "unacceptable" violence.
"I understand why people might be upset, but I think damaging property is fine, as long as we don't physically harm anyone," Alma said.
Restaurants, hotels and residential buildings have mostly been spared, prompting surreal scenes of Parisians enjoying their usual Saturday lunch with friends while crowds wreaked havoc outside.
Locals watched the scenes unfold from the safety of their apartments.
"What a sight," said Jules, a 29-year-old civil servant.
"They must have some pretty deep anger. They're a part of society who doesn't feel integrated."
While he agreed with the right to protest, he said the looters were "undermining their own goals".
"Just look at the state of the street," he told AFP.
Near the iconic Place de la Republique in central Paris, broken glass and debris littered the roads, as a pile of burning bicycles belched out thick smoke.
Law enforcement was absent from the area, having clashed with protesters there earlier in the day.
Header image: People walk past a vandalised Chanel store, the day after clashes during a national day of demonstrations against the cost of living and rising fuel prices, in Paris, France, October 18, 2026. — Reuters

title: 'Serious incident' at Canada base causes deaths, sparks fire: govt
text:
Published October 18, 2026
A "serious incident" at a military base in western Canada killed and injured multiple people and sparked a huge blaze on Saturday, the government said.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney posted on X that "a serious incident creating a major fire" had occurred at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright military base in western Alberta province.
There were "both fatalities and injuries" as a result of the incident, the country's defence minister, David McGuinty, said at a news conference.
Neither offered details on the number of casualties or the nature of the incident.
"I'm saddened to share that there have been both fatalities and injuries as a result of an incident on the base," identified as Wainwright in Alberta, McGuinty said.
"We will have more to say in the coming hours and days," McGuinty said.
He did not say how many people were killed or injured, or what caused the "tragic" situation at the base in the east-central part of the province, about 210 km (130 miles) east of Edmonton.
A major fire was still burning on Saturday evening, he said, adding: "I cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory."
The Canadian military and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police are investigating the incident, McGuinty said.
CFB Wainwright had 1,310 military and civilian personnel stationed there as of 2021, according to census data. The town of Wainwright, population about 6,600, is just north of the base.
The municipality posted on social media that the fire had crossed the base fence into the nearby district, but no evacuation orders had been issued.
General Jennie Carignan, the chief of Canada's Defence Staff, said on social media that the Canadian forces are fully engaged with federal, provincial and local authorities.
"Our priority remains the welfare of our members, their families and their community," she said.

title: Saudi-led coalition says helicopter crash in Najran kills two crew members
text:
Published October 18, 2026
A reconnaissance AH-6i helicopter crashed in the Najran region of Saudi Arabia due to a technical malfunction, killing its two crew members, the Saudi-led coalition's spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki said in a statement on Sunday.
The helicopter crashed in an area under the jurisdiction of the Saudi National Guard Ministry, the statement added.
The southwestern area of Najran has been subject to attacks by Iran-aligned Houthis in recent weeks as fighting between the coalition and the Yemen-based fighter group escalated, with the Yemen conflict becoming another front in the US-led war with Iran.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said in a post on X on Saturday that the group had shot down a Saudi Apache helicopter near Najran while it was carrying out what he described as hostile activities targeting Houthi positions along the border.
Al-Maliki commented on Saree's post on Sunday with a photo of several Apaches lined up, saying: "You claim to have shot it down, but it will enter the battlefield soon."
The incident occurred as Saudi Arabia remains on heightened alert amid a renewed wave of attacks by Yemen’s Houthi militia.
Since Yemen's conflict flared up again in July after a years-long hiatus, Saudi Arabia has faced sustained Houthi missile and drone attacks targeting its oil installations, tankers and transit hubs, including an attack on Riyadh's airport last week that killed 13 people.
Saudi Arabia said on Saturday that it had intercepted a fresh wave of drones, as its ally Egypt weighed helping the kingdom defend against repeated attacks by Yemen's Houthis.
The interceptions came as Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said he was willing to "carry out any measure to protect" Saudi Arabia if its leaders requested it.
Sisi said Egypt was not seeking to intervene in regional wars but added that it was "inconceivable" for Cairo to stand by while the kingdom was "harmed or its security and stability threatened".

title: Kolkata festival stampede kills 17, injures dozens; authorities fear death toll could rise
text:
Published October 18, 2026
KOLKATA, INDIA: A stampede at a Hindu religious festival in the eastern Indian city of Kolkata killed 17 people and injured 25 others on Saturday, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said, as Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced compensation for the victims' families.
The incident occurred at around 7:40 pm local time at the exit gate of the Sarada Park, also known as the Chorbagan, Durga Puja pandal in the city's Girish Park area, according to a statement by Kolkata Police.
Police attributed the incident to heavy crowds of festival visitors amid rainfall. The injured were rescued and taken to Medical College and Hospital for treatment, the police statement said, adding that police reinforcements, firefighters, disaster management personnel, ambulances and medical teams had been deployed.
The pandal was closed to visitors following the incident, police said.
Adhikari said 17 people had been brought dead to hospital and 25 others were injured. He visited the hospital where the injured were being treated, according to reports by Press Trust of India.
Modi expressed sorrow over the deaths and extended condolences to the bereaved families, the Prime Minister's Office said in a statement published by the government's Press Information Bureau.
The government announced compensation of 200,000 rupees ($2,106) from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund for the next of kin of each person killed, while those injured would receive 50,000 rupees each, the statement said.
The government also said the West Bengal administration was providing assistance to affected families.
Durga Puja is one of the largest annual religious and cultural festivals in West Bengal, drawing large crowds to temporary structures known as pandals, where idols of the Hindu goddess Durga are displayed for worship.
The festival celebrates the goddess's victory over the demon Mahishasura and is marked by elaborate decorations, religious ceremonies and public gatherings across the state.
The cause of the crowd surge was not independently established in the official information available. Reports carried by Indian media cited differing accounts of how the incident unfolded, including the impact of rainfall and a rush among people near the venue's entrance and exit.

title: US envoy to Israel rejects report accusing aide of suppressing cables to shield Netanyahu
text:
Published October 18, 2026
A senior adviser to US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee allegedly blocked, delayed or rewrote diplomatic reports on Israeli government actions to present Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government in a more favourable light, a New York Times investigation has found.
The investigation identified David Milstein, who joined the US Embassy in Jerusalem in April 2025, as the official accused of intervening in reporting on Israeli settlement expansion, violence by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank and the humanitarian crisis in Gaza.
The newspaper said it interviewed 15 US officials who had worked with Milstein, nine former diplomats and reviewed dozens of internal cables, memos and other communications.
Officials told the newspaper they were concerned that policymakers in Washington were not receiving a complete or accurate account of events on the ground.
One of the most significant cases concerned Israel’s approval of a record number of settlements in the occupied West Bank in late March.
Embassy staff drafted an urgent report for Washington after concluding that the move could conflict with President Donald Trump’s stated opposition to annexation of the territory. Three US officials briefed on the process told the newspaper that Milstein blocked the report from being sent.
The alleged intervention raised questions about whether Washington was receiving timely assessments of Israeli policies that could affect US diplomatic objectives.
The investigation also detailed alleged interference in embassy reporting on violence by Israeli settlers in the West Bank.
As attacks increased in the spring, embassy staff sought to report concerns that the Israeli government was failing to take adequate action. Instead, according to three officials cited by the newspaper, a cable sent to Washington praised Israel for “cracking down” on the attacks.
The newspaper reported that other assessments also presented Israeli efforts in a more favourable light than the original reporting prepared by embassy staff.
Another case concerned the humanitarian situation in Gaza after Israel halted aid deliveries in 2025.
US diplomats drafted a cable warning of worsening conditions and concerns about the US-backed Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF), which had been established as an alternative aid-distribution mechanism.
Milstein reportedly sent a separate cable that portrayed the foundation more favourably than the original assessment. The reported discrepancy raised concerns about whether Washington was being given an accurate account of the risks and shortcomings associated with aid distribution.
The investigation also alleged that Milstein suppressed a detailed embassy report concerning the killings of nine Palestinian Americans by Israeli settlers and security forces in the occupied West Bank over four years.
The report had been prepared after members of Congress sought information about the deaths. According to officials familiar with the matter, embassy staff found that most investigations had made little progress, some had been closed, and no one had been prosecuted.
Milstein reportedly argued that the embassy should instead send a letter stating that Israel was handling the investigations properly.
The alleged intervention was particularly significant because lawmakers were seeking information from the US government about the deaths of American citizens and the status of investigations into them.
The newspaper said Milstein began requiring approval of communications from the embassy section dealing with Palestinian affairs soon after arriving in Jerusalem.
According to officials with direct knowledge of the process, the volume of cables fell from several a week to only a handful a month. Some staff members reportedly became reluctant to prepare assessments because they feared the reports would be blocked, delayed or rewritten.
Former US diplomats told the newspaper that withholding or materially altering information sent to Washington could undermine the policymaking process by preventing senior officials from making decisions based on a full assessment of developments.
It remains unclear how much Huckabee knew about the alleged interventions or whether they affected White House policy. Officials told the newspaper that the ambassador had sometimes worked with Milstein to limit or reshape reporting, but had also reined in the aide when he believed he had gone too far.
Huckabee rejected the investigation’s findings but did not address the individual cases in detail.
“The elements of the story The New York Times is trying to assemble are so lacking in fact that it ranks up with other Times farcical endeavors,” he said, adding: “I personally and categorically refute the elements of your proposed ‘story’.”
The State Department responded: “The entire team at State remains focused on advancing President Trump’s America First agenda.” The White House referred the newspaper to the department.
The investigation also noted that previous US ambassadors to Israel had political advisers who sought to influence reporting, and that reviewing or amending embassy communications can form part of senior officials’ responsibilities. The central allegation against Milstein, however, is that he went beyond routine review by suppressing reports or changing their substance.
The findings raise broader questions about oversight of diplomatic reporting and whether political considerations can prevent US policymakers from receiving candid assessments of the actions of a close ally.

title: Riyadh reports fresh drone interceptions as Cairo considers steps to defend kingdom
text:
Published October 18, 2026
Saudi Arabia said on Saturday that it had intercepted a fresh wave of drones, as its ally Egypt weighed helping the kingdom defend against repeated attacks by Yemen's Houthis.
Riyadh leads a military coalition supporting Yemen's internationally recognised government in its war against the Houthis. A military spokesman for the Iran-backed group said on Saturday that dozens of Saudi strikes over the past day had killed and wounded "numerous" people.
Since Yemen's conflict flared up again in July after a years-long hiatus, Saudi Arabia has faced sustained Houthi missile and drone attacks targeting its oil installations, tankers and transit hubs, including an attack on Riyadh's airport last week that killed 13 people.
A spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition said on Saturday that it had "intercepted and destroyed four drones over the past few hours in the regions of Riyadh, the Eastern Province, and the South".
The interceptions came as Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said he was willing to "carry out any measure to protect" Saudi Arabia if its leaders requested it.
Sisi said Egypt was not seeking to intervene in regional wars but added that it was "inconceivable" for Cairo to stand by while the kingdom was "harmed or its security and stability threatened".
"I'm not talking about fighting anyone or attacking anyone," he said. "We are speaking only about defence."
Although Egypt is a member of the anti-Houthi coalition, its role has largely focused on Red Sea maritime security rather than the fighting in Yemen.
Egypt and Saudi Arabia have historically close relations and strategic economic ties.
Egypt's parliament will hold an emergency session on Sunday at Sisi's request.
The repeated Houthi strikes have prompted foreign embassies to warn their citizens against using Saudi airports or travelling to the kingdom altogether.
Saudi Arabia's Education Ministry on Saturday announced an extension of remote learning measures for students in Riyadh and nearby Diriyah.
Saudi Arabia has accused Iran of encouraging the Houthis' recent escalation, a charge Tehran denies.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday that Tehran supported a "comprehensive political process as the only practical and sustainable way to resolve" the conflict on the Arabian Peninsula.
He also reiterated Iran's offer to mediate between the two sides.
Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh previously said Riyadh had not responded to Iran's offer.
However, Yemeni Foreign Minister Afrah al-Zouba rejected the proposal in a statement on X on Saturday, saying "the Tehran regime is a party to the war against Yemenis, not a mediator".
The Houthis are part of Iran's "Axis of Resistance" against Israel and the United States, but both the group and Tehran insist that the Houthis act independently.
Saudi Arabia has carried out daily airstrikes against the Houthis in Yemen, where government forces are seeking to reverse gains made by the group in a lightning offensive in September.
On Saturday, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said Riyadh had carried out 53 strikes in the capital, Sanaa, and six other provinces over the past 24 hours, causing "numerous dead and wounded".
A Houthi-affiliated news agency had earlier accused Saudi warplanes of targeting "civilian residences" in Dhamar and Taiz provinces, killing 12 people and wounding more than 30.
It alleged that the strikes had been carried out "using cluster bombs, which are banned internationally".

title: French police clash with protesters as tens of thousands rally over cost of living
text:
Published October 17, 2026
Clashes broke out between police and protesters in cities across France on Saturday as tens of thousands of people took to the streets in some of the country's most violent protests in years over rising costs and declining public services.
Some 272 people had been arrested by mid-afternoon after violent incidents involving hooded individuals, including in Paris, Marseille in the south, Rennes in the northwest, Toulouse in the southwest and Angers in the west, the Interior Ministry said.
"Such actions include attempted looting, confrontations with law enforcement, the setting of fires to street furniture and the targeting of seats of power and media outlets," it said, blaming the unrest on what it described as the "ultra-left".
In Lyon, in east-central France, protesters also set ablaze a tourist office.
The protests began last month at high schools in Paris' poor northern suburbs, where anger over teacher shortages and shabby facilities evolved into a broader movement focused on inequality, public spending and living standards.
"We are fighting because the cost of living is too harsh, because the price of fuel is too high, because high school pupils are being violently attacked and hurt all over the country just for trying to protest and ask for more teachers and decent learning conditions," said Lola, a 19-year-old protester in Paris.
A large police presence was visible in central Paris, especially near landmarks such as the Champs-Elysees and the Arc de Triomphe, which were excluded from the routes of two authorised demonstrations.
Protesters in high-visibility vests blocked streets, recalling the Yellow Vest movement that marked President Emmanuel Macron's previous term in office.
In Marseille, the mayor said the town hall had been vandalised and that additional police were being sent to the city following talks with the prime minister and interior minister.
About 100 people walked towards the start of the protests shouting "All cops are bastards", according to a Reuters witness.
Macron, who urged calm on Friday, is entering the final stretch of his presidency amid a fragmented political landscape and growing pressure over the economy.
France's efforts to reduce public debt have failed to reassure investors, pushing government borrowing costs to their highest levels in more than two decades.
Police tactics have drawn criticism following a series of injuries among demonstrators, including a teenager who lost a hand after picking up a stun grenade. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said more than 900 police officers had also been injured in previous protests.
The police watchdog is investigating at least two dozen allegations of police violence. France suspended the use of stun grenades during the student demonstrations, but Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said they could be used on Saturday.
Calls on social media for veterans of previous protest movements to join the demonstrations appeared to have broadened participation, raising the prospect of larger.
The Yellow Vest movement emerged in 2018 in opposition to diesel taxes before expanding into a wider protest against living costs and inequality. The movement subsided after Macron announced billions of euros in tax cuts.
Yannick Maillou, a teacher from La Creche in western France who participated in the Yellow Vest movement, said several gathering points had been organised locally for Saturday's protests, with labour unions also encouraging participation.

title: Pope Leo returns to Vatican four days after cancer surgery
text:
Published October 17, 2026
VATICAN CITY: A smiling Pope Leo left hospital in Rome on Saturday afternoon and returned to the Vatican four days after surgery for lung cancer, an illness that has prompted speculation about how his 17-month papacy might change.
The pope walked unaided to his waiting car, waving to well-wishers outside Rome's Gemelli Hospital. He stopped to speak to a 13-year-old girl named Varvara from Ukraine who has been in Italy for cancer treatment.
Leo, 71, was pictured smiling broadly and waving through an open window when his black SUV left the hospital grounds. He appeared in good spirits as he left the hospital in video released by the Vatican.
He shook hands with a group of Franciscan friars, one of whom said: "This is the second time (we have met). Let's hope there will be a third and fourth."
The pope laughed and replied: "Many times, but not for these reasons."
His doctors had said earlier on Saturday that he was well enough to return home after they carried out the latest blood tests and chest imaging, and that he was able to perform normal daily activities independently.
Leo, who had an operation on Tuesday to remove the lower lobe of his right lung, will hold his first public engagement since surgery when he will lead weekly prayers with pilgrims from his apartment overlooking St. Peter's Square at noon (1000 GMT) on Sunday.
He has been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer. The diagnosis for a pope known to be relatively young and energetic and who was elected only in May 2025 caused shock and raised questions about the future shape of his papacy.
The pope's doctors have said his surgery was completed successfully, without complications. They have not yet disclosed the size of the tumour or whether the disease had spread to nearby lymph nodes, key factors in determining prognosis.
Dr Stefano Margaritora, the pope's lead surgeon, said that Leo could be fully recovered in another 10 days and that there was no reason to call off his planned visit to South America next month.
"As for a long trip involving air travel in about three weeks, I would say there are no clinical reasons why it should not take place," he told the Vatican News website.
Leo is planning to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17, in one of the most intense trips arranged for a pope in decades.
Margaritora said the tumour had been discovered by chance during what he called a routine abdominal examination.
The Vatican signaled on Friday that Leo, known for following a busy schedule, intended to keep up his commitments, as some cardinals began to publicly express concern about the pope's health.
In a sign the pope was back to work, Leo held a phone call on Friday with Russian President Vladimir Putin, urging a ceasefire to help get vital supplies into Oleshky, a Russian-controlled Ukrainian town.
Lebanese pilgrim Abdul Halim Fatha was in St Peter's Square as Leo arrived back at the Vatican and expressed sadness over the pope's cancer diagnosis. "But I know God will be with him and protect him," he said.

title: Landfill waste could power low-carbon cement production to cut emissions
text:
Landfill waste could power low-carbon cement production to cut emissions
- By Kumail Shah -
- Oct 20, 2026
Non-recyclable trash that usually ends up in landfills could help reduce carbon emissions in the construction industry by replacing fossil fuels in cement production. Researchers at Adelaide University have reviewed how refuse-derived fuel, or RDF, could address both waste problems and pollution from cement manufacturing.
Cement is essential for building roads, bridges, and buildings, but making it produces about 8% of the world’s carbon dioxide emissions.
Making cement needs very high heat in industrial kilns, which usually comes from burning coal and other fossil fuels. At the same time, large amounts of burnable, non-recyclable waste are sent to landfills every day. By turning this waste into fuel and burning it with traditional energy sources, a method called co-processing, factories can use less coal.
Ph.D. candidate Geethmi Thisakya from the School of Civil Engineering and Construction led the review, with Dr. Navodana Rodrigo, Dr. Chamitha Wijewickrama, and Professor George Zillante.
The team reviewed 211 academic papers published from 1991 to July 2025, focusing on 48 articles and seven regulatory documents. Thisakya noted that linking waste management to reduced industrial emissions requires more than replacing coal with trash. It also requires consistent fuel quality, strong regulations, and clear evidence of economic and environmental benefits.
The study also found that many people confuse refuse-derived fuel with solid recovered fuel (SRF), which is a more strictly defined type of waste fuel. Different terms and quality standards make it hard for the industry to compare studies, follow laws, and ensure safe kiln operations. Better quality control and clearer rules will help cement makers feel more confident about using waste-based fuels.
The researchers say that while reusing and recycling materials should still come first, RDF is a good option for burnable trash that cannot be recycled. They suggest that future research should improve how fuels are classified and test how these alternatives work in different industries and regions.

title: Fazal ur Rehman says he would demand PM’s office, not governorship
text:
Fazal ur Rehman rejects governorship reports, says he would seek PM’s office
- By Web Desk -
- Oct 20, 2026
Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazal ur Rehman has rejected reports about his alleged interest in a governorship, saying that if he makes a demand, it would be for the office of prime minister, not governor, ARY News reported.
In a statement on October 20, Fazal ur Rehman described the reports about the governorship as completely false and an insult to him.
He also rejected the results of the 2024 general elections and demanded fresh, immediate and transparent elections in the country.
The JUI-F chief said his party had no links with the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) or any other organisation. He said his party had made sacrifices in the fight against terrorism, but its leaders, office-bearers, religious scholars and seminaries were also facing security threats.
Fazal ur Rehman said his own life and the seminaries associated with him were no longer safe.
Commenting on constitutional amendments, he said his party had withdrawn amendments under the 26th Constitutional Amendment that, in his view, would have weakened the system.
He alleged that the same amendments were later passed under the 27th Constitutional Amendment by purchasing the support of lawmakers.
The JUI-F chief also criticised the country’s economic situation, saying the economy remained weak and government measures were having no impact on the public.
Referring to talks and the issue of military operations, Fazal ur Rehman questioned the grounds for negotiations after killings had already taken place. He also asked where the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) government had obstructed the operation.
His remarks came as he rejected the 2024 election results and reiterated his demand for fresh elections, while raising concerns over security threats, constitutional changes and the state of the economy.

title: Turkey name Yalcin as head coach to replace Montella
text:
Turkey name Yalcin as head coach to replace Montella
- By Reuters -
- Oct 20, 2026
Turkey have appointed Sergen Yalcin as head coach on a four-year contract to replace the sacked Italian Vincenzo Montella, the country’s football federation (TFF) announced on Tuesday.
The 53-year-old former Turkey midfielder steps into the job following Montella’s dismissal earlier this month after a difficult UEFA Nations League campaign.
Turkey sit bottom of Group A1 after four consecutive losses, having also suffered a group stage exit from the 2026 World Cup.
“We wish Yalcin success in his new role and hope this decision proves auspicious for our country and our national team,” the TFF said in a statement.
A prominent figure in Turkish football, Yalcin won 37 caps from 1994 to 2003, featured at Euro 1996 and Euro 2000 and played for Besiktas, Fenerbahce, and Galatasaray.
As a manager, Yalcin guided Besiktas to a domestic double of Super Lig and Turkish Cup in the 2020–21 season. He ended a second stint in charge of Besiktas in May.

title: Oman’s labor law explains annual leave for expats
text:
Oman’s labor law explains annual leave for expats
- By Web Desk -
- Oct 20, 2026
The Bureau of Emigration and Overseas Employment of Pakistan has issued labor rights guidelines for Pakistani workers employed in Oman, highlighting annual leave entitlements, leave arrangements, travel benefits and end-of-service payments.
The guidelines explain the provisions of Oman’s Labour Law, promulgated under Royal Decree No. 53/2023, which guarantees employees at least 30 days of annual leave with full pay under Article 78.
Employees can take annual leave after completing at least six months of service with their employer.
They may carry forward up to 30 days of unused leave, although this limit may be exceeded if work requirements prevent them from taking their leave. Annual leave periods may also be combined by mutual agreement.
The law provides an additional benefit for non-Omani workers, entitling them to return air tickets during annual leave to travel to their home country and back to their workplace after the leave period.
It also states that employees cannot waive their right to annual leave. However, an alternative leave arrangement may be introduced in sectors specified by the Minister of Labour, provided it offers greater benefits to workers.
Article 81 sets out further rules governing annual leave.
Employers may divide annual leave into separate periods according to operational requirements, although this provision does not apply to young workers.
Where work demands require it, employers may postpone an employee’s annual leave for up to six months.
The law also seeks to ensure that workers receive adequate rest, requiring every employee to take at least 30 days of annual leave once every two years.
In certain circumstances, employers may compensate workers financially for unused annual leave, calculated based on their basic wage, provided the employee gives written consent.
If employment ends before a worker has used their accumulated annual leave, the employer must pay compensation equivalent to the employee’s full wage for the outstanding leave days.

title: Angel Reese rewrites WNBA history with record-breaking 30-15 finals masterclass
text:
Angel Reese rewrites WNBA history with finals masterclass
- By Zaeem Basir -
- Oct 20, 2026
Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese continues to show the world that her presence in women’s pro hoops isn’t just hype, setting the all-time bar by when she became the youngest to record a double-double with 30 points and 15 rebounds in a WNBA Finals game.
In arguably the biggest game of her career to date, Reese led the Dream to what proved to be an eye-opening, record-setting performance, turning in 30+ points with a 15-rebound night and officially becoming the youngest player to record a 30/15 with at least 24 years, 166 days.
Reese’s impressive stat line has her in a very exclusive club. Her 30 and 15 performance moves her into an elite group of just three other players to accomplish the feat, alongside WNBA champions Breanna Stewart (who did it twice) and Jonquel Jones.
Reese maintained her attack mode even with aggressive post defense and through some hard-nosed defense from Atlanta’s physical forwards, as she owned the offensive boards and relentlessly kept her team on top in certain stretches.
Although it was not reflected in the box score, there is no denying that the young superstar’s historic night has been making waves in popular culture as well, showcasing her appeal as one of the most recognizable faces of her generation.
Famous musicians, like up-and-coming rapper Latto, joined the fun on the day of Reese’s record-breaking night.
As the WNBA experiences an unprecedented increase in fan interaction, media coverage, and global audiences, Reese’s journey so far exemplifies the long list of talent fueling the ascendence of women’s sports today.
Becoming an indispensable part of a franchise from the start so early in her career, Reese proved with her presence that her hustle, rebounding, and intense passion could power a team during the most intense moments of the season.
Angle Reese’s 30-15 record- setting night in the Finals will remain one of the most memorable in the book of her career, paving the way for Angel Reese’s early WNBA success.

title: Angel Reese's historic night is lost in mid-game meltdown in WNBA finals
text:
Angel Reese's historic night is lost in mid-game meltdown in WNBA finals
- By Zaeem Basir -
- Oct 20, 2026
Finals will be remembered for Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese’s iconic, world-breaking display against the Golden State Valkyries.
Overcoming the pressure of a 1-1 series tie, Reese put on a clinic inside with an incredible 30 point, 16 rebound, 3 assist, 2 block effort on 62.5% shooting. Her physicality on the glass and scoring prowess in the paint was matchless in playoff history as Reese powered the Dream to a 79-65 victory and a deadlock in the series heading into Atlanta on Monday.
Any other player would be happy with a stat line of this magnitude, which would turn Reese in to just the fifth player in WNBA history to put up a 30 point 15 rebound game in the postseason – behind Candace Parker, Lisa Leslie, and Louisa Harris.
But a high-octane third quarter exploded the night and a combustible emotional explosion that took everyone — including pundits and even watching fans — by complete surprise.
The failure to run a play without of us, without the basketball, when it appeared she wasn’t getting it when she needed it, and moments after tumbling to the court as a result of a collision, Reese burst into a loud, protracted scream of rage on the floor, calling loudly for the ball and in body language, threatening to turn around and walk off — moments that recalled much of the criticism the team was taking after its first setback and immediately rekindled speculations that a problem of chemistry could make a title impossible for the Dream.
Thankfully, that breaking point of friction was the very spark Atlanta needed. Rather than letting the rift widen, the confrontation rallied the team. Her teammates acclimated to her aggressive need and provided her the rock during a resounding 18-4 binge that basically sealed the deal for the road team.
Veteran coaches and players expertly handled the volatile situation, channeling Reese’s combative rage into solid court performance instead of destructive behavior.
So what should have been a PR catastrophe and locker-room rupture of epic proportions has become, instead, a gritty story of perseverance and perseverance.
As the WNBA Finals move back to Georgia, Reese’s emotional hysteria has been, in equal parts, the powerful, unrelenting soul that makes her a once-in-a-generation player, and the stick of dynamite that the Dream must delicately diffuse. If Atlanta can keep all that passion focused on bringing down championships, Reese’s historic night may be the moment that pushed her team over the edge.

title: Bavuma hits 179 to lead South African fightback
text:
Bavuma hits 179 to lead South African fightback
- By AFP -
- Oct 20, 2026
Temba Bavuma hit a career-best 179 to lead a dramatic South African fightback on the third day of the second Test against Australia at St George’s Park on Tuesday.
The South African captain shared century partnerships with Marco Jansen (85) and Simon Harmer (82) as the hosts posted 425 for nine declared – a total which seemed improbable after they were 97 for five overnight.
It was Bavuma’s third day at the crease after battling through bowler-friendly conditions on the first two rain-shortened days.
The situation looked dire for the world Test champions when the sixth wicket fell on 110 early in the day but the tall Jansen changed the tempo of the game as he hammered nine fours and three sixes off 100 deliveries.
Jansen dominated a seventh wicket partnership of 132 off 186 balls but Bavuma became more assertive when he was joined by Harmer after Jansen clipped Scott Boland to midwicket in the first over with the second new ball.
Bavuma and Harmer added a South African Test record 182 for the eighth wicket.
Harmer and Bavuma fell off successive balls before Bavuma declared to leave Australia with a short period to bat before the close.

title: Warner questions 'pathetic' crowds in South Africa-Australia series
text:
Warner questions 'pathetic' crowds in South Africa-Australia series
- By Web Desk -
- Oct 20, 2026
Former Australia opener David Warner has slammed the poor fan attendance in the ongoing Test series against South Africa.
Australia comprehensively defeated South Africa by 214 runs in the first Test played in Durban in front of a sparse crowd. The fans were also in low-attendance during the first two days of the rain-affected second Test in Gqeberha.
Warner took to X and shared his disappointment over the empty stands during the series.
“We keep hearing how important Test cricket is, but where are the fans in South Africa? Empty stands, no atmosphere, and we’re supposed to believe the format is thriving?,” he wrote.
He said it was pathetic that fans were not turning up to watch Test cricket, arguing that the format could not be called the pinnacle of the game under such circumstances.
“You can’t keep calling Test cricket the pinnacle of the game if no one turns up to watch it. Harsh reality, but someone has to say it. Pathetic,” he added.
After a low-attendance in Durban during the first Test, the Kwa-Zulu Natal Cricket Union (KZNCU) said that they would launch a review into the reasons behind sparse crowds.
Only 20,000 fans turned up for the series opener, which was also the first Test in South Africa between both countries since the infamous Sandpaper gate. It was also the Proteas first Test at home since January 2025.
KZNCU CEO Heinrich Strydom also lamented the empty stands and said both teams deserved greater support from crowd.
“A Test match of this quality, featuring the Proteas and Australia, deserved greater support in the stands,” Heinrich Strydom, KZNCU CEO, said in a statement.
“While we recognise that supporters face competing demands on their time and finances, we must also understand better what influences their decisions to attend and what more we can do to make live cricket an attractive and worthwhile experience,” he added.

title: Minhas stars as Pakistan sink England in tri-series clash
text:
Minhas stars as Pakistan sink England in tri-series clash
- By Web Desk -
- Oct 20, 2026
Arafat Minhas delivered an all-round performance as Pakistan thrashed England by 88 runs in the second match of the ODI tri-series at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Tuesday.
Set a challenging 303, England were bowled out for 215 inside 38.4 overs despite a strong start. Tom Banton top-scored with 57 off 53 balls, hitting two sixes and five fours. Ben Duckett made 45 after facing 46 deliveries with the help of eights fours.
The duo laid a solid foundation for the visitors in the chase, forging a 91-run stand in 14.3 overs.
However, Pakistan bowlers made a strong comeback in the middle overs, reducing the Three Lions to 128-3 inside 20 overs. Skipper Harry Brook managed only five.
After quick wickets, Joe Root and Sam Curran shared a 37-run partnership for the fourth wicket. Root struck two fours in his 33 from 37 whereas Curran contribute with 27 runs to his name.
Minhas bowled Root in the 28th over as England suffered a collapse from which they could not recover from. They lost their last five wickets for 38 runs, with Minhas capping off an excellent performance by running out Gus Atkinson (7) to bring an end to England’s innings.
The left-arm spinner registered the figures of 6/40 in 8.4 overs. Haris Rauf also chipped in with two wickets.
Earlier, Hasan Nawaz and Arafat Minhas struck counterattacking half-centuries as Pakistan posted 302-9.
After being put in to bat by England captain Harry Brook, Pakistan endured a difficult start as both openers departed inside the first six overs, leaving the hosts struggling at 31-2.
Experienced batter Babar Azam attempted to steady the innings alongside youngster Saad Baig, who had made his ODI debut against Sri Lanka in the tournament opener. The pair added 28 runs before Babar departed for a cautious 34 off 52 deliveries.
Baig then combined with Salman Ali Agha, who failed to capitalise on his start and was dismissed for 16.
With Pakistan under pressure, Hasan Nawaz walked in and immediately adopted an aggressive approach to shift the momentum in the hosts’ favour.
The right-handed batter dominated a 52-run partnership for the fifth wicket, contributing 31 runs before Baig’s innings came to an end. The young wicketkeeper-batter departed after scoring 35 off 54 deliveries.
Nawaz subsequently found support from Arafat Minhas as the duo launched a crucial recovery, adding 78 runs off 74 balls for the sixth wicket. Their partnership helped Pakistan cross the 200-run mark and laid the foundation for a competitive total.
However, Nawaz’s entertaining innings ended when England pacer Jamie Overton produced a perfectly executed yorker to dismantle his stumps. The 24-year-old departed after scoring 79 off 74 balls, an innings featuring five fours and four sixes.
Following his dismissal, Minhas joined forces with Faheem Ashraf, and the pair maintained Pakistan’s scoring momentum during the closing stages.
The two all-rounders stitched together a brisk 72-run partnership off just 49 deliveries for the seventh wicket, putting England’s bowlers under further pressure.
During the partnership, Minhas brought up his maiden ODI half-century, continuing his impressive contribution with the bat. The left-handed batter eventually fell to Sonny Baker after scoring 59 off 58 deliveries, including nine boundaries.
Faheem, meanwhile, played an aggressive cameo of 39 runs off 26 balls, smashing five fours and a six before being dismissed by Sam Curran in the penultimate over.
Haris Rauf struck a boundary on the final delivery of the innings as Pakistan finished with 302-9 in their allotted 50 overs, setting England a target of 303 runs.
For England, Sonny Baker was the pick of the bowlers with figures of 3-65, while Gus Atkinson claimed two wickets for 35 runs. Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Adil Rashid and Sam Curran chipped in with one wicket apiece.

title: Emery adamant injuries 'no excuse' for Aston Villa
text:
Emery adamant injuries 'no excuse' for Aston Villa
- By AFP -
- Oct 20, 2026
Aston Villa manager Unai Emery is determined to avoid using his squad’s injury problems as an excuse ahead of their Champions League tie at home to Viking on Wednesday.
Villa endured a difficult start to the season but have won four of their last five matches in all competitions, with Johan Manzambi’s first-half header securing a 1-0 Premier League win at Newcastle on Saturday.
But 21-year-old Switzerland international Manzambi was substituted in the 72nd minute and Emery said Tuesday he will play no part against Viking because of a “small injury”.
Manzambi joins the likes of defenders Matteo Ruggeri and Aaron Wan-Bissaka on Villa’s injury list.
“We are accepting of the injuries we had before,” Emery told a pre-match press conference.
“So many players we had injured in our process here and now we’re still having some, like (Amadou) Onana for a long time, like Matteo for more or less two months.
“Coming back and joining us is Ian Maatsen, he’s joined us and is training with us this week.
“Manzambi has a small injury, he’s not available for tomorrow. Aaron has an injury as well, more or less we expect three or four weeks.”
The Spaniard added: “We have enough players, no excuses, and tomorrow we’ll find solutions in case we need to get our performance, of course, collectively and individually in each position.”
Villa thrashed Fenerbahce 6-0 last week and will be looking for a third successive European win when they host Viking.
But the Norwegian side arrive at Villa Park buoyed by a 3-3 draw with German giants Bayern Munich last week.
“Every team that plays Champions League because they deserve it, and they are dangerous,” said Emery.
“Viking drew against Bayern Munich last week, they lost against Stuttgart. They are with Bodo/Glimt in the league first and second with the same points.
“Viking are a new team as well with the capacity to draw with Bayern Munich and compete against Stuttgart and compete against us tomorrow. This is the Champions League and it is very difficult.”

title: Pakistan approves new auto policy, rejects IMF proposal
text:
Pakistan approves new auto policy, rejects IMF proposal to raise EV sales tax
- By Web Desk -
- Oct 20, 2026
According to the policy document, the government has set a target of increasing vehicle exports to $6 billion. The policy also includes measures to increase the production of locally manufactured auto parts, improve technology and gradually reduce import duties on vehicles.
The government has rejected the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) proposal to increase sales tax on electric vehicles (EVs) to 18 per cent.
However, the policy proposes a 10 per cent federal excise duty on electric vehicles valued at more than $75,000.
Electric vehicle taxes and financing
Under the new policy, sales tax on battery electric vehicles will remain at one per cent from 2026 to 2031. Range-extended electric vehicles will face a six per cent sales tax, while plug-in hybrid vehicles will be subject to a nine per cent rate.
The policy also proposes reducing import duties on electric vehicles in phases. Lower tariffs have been proposed for small electric vehicles valued below $15,000.
The financing limit for electric vehicles is set to increase from Rs3 million to Rs10 million, while the maximum financing period will be extended from three to five years.
The policy aims to make smaller vehicles more accessible to low-income consumers. Sales tax on electric vehicles will be reduced gradually until 2031, according to the policy document.
Export targets and incentives for manufacturers
The government has set a target of increasing auto parts exports to $1.2 billion by fiscal year 2030-31.
Under the proposed framework, vehicle manufacturers will have mandatory export targets. Companies meeting the requirements will be eligible for compensation equal to five per cent of their export value. An additional 10 per cent incentive has been proposed for exports above the previous year’s level.
Companies that fail to meet their export targets will face penalties. Manufacturers that miss their targets for two consecutive years could have their manufacturing certificates cancelled.
The policy also sets new targets to increase the use and production of locally manufactured auto parts. Companies that fail to meet local production targets could lose their incentives.
To improve competition, tariffs in the automotive sector are to be reduced to 15 per cent by 2030-31.
Automotive Development Levy and industrial growth
The policy proposes an Automotive Development Levy on vehicles with engine capacities above 1,000cc.
The government estimates that the levy could generate more than Rs232 billion over five years. The funds are proposed to support export incentives, industrial development programmes and technology upgrades for auto parts manufacturers.
The policy also proposes allocating funds for the technological development of local auto parts manufacturers.
Legislation related to the Automotive Development Levy is targeted for completion by December 2026.
Safety standards and consumer protection
The new policy proposes establishing the Pakistan Automotive Testing Institute to support research, certification and independent audits in the automotive sector.
Global safety standards are proposed for both locally manufactured and imported vehicles. Vehicle manufacturers will also be required to include consumer protection provisions in their agreements with buyers.
The policy proposes two audits each year to improve transparency in the sector. Payments for local production and export incentives will be subject to third-party audits.
It also sets new targets for training skilled workers to meet the automotive industry’s requirements.
The policy is intended to increase domestic production, expand exports and improve the competitiveness of Pakistan’s automotive industry over the next five years.

title: New study shows how fair river water sharing boosts the economy
text:
New study shows how fair river water sharing boosts the economy during droughts
- By Kumail Shah -
- Oct 20, 2026
Freshwater rivers support daily needs such as household plumbing, industrial operations, and farming. However, severe droughts often strain these important waterways.
Upstream communities get first access to flowing water, so their usual withdrawals can leave downstream areas with little water during dry periods. Even if everyone follows the rules, those farther downstream often face serious shortages because of their location.
A recent study in Water Resources Research shows that flexible water-sharing plans can help stretch limited supplies. Jiheun Kim, a Ph.D. researcher at North Carolina State University, led a team that studied almost thirty years of water data from the Yeongsan River Basin in southwestern South Korea.
Rather than using the same conservation cuts for everyone, the team tested a system where water limits get stricter for upstream and midstream users as droughts get worse. In the most severe cases, withdrawals would stop completely.
Limiting water use helps downstream communities, but it can hurt upstream farmers and factory workers. The researchers wanted to see if the overall economic benefits of better water access downstream could make up for the losses upstream.
Their computer models showed that working together with these restrictions raised the total economic value in the river basin by about 4 million USD. Water managers could use this extra value to encourage upstream users to cooperate, either by lowering their utility fees or giving them financial help during droughts.
But the study also found that trying to split water exactly equally can cause problems. If some groups have to give up too much, they may not want to take part.
The researchers also tested what happens when water demand goes up and less water is released from farm reservoirs. In these tough situations, the system did not work as well. The economic benefits got smaller, so there was not enough money to fully repay upstream users for what they gave up.
Since these results come from computer models and not real-world tests, putting them into practice would need careful tracking of water use, clear laws, and agreement from local people to accept payments.
In the end, the research shows that getting through water shortages takes more than just saving water. It calls for smart, cooperative sharing so that every community gets what it needs.

title: Disney explores Star Wars Battlefront 3 development with Bungie
text:
Disney explores Star Wars Battlefront 3 development with Bungie and EA DICE
- By Kumail Shah -
- Oct 20, 2026
Fans have been waiting for a sequel to Star Wars Battlefront II since 2017, and now there are signs of progress. US gaming magazine Electronic Gaming Monthly (EGM) reports that Disney is very interested in a third game and is already searching for a development studio.
Two well-known studios are in the running: EA DICE and Bungie. This information comes from the “Quartermann” rumor column in EGM issue 265, published on October 9. Gaming journalist Jeff Grubb talked about this on his Game Mess Mornings podcast on October 19. At 22:42 in the episode, Grubb reads the Battlefront report.
Most fans probably expected DICE to be considered, since the Swedish studio made Star Wars Battlefront (2015) and Battlefront II (2017). Bungie is a more surprising option. Known for Halo and Destiny, Bungie is now owned by Sony and has mostly worked on its own games lately. Taking on an EA series would be a new direction for them.
Because of Bungie’s financial struggles, Jeff Grubb thinks it is possible the studio could get involved. Sony recently took big losses on Bungie and announced major layoffs in June 2026. Working on a well-known franchise like Star Wars could give Bungie new opportunities. Still, Grubb believes DICE is more likely to be chosen.
News about Battlefront 3 has excited fans on Reddit, but the two possible developers are getting mixed reactions. Reports say both Bungie and DICE have lost many experienced staff in recent years and have changed a lot. However, Bungie still gets praise for the great gunplay in the Destiny games.
Some fans would love to see a Battlefront game with shooting mechanics as satisfying as Destiny’s. It is still unclear if or when Star Wars Battlefront 3 will happen. EGM says that so far, neither studio has officially agreed to make the game.

title: Apple iPhone Duo foldable screen shows soft crease in early customer testing

- By Kumail Shah -

The Apple iPhone Duo will officially start shipping on Friday, October 23. Still, a few customers managed to get the first foldable iPhone a bit earlier.
A hands-on video below shows that Apple has not completely fixed the “crease problem,” even though early reports from the launch event suggested it was solved.
The Apple iPhone Duo uses a different approach than its competitors. The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 ($1,699 on Amazon) has a flexible but hard surface made with “Ultra Thin Glass.” In contrast, Apple uses a softer cover that is cheaper to replace if it gets scratched.
The video below shows that this hinge and display design makes the foldable screen especially soft just above the hinge.
If you run your finger across this area, the crease is easy to see and can even be felt. But when the display is untouched, the crease is hardly noticeable.
It is not clear how this design will hold up over time. On many foldable phones, the crease in the middle of the screen gets more noticeable the more the phone is folded and unfolded.
The official shipping start on Friday will likely bring more videos showing the Apple iPhone Duo’s display crease in detail. Until then, no final conclusions should be drawn.
