title: Russia slams Florida arrest warrant for Cuba's Raul Castro
text:
Russia slams Florida arrest warrant for Cuba's Raul Castro
- By AFP -
- Oct 20, 2026
Moscow on Tuesday slammed a Florida arrest warrant issued for former Cuban president Raul Castro under state murder charges, denouncing the accusations against him as “baseless and contrived”.
Raul Castro, 95, is wanted on murder charges connected to the February 24, 1996, shooting down of two civilian aircraft from “Brothers to the Rescue,” an organisation assisting Cubans fleeing to Florida by sea.
“Raul Castro ordered the murder of four Floridians in cold blood, and Florida will never stop pursuing accountability for that communist conspiracy,” Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier said in a statement.
Castro, brother of the late revolutionary leader and US nemesis Fidel Castro, was indicted on federal charges related to the incident in May.
Russia, a close ally of Cuba since the Soviet era, said in a statement that it “categorically rejected and strongly condemned” the Florida arrest warrant, and reaffirmed Moscow’s “unwavering solidarity” with the island nation.
“Bringing a baseless and contrived accusation more than 30 years after the events can only be seen as an act of vengeance by the anti-Cuban lobby in Miami,” its foreign ministry charged.
The Florida arrest warrant came as President Donald Trump’s right-wing administration steadily ramped up economic, political and legal pressure on the Cuban communist government.
Trump previously seized on a US indictment to justify military action in January that toppled Venezuela’s then-president Nicolas Maduro, a staunch ally of the Cuban authorities.
Current Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel has said the US federal indictment against Castro has “no legal basis” and was an attempt “to justify the folly of a military aggression against Cuba.”

title: Pakistan, US discuss advancing bilateral trade agreement
text:
Pakistan, United States discuss advancing bilateral trade agreement
- By Shoaib Nizami -
- Oct 20, 2026
Islamabad – October 20, 2026: Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan held a meeting with United States Chargé d’Affaires Natalie A. Baker to discuss strengthening bilateral economic relations, accelerating ongoing trade agreement negotiations, expanding market access and exploring new opportunities for cooperation in agriculture, minerals, technology and investment.
Rana Ihsaan Afzal Khan, Coordinator to the Prime Minister on Commerce and Industries, Secretary Commerce Jawad Paul and senior officials of the Ministry of Commerce also attended the meeting.
Welcoming the U.S. delegation, Federal Minister Jam Kamal Khan emphasized the importance Pakistan attaches to its longstanding economic partnership with the United States. He said both countries possess considerable potential to expand bilateral trade through enhanced market access, greater private-sector engagement and investment in emerging sectors.
The Minister highlighted Pakistan’s efforts to diversify its export markets and strengthen international commercial partnerships despite prevailing regional and global economic challenges. He said deeper economic engagement with the United States could create new opportunities for businesses, enhance industrial competitiveness and contribute to sustainable economic growth.
Both sides reviewed progress on the ongoing Pakistan–U.S. bilateral reciprocal trade agreement negotiations and expressed their commitment to advancing discussions towards a mutually beneficial outcome.
Secretary Commerce Jawad Paul, while briefing the meeting on the status of negotiations, informed that substantial progress had been achieved on several important provisions of the proposed agreement. A few technical points need to be discussed with the USTR.
The meeting also discussed market access opportunities for Pakistani agricultural products, particularly mangoes and dates. Secretary Commerce Jawad Paul highlighted the need to expedite the visit of relevant U.S. inspection teams for mango export arrangements and sought progress on the pending market access process for Pakistani dates. He emphasized that greater access to the U.S. market would create valuable export opportunities, particularly for growers and businesses in Balochistan.
The U.S. delegation welcomed the discussion and indicated its willingness to follow up with the relevant American authorities on these matters. Both sides also explored opportunities to enhance agricultural trade, particularly U.S. exports of cotton and soybeans to Pakistan.
Secretary Commerce Jawad Paul highlighted the importance of competitive pricing and trade financing in facilitating greater imports from the United States. Discussions included possible financing arrangements and closer coordination with relevant trade institutions and industry associations to strengthen bilateral agricultural commerce.
Federal Minister Jam Kamal Khan underlined Pakistan’s significant potential in agriculture, food processing, livestock and value-added production. He encouraged American companies to explore investment opportunities in modern agricultural machinery, food processing technologies, cold-chain infrastructure and improved farming practices.
The Minister also invited American businesses and agricultural organizations to participate in FoodAg 2026, scheduled to be held in Karachi from November 23 to 26. He said the exhibition would provide an important platform to connect international buyers and investors with Pakistan’s growing agricultural and food-processing industries.
The U.S. Chargé d’Affaires appreciated Pakistan’s efforts to promote agricultural trade and expressed interest in facilitating greater engagement between American agricultural technology companies and Pakistani businesses.
Highlighting Balochistan’s economic potential, Jam Kamal Khan identified dates, olive oil and other agricultural products as promising areas for value addition and export development. He said international cooperation could help improve processing facilities, product quality, packaging and access to global markets, while creating opportunities for small enterprises, farmers and women entrepreneurs.
Minerals and mining also featured prominently in the discussions, with both sides exploring opportunities for investment, technical cooperation, skills development and responsible resource development.
The U.S. delegation conveyed continued interest in strengthening cooperation in Pakistan’s mineral sector, including opportunities for American companies to contribute technical expertise, investment and commercial partnerships.
The Minister also highlighted the industrial potential of Hub, Balochistan, noting its strategic proximity to Karachi and opportunities for investment in manufacturing, industrial infrastructure and special economic zones. He welcomed the existing presence of American companies in Pakistan and encouraged further private-sector investment.
During the discussion on regional trade connectivity, Secretary Commerce Jawad Paul highlighted challenges arising from disruptions to traditional land trade routes, particularly those connecting Pakistan with Afghanistan and Central Asian markets.
He observed that uninterrupted regional connectivity, predictable trade arrangements and efficient logistics were essential for sustaining export growth and maintaining long-term commercial relationships.
Federal Minister Jam Kamal Khan emphasized that Pakistan remained committed to strengthening its economic resilience, improving the business environment and expanding trade opportunities while taking into consideration broader regional developments.
Both sides acknowledged the importance of continued institutional dialogue, stronger business-to-business contacts and practical cooperation in promoting shared economic interests.
Concluding the meeting, Federal Minister Jam Kamal Khan reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to developing a forward-looking economic partnership with the United States, based on mutual respect, shared opportunities and sustainable commercial growth.
U.S. Chargé d’Affaires Natalie A. Baker appreciated the constructive discussions and reiterated the United States’ interest in expanding economic engagement with Pakistan, particularly in trade, agriculture, technology and investment.
Both sides agreed to maintain close coordination to advance ongoing trade negotiations, address market access issues and explore new opportunities for mutually beneficial economic cooperation.

title: Mir Raza case: Commission recommends JIT under DIG Irfan Baloch
text:
Mir Raza case: Commission recommends JIT with ISI, Rangers, NCCIA representatives
- By Sanjay Sadhwani -
- Oct 20, 2026
KARACHI: The judicial commission investigating the death of Mir Raza Ali has raised serious questions about the police investigation, the handling of medical and digital evidence, and the initial conclusion that he died by suicide. The commission has recommended a new joint investigation team (JIT) to conduct a comprehensive investigation into all aspects of his death.
The 70-page report, headed by Justice Umar Sial, was submitted to the Sindh chief minister on October 15. The commission held 20 meetings between August 27 and October 7 and recorded statements from 50 witnesses.
According to the report, the police initially declared Mir Raza’s death a suicide on the basis of the preliminary post-mortem report. His family challenged that conclusion, citing marks of violence on his body and other evidence.
The police surgeon identified shortcomings in the initial post-mortem report and recommended another examination. Mir Raza’s body was re-examined on August 8. The final report identified a bullet wound entering from the back as the cause of death.
The commission said it was not appropriate to conclude that the death was a suicide while ignoring contradictions in the medical evidence. It criticised the police for maintaining their initial position despite conflicting medical findings and failing to meet basic investigative requirements.
JIT recommended to investigate all aspects of death
The commission recommended that the Sindh government establish a JIT to investigate all aspects of Mir Raza’s death. Representatives of the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Rangers and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) should be included in the team.
It also called for further investigation into possible blackmailing or a revenge killing. The commission stressed that the available material was not sufficient to reach a final conclusion about an organised cover-up or criminal responsibility.
The report recommended further investigation into suspicious vehicles and individuals present at a guest house. It also raised questions about the leadership and supervision of DIG Amir Farooqi and DIG Farukh Ali Lanjar.
Police criticised over digital evidence
The commission raised serious concerns about the handling of CCTV footage, mobile phones, an Apple Watch and other digital evidence.
According to the report, police failed to take important CCTV recordings into legal custody through the proper procedure. Instead, footage displayed on monitors was recorded using mobile phones. The original digital video recorders were not secured in accordance with legal requirements.
The report also identified gaps in the record of evidence transfers and noted that some actions were not entered in the daily police diary. Police statements about obtaining and preserving footage contained contradictions.
The commission questioned the procedures used to take custody of the phone, obtain digital data and access information stored on the Apple Watch. Attempts to enter unauthorised passcodes made the phone’s data inaccessible and caused difficulties in retrieving information from the watch, affecting the investigation.
It also questioned how some digital evidence reached the media. The commission asked why private messages and financial information were disclosed, potentially damaging the family’s reputation.
Financial difficulties not enough to establish cause of death
The commission examined the police position that Mir Raza’s alleged financial difficulties could have led him to die by suicide.
The report said the police referred to statements from creditors and business partners regarding outstanding liabilities. However, the commission stressed that financial problems alone do not establish that a person would die by suicide or that financial pressure was the cause of death.
It said the available material did not justify treating financial difficulties as the definitive cause. The commission called for an independent investigation into Mir Raza’s behaviour and circumstances despite the reported financial pressure.
A message to Sarem bin Tahir referring to Rs30 million was also mentioned in the report. The commission treated the possibility of blackmail as a matter requiring further investigation.
Dr Osama Sheikh’s conduct criticised
The judicial commission strongly criticised medico-legal officer Dr Osama Sheikh, describing his conduct as extremely immature, childish and unprofessional. The report said his behaviour was not appropriate for a medical professional.
The commission recommended that Dr Osama should not be assigned medico-legal duties for at least two years and should undergo proper academic and practical training before being given such responsibilities again.
It also observed that his conduct gave the impression that he might have been acting under someone’s influence.
The commission’s observations came amid questions over the initial post-mortem report prepared by Dr Osama, which was later challenged over discrepancies in the medical findings. The final post-mortem report identified a bullet wound entering from the back as the cause of Mir Raza Ali’s death.
The commission also praised head clerk Zeeshan for his conduct, describing him as the only police official who brought credit to the Sindh Police in the case. It recommended that he receive recognition and further training.
Questions over changes to the medical board
The commission also questioned the sudden change in the medical board constituted to examine Mir Raza’s body.
According to the report, an eight-member board was formed under Karachi Police Surgeon Dr. Summaiya Syed. On August 7, the health department reduced its membership to five and included doctors from Hyderabad and Jamshoro. The family rejected the revised composition.
The change delayed the process of exhuming the body. Following public pressure and a legal notice, the original eight-member board was restored, and the examination was completed on August 8.
The commission described the sudden change as unusual, unclear and legally questionable. It also raised questions about the role of the relevant health department officials.
Commission examines August 9 meeting at Chief Minister’s House
The report also discussed a meeting held at the Chief Minister’s House on August 9, which prompted speculation about its purpose.
The commission said it found no evidence that the meeting was intended to pressure Dr Osama Sheikh or secure a report favouring the police. It acknowledged that the chief minister had the authority to receive a briefing on a matter of significant public interest.
However, the commission said inviting the police surgeon to the meeting would have been appropriate in the interests of transparency.
Action recommended against police officials
The commission criticised the performance of several police officers and recommended departmental and criminal proceedings where warranted.
It recommended a comprehensive inquiry against SHO Adeel Afzal, along with his interim suspension. Departmental action and interim suspension were also recommended against Sub-Inspector Shabbir Laghari.
The commission further recommended departmental action against SHO Kamran Qureshi and his removal from the post.
The report called for further scrutiny of the relevant health department officials and an investigation into the possible loss of important evidence.
The commission said shortcomings in the initial police response and subsequent investigation had damaged public confidence. It warned that serious failures in preserving evidence could affect legal proceedings.
It stressed that further investigation was necessary to establish responsibility and examine the possibility of a cover-up or other criminal conduct. The commission said justice and the restoration of public trust would remain difficult without addressing the identified failures.

title: Petrol prices determined on seven-day average, NA told
text:
Petrol prices determined on seven-day average, NA told
- By Azhar Farooq -
- Oct 20, 2026
ISLAMABAD: Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik said on Tuesday that petroleum prices were determined under a transparent formula based on a seven-day average.
Responding to a calling attention notice regarding the daily determination of petroleum prices instead of the previous fortnightly mechanism, the minister said the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) calculated prices based on the seven-day average. He added that the authority had also published the formula on its website.
Referring to the history of petroleum price revisions, Ali Pervaiz Malik said prices had previously been revised annually, before the practice shifted to monthly and later fortnightly adjustments.
He said Pakistan imported all its oil requirements, while volatility in international markets made it necessary for the government to ensure an uninterrupted supply chain and prevent profiteering and hoarding.
The minister said keeping domestic petroleum prices aligned with international market rates helped reflect global price fluctuations in the local market. The approach also helped maintain supply chain security, he added.
He said international oil price trends generally became clearer after three to four days, indicating whether prices were moving upwards or downwards. The existing pricing mechanism had helped improve fuel availability at petrol pumps and reduce difficulties faced by consumers, he added.

Ali Pervaiz Malik said the government had introduced the seven-day average mechanism to address supply-related issues and ensure the availability of petroleum products across the country.

title: UK defence bosses' homes targeted by pro-Palestinian group
text:
UK defence bosses' homes targeted by pro-Palestinian group
- By AFP -
- Oct 20, 2026
London: UK police said they were probing vandalism incidents after a pro-Palestinian group appeared to claim attacks on properties belonging to executives and employees at defence industry firms.
The group called “The List” claimed on a website to have been behind three attacks in recent weeks, including one on the home of someone who they said was a “key engineer” at defence contractor Leonardo.
“We are aware of an incident which targeted the property of a Leonardo employee last weekend,” a company spokesperson said in a statement sent to AFP on Monday.
“We are also assisting Counter Terrorism Police with their ongoing investigation into this incident,” they added.
Police Scotland confirmed officers were called on October 11 to a “report of vandalism to a property and cars” in Dunfermline, north of Edinburgh, where Leonardo has a site.
A video on the group’s website appears to show an individual tagging vehicles and the walls of a building with red paint.
The Sunday Times reported that The List had targeted three locations, including in Hampshire in southern England, where they reportedly slashed the tyres of a car belonging to an executive at Ultra Intelligence & Communications.
The List claimed on its website to have targeted the chief operating officer of Ultra, which it accused of working with Israeli arms company Elbit.
“We were called on Saturday, October 10, to a report of a criminal damage incident in Fleet,” Hampshire police said in a statement quoted by the Times.
Read Also: French EU lawmaker throws Israeli flag on the floor
“It was reported that red paint had been thrown across the front of the house and two car tyres had been damaged,” the police force added.
The group also said it targeted the home of the director of technology manufacturing firm Keysight.
The Palestine Action group was proscribed as a “terrorist” organisation by the UK government last year after a series of attacks targeting defence companies, including Elbit and Leonardo.
On its website, The List said it “escalated our actions against the home addresses of some of the most highly complicit companies in the ongoing genocide of our brothers and sisters in Palestine.”
“Our list of complicit actors remains long, compiled through leaks, hacking and whistleblowers. If you work with Elbit, expect us,” the group added.
Launched in retaliation for Hamas’s deadly October 7, 2023 attacks, Israel’s war in Gaza has killed more than 74,000 people, according to the territory’s health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
Israel has repeatedly denied accusations of genocide.

- Oct 20, 2026
Cairo: Israeli settler attacks risk setting off an “explosion” in the occupied West Bank, a senior Palestinian leader told AFP, while urging that the response remain peaceful.
Jibril Rajoub, the secretary general of the central committee of the Palestinian Authority’s ruling Fatah faction, said he called for “peaceful confrontation” as he took part in meetings in Cairo with other Palestinian movements including Gaza-based rival Hamas, which led the October 7, 2023 attacks against Israel.
“The terrorism carried out by the army and settlers, under the supervision of the Israeli government… is a prelude to a coming reaction and explosion,” Rajoub told AFP in Cairo.
But he said that a “peaceful, nonviolent struggle is a necessity and a strategic choice for all Palestinians”.
“Bloodshed is no longer an acceptable option,” he said, calling for “peaceful confrontation with the occupation, despite the crimes it commits”.
Settlers have carried out daily physical attacks, thefts and other attacks against Palestinians, with the violence intensifying in the run-up to October 27 elections, in which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, governing with the fiercely pro-settlement far-right, is seeking a new mandate.
Violence has picked up as extremist settlers seek to stop the Palestinian olive harvest, an annual season with cultural resonance for the community.
More than 500,000 Israelis live in West Bank settlements, which are considered illegal under international law, surrounded by around three million Palestinians.
The talks in Cairo came after Palestinian leader Mahmoud Abbas, who has ruled since 2005, delayed elections slated to start next month until September 2027.
Rajoub said the talks called for “unified political representation” with the principle of a “single authority” and “only one legitimate armed force”.
Read Also: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats, beat French mayor
Hamas took over Gaza in 2007, dividing the two Palestinian territories. Israel has vowed to obliterate Hamas after the October 7, 2023 attack, the deadliest day in Israel’s history. The Hamas attack resulted in 1,221 deaths.
At least 1,125 Palestinians have died in the West Bank since October 2023, mostly by the Israeli military, according to an AFP tally based on Palestinian health ministry figures.
Settler attacks have killed 23 Palestinians in that timeframe, according to the United Nations.
Palestinian attacks have killed at least 49 Israelis in the same period, according to Israeli figures.
In Gaza, the Israeli offensive has killed 74,459 Palestinians since October 2023, according to figures under the health ministry run under Hamas. The United Nations generally considers the figures reliable.

title: Israel kills four people including a married couple in Gaza
text:
Israel kills four people including a married couple in Gaza
- By Reuters -
- Oct 20, 2026
CAIRO: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least four Palestinians, including a married couple and a 17-year-old, in separate incidents in the Gaza Strip on Tuesday, health officials said.
Medics said an Israeli airstrike killed Akram Yassin and his wife Dina Abu Baker in an apartment in Gaza City.
In Khan Younis, in the south, medics said a 17-year-old boy was killed by Israeli gunfire near the Qizan Al-Najar neighbourhood, while another was killed by Israeli gunfire in the Zeitoun suburb east of Gaza City, taking Tuesday’s death toll to at least four.
The Israeli military did not immediately comment on either of the two gunfire incidents.
Palestinians inspected the aftermath of the strike on the apartment in Gaza City before gathering for the couple’s funeral.
“We’re supposed to be in a ceasefire period, but honestly, we are not seeing a ceasefire or anything. The war is still going on, assassinations are continuing, and the shelling has not stopped,” said Mahmoud Yassin, whose brother was killed.
Israel, which says the Hamas group has been rearming and launching attacks in violation of the ceasefire, has stepped up strikes on the group in recent weeks.
Hamas has denied trying to carry out attacks or rebuild its arsenal and accuses Israel of undermining the Gaza peace deal.
The ceasefire, brokered by the US a year ago, calls for the eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made towards implementing a deal to end the conflict that includes terms for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops.
Gaza health officials have said at least 1,500 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli fire since the ceasefire. Israel says four of its soldiers have been killed by militants in Gaza over the same period.
Read Also: Gaza teen amputees recount hopes, lost dreams in Jordan centre

title: Pakistan pays Rs490bn in interest on domestic, foreign debt
text:
Pakistan pays Rs490bn in interest on domestic, foreign debt
- By Azhar Farooq -
- Oct 20, 2026
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan paid Rs490bn in interest on domestic and foreign debt during the first nine months of the last fiscal year, highlighting the growing burden of debt servicing on the national exchequer, according to documents submitted to the National Assembly.
The Ministry of Finance sumitted the documents, also detailing the utilisation of foreign loans and the progress of major development projects being financed through external borrowing.
A significant portion of foreign loans was used to support the balance of payments and provide cash support, with $11.42 billion allocated for these purposes, according to the documents.
The government also utilised $3.09 billion in foreign loans for energy projects and $1.69 billion for flood rehabilitation.
According to the Ministry of Finance, 14 major national projects are being financed through external borrowing. Seven major projects under the Ministry of Energy are also being developed with foreign loans.
Read Also: Aurangzeb calls for taxpayer trust, policy stability to encourage private investment
The documents revealed that the $3.38 billion Saudi Oil Facility programme was being financed through external borrowing. In addition, a $2 billion International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation (ITFC) oil and LNG financing programme was supported through borrowed funds.
Several major energy and infrastructure projects are also being financed through foreign loans. These include $247.6 million for the Jamshoro power project, $475 million for the Tarbela extension project, $225 million for the Dasu hydropower project and $93.22 million for the Mohmand Dam project.
The Transmission Modernisation Project is also being financed through an external loan of $192.87 million, the documents stated.
Other projects being supported through foreign borrowing include the Sukkur-Multan Motorway and the Karachi Mobility Project.
The documents further disclosed that a $1.5 billion Building Resilience programme was among the initiatives supported by external financing. Projects relating to higher education, climate change and natural disaster management are also being financed through foreign loans.
The total value of the 14 major projects being implemented with external financing stands at $11.86 billion, according to the Ministry of Finance.

title: Nawaz, Minhas propel Pakistan to fighting total
text:
Nawaz, Minhas propel Pakistan to fighting total
- By Web Desk -
- Oct 20, 2026
Hasan Nawaz and Arafat Minhas struck counterattacking half-centuries as Pakistan posted 302-9 against England in the second match of the ODI tri-series at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Tuesday.
After being put in to bat by England captain Harry Brook, Pakistan endured a difficult start as both openers departed inside the first six overs, leaving the hosts struggling at 31-2.
Experienced batter Babar Azam attempted to steady the innings alongside youngster Saad Baig, who had made his ODI debut against Sri Lanka in the tournament opener. The pair added 28 runs before Babar departed for a cautious 34 off 52 deliveries.
Baig then combined with Salman Ali Agha, who failed to capitalise on his start and was dismissed for 16.
With Pakistan under pressure, Hasan Nawaz walked in and immediately adopted an aggressive approach to shift the momentum in the hosts’ favour.
The right-handed batter dominated a 52-run partnership for the fifth wicket, contributing 31 runs before Baig’s innings came to an end. The young wicketkeeper-batter departed after scoring 35 off 54 deliveries.
Nawaz subsequently found support from Arafat Minhas as the duo launched a crucial recovery, adding 78 runs off 74 balls for the sixth wicket. Their partnership helped Pakistan cross the 200-run mark and laid the foundation for a competitive total.
However, Nawaz’s entertaining innings ended when England pacer Jamie Overton produced a perfectly executed yorker to dismantle his stumps. The 24-year-old departed after scoring 79 off 74 balls, an innings featuring five fours and four sixes.
Following his dismissal, Minhas joined forces with Faheem Ashraf, and the pair maintained Pakistan’s scoring momentum during the closing stages.
The two all-rounders stitched together a brisk 72-run partnership off just 49 deliveries for the seventh wicket, putting England’s bowlers under further pressure.
During the partnership, Minhas brought up his maiden ODI half-century, continuing his impressive contribution with the bat. The left-handed batter eventually fell to Sonny Baker after scoring 59 off 58 deliveries, including nine boundaries.
Faheem, meanwhile, played an aggressive cameo of 39 runs off 26 balls, smashing five fours and a six before being dismissed by Sam Curran in the penultimate over.
Haris Rauf struck a boundary on the final delivery of the innings as Pakistan finished with 302-9 in their allotted 50 overs, setting England a target of 303 runs.
For England, Sonny Baker was the pick of the bowlers with figures of 3-65, while Gus Atkinson claimed two wickets for 35 runs. Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Adil Rashid and Sam Curran chipped in with one wicket apiece.

title: Driver arrested after viral assault on female TikToker in Lahore

Driver arrested after viral assault on female TikToker in Lahore

title: Swiatek pulls out of Ningbo Open with thigh injury
text:
Swiatek pulls out of Ningbo Open with thigh injury
- By AFP -
- Oct 20, 2026
Iga Swiatek has withdrawn injured from the Ningbo Open, where she had hoped to earn vital points towards qualifying for the year-end WTA Finals, tournament organisers announced on Tuesday.
The Polish player, ranked ninth in the race to the Finals ahead of this week’s 500-level event in China, is battling it out with seventh-placed Karolina Muchova and 10th-placed Marta Kostyuk for the eighth and final berth at the tournament.
This season’s Finals will take place at Indian Wells on November 8–15.
Czech Muchova is not competing this week, while Ukrainian Kostyuk is seeded third in Ningbo.
“After careful consideration, I’ve decided to withdraw from the tournament,” six-time Grand Slam winner Swiatek said in a statement released by the tournament.
“I’ve been experiencing an ongoing problem with my left thigh over the past weeks and I feel that giving myself the time to rest and recover is the right decision.”
The 25-year-old was hampered by the same thigh issue during her defeat last week in the semi-finals in Wuhan against her compatriot Maja Chwalinska, who went on to win the title.
Swiatek is replaced in the draw in Ningbo by Russia’s Anastasia Zakharova.

title: Gold prices fall in Pakistan as rising oil prices fuel inflation concerns
text:
Gold prices fall in Pakistan as rising oil prices fuel inflation concerns
- By Anjum Wahab -
- Oct 20, 2026
KARACHI: Gold prices declined in Pakistan on Tuesday, tracking losses in international bullion markets as rising oil prices heightened inflation concerns.
The price of 24-karat gold per tola fell by Rs3,600 to Rs435,436, according to rates issued by the All Pakistan Sarafa Gems and Jewellers Association (APSGJA).
Similarly, the price of 24-karat gold per 10 grams decreased by Rs3,086 to Rs373,316, while 10-gram gold of 22-karat purity declined by Rs2,829 to Rs342,218.
In the international market, gold prices dropped by $36 to $4,129 per ounce, the association reported.
Meanwhile, silver prices remained unchanged in the domestic market, with the price per tola standing at Rs6,234 and 10 grams at Rs5,344. International silver prices also remained stable at $57.56 per ounce.
Rising energy costs have added to concerns about persistent inflation, potentially limiting the Federal Reserve’s ability to ease monetary policy.
Read More: Oil majors face spending test from Iran war windfall cash
“Persistent inflationary pressures, driven by high energy prices, continue to support expectations of further monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve,” said Ricardo Evangelista, director and CEO of ActivTrades.
Oil prices advanced on Tuesday, with Brent crude hovering near a five-month high as traders factored in geopolitical risks stemming from Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf.
Gold is traditionally regarded as a hedge against inflation and a safe-haven asset during periods of economic and geopolitical uncertainty. A weaker US dollar can also make gold more affordable for buyers using other currencies, potentially supporting demand.
However, traditional safe-haven assets have delivered mixed performance amid this year’s market volatility. Concerns over the Iran war, elevated energy prices, uncertainty surrounding technology stocks linked to artificial intelligence, and mounting government debt have contributed to market uncertainty.
Despite gold’s traditional appeal during periods of instability, prices came under pressure following the outbreak of the Iran war as investors sold previously strong-performing assets to cover losses elsewhere. Government bonds, traditionally viewed as among the safest investments, have also experienced heightened volatility.

title: Sindh cabinet decides to make Mir Raza Judicial Commission report public
text:
Sindh cabinet decides to make Mir Raza Judicial Commission report public
- By Sanjay Sadhwani -
- Oct 20, 2026
KARACHI: The Sindh Cabinet has decided to make the judicial commission probe report regarding the Mir Raza case public, ARY News reported.
The decision was made during a cabinet meeting chaired by Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah at the Chief Minister’s House today.
The cabinet decided to publicize the report prepared by the judicial commission led by Justice Umar Sial and instructed that it be uploaded to the Home Department’s website today.
In addition, CM Murad Ali Shah formed a special committee to ensure the implementation of the report’s recommendations. The committee comprises Home Minister Zia-ul-Hassan Lanjar, Nasir Hussain Shah, Saeed Ghani, and the Advocate General of Sindh.
The Chief Minister also directed authorities to immediately provide a copy of the probe report to the family of Mir Raza.
The reported was presented before the cabinet from seven different envelops.
Earlier yesterday, the father of slain entrepreneur Mir Raza demanded the formation of a Joint Investigation Team (JIT) to probe his son’s murder, ARY News reported.
Speaking to the media outside the court alongside his counsel, advocate Jibran Nasir, Mir Hussain stated that the police had shown negligence in investigating his son’s case, adding that their fears were confirmed by the judicial commission’s findings.
He demanded that Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah and Faryal Talpur hand over the judicial commission’s report to the family and make it public following the cabinet meeting.
He also called for action against the police officers found negligent by the judicial commission, noting that the family had repeatedly highlighted through the media the police’s poor performance, shortcomings, and deficiencies in the investigation.
Furthermore, he stated that the judicial commission’s proceedings had validated their concerns, reiterating his demand for strict action against the responsible police officers.

title: Italy to send 500 troops to Milan after clashes
text:
Italy to send 500 troops to Milan after clashes
- By AFP -
- Oct 20, 2026
ROME: Italy is preparing to send 500 troops to Milan after looting and clashes between police and mostly young protesters, with some luxury brands shutting their shops in the city.
A cabinet meeting on Tuesday is expected to give the go-ahead to the deployment and approve policing powers for soldiers temporarily supporting law enforcement in the city.
Hundreds of protesters were detained during two days of clashes in Milan on Saturday and Sunday and dozens of police officers were injured.
Several shops in the fashion hub were looted. Some shops this week have remained closed or removed window displays and beefed-up security.
More protests are expected on Saturday.
The government is also considering a wider crackdown, including restrictions on public gatherings, easing rules on detention for minors and harsher sanctions for their parents.
Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini called the clashes “shameful” and said on RTL 102.5 radio that the cabinet meeting would announce a series of “immediate measures” including the troop deployment.
Defence Minister Guido Crosetto said on Monday hoped the cabinet meeting would approve provisions for the army “to allow them to act like law enforcement”.
Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Saturday said the violent perpetrators were “thugs who exploit demonstrations to spread chaos, attack those who guarantee security, and hold entire cities hostage.”
“To demonstrate is a right. To lay our cities to waste is not,” she wrote on X.
High school and university students, farmers and truck drivers are leading nationwide protests in Italy, mainly against the rising cost of living.
Hard-right leader Meloni faces elections next year in which the state of the economy, security and immigration are likely to be the key issues.

title: Azma Bokhari wins defamation case against Moeen Qureshi
text:
Azma Bokhari wins defamation case against Moeen Qureshi
- By Abid Khan -
- Oct 20, 2026
LAHORE: Punjab Information and Culture Minister Azma Bokhari has won a defamation case against Punjab Assembly Opposition Leader Moeen Ud Din Riaz Qureshi, with the Lahore Defamation Tribunal ordering him to pay Rs3 million in damages.
The tribunal issued a brief written judgment in the case, directing Qureshi to pay Rs3 million to the provincial minister over allegations he made against her during a television programme.
Bokhari had filed a defamation suit against Qureshi, seeking Rs840 million in damages, alleging that he had made baseless and fabricated accusations that damaged her reputation and credibility.
The case stemmed from remarks Qureshi made following the visit of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to the Punjab Assembly.
Qureshi had alleged that Bokhari facilitated the entry of 150 to 200 paid individuals into the provincial assembly during the visit. He also claimed that journalists who questioned Afridi were paid employees of the provincial information minister.
According to the tribunal’s judgment, Qureshi admitted that he had made the statements during a television programme but failed to produce evidence substantiating his allegations. The tribunal further observed that his lawyers could not establish the claims during their arguments.
Bokhari approached the Lahore Defamation Tribunal in January 2026 under Section 3 of the Punjab Defamation Act 2024, seeking damages over the allegedly defamatory remarks.
Her petition stated that the allegations had been broadcast on television and circulated on social media, including through the official Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) social media account, reaching millions of people.
The minister maintained that the statements had seriously harmed her reputation, dignity and credibility.
Afridi visited Lahore on December 26, 2025, for a three-day trip that included political engagements and a visit to the Punjab Assembly. His visit to the provincial legislature was marked by altercations between members of his delegation and security personnel.

title: Sindh schools in dangerous premises directed to stop work

Schools in old buildings directed to stop work in Sindh

title: Bayern set for Arsenal test without red-hot Olise
text:
Bayern set for Arsenal test without red-hot Olise
- By AFP -
- Oct 20, 2026
Champions League hopefuls Bayern Munich are set for an early test of their title credentials when they host English champions Arsenal on Wednesday without in-form winger Michael Olise.
The London-born Olise, who started in Arsenal’s junior system, is suspended after picking up two yellow cards inside a minute in Bayern’s 3-3 draw with Viking last week.
After seeing a first yellow for a foul, a clearly frustrated Olise responded to some verbal provocation from Viking captain Zlatko Tripic by throwing the ball at his head to be sent off for the first time in his career.
After being thrust into Ballon d’Or contention due to last season’s stellar showing, the former Crystal Palace winger has continued his excellent form this campaign.
Olise has nine goals and five assists from 10 games in all competitions for Bayern.
With Jamal Musiala struggling with injury and illness and both Serge Gnabry and Lennart Karl well off their best form, Olise and the ever-reliable Harry Kane have shouldered Bayern’s attacking burden so far this season.
The England captain has nine goals and six assists in 10 games. With Bayern 2-0 down away at Viking last week, Kane almost single-handedly engineered a comeback, scoring twice and setting up another.
Speaking after Bayern’s ruthless 6-1 victory over RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga on Saturday, Kane said Bayern would miss Olise but called on the rest of their star-studded squad to step up.
“Missing one of your biggest players, you’re going to feel it for sure, but that’s where other people have to step up and show they can take their opportunity,” Kane said.
“We talk about the squad a lot, we talk about being ready for your moment and whoever plays will have to be ready.”
One of the many positives to come out of Saturday’s thumping win over Leipzig was the performance of Luis Diaz.
The 29-year-old had cut a frustrated figure after a poor start to the season but scored three goals and set up another in one of his best performances since moving from Liverpool in 2025.
‘One of the best’
Despite swapping north London for the Bavarian capital back in 2023, former Tottenham captain Kane has seen plenty of Arsenal since joining Bayern.
Bayern faced the Gunners in two quarter-final legs in 2023-24, progressing by just a goal, but were outclassed in a 3-1 defeat in the league phase of last year’s competition.
With domestic and international matches coming thick and fast, Kane has not had time to exchange pleasantries with any of his Gunners rivals.
“I spoke to them a bit in the international break previously and we knew the game was coming up, but I think we’re all too busy right now to text each other, with a game every three days,” he explained.
Saturday’s thrashing of Leipzig once again showed the perennial German champions are a cut above their domestic rivals and Kane said Bayern were relishing a chance to take on Mikel Arteta’s side.
Still smarting from last year’s painful loss on penalties to Paris Saint-Germain, Arsenal have started strongly, winning 10 of 11 games in all competitions.
“It’s a big game and we’re playing against one of the best teams in Europe, you have to always enjoy these occasions,” Kane said.
“We’re testing ourselves against one of the best, we’re here at home, the energy, the fans, it’s going to be a special night.”

title: Surgical sponge found in woman’s abdomen after one year of operation
text:
Surgical sponge found in woman’s abdomen after one year of operation
- By Web Desk -

MUZAFFARABAD: Prime Minister of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Iftikhar Ali Gillani has taken notice of a severe medical negligence case at the District Headquarter (DHQ) Hospital in Bagh, ARY News reported.

A committee headed by Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal has also been constituted to oversee administrative reforms at PIMS. The committee includes the law minister, vice chancellors of medical universities and health experts, sources said.

Sources said a special committee has already submitted its report and recommendations regarding PIMS to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

title: Real Madrid's rough Diomande starting to shine as Leipzig visit
text:
Real Madrid's rough Diomande starting to shine as Leipzig visit
- By AFP -
- Oct 20, 2026
When Real Madrid splashed a club record 140 million euros ($157m) to sign Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig this summer, it was because of his clear potential to become one of the game’s stars, as showcased at the 2026 World Cup.
That talent has begun to unveil itself in recent matches, with Diomande lashing in a spectacular strike against Sevilla on Sunday in La Liga ahead of a reencounter with his former side Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday.
Diomande’s sheer potential was not, however, the only reason Madrid forked out.
President Florentino Perez pledged to fans during his campaign for reelection in June that he would pay a fee of that magnitude for a new star as Madrid tried to rebuild following two seasons without a major trophy.
Diomande had demonstrated exciting promise, shining with Leipzig during just one season in Germany after emerging at Spanish side Leganes.
The 19-year-old did not join Madrid to fill an obvious vacancy, with his arrival actually exacerbating an overbooking in attack.
On the same day Diomande’s transfer was announced, Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior signed a new deal until 2032 with Los Blancos.
Madrid struggled last season to find a balance with Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius on the pitch together, let alone throwing a new attacking star carrying a record price tag into the mix.
For a combination of those factors, it should not come as a surprise that Diomande is still finding his footing in the Spanish capital.
The youngster has shown flashes of his great quality, without yet firmly establishing himself as an essential figure for coach Jose Mourinho, although he is improving.
Diomande scored his first goal for the club against Villarreal on October 10, securing Real Madrid a 1-0 win.
The winger’s superb finish was not the main talking point though, after Vinicius was dismissed later in the game and subsequently banned for four matches.
That further opened the door for Diomande to settle in, with the winger starting on the left wing in Sunday’s 4-1 rout of Sevilla, in which he lashed home from long range in the final stages.
Diomande also assisted the opener for Arda Guler, in his best performance for the club thus far. In total he has two goals and three assists in 11 appearances across all competitions.
“He has a lot to improve, he’s young, he’s still naive, he’s still not the finished article,” said Mourinho on Sunday.
“At Real Madrid, the demands are very high… but he had a great game, he’s growing.”
‘I will die trying’
Diamonds form under pressure, and thus far in his career Diomande has handled it on and off the pitch.
He suffered rejection after leaving the Ivory Coast to go to school in Florida in the United States, unable to reach a deal with MLS sides Charlotte FC and Colorado Rapids.
Eventually the winger’s senior debut came with Leganes against Real Madrid in March 2025, and in 10 games for the club he netted twice, earning himself a move to Germany.
Diomande helped Leipzig reach the Champions League with 12 goals and eight assists, and he was named “rookie of the year” in the Bundesliga, before his Madrid move.
The winger said he is spurred on by tragedy from his life. His sister Roxane died at age 15 in 2025 after her drink was spiked, Diomande explained in an open letter, published by The Player’s Tribune in June.
“You were the one who always believed that I could be the next Cristiano (Ronaldo), when everybody else laughed,” wrote Diomande to his late sister.
“You were telling everybody, ‘My brother is going to be the greatest in the world’. I will prove that you were right, or I will die trying.”
At the home of the record 15-time European champions, Diomande has the platform to do that.
“He has to improve his finishing… assist better… but that will come,” added Mourinho.
“I remember when Vinicius arrived (and struggled), and in two or three years Vinicius was a top drawer player.”
Vinicius is not suspended in Europe put Diomande will be hoping Mourinho gives him another chance to shine against his former side Leipzig on Wednesday, as Madrid aim for a third win from three Champions League games.

title: Waseem Abbas case: Contractor claims car skidded, child slipped into its path in Multan
text:
Waseem Abbas case: Contractor claims car skidded, child slipped into its path in Multan
- By Web Desk -
- Oct 20, 2026
MULTAN: Contractor Touqeer Nazir, the suspect in the death of 15-year-old orphan Waseem Abbas, has claimed that his car skidded while he was attempting to stop the teenager from running away from work, resulting in the fatal incident at a private housing society.
Touqeer said that Waseem had repeatedly left work without permission. He claimed that he initially chased the boy on foot but could not catch him, prompting him to return and bring his car.
Touqeer said he spotted Waseem near a street corner and accelerated, intending to position the vehicle ahead of the teenager to block his way. However, he claimed, the car skidded and failed to stop, while Waseem slipped and became trapped between the vehicle and a house’s gate.
Eyewitnesses, however, disputed the suspect’s account, claiming that the incident was not an accident and alleging that the car had deliberately been driven into the teenager.
Speaking to the media, Shoaib Haider, general secretary of the orphanage where Waseem had lived, said the teenager had been residing at the facility for five years and wanted to learn electrical work.
He said Waseem had been working with Touqeer for only six days before the incident.
Read More: Waseem Abbas murder case: Lawyers beat up contractor Touqeer in Multan court
Haider questioned the contractor’s explanation that the car had skidded, saying the available video footage did not apparently support the claim. He said the incident appeared as though the teenager had been struck deliberately, while adding that the circumstances surrounding Waseem’s decision to leave work would need to be established during the investigation.
Haider also said another boy who had been working with Touqeer was brought back, although he did not provide further details.
Meanwhile, Waseem’s paternal uncle, Jafar Hussain, accused the suspect of killing his nephew and demanded justice for the family.
Hussain said Waseem’s father had died nine years ago and that the boy had been admitted to the orphanage by his maternal grandfather and paternal uncle.
In the meantime, Waseem’s funeral prayers were offered late at night in his native village of Mouza Daulatpur in Muzaffargarh, where he was subsequently buried in the ancestral graveyard.
According to local reports, the funeral was held promptly because of the condition of the body. Close relatives and officials of the orphanage attended the funeral.
Police have arrested Touqeer in connection with the case. The investigation is continuing to establish the circumstances of the incident and determine whether the teenager’s death was accidental or deliberate.

title: US envoys Witkoff, Kushner to take part in Ukraine talks in Oslo: Norway
text:
US envoys Witkoff, Kushner to take part in Ukraine talks in Oslo: Norway
- By AFP -
- Oct 20, 2026
OSLO, Norway: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will take part in talks in Oslo Tuesday with Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky and the leaders of Norway and Finland, Norway’s government said.
“Ukraine has requested that US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner join the meetings. I am pleased that they are able to participate,” Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store said in a statement.
Witkoff will travel to Oslo and take part in person while Kushner will participate remotely, Norway said.
Store and Finnish President Alexander Stubb will also take part in the talks.
“Diplomatic efforts have previously taken place in several countries, and Norway and Finland are pleased to be able to continue this work. The aim is to put diplomatic efforts on a more constructive path,” Store said.
During his visit in Oslo, Zelensky will also meet with Norway’s king and visit parliament.
News outlet Axios had earlier cited an anonymous US official as saying that Witkoff would then travel to Russia, “where he hopes to meet with President Vladimir Putin and present ideas”.
The White House did not immediately respond to an AFP request for confirmation.

title: Sophie Cunningham explains her impact beyond stats
text:
Sophie Cunningham explains her impact beyond stats
- By Web Desk -
- Oct 20, 2026
With the WNBA offseason in full swing, the name most discussed among Fever fans lately has been Sophie Cunningham. After a breakout 2023 season that set new franchise records for wins, Cunningham finds herself on the open market with significant intrigue.
Looking back on Indiana Fever’s historic season: The Fever had a great streak and ended the season at 28-16. Looking back on a memorable playoff loss in the first round to Las Vegas Aces, Cunningham talked about the team’s chemistry and work ethic during an episode of her No Hesitation podcast.
“We were so good, and it was so much fun,” Cunningham said on the podcast. “The squad really loved each other. … We do have a lot to be proud about. It stinks because we’re all just so competitive and we just want a championship at the end of it.”
Addressing Free Agency Rumors and Criticisms
As her contract wound down, Cunningham received plenty of feedback from sports commentators about whether the Fever should re-sign her or go elsewhere.
Cunningham had never been one to hold her tongue, and she responded to outside opinions about her on her podcast, sticking up for herself and saying that she was a fighter.
“I have no idea what’s next,” Cunningham said when asked about her upcoming free agency. “I think a lot of us are on free agency right now, so who knows? I think when we get a little bit older and we think back on this season we’re going to be extremely proud of what we were able to do the months of July and August.
What Lies Ahead?
With the WNBA free-agency negotiating period beginning soon, the Indiana Fever front office has some significant roster decisions to make. Whether Cunningham comes back to Indiana as a veteran presence and intense competitor in hopes of another run or experiences the great escape to a different franchise, it is all to be determined.

title: PIA begins interviews for air hostesses recruitment in Karachi
text:
PIA begins interviews for air hostesses recruitment in Karachi
- By Salah Uddin -
- Oct 20, 2026
KARACHI: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) has initiated interviews for air hostesses to be hired for its Karachi-based operations, ARY News reported.
The interviews for shortlisted candidates are currently underway at a local hotel.
The recruitment session is being chaired by PIA Chief Human Resources Officer Athar Hussain.
PIA has already completed the interview process for air hostesses for its Lahore and Islamabad bases.
It is pertinent to mention here that the PIA had announced a recruitment drive for air hostesses at its Karachi base in start of October.
The national carrier was seeking applications from female candidates aged 20 to 28 for cabin crew positions.
Interested candidates were asked to submit their resumes and applications online through the PIA portal.
According to a PIA communique, the deadline to submit online applications was October 7.
A bachelor’s degree has been set as the minimum educational qualification for the post of air hostess.
Before this, PIA initiated recruitment drives for its Lahore and Islamabad bases.
Earlier, the PIA imposed new restrictions on air hostesses during flight duties.
PIA issued a circular stating that air hostesses can possess only one packet of cigarettes during flight duty.
The circular further clarified that an air hostess is allowed to have only twenty cigarettes during a single flight duty.
Legal action will be taken against air hostesses who violate the new restrictions.
Under such legal action, violators can be suspended or removed from flight duties.
In June this year, the PIA issued a new directive imposing strict restrictions on smoking and the possession of tobacco products by cabin crew members.
Under the new policy PIA flight attendants have been prohibited from carrying cigarettes, cigars or other tobacco products in their personal luggage.
The airline has also imposed a complete ban on smoking during flights, hotel stays and in public places while crew members are on duty.
The move is expected to create challenges for crew members who are habitual smokers, as the restrictions significantly tighten existing regulations governing staff conduct.
PIA management has directed all crew members to ensure full compliance with the new policy, warning that any violation will result in immediate suspension and disciplinary proceedings.

title: Rawalpindi Police launch search for youth filmed performing one-wheeling stunt with girl
text:
Rawalpindi Police launch search for youth filmed performing one-wheeling stunt with girl
- By Babar Malik -
- Oct 20, 2026
RAWALPINDI: A case has been registered against an unidentified youth after a video of him performing dangerous one-wheeling stunts with a girl on a motorcycle went viral on social media, ARY News reported.
The case was registered on the complaint of the Incharge Traffic Cantt following notice taken by Chief Traffic Officer (CTO) Rawalpindi, Farhan Aslam.
Following the registration of the First Information Report (FIR), police launched an investigation to identify and locate the suspect using Safe City surveillance cameras across the city.
However, no arrests have been made so far.
Earlier, Punjab Police is continuing to take vigorous action against violations of the Anti-Kite Flying Act across the province, a police spokesperson said.
While giving details, the police said that this year, 11,397 accused have been arrested and 10,849 cases have been registered for violating the Anti-Kite Flying Act across the province.
During the period 599,340 kites have been recovered from the accused.
The police further said that 5740 accused were arrested in provincial capital Lahore while 5466 cases were registered. From Lahore over 2,17,000 kites and 7875 string spinning wheels (Charkhi) were recovered.
Inspector General of Police Punjab has issued clear instructions that the illegal kite flying will not be tolerated anywhere in the province. The police chief has also ordered arrest of the people involved in illegal metal string and online kite business.
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz has approved a 10-day Basant festival to be celebrated across the province, ARY News earlier reported.
The Chief Minister directed authorities to organize the 10-day event to mark the arrival of 2027.
In accordance with her instructions, the Basant festivities will run across the province from January 29 to February 7, 2027.
The decision comes after the festival made a grand return to the province last year following a hiatus of 25 years.
Earlier, authorities in Lahore appealed to residents to complete safety measures ahead of Basant 2027, saying the steps are aimed at protecting lives and ensuring a safe festival.
The district administration in Lahore has also imposed a complete ban on the transportation of kite-flying materials through courier companies and transport services in the city.

title: Karachi: Differently-Abled Teen Robbed at Gunpoint in Baldia
text:
Differently-abled teen robbed at gunpoint in Karachi’s Baldia Town
- By Afzal Khan -
- Oct 20, 2026
KARACHI: Armed robbers allegedly assaulted a differently-abled teenager and snatched his mobile phone at gunpoint in the Abidabad area of Baldia Town in Karachi, with CCTV footage showing the suspects fleeing after the incident.
According to the victim, the suspects subjected him to violence, pointed a firearm at his head and threatened to kill him before snatching his mobile phone and escaping.
The victim said the robbers threatened his life during the incident, leaving him frightened and vulnerable.
CCTV footage of the incident, reportedly showing the suspects fleeing after the robbery, has surfaced.
Police said they were collecting details about the incident and assured that the suspects would be arrested soon. Further investigation is underway.
In a separate incident reported on October 15, 2026, a Karachi resident was deprived of his car and mobile phone at gunpoint after responding to a prospective buyer who had contacted him through an online vehicle-sale advertisement.
According to the complainant, Usman, a resident of the Tariq Road area, he had advertised his 2022-model car for sale on an online application. A man subsequently contacted him and arranged to inspect the vehicle.
Usman said the suspect asked him to bring the car near a school in Block 3 of Delhi Mercantile Society. The man expressed interest in purchasing the vehicle but requested a test drive.
Karachi man robbed of car after posting online sale advertisement
According to the complainant, the suspect drove the car to Liberty Chowk, where another accomplice was waiting. The second suspect joined them, and the two proceeded towards Shahrah-e-Faisal.
Usman alleged that both men then brandished firearms, snatched his mobile phone and forced him out of the vehicle before fleeing with the car.
The incidents highlight continuing concerns over street crime in Karachi, with police investigations underway in both cases.

title: Oil majors face spending test from Iran war windfall cash
text:
Oil majors face spending test from Iran war windfall cash
- By Reuters -
- Oct 20, 2026
LONDON: Oil majors are set to post a big jump in third-quarter profit as the US-Israeli war on Iran has boosted refining and trading results, while investors will monitor how wisely they use their cash piles and whether they resist a spending spree.
The severe disruption of the Strait of Hormuz since US-Israeli airstrikes began the war in February has pushed energy prices to multi-year highs, allowing trading desks to profit from the volatility.
In a sector notorious in the past for boom and bust, the majors have all promised this time to refrain from losing control of costs in what is one of the highest-earning years for global oil producers in recent memory.
Shell, BP, and TotalEnergies all expect refining margins to increase three- to fourfold in the third quarter from a year ago, with Shell guiding for a record high of $42 a barrel. TotalEnergies expects cash flow from its refining and chemicals business to double to around $4 billion from the previous quarter.
Exxon signalled higher refining margins in the quarter could boost downstream profit by $4.5 billion versus the previous quarter.
ARE MAJORS ADAPTING THEIR SPENDING PLANS?
As majors report third-quarter results at the end of the month, investors are asking whether they will stick to their existing spending plans in times of exceptional earnings, wrote RBC Capital Markets analyst Biraj Borkhataria in a research note.
So far Chevron and Exxon have used the money to pay down debt. Investors in Chevron will monitor investment in Venezuela and its progress toward extending its contract to operate the TCO joint venture in Kazakhstan, which is developing the country’s largest oilfield, analysts said.
HSBC expects Shell to announce a $3.5 billion buyback for the fourth quarter, after it reduced the pace of its buyback programme to a quarterly $3 billion earlier this year.
BP’S FORTUNES TURN
After the major’s trading update last week, investment bank TPH called BP its favourite name among European majors. It said BP’s underlying profit could exceed $7 billion, versus $5.7 billion in the second quarter, boosted by refining and gas marketing and trading.
