That cash is going toward repairing BP’s balance sheet. Citi data shows BP’s net debt to operating cash flow falling from 1.7 times at the end of 2025, the highest of the five biggest majors, to an expected 0.8 times by the third quarter.
BP is likely to discuss its future capital allocation during its third-quarter earnings, HSBC said, as BP hits a target to reduce its net debt about a year early, also helped by pausing its buyback programme this year. BP has flagged a strategy update on December 15.
“We believe the priority will remain firmly on deleveraging, with stable capex and no buyback resumption before 2028,” said HSBC’s Kim Fustier and Sadnan Ali in a note.
Shell and Total are due to report on October 29 while BP, Chevron and Exxon are due on October 30.

title: Muridke; Seven brick kiln workers sustain serious burn injuries
text:
Muridke; Seven brick kiln workers sustain serious burn injuries
- By Web Desk -
- Oct 20, 2026
MURIDKE: Seven workers of a brick kiln sustained serious burn injuries in fire at their workplace, rescue officials said on Tuesday.
“Injured workers have been shifted to Tehsil Headquarter (THQ) hospital, while four labourers having critical injuries have been referred to Lahore hospital,” according to the rescue sources.
Injured workers have been identified as Tasleem, Sajjad, Basharat Ali, Mubarak Ali, Fahim ul Hassan and Usman.
Rescuers controlled the blaze erupted at the kiln, while police inquiring into the incident.
Eyewitnesses of the incident have said that the fire erupted while burning carbon at the brick kiln. “The workers sustained serious burn injuries on their faces and legs,” witnesses said.
It is to be mentioned here that a young worker was reported burnt alive after falling into the brick kiln furnace at Chak Nadir Shah of Bahawalnagar on October 02.
According to the family of Gulab Ali (17) and eyewitnesses, he had been working as a labourer at a brick kiln alongside other family members for the past few years.
On Friday night, while he was busy feeding fuel mixture into the kiln, his foot slipped and he fell into the burning furnace. He was burnt alive within a few minutes and his coworkers were unable to save him since neither the victim nor other workers were wearing protective gear or other safety equipment.
The family demanded a probe, legal action against the brick kiln owner, and financial compensation.

title: PHC hears petitions against Governor's Rule, Emergency in KP
text:
PHC hears petitions against Governor's Rule, Emergency in KP
- By Web Desk -
- Oct 20, 2026
PESHAWAR: A bench of the Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Tuesday served notices to the federal government, Attorney General and Advocate General over petitions against imposition of the Governor’s Rule and Emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
A high court bench comprises of Justice Ijaz Anwar and Justice Muhammad Faheem Wali heard the case.
Petitioners’ lawyer Barrister Sameer Khosa argued that the constitutional requirements were not fulfilled in proclamation of the emergency and the governor’s rule in the province.
Lawyer argued that the provincial legislature, chief minister and the cabinet of ministers was present and the provincial affairs were being run according to the normal routine.
He pleaded to the court to declare the Governor’s Rule and Emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa as unlawful and reinstate the provincial assembly.
Tehreek Tahafuz-e-Aaeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP), an alliance of six opposition parties, on Friday approached the Peshawar High Court (PHC), challenging the imposition of Governor’s Rule and an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), as well as the suspension of the provincial government.
The petition seeks to have the measures declared unconstitutional and set aside. The alliance has also requested the court to schedule an early hearing.
The petition contends that imposing Governor’s Rule and an emergency despite the presence of an elected provincial government violates the Constitution.
It argues that the measures contravene Articles 1, 2A, 4, 9, 10, 10A, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19, 19A, 25, 130, 175(3), 232, 234 and 245 of the Constitution, and urges the court to declare the action null and void.
President Asif Ali Zardari on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif signed the summary for the imposition of an emergency and Governor’s Rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution to maintain law and order.
The presidential proclamation has cited an extraordinary surge in terrorist incidents and serious security threats as grounds for taking emergency constitutional measures in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
According to the proclamation, terrorist attacks on government installations and law enforcement agencies have increased, posing serious risks to security and public order.
The declaration states that the provincial government has failed to take adequate measures to address terrorism and lawlessness.

title: Balochistan achieves major milestone in polio eradication: Provincial Health Minister
text:
Balochistan achieves major milestone in polio eradication: Provincial Health Minister
- By Attiya Akram -
- Oct 20, 2026
QUETTA: Balochistan has achieved a remarkable milestone in its anti-polio efforts, as all 23 environmental samples tested negative for the virus, Provincial Health Minister Bakht Muhammad Kakar announced, ARY News reported.
The health minister stated that no new polio cases have been reported in the province over the past two years—a success he attributed to continuous hard work and effective government policy.
Bakht Kakar emphasized that oversight by the Chief Minister of Balochistan and the Chief Secretary played a vital role in achieving these positive results.
He also commended the dedication of polio workers, the health department, and parents, highlighting that the vaccination campaigns continued successfully despite security risks and challenging terrain.
Acknowledging the bravery of frontline workers, the minister remarked that the sacrifices of those who were martyred or injured during polio drives remain unforgettable.
He reaffirmed the government’s resolve to sustain these efforts until polio is completely eradicated from the province.
Earlier, a one-week national anti-polio campaign will kick-start on November 2 in 97 selected districts of the country, the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) informed.
During the campaign, as many as 23.9 million children under the age of five will be administered polio drops, with polio workers going door-to-door.
Almost 9.278 million children will be administered polio drops in 13 selected districts of Punjab, while drops will be given to almost 6.883 million children in 20 selected districts of Sindh.
On the other hand, 4.808 million children in 27 selected districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) will receive the drops, whereas 2.217 million children will be covered across 31 selected districts of Balochistan.
Additionally, more than 447,000 children will be administered polio drops in Islamabad, and as many as 153,000 children will be covered in three selected districts of Gilgit-Baltistan.
During the anti-polio drive, more than 183,000 children will receive polio drops in two selected districts of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK).
According to the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC), securing a polio-free future for children is a shared responsibility.
The NEOC has urged parents to fully cooperate with polio teams to eradicate the menace of polio.

title: Details emerge in Waseem Abbas murder case in Multan
text:
Details emerge in Waseem Abbas murder case in Multan
- By Web Desk -
- Oct 20, 2026
MULTAN: More details have emerged about the death of 15-year-old Waseem Abbas, an orphan who was killed after being struck by a speeding car in a private housing society, as his family members recounted his background and demanded justice.
Waseem’s cousin, Nadeem, and maternal grandfather spoke to the media about the circumstances surrounding the teenager’s life and death.
Nadeem said Waseem had been living in an orphanage for the past six years. He described the teenager as naughty, saying that Waseem often expressed reluctance to continue learning electrical work, insisting that he wanted to return home instead.
According to the family, Waseem had not returned home since he began working as an apprentice electrician. The family members said they did not know Touqeer Nazir, the suspect accused of chasing the teenager, and had never met him.
Waseem’s maternal grandfather said he had personally admitted the boy to the orphanage, hoping that he would receive an education and have a better future rather than face hardship on the streets.
He said that after Waseem’s father died, the boy’s mother was married to his paternal uncle. Following the marriage, Waseem and his brother were placed in an orphanage, according to the grandfather and local residents.
The grandfather demanded that the person responsible for Waseem’s death be punished.
15-year-old electrician deliberately run over by contractor in Multan
Meanwhile, police have arrested Touqeer Nazir, a contractor accused of chasing the teenager in a vehicle. The vehicle involved in the incident has also been taken into custody, and a murder case has been registered against the suspect on the complaint of the police.
According to police, Waseem had been learning electrical work from Touqeer. In his initial statement, the suspect claimed that the teenager would leave work without permission and that he had attempted to stop him.
The suspect reportedly said he followed Waseem in his car because he wanted to catch him. Police said the teenager was allegedly chased on foot before the suspect pursued him in a vehicle, accompanied by another man identified as Amjad Ali.
During the pursuit, the speeding car struck Waseem, causing him to hit the gate of a house. He died at the scene, according to police.
Orphanage administrator Jawad Haider confirmed that Waseem was an orphan who had been living at the facility. He said the teenager had been handed over to Touqeer to learn electrical work.
Waseem, a resident of Muzaffargarh, was 15 years old.

title: Today Is the deadline to pay second Hajj installment: Religious Affairs Ministry
text:
Today Is the deadline to pay second Hajj installment: Religious Affairs Ministry
- By Zahid Mashwani -
- Oct 20, 2026
ISLAMABAD: Today is the final day to pay the second installment of Hajj expenses under the government Hajj scheme, ARY News reported.
A whopping 97,000 prospective pilgrims have already submitted their payments, bringing the total amount received through the digital Hajj portal to Rs 61 billion for the second installment.
Among the digital payments, 45,245 individuals paid via 1Link, while 3,685 paid using debit or credit cards. On the other hand, 47,563 applicants paid through manual bank challans.
A spokesperson for the Ministry of Religious Affairs urged remaining pilgrims to submit their dues today, emphasizing that today is the strict deadline for the second installment under the government scheme.
The spokesperson informed that prospective pilgrims can pay their installment online via the National IT Board’s Hajj portal or through the Pak Hajj app. Applicants were advised to clear their dues promptly to avoid the cancellation of their applications.
Additionally, the spokesperson noted that the mandatory medical fitness certificate is available on the Hajj portal. Pilgrims must download the form, have it verified by an authorized doctor, and upload the signed certificate back onto the portal.
Pilgrims are strongly encouraged to use the Pak Hajj app for regular updates and instructions, the spokesperson added.

title: Aurangzeb calls for taxpayer trust, policy stability to encourage private investment
text:
Aurangzeb calls for taxpayer trust, policy stability to encourage private investment
- By Hamid Ur Rehman -
- Oct 20, 2026
ISLAMABAD: Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb on Tuesday pledged to restore public trust and credibility in the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), stressing that taxpayer confidence, policy predictability and stronger enforcement were essential to building a modern and growth-friendly tax system.
Addressing a two-day high-level workshop titled “Reforms for a Modern and Growth-Friendly Tax System in Pakistan” in Islamabad, convened by the Ministry of Finance in collaboration with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Aurangzeb said ongoing reforms had helped increase the FBR’s tax-to-GDP ratio from 8.8 per cent to 10.3 per cent.
He also highlighted a 40 per cent increase in tax revenues over the last two fiscal years, attributing the improvement to stronger enforcement and new policy measures.
Explaining the increase in the tax-to-GDP ratio, the finance minister said 0.9 percentage points of the 1.5-percentage-point rise came from enforcement measures, while the remaining 0.6 percentage points resulted from new policy initiatives.
“We stopped leakage, theft and corruption,” Aurangzeb said, adding that deeper enforcement would play an increasingly important role in the next phase of tax reforms.
He said the government was continuing to strengthen the tax system, broaden the tax base and improve revenue collection to support economic stability and sustainable growth.
Emphasising the need for a predictable business environment, Aurangzeb said the private sector required policy continuity to make long-term investment decisions.
“We cannot continue to give surprises to private-sector investment at every single budget,” he said, stressing that consistency in government policies was essential to encouraging investment.
The minister identified political consensus, stronger institutions and taxpayer trust as key enablers of sustainable tax reform. He also underscored the importance of cooperation between the federal and provincial governments in achieving broader agreement on tax policies.
“Bringing trust and credibility back into the tax authority” was among the most important priorities, he said, highlighting the need to improve the relationship between taxpayers and the tax administration.
The workshop brought together senior government officials, representatives of the IMF and the World Bank, international tax experts, academics and private-sector leaders to discuss priorities for modernising Pakistan’s tax system and strengthening its contribution to sustainable economic growth.
Finance Ministry rejects claim of Rs20 billion daily increase in government debt
The programme features six substantive sessions covering taxation and economic growth; modernisation of Pakistan’s tax system; a unified sales tax regime across the federation and provinces; a simpler and more neutral income tax system; tax administration, digitalisation and taxpayer trust; and fiscal federalism and provincial tax revenues.
Aurangzeb delivered the opening remarks alongside Jihad Azour, Director of the IMF’s Middle East and Central Asia Department, and Rodrigo Valdés, Director of the IMF’s Fiscal Affairs Department.

title: Gas prices set to surge as IMF presses govt to pass on cost hikes: Finance Ministry sources
text:
Gas prices set to surge as IMF presses govt to pass on cost hikes: Finance Ministry sources
- By Shoaib Nizami -
- Oct 20, 2026
ISLAMABAD: In another piece of bad news for the masses, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has pressured the government to transfer the increase in gas prices to consumers, ARY News reported, citing sources in the Ministry of Finance.
Ministry of Finance sources state that circular debt in the gas sector has surpassed Rs 3,600 billion.
Meanwhile, the government has started working on a deregulation project in the gas sector. Under this plan, the government intends to privatize both gas distribution companies and attract private sector investment into the sector.
The deregulation and investment plan will soon be presented to the Prime Minister.
Sources said that the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Petroleum, and relevant departments have been directed to prepare the proposal.
According to sources, the proposed gas sector deregulation is being considered in line with IMF conditions and was previously discussed during the last economic review.
This development comes as a blow to the public, as the burden of price hikes will be passed on to consumers, alongside an increased role for the private sector.
Once the Prime Minister approves the initial proposal, a final decision will be taken.

title: Audit flags Rs920mn in alleged irregularities during PTI govt in KP
text:
Audit flags Rs920mn in alleged irregularities during PTI govt in KP
- By Laiq Ur Rehman -
- Oct 20, 2026
PESHAWAR: Alleged financial irregularities amounting to Rs920 million have been reported in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Education Department during a single year of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) government, raising questions about financial oversight and the use of public funds.
The reported irregularities were carried out during the tenure of Shahram Khan Tarakai as provincial minister for Elementary and Secondary Education.
According to the reported findings, irregularities amounting to Rs374.3 million were identified in the provision of tablets to newly recruited teachers hired through district education officers.
A total of Rs424.7 million was spent on distributing tablets among 15,000 individuals. A committee was subsequently formed to investigate the matter. However, according to the scrutiny committee’s report, only 1,779 tablets were returned to the Directorate, while the remaining 13,221 tablets could not be accounted for.
Separately, alleged irregularities amounting to Rs48.7 million were reported in the procurement of paper by the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE), Mardan, during the fiscal year 2022–23.
The report further stated that the award of a contract to a favoured firm in violation of government rules and regulations allegedly caused a loss of Rs192 million to the public exchequer.
Mahmood Achakzai questions whereabouts of KP chief minister, 8 MNAs
In another case, the board chairman reportedly withdrew Rs7.1 million under the head of executive allowance, despite not being entitled to the allowance.
According to the audit report, the purchase of smartphones also resulted in an alleged loss of Rs13 million to the public exchequer.
The reported findings raise concerns about procurement procedures, the distribution of public assets and compliance with financial regulations in the provincial education sector during the PTI government.

title: Trump's approval falls to record low of 31% as midterms near, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
text:
Trump's approval falls to record low of 31% as midterms near, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
- By Reuters -
- Oct 20, 2026
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump’s approval rating fell to a record low as Americans worried about high gasoline prices and appeared ready to punish his Republican Party in the November 3 congressional elections, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that closed on Monday.
Some 31% of Americans approve of Trump’s performance in office, down a percentage point from two weeks earlier and the lowest level in either of his presidential terms, the four-day poll showed.
Asked which party they would vote for if the congressional elections were held today in what is known as a “generic ballot” question, some 47% of registered voters in the nationwide poll picked Democrats and 35% chose Republicans. The 12-point Democratic advantage was the widest over the current election cycle and could bolster Democratic hopes of seizing control of the US House of Representatives and the US Senate.
For Republicans, losing control of either chamber could complicate Trump’s agenda in the last two years of his term.
Generic ballot polls are national polls that provide an overall view of which party poll respondents want to see in charge in Congress.
While these polls provide a view of national public sentiment, they do not capture all the nuances of the state-by-state and district-by-district contests that determine control of the Senate and House, contests in which Republicans hold some structural advantages.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll two weeks earlier showed Democrats leading Republicans by 7 points, 44% to 37%.
Much of the drop in support for Republican congressional candidates was due to a larger share of women saying they would pick Democrats. Some 50% of female voters said they would vote Democratic, compared to 32% eyeing Republican candidates. Men also favored Democrats, but by a smaller margin.
Trump’s popularity has suffered since he ordered military strikes on Iran in February alongside US ally Israel. The war triggered a surge in gasoline prices, hitting household finances. Some 68% of Americans disapprove of Trump’s handling of the economy, including 37% of self-identified Republicans.
Voters in the poll picked Democrats over Republicans as the better stewards of the economy, by 40% to 33%.
The survey, which was conducted online, gathered responses from 1,679 US adults, including 1,279 registered voters. The poll’s results had a margin of error of 2 percentage points for all respondents and 3 points for registered voters.

title: Alberta rejects plan for referendum on leaving Canada: media
text:
Alberta rejects plan for referendum on leaving Canada: media
- By AFP -
- Oct 20, 2026
EDMONTON, Canada: Canada’s province of Alberta overwhelmingly rejected a plan to hold a binding independence referendum, media projected Tuesday, in a decisive defeat for separatists that drew support from allies of US President Donald Trump.
Public broadcaster CBC projected a clear win for the federalist side, with official results showing more than 76 percent support for national unity, with roughly at least a third of the votes counted.
Canada was waiting Monday for the results of a vote on whether the oil-rich province of Alberta wants a binding independence referendum, following a divisive campaign that tested national unity.
Prime Minister Mark Carney has argued the vote has been held “at the worst possible time,” citing the need for national stability as US President Donald Trump wages a trade war and levels annexation threats.
Polls indicated less than a quarter of people in the western province want independence, but separatist leader Mitch Sylvestre told AFP on Monday he remained optimistic.
Alberta’s elections authority said all polls had closed by 10:10 pm (0410 GMT Tuesday), but vote counting had been underway for several hours, including tallies of the 1.4 million advance ballots cast. There are 3.1 million eligible voters in the province.
At the federalist election night party in Edmonton, a band warmed up ahead of an anticipated positive result.
“It was amazing to see the enthusiasm and resolve among Canadians,” said Thomas Lukaszuk, who heads Forever Canadian, the group that campaigned across the province for national unity.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith, a conservative, said she voted against independence but called the referendum to settle an issue that has divided the province.
If a majority wants to separate, she has pledged to hold a binding referendum.
If the federalists win, Smith said the secession question should be considered closed.
Foreign influence?
Alberta has the world’s fourth-largest proven oil reserves, and much of the separatist momentum has been driven by anger over oil industry management.
Smith has blamed Carney’s predecessor Justin Trudeau for igniting the separatist fire, accusing him of trying to crush oil production to advance his pro-climate agenda.
Alberta’s independence push has also drawn sustained interest from Trump allies.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called Alberta a “natural partner” for the United States. Elon Musk, the world’s richest person and a top Trump supporter, posted on X this month that Alberta “should separate.”
Separatist leaders have also held meetings at the US State Department and with Republican political operatives.
‘Huge uncertainty’
Carney, who grew up in Alberta, has worked to improve relations between the province and Ottawa since taking office last year.
He has partnered with Smith on advancing a new pipeline to export more Alberta bitumen overseas, a project considered a nonstarter during Trudeau’s tenure.
But he has also warned Albertans that even a nonbinding vote on independence would be a “dangerous bluff,” drawing on his experience during Brexit, when he was the Bank of England’s governor.
He said the “huge uncertainty” that followed the Brexit vote hurt the British economy, cautioning Alberta over unintended economic consequences.

title: Hegseth meets Netanyahu in unannounced visit to Israel, source says
text:
Hegseth meets Netanyahu in unannounced visit to Israel, source says
- By Reuters -
- Oct 20, 2026
JERUSALEM: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during an unannounced visit to Israel on Monday, a person familiar with the matter said, as tensions flare between the US and Iran.
The person did not say what the two men discussed during the meeting, first reported by Axios. The Pentagon declined to comment. The Israeli prime minister’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Hegseth said in a social media post that he had visited US service members in the Central Command area of responsibility, which covers the Middle East, northeast Africa and parts of Asia.
Israel’s Army Radio reported his meeting with Netanyahu took place at an air force base in Israel’s southern desert.
Hegseth’s visit comes amid rising tensions in the Middle East war as tensions flare between the U.S. and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz and as Yemen’s Iran-allied Houthis intensify their attacks on Saudi Arabia.
It also came a day after US President Donald Trump endorsed Netanyahu in next week’s parliamentary election in Israel, the country’s first ballot since the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack on southern Israel.
US and Israeli forces launched joint strikes against Iran in late February, setting off the wider Middle East war. Netanyahu told Israeli media this month that he’s not seeking to attack Iran before the October 27 Israeli election. Trump has said he will not attack Iran before US midterm elections in November.

title: US bans use of China's DeepSeek by govt agencies
text:
US bans use of China's DeepSeek by govt agencies
- By AFP -
- Oct 20, 2026
NEW YORK: The US government on Monday ordered its agencies to stop using artificial intelligence tools from Chinese startup DeepSeek, as the countries race for dominance in the fast-moving sector.
A notice from the Department of Homeland Security announced the ban on products developed by DeepSeek — and tools created using DeepSeek by third parties — saying they must be removed from IT devices.
The department can issue direction to civilian agencies, but not the military or intelligence services. Washington’s Department of Defense did not respond to an AFP request for comment.
“DeepSeek’s models present multiple threat vectors,” said a document attached to Monday’s notice.
Use of DeepSeek AI tools “may result in the transfer of sensitive data to (China) if used by US government employees or vendors,” the department warned.
Its servers are located in China, where the legal system permits the government “extensive authority” to access private company infrastructure, it said.
AFP has contacted DeepSeek for comment.
DeepSeek, one of China’s top AI labs, shook up the industry in January 2025 with a low-cost, high-performance chatbot, challenging assumptions of US dominance.
The firm released a long-awaited new model, V4, in April, and this month updated a faster, more lightweight version of V4.
The United States has accused DeepSeek and other top Chinese AI firms of systematically stealing the capabilities of cutting-edge models developed by American rivals.
Despite their fierce competition in the field, China and the United States in September agreed to set up a “communication channel” for AI incidents.
The topic is expected to arise again when the countries’ leaders meet next month at a summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

title: Iran foreign minister says Russia, Iran have 'never' worked so closely
text:
Iran foreign minister says Russia, Iran have 'never' worked so closely
- By AFP -
- Oct 20, 2026
TEHRAN: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tuesday that Russia and Iran have “never” worked so closely, as Moscow seeks to play a mediating role in the Middle East war.
Araghchi hosted his Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov in Iran on Monday, in his first visit since the outbreak of the conflict.
“We covered everything from Europe to West Asia, including Lebanon, Palestine, Ukraine and Yemen. Also focused on expansion of economic and nuclear cooperation,” Araghchi wrote on X.
“Never in our history have Iran and Russia worked as closely as now.”
Lavrov said ahead of the visit that Moscow’s efforts “aimed at preventing the return of a large-scale war”, with talks stalled between the United States and Iran.
His visit came after Russian President Vladimir Putin told his Iranian counterpart Masoud Pezeshkian this month that Moscow was prepared to contribute to mediation efforts.
Russia and Iran, two of the most heavily sanctioned nations in the world, maintain close ties.
The Middle East war erupted in February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran. A ceasefire in April and a US-Iran memorandum of understanding in June have failed to stop fighting in and around the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran claims control over the strategic waterway — through which one-fifth of the world’s oil passes in normal times — and regularly targets vessels that cross without its authorisation.
In response, Washington has been maintaining a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports.
The Russian foreign ministry said ahead of Lavrov’s visit to Iran that discussions were expected to focus on “ways to resolve the acute international crisis triggered by the unlawful aggression of the US and Israel” against the Islamic republic.
The ministry said the war had been a blow to stability and security “not only in the near and Middle East, but also on a global scale”.

title: Brentford working with police after rugby ball launched towards stadium
text:
Brentford working with police after rugby ball launched towards stadium
- By Reuters -
- Oct 20, 2026
Brentford said on Monday they were working with police to identify those responsible after a rugby ball appeared to be kicked from a nearby rooftop towards their Gtech Community Stadium during Saturday’s Premier League defeat by Liverpool.
A viral video on social media showed a man kicking the ball from a nearby rooftop towards the stadium, where it appeared to bounce off the roof, while a separate clip showed staff carrying it away.
“Brentford Football Club is aware of an incident involving an item being kicked from a height towards the field of play during Saturday’s match against Liverpool,” the club said in a statement.
“Such behaviour is dangerous and potentially very harmful.
“The matter has been referred to the police and the club is supporting the relevant authorities in their investigation to help identify those responsible and take appropriate action, which may result in criminal prosecution.
“The matchday safety of fans, staff, players and officials is of utmost importance, and the club will support all efforts to ensure action is taken.”
Brentford lost the game 2-1 after surrendering a first-half lead and finishing with nine men.
The Gtech Community Stadium is surrounded by residential and commercial buildings.
Brentford are sixth in the league standings with 10 points from seven matches and visit Hull City on Sunday.

title: 15-year-old electrician deliberately run over by contractor in Multan
text:
15-year-old electrician deliberately run over by contractor in Multan
- By Yasir Sheikh -
- Oct 20, 2026
MULTAN: A 15-year-old boy, Waseem Abbas, was killed after being hit by a speeding car in a private housing society in Multan. Police have arrested the contractor accused of chasing the teenager in a vehicle.
According to police, the main suspect, Touqeer Nazir, has been arrested, the vehicle taken into custody and a case registered. Further investigation into the incident is underway.
In his initial statement to police, Touqeer Nazir said Waseem had been learning electrical work from him. He claimed the boy would leave work without permission and that he had tried to catch him.
The suspect said he drove the car behind Waseem because he wanted to stop him, according to his initial statement.
Police earlier said the boy had left the job and was chased by the contractor. The suspect allegedly pursued him on foot before following him in a car along with another man, Amjad Ali.
During the chase, the speeding car struck Waseem. He hit the gate of a house and died at the scene, police said.
According to orphanage administrator Jawad Haider, Waseem Abbas was an orphan who lived at an orphanage.
Haider said Waseem had been handed over to Touqeer Nazir to learn electrical work.
The deceased was a resident of Muzaffargarh and was 15 years old.
Police said further investigation into the circumstances surrounding Waseem’s death was ongoing.

title: France announces curfews as government grapples with unrest
text:
France announces curfews as government grapples with unrest
- By AFP -
- Oct 20, 2026
France announced partial curfews in Paris and other cities on Monday after weekend demonstrations over soaring prices degenerated into some of the worst street violence in recent years.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu did not rule out imposing a state of emergency after the interior minister said police had “lost control”.
Tourists in Paris had a taste of the disruption on Monday when they found the Louvre closed because of a small group of student protesters.
Facing accusations that it failed to anticipate and respond to the violence, the government has vowed to re-establish order, while officials scrambled to contain public anger.
The unrest, erupting just six months before France elects a successor to President Emmanuel Macron, threatened to continue, with organisers calling for a new round of protests next Saturday.
Authorities said partial curfews would be enforced from Monday evening to Tuesday morning in a number of cities including Paris, Lille and Lyon, to protect businesses.
In the capital, a curfew was ordered from 11:00 pm (2100 GMT), while demonstrations were banned from 8:00 pm.
“I’m absolutely determined to restore public order”, Lecornu said.
Other European countries have also seen demonstrations over rising prices, with smaller clashes breaking out in Milan and Belgium over the weekend and protests simmering in Spain and Portugal.
Some half a million people turned out across France on Saturday to denounce the surging cost of living, a culmination of four weeks of protests that began with students demanding better conditions at high schools.
What started as peaceful demonstrations descended into violence in many cities, as masked groups attacked law enforcement, broke into public buildings and set some ablaze, looted shops, and set fire to cars, bicycles and scooters.
Listings for ‘stolen goods’
On Monday, France’s digital minister, Anne Le Henanff, urged online resale platforms to remove listings for “stolen items” following Saturday’s looting and summoned representatives of companies including Vinted and eBay.
After the weekend scenes of chaos, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez offered his resignation, but Macron refused to accept it.
More than 2,500 people were arrested and nearly 1,000 members of the security forces injured. Protesters were also hurt, with one demonstrator’s hand blown off by a police crowd-control grenade.
Macron acknowledged failures in the government response, which had seen 60,000 law enforcement personnel deployed on Saturday.
Nationwide, more than 2,513 people have been taken into police custody since the weekend, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said. He added that 67 had been jailed and “dozens” of criminal cases opened.
Darmanin also said authorities would use facial recognition on social media to identify perpetrators.
At least 3,000 shops were damaged, with the cost running into hundreds of millions of euros.
In an address to the nation Sunday, Macron slammed the “unbridled” violence.
The European Union called the violence “unacceptable” but warned that the right to peaceful protest “must be protected” in France.
Germany condemned the violence and updated its travel advice for France, saying “further outbreaks of violence in the coming days cannot be ruled out”.
China has warned citizens travelling to France to be aware of risks and take safety precautions, state broadcaster CCTV reported.
Louvre blocked
In Paris on Monday, a dozen demonstrators blocked the entrance to the Louvre, the most visited museum in the world, while bewildered tourists looked on.
“We don’t want to get involved. We want to stand back and get away from them,” Pat Boland, a tourist from Australia, said of the protests.
The pensioner, 73, spoke to AFP outside barricades that had been erected at the Louvre, which was closed because a small group of protesters stood by its famed glass pyramid entrance.
The unrest has flared before presidential elections in April and May that will elect a new French president after a decade of centrist Macron.
Marine Le Pen, the far-right presidential candidate, is riding high in the polls.
The government has accused ultra-left groups of stoking the violence to boost the chances of the far-left firebrand Jean-Luc Melenchon in the presidential polls.
The interior minister and intelligence services were to meet late Monday to discuss the violence.
Europe
During the weekend, clashes broke out on the sidelines of a cost-of-living demonstration in Milan.
“I’m very worried because it’s a new phenomenon, which also originates from an international scenario and therefore feeds itself,” mayor Giuseppe Sala said.
In Belgium, police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in Brussels and Liege.
In Spain protesters have set up tents in the heart of Madrid to denounce soaring housing costs, with similar encampments going up in neighbouring Portugal’s main cities of Lisbon and Porto.

title: Cristiano Ronaldo gets 30-day ban and €255 fine
text:
Cristiano Ronaldo gets 30-day ban and €255 fine
- By Sher Muhammad -
- Oct 20, 2026
After Cristiano Ronaldo left the national team’s camp and had a falling out with coach Jorge Jesus, the Portuguese Football Federation banned him for thirty days. A fine of 255 euros has also been imposed by the Federation’s Disciplinary Council.
It is pertinent to note that after arguments with the coach, Cristiano Ronaldo quit the national team camp three weeks ago.
International news agency Reuters reported that before a Nations League game against Denmark this month, top football player Cristiano Ronaldo reportedly abandoned the national team’s camp in Copenhagen. He had previously been listed among the substitutes in a match versus Norway instead of being fielded.
Regarding his involvement in the game, Ronaldo had claimed that coach Jorge Jesus had broken his word twice. Although he did not rule out the prospect of Ronaldo rejoining the team after Portugal’s 2-1 triumph, the coach denied the existence of any such arrangement.
The Disciplinary Council of the Portuguese Football Federation claims that Ronaldo willfully broke the code of conduct. The report about the incident in question had surfaced two days prior to the commencement of proceedings in this case on October 9.
It is unclear from the federation’s announcement which games or activities will be subject to the 30-day ban and whether the time already completed during the interim suspension will be applied.
Notably, Ronaldo has expressed regret for leaving the camp without his colleagues and for neglecting to greet the supporters during the game against Norway. Additionally, he declared that after serving his suspension, he will be available for the national team.
Everyone in the Portuguese Football Federation wants Ronaldo to rejoin the national squad once the issue is settled, according to Pedro Proença, head of the organization.

title: Mashal Yousafzai links PTI’s support for 28th Amendment to founder’s relief
text:
Mashal Yousafzai links PTI’s support for 28th Amendment to founder’s relief
- By Asim Mallick -
- Oct 20, 2026
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Senator Mashal Yousafzai has linked support for the proposed 28th Constitutional Amendment to relief for party founder Imran Khan, saying she and 25 other senators would vote in favour of it if he benefited from the amendment.
Speaking on ARY News programme Khabar, Yousafzai said that if the matter concerned Imran Khan’s release, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan would vote before her. She added that she would not have discussed the proposed amendment if Imran Khan had opposed the provisions being considered.
Mashal Yousafzai criticises Achakzai’s role in talks
Yousafzai also criticised Mahmood Khan Achakzai over his role in negotiations for Imran Khan, saying he had failed to fulfil the responsibilities expected of him.
She said Imran Khan had selected Achakzai to hold talks, but little progress had been made over the past year.
According to Yousafzai, Achakzai should have represented the opposition in the recent negotiations. However, she claimed he had travelled to Quetta during the talks and was not responding to calls.
She further alleged that Achakzai returned after PTI lost its government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. She said that whenever the issue of negotiations arose, Achakzai expressed reluctance to visit the speaker’s chamber.
Yousafzai said national interests should take precedence over personal interests. She also claimed that Achakzai had entered the assembly on PTI’s seats under Form 47.
The senator criticised the role of Tehreek Tahaffuz Ayeen-e-Pakistan and said PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan had told its members that he would not sit with them in the future.
Mashal Yousafzai defends Barrister Saif’s role
Yousafzai said PTI’s dispute with the PML-N concerned seats, adding that Achakzai had no issue with the prime minister and should therefore have participated in the talks.
She said Barrister Saif had maintained contacts with both sides and made efforts to arrange meetings with Imran Khan. According to her, Saif had also played a role when meetings with Bushra Bibi were stopped.
Yousafzai said Salman Akram Raja and Intizar Panjutha had been unable to make progress on the issue at Adiala Jail.
She also said Asad Qaiser was upset with Barrister Saif over a personal matter and claimed that Qaiser wanted his brother to become the chief minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
According to Yousafzai, Barrister Saif had helped Qaiser meet Imran Khan at Adiala Jail. She said Imran Khan rejected Qaiser’s proposal, adding that Saif could not be blamed for the decision.
The senator said PTI was a national party and had no objection to having governments in more provinces.
PTI long march strategy remains unclear, says Mashal Yousafzai
Yousafzai said efforts had been made to make Meena Khan the chief minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Discussing the party’s long march, she said those responsible for Plans B, C and D were not responding, leaving other party members unaware of the strategy.
She named Shahid Khattak and Shafi Jan among those who were not responding to calls and said the plan remained unclear. She added that Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had not shared the plan with anyone and that it had gone with him.
Yousafzai said a limited group had prepared the long march strategy to prevent it from being leaked. She complained that party decisions had previously been made elsewhere, while other people faced criticism.
She said PTI decisions would now be made through voting and that no specific group would be allowed to make decisions on its own.
Yousafzai added that the long march did not appear to be making progress and said Shahid Khattak could explain the strategy if he came forward.

title: Petrol and diesel prices reduced, OGRA issues new rates
text:
Petrol and diesel prices reduced, OGRA issues new rates
- By Aleem Malik -
- Oct 20, 2026
ISLAMABAD: The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) has announced a reduction in petrol price and diesel rate, according to a notification.
Petrol price has been reduced by Rs5.16 per litre, bringing the new price to Rs381.14 per litre.
The diesel rate has been cut by Rs7.69 per litre, with the new price set at Rs389.27 per litre.
Petrol Relief Scheme:
Under the Petrol Relief Scheme, motorcycle and Cingchi rickshaw owners get a Rs.100 per litre discount on up to 20 litres of petrol per month.
Owners of vehicles with engines up to 800cc are eligible for discounted petrol of up to 30 litres per month.
How to register
To register for the discounted petrol, applicants should send an SMS containing the following information to 9771: citizens write REG, CNIC number, Vehicle registration number, First word of the province name and Vehicle registration date.
Once registration is completed, applicants will receive a confirmation message on their mobile phone.
How to obtain the petrol token
Before visiting a petrol station, applicants should send TOK to 9771.
They will then receive a token number by SMS. The token number should be presented at the petrol station to claim the discounted petrol.
A confirmation message will be sent after the transaction is completed.

title: NADRA warns citizens against fake arms license websites
text:
NADRA warns citizens against fake arms license websites
- By Web Desk -
- Oct 20, 2026
The National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) in Pakistan has warned residents of Punjab against fraudulent websites claiming to offer civilian arms licence application services.
The authority said scammers were using fake online platforms to target applicants, charging excessive fees and putting their personal information at risk.
NADRA urged citizens to check website addresses carefully before submitting applications, sharing identity documents or making payments. It also advised applicants to avoid unverified websites claiming to facilitate the licensing process.
The authority stressed that using fraudulent platforms could expose applicants to financial losses and the misuse of sensitive personal data.
Citizens seeking civilian arms licences have been advised to use only verified and official channels and to confirm the authenticity of any website before proceeding.
NADRA also advised applicants to remain highly vigilant and avoid using unofficial arms license websites, as most of them are likely fake.

title: Xiaomi Redmi K100 launch date and key specifications officially revealed
text:
Xiaomi Redmi K100 launch date and key specifications officially revealed
- By Kumail Shah -
- Oct 19, 2026
Xiaomi launched the Redmi K100 Pro and K100 Pro Max in China in August 2026. The company has now announced the launch date for the regular Redmi K100 and shared its design and some key specs.
Official promo images show the Redmi K100 in a “Firefly Green” color. The phone has a large rectangular camera module on the back with space for two cameras and features “Sound by Bose” branding.
The Redmi K100 will have a 6.83-inch display with a 165Hz refresh rate and peak brightness of 3,500 nits. Xiaomi also confirmed a 480Hz multi-finger touch reporting rate and a 3,500Hz instant touch sampling rate.
Xiaomi’s new phone will run on the Snapdragon 8 Elite chipset, a flagship 3nm chip first released in 2024 and also used in the Redmi K90 (currently $548.33 on TradingShenzhen). It will also include a D2 gaming chip and come with HyperOS 4 software.
The flagship phone is set to launch in China on October 27, 2026. There is no word yet on an international release, but it may launch outside China under the Poco brand. For context, the K100 Pro and K100 Pro Max were released internationally as the Poco F9 Pro and Poco F9 Ultra.

title: Kuwait Traffic Department launches huge crackdown on transporting passengers illegally
text:
Kuwait Traffic Department launches huge crackdown on transporting passengers illegally
- By Zaeem Basir -
- Oct 19, 2026
A recent dramatic security operation by Kuwait’s General Traffic Department (GTD) – a ministry of interior department – has been designed to crack down on violations by drivers and to root out all illegal transportation providers in the country.
The operation, which was personally led by GTD Director General Brigadier General Rashid Hammoud and with Assistant Director Ayoub Al-Ayoub taking part in the strike action, involved a crackdown against public buses and private cars used for unlicensed transport services.
At the conclusion of the total operation, traffic officers issued 338 violations for different traffic violations and also issued 26 violations for persons using privately owned cars without the required permits to carry passengers for a fee.
Furthermore, the authorities of the General Traffic Department (GTD) seized 27 vehicles, and referred 27 violators directly to traffic custody in preparation for traffic administrative and legal procedures.
The GDT officials emphasized that the violators will be subjected to harsh penalties, which are part of a comprehensive campaign in all governorates of Kuwait to regulate and organize traffic movement
To ensure the safety of the public transported by publicly designated transportation, including the public authorities to ensure the safety of the public transported by the transit company.

title: Finance Ministry rejects claim of Rs20 billion daily increase in government debt
text:
Finance Ministry rejects claim of Rs20 billion daily increase in government debt
- By Web Desk -
- Oct 19, 2026
ISLAMABAD: The Ministry of Finance has rejected reports claiming that Pakistan’s government debt is increasing by Rs20 billion daily, saying such figures do not present an accurate picture of the country’s debt situation, ARY News reported.
In its clarification, the ministry said government debt should be assessed in relation to the country’s gross domestic product (GDP) rather than through daily borrowing figures alone.
According to the ministry, Pakistan’s debt-to-GDP ratio has declined from 75 percent to below 68 percent, while the rate of debt growth has fallen from 26 percent to 7.7 percent.
The ministry said the rate of debt growth in the fiscal year 2026 was the lowest recorded in the past two decades. Between fiscal years 2007 and 2026, the average annual growth rate of debt stood at 16.7 percent, it added.
The ministry also reported a reduction in central government debt in August 2026, when it declined by Rs689 billion.
External debt ratio declines
The Finance Ministry said Pakistan’s external debt-to-GDP ratio had fallen from 33 percent to 23 percent.
It added that external debt increased by an average of $1.7 billion annually between fiscal years 2022 and 2026, compared with an average annual increase of $6.4 billion between 2015 and 2022.
Debt servicing costs fall
According to the ministry, debt servicing costs declined from Rs8,900 billion to Rs6,900 billion.
The ratio of debt servicing costs to federal revenue also decreased from 64 percent to 38 percent, it said.
The ministry further stated that the government had repaid more than Rs5,920 billion in expensive debt before maturity.
It also reported that the average maturity of domestic debt increased from 2.7 years to approximately four years.
Foreign exchange reserves rise
The Finance Ministry said Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves had increased to $21.5 billion by September 2026.
The ministry maintained that the debt-to-GDP ratio had declined, debt growth had slowed, debt servicing costs had decreased and foreign exchange reserves had strengthened.
It reiterated that presenting government borrowing as a daily increase of Rs20 billion did not accurately reflect the overall debt position.

title: Christiane Amanpour to leave CNN
text:
Christiane Amanpour to leave CNN
- By Reuters -
- Oct 19, 2026
CNN chief international anchor Christiane Amanpour will leave next year, after 43 years with the network, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters on Monday.
The news channel has recently come under the ownership of Skydance, whose CEO David Ellison has faced criticism over his stewardship of CBS News.
Christiane Amanpour will end her daily shows across CNN and PBS at the end of this year. She will continue to host a weekly program on CNN through May and work on a transition through June. Amanpour, whose first major assignment was covering the first Gulf War, went on to report from conflicts in Bosnia, Rwanda, Afghanistan, Ukraine and Iran over a career spanning more than three decades.
The announcement comes as Skydance, formerly Paramount Skydance, completed its $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery earlier this month, bringing CNN and CBS News under the same corporate roof.
CNN chief Mark Thompson and CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss will keep their roles, with both reporting to David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz. The deal has drawn scrutiny on Capitol Hill, where lawmakers have criticized Ellison for allegedly tailoring news coverage at CBS News to favor President Donald Trump.
Christiane Amanpour is a British-Iranian journalist and one of the most recognizable international correspondents of the past 30 years. She first gained prominence at CNN covering the first Gulf War in 1990 from Baghdad, and went on to report from major conflict zones including Bosnia, Rwanda, Afghanistan, Iraq, Ukraine and Iran. Known for her on-the-ground reporting and tough interviews with world leaders, she became CNN’s Chief International Anchor and hosted Amanpour, the network’s flagship global affairs interview program. She also anchored a weekly edition of the show on PBS, making her a rare dual presence on both cable and public television in the U.S.
Her career has been defined by a focus on war, diplomacy, and human rights, with a reporting style that blends eyewitness coverage with in-depth interviews. Over the decades she has interviewed presidents, prime ministers, and activists across five continents, and has won multiple awards including several News & Documentary Emmys and a Lifetime Achievement Award from the International Women’s Media Foundation. In late 2025 it was announced she would step down from her daily CNN and PBS shows at year’s end, while continuing a weekly CNN program into 2026.

title: Sophie Cunningham WNBA free agency forces dilemmas for Fever
text:
Sophie Cunningham's WNBA free agency forces key offseason dilemmas for Fever
- By Zaeem Basir -
- Oct 19, 2026
With the WNBA offseason fully upon us, veteran guard Sophie Cunningham is among the top storylines unfolding as free agency looms and the Indiana Fever look to make some difficult roster decisions.
A relentless defender, a perimeter sharpshooter and a fiery competitor, Cunningham is in the prime of her career and one of the best available free agents on the market.
From Indiana’s perspective, the decision rests on whether the Fever want to pay a premium for veteran leadership and shooting while also sacrificing some room to maneuver their salary cap as they set around their No. 1 pick to close the season.
All of the league’s front offices are tracking the Fever’s approach to Cunningham’s market value and availability as clubs piece together more balance and shooting on their rosters going into the new season.
Especially for Indiana, it’s a nuanced proposition as the franchise aims to craft a sustainable contender that can contend and compete in the playoffs for years to come.
Finding that long-term perimeter complement for an emerging star to go along with championship experience is tantalizing, but the timing is imperative for the front office in this scenario.
Finally, the way the Indiana Fever handle Sophie Cunningham’s free agency might just determine the biggest move of the offseason – and all of the ripple effects that come with it.
In the middle of trade talk and front-office calls, the league is watching to find out where the veteran guard will play this season. Wherever she ends up, Cunningham’s team will have a ripple effect, changing the playoff picture in big ways.

title: Godox A2 MagSafe xenon flash debuts for iPhone 15 and newer models

Godox A2 MagSafe xenon flash debuts for iPhone 15 and newer models

The Godox A2 brings a xenon flash to the Apple iPhone. This round flash attaches to the back of the iPhone with MagSafe. Because it connects over Bluetooth, you can also use it wirelessly and place it at any angle you want.

The Godox A2 xenon flash for smartphones is available for about $85 on Amazon. You can find more information on the Godox website. Right now, it only works with Apple iPhones from the iPhone 15 and newer, including the iPhone 16e and iPhone Air.

title: Finance Minister reviews proposed roadmap for gas sector restructuring, deregulation
text:
Finance Minister reviews proposed roadmap for gas sector restructuring, deregulation
- By Shoaib Nizami -
- Oct 19, 2026
Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue, Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb on Monday chaired a high-level meeting to review the proposed restructuring and deregulation roadmap for Pakistan’s gas sector, focusing on financial sustainability, operational efficiency, consumer welfare and greater private-sector participation.
The proposed reforms aim to establish a financially sustainable, efficient and competitive gas market that supports businesses, encourages private investment and protects consumer welfare, said a press release issued by the Ministry of Finance.
The meeting discussed a phased transition towards greater competition, supported by effective regulation, improved operational performance and a more sustainable approach to gas pricing and supply.
Participants reviewed key sectoral challenges, including circular debt, cross-subsidies, unaccounted-for-gas (UFG) losses and supply-demand imbalances. Discussions focused on addressing legacy liabilities, improving the financial viability of gas utilities and ensuring that existing financial pressures do not undermine the proposed market structure or place an undue burden on consumers.
A sustainable resolution of legacy circular debt and a clear approach to address cross-subsidies were identified as important to the viability of restructured entities and the transition to a competitive market.
The meeting also discussed the expected outcomes of the reform framework, including enhanced energy security, increased private-sector investment, reduced fiscal and sovereign risks, greater business-to-business transactions, more stable and sustainable gas pricing, improved access to competitively priced gas for exporters, and lower system losses through stronger efficiency benchmarks and performance-based incentives.
The Finance Minister emphasized the importance of aligning all stakeholders around a practical and implementable reform architecture. The proposed framework draws on international experience, including gas-sector reforms in Türkiye and the United Kingdom, while taking into account Pakistan’s institutional structure, market conditions and consumer interests.
Participants also stressed the need for careful sequencing to safeguard security of supply, protect regulated consumers and create a predictable environment for private-sector participation.
The proposed framework will be presented to the Prime Minister, following which further technical work and stakeholder consultations will help refine the reform approach and support an orderly transition.
The meeting reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to advancing gas-sector reforms in a phased and consultative manner to strengthen financial sustainability, improve operational efficiency, attract investment and develop a more competitive gas market while safeguarding consumer interests.
The meeting was attended by the Federal Minister for Petroleum, the Adviser to the Prime Minister on Privatization, the Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Energy, senior officials from the Petroleum and Finance Divisions, representatives of gas utilities and the World Bank team.

title: Alberta votes on leaving Canada; separatist movement
text:
Alberta votes on leaving Canada; separatist movement likely to outlast expected defeat
- By Reuters -
- Oct 19, 2026
CALGARY: Oil-rich Alberta holds a nonbinding referendum on Monday on whether the western province should secede from Canada, a debate many believe will not be settled by what is widely expected to be a defeat for the separatist cause.
Polls have consistently shown that a majority of Alberta voters oppose splitting from Canada. Economic grievances have fueled the independence campaign in the province, which is home to 5 million people and slightly smaller than Texas despite having one-sixth the population.
The Alberta separatist movement adds to the pressures on Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, who has made defending Canada’s sovereignty a central mission as he confronts US tariffs and President Donald Trump’s repeated calls for Canada to become the 51st state.
Many Alberta separatists believe the Liberal Party-led federal government in Ottawa has constrained the Conservative-governed province’s oil industry through environmental policies, and that Alberta, the country’s energy heartland, contributes more to Canada’s economy than it receives in return.
“Canada has an imbalanced system which feeds the central population and government at the expense of the outlying producing provinces such as Alberta,” said Cory Morgan, founder of a pro-separation advertising organization called Pathway to Independence.
Carney, who grew up in Alberta, spent much of the past week campaigning for the “stay” side, urging supporters to vote and appealing to national pride.
Polls are scheduled to close at 8 p.m. MDT on Monday (0200 GMT on Tuesday) with results published as they arrive.
An Angus Reid poll released Friday showed 66% of Albertans plan to vote to remain in Canada, but three in five believe “there will never be an end to the separatist movement” in the province.
“This issue is not going away now. Because the separatists are mobilized. They’ve networked. They’re connected,” said Mount Royal University political scientist Duane Bratt in Calgary.
While separatist sentiment has existed in the province for decades, Premier Danielle Smith is the first Alberta leader to put the question to voters. Smith, who has urged Albertans to remain in Canada, called the referendum after months of pressure from a small but vocal flank of her governing United Conservative Party.
If a majority votes in favor, Smith has said she would seek a binding referendum on separation.
“Separating, to my point of view, is completely ridiculous,” said Ross Watson of Calgary after casting his ballot in favor of “remain” in an advance poll last week.
“I think the grievances that people have are completely unfounded. But I also think these people will probably never shut up.”
SENDING A MESSAGE
Monday’s referendum is the first time a vote on separation from the rest of Canada has been held in a province outside majority French-speaking Quebec, where separatist sentiment derives from language and cultural differences.
In Alberta, the issue is more about dollars than identity. Carney has appealed to national pride in arguing Alberta should remain part of Canada.
“Canada is not a transaction between provinces. It’s not about gross and net, gives and gets,” Carney said Friday in Red Deer, Alberta.
Partly to address the grievances that have driven separatist sentiment in Alberta, Carney has overturned some environmental policies and supported a proposed oil pipeline that would increase Alberta’s exports to Asia.
Among the one-third of Albertans who would vote in favor of a future binding referendum on separation, 60% told pollsters their motivation was to “send a message” to Canada’s federal government. Only 37% of respondents to the Angus Reid poll said their motivation was an independent nation.
Separatist groups have published transition plans, but key questions about how independence would work on issues such as defence, currency and border controls remain unresolved.
Bratt said the real question is where the movement goes from here.
“Do they focus on generating support for a future referendum? Or do they splinter off and create their own party — a real, powerful separatist party?” Bratt said.

title: Food Deptt raises daily wheat release to 4,000 tonnes in KP
text:
Food Deptt raises daily wheat release to 4,000 tonnes in KP
- By Agencies -
- Oct 19, 2026
PESHAWAR: In response to a ruling by the Peshawar High Court and instructions from the Cabinet Oversight Committee, the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Food Department raised the daily wheat release quota from 3,000 to 4,000 metric tonnes.
The National Reserve Center (NRC) warehouses in Azakhel will provide the extra 1,000 metric tonnes of functioning flour mills in order to ensure prompt utilisation of stockpiled wheat and prevent additional losses.
The Food Department has announced that the additional quota would be allocated to each district in accordance with the 43.84 million people in the province.
The Director of Food has issued necessary instructions to all district food controllers and rationing controllers to implement the revised allocation.
Under the revised arrangement, Peshawar will receive an additional 116 metric tonnes daily, followed by Mardan with 67 tonnes, Swabi with 46 tonnes, Charsadda with 45 tonnes, Nowshera with 43 tonnes and Lower Dir with 40 tonnes.
Other allocations include 39 tonnes for Lower Swat, 35 tonnes for Abbottabad, 44 tonnes for Mansehra, 45 tonnes for Dera Ismail Khan, 33 tonnes for Bannu, 32 tonnes for Bajaur and 30 tonnes for Kohat. The remaining quota has been distributed among other districts according to their respective allocations.
The department decided to release the additional wheat after a report by the Storage and Enforcement Officer at NRC Azakhel highlighted damage to stored stocks caused by recent flash flooding.
According to the report, floodwater entered the warehouses and affected the lower layers of wheat bags. Six of the centre’s 11 warehouses sustained damage, while the remaining five stayed safe.
The report recommended the immediate release of stocks to prevent further damage, particularly in view of forecast rainfall.
To ensure transparency, the Director of Food has directed district food controllers and rationing controllers to submit verified lists of operational flour mills to the release committee before lifting wheat stocks. The move aims to maintain a proper record of wheat release and distribution.
The notification also makes it mandatory to update all records relating to wheat allocations, transportation and release on the ICT application without delay.
Government flour produced from the additional wheat will be distributed to consumers through authorised dealers at officially announced pricing, according to relevant officials.
To ensure that the public benefits from the increased supply of wheat, the department has instructed all concerned officials to closely monitor district allocations, confirm that flour mills are functioning, and guarantee the sale of government flour at set prices.

Abu Dhabi’s Department of Culture and Tourism (DCT Abu Dhabi) is working in close partnership with Sphere Entertainment to develop the project, which is the company’s first outside the US.
The completed venue, situated between Yas Mall and Sea World Abu Dhabi, will offer a versatile seating capacity of up to 20,000 people, and is set to be delivered by the end of 2029.
In addition to its unmistakable architecture, Sphere Abu Dhabi will deliver a broad spectrum of entertainment offerings such as international concert residencies, combat sports and immersive original productions that embrace Emirati culture and highlight the talent of the region.
