title: 'Enjoying what you can't eat': Perfumers test weight-loss drug users
text:
'Enjoying what you can't eat': Perfumers test weight-loss drug users' appetite for food-inspired scents
- By Reuters -
- Oct 19, 2026
LONDON/VERSOIX, Switzerland, Oct 19: From cherry and banoffee pie to tabasco and sesame, the list of food aromas popping up in luxury fragrances keeps growing. Now some perfume makers are starting to ask if weight-loss drugs might be reshaping what consumers want in a scent.
So-called gourmand fragrances like Thierry Mugler’s pioneering cotton candy-inspired Angel and Nina Ricci’s toffee apple scent Nina have been around for decades. More recent growth in the segment has been attributed to the pandemic-era boom in online retail — when familiar food associations helped sales of perfumes that cannot be smelled before purchase — and the growing prominence of Gen Z consumers.
But as scent makers experiment with more novel flavour aromas, Reuters conversations with eight fragrance manufacturers and top perfume brands revealed how they are assessing GLP-1 users’ responses to these food-linked smells.
Givaudan and IFF , two of the world’s largest flavour and fragrance houses, British-owned scent maker CPL Aromas and French cosmetics giant L’Oreal all said they have explored the link between the increasingly popular drugs and scent preferences.
All four companies, as well as four scientists Reuters spoke to, stressed that more research was needed.
RESEARCH SUGGESTS GLP-1 USERS SEEK PLEASURE IN SCENTS
Common negative side effects of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs like Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy and Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro include nausea and gastrointestinal issues. Researchers are also looking at other potential effects, some unexpected, including a reduction in alcohol cravings or urges to gamble and impulse-shop, and changes to smell and taste.
“(GLP-1 drugs having) a chemosensory effect is not a far-fetched idea,” said Paule Joseph, co-director of the National Smell and Taste Center at the US National Institutes of Health.
As GLP-1 drugs reshape appetite, they also affect the tissue of the olfactory bulb that processes odour, although Joseph said it was too early to predict how, or even if, that might impact odour perception.
Research conducted by IFF suggests GLP-1 therapies may spark a greater interest in scent as a source of sensory pleasure, said Celine Manetta, health and wellness director, R&D, at IFF Scent.
IFF is already using such insights to identify notes and produce fragrances that evoke emotional responses, she said.
L’Oreal, observing findings that show GLP-1 users crave pleasure, fragrances and scents, has drawn similar conclusions.
“They compensate for the pleasure of food, or pleasure of taste, with other forms of enjoyment,” said L’Oreal Paris’ Global Brand President Laetitia Toupet.
Givaudan has been studying the possible link for around a year, said Arnaud Guggenbuhl, the Swiss firm’s global head of marketing for fine fragrance.
GLP-1 use can alter fragrance preferences, he said, with some beloved smells suddenly repellent while other scents become appealing. The overall trend, the company found, was an increase in interest in fragrance and perfume.
Givaudan is now expanding its gourmand offering, creating fragrances that reproduce the layered scent of cakes like banoffee, panettone and cupcakes.
“You can have the crispy part, the tarty part, the milky part and the creamy part,” Guggenbuhl said. “The full fragrance smells like a true cake.”
STILL ENJOYING WHAT YOU CAN’T EAT
Unlike manufacturers, which develop the scents used as ingredients in perfumes, fragrance brand owners like Puig (PUIGb.MC), opens new tab and Coty are generally not researching the possible GLP-1 link.
But they are keenly attuned to what is happening in the market — both in terms of growth trends and shifts in taste — and are taking steps to adapt.
Over 1 billion people globally are now obese, according to the World Health Organization. That provides an enormous pool of potential customers for weight-loss drugs. Pharmaceutical companies and analysts predict the GLP-1 market may be worth up to $150 billion by 2030.
That could also mean a bigger perfume market.
Gourmet and edible is now the second-largest fragrance group for product innovation behind floral scents, said Clotilde Drape, global beauty analyst at market analysis agency Mintel, with its share having risen to 24% over the last year from 9% two years earlier.
A study of GLP-1 users in the US by market researcher NIQ, meanwhile, found they spent 26% more on fragrances than the typical person.
“GLP-1 users are overall more invested in beauty, as they spend more across most categories,” said Anna Mayo, NIQ’s vice president of beauty and personal care thought leadership.
Both Coty and Puig expect traditional vanilla-based scents, such as Burberry’s (BRBY.L), opens new tab Goddess perfume and Yves Saint Laurent’s Libre Eau de Parfum, to remain popular. But other edible notes are becoming more prominent, they told Reuters.
“There has been a more sophisticated, more adult evolution. There are now many different notes available on the market: boozy, whisky, rum, tequila,” said Gregorio Sola, senior perfumer and creative director at Puig.
Perfumers are also incorporating spicy components like tabasco and bitter notes of cocoa.
Gen Z consumers in particular are seeking savoury, salty fermented and roasted aromas over sweetness, said Nelly Di Mercurio, global marketing and communications director at CPL Aromas. Sesame, miso, rice, truffle and even matcha-based fragrances were also emerging, she said.
And Jean Holtzmann, chief brands officer for Coty’s prestige division, pointed to new combinations of vanilla with nuts like pistachio.
“The next generation of gourmand is … about taste and texture rather than just being sweet,” he said.
Givaudan’s Guggenbuhl, for his part, believes creaminess — banana, whipped cream and warm milk — will be the next trend to sweep the market. But regardless of the flavour, with GLP-1 users set to remain a driving force, he sees no letup in the expansion of gourmand fragrances.
“What they cannot eat anymore, they still want to enjoy.”

title: WNBA silent after Finals teams skip national anthem
text:
WNBA silent after Finals teams skip national anthem
- By Zaeem Basir -
- Oct 19, 2026
Leaves the Court During Anthem So close to the start of Game 1 of the WNBA Finals on Tuesday night, the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries stopped proceedings and headed to the locker room, returning to the court just after the singing of the national anthem had concluded.
Their abrupt departure, per the league’s own guidelines that instruct players, coaches and team staff to line up along the sidelines or foul lines for the anthem, has been met with fierce discussions among sports fans and pundits as to what may have prompted the collective exit… and return.
Since then, the league, the Atlanta Dream and the Golden State Valkyries have been mum, ignoring follow-up phone calls from media and refusing to explain to the public what their actions imply.
Reporters covering the game said neither team spoke to the anthem omission during post-game press conferences, and the WNBA has yet to tell the media how, if at all, the league plans to discipline the players or enforce the presence of the anthem during Game 2, which is next week.
All of this adds to the mysterious lack of public knowledge about the teams’ decisions ahead of what will now be a three-game series.
With the league’s management of the protocol enforcement under a spotlight, sports commentators on the issue say the debate has bigger implications for how professional sports are managed and held publicly accountable.
With the league’s public documentation of what it expected from pregame ceremonies and a lack of any public statement from the league or the teams, it appears to be an open-ended question to whether players will stay on the court for the next anthem or if the league will issue any official instructions – all eyes will definitely be on the court as the high-profile playoff series continues.

title: Crime rate in Punjab has gone down drastically, says Azma Bukhari
text:
Crime rate in Punjab has gone down drastically, says Azma Bukhari
- By Web Desk -
- Oct 19, 2026
Punjab Information Minister Azma Bukhari has described the rise in rape cases in the province as alarming, while rejecting claims that overall crime has increased.
Speaking at a press conference in Lahore, Azma Bukhari criticized journalists who had reported an increase in crime, saying those who considered themselves senior journalists should verify information before posting on social media.
She alleged that many people were trying to undermine the chief minister out of jealousy.
Bukhari also criticized what she called prominent journalists, accusing them of relying on reports circulated by propaganda cells.
“I feel sorry for journalists who claim that crime has increased in Punjab. They should verify information before posting on social media,” she said.
She also acknowledged the rise in rape cases, describing it as a matter of serious concern. She stressed that Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz had adopted a zero-tolerance policy towards incidents of sexual violence.
The minister also claimed that motor vehicle theft had fallen by 75%, adding that the overall crime rate in the province had declined into negative territory.

title: Norway targets 'harmful' social media, games with under-16 ban
text:
Norway targets 'harmful' social media, games with under-16 ban
- By Reuters -
- Oct 19, 2026
OSLO: Norway’s planned social media ban for children will include provisions targeting “harmful platforms”, the government said on Monday, naming messaging and gaming services Roblox, Snapchat and TikTok among those affected.
The Nordic country said in April it would present a bill in parliament by the end of the year to ban children from using social media until they turn 16, making technology companies responsible for age verification. It did not name any platforms at the time.
Several European nations are seeking to rein in children’s social media use after Australia took the lead with the world’s first ban on under-16s last December, which included apps such as Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat and YouTube.
Norway’s government said in a statement on Monday that its bill was intended to address the full range of risks children face on social media and that it would affect “many platforms”.
“This includes everything from exposure to harmful content and addictive features to illegal marketing and unwanted contact from strangers,” Children and Families Minister Lene Vaagslid said in the statement.
The planned legislation provides tech companies with an incentive to remove harmful content and addictive features, she said.
The ministry went on to define what it called harmful platforms as “social media that, through its design, features or content, poses a risk to children’s emotional, cognitive or physical development or safety.”
“The government believes that platforms such as TikTok, Roblox, and Snapchat will be covered by the law,” it said.
It did not immediately respond to a question about which other apps could be affected.
Snap Inc, Roblox Corporation and TikTok owner ByteDance did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Children and young people will still have access to messaging services and games that are deemed harmless, the ministry said.

title: Dell releases new 14S laptop featuring Intel Wildcat Lake chips
text:
Dell releases new 14S laptop featuring Intel Wildcat Lake chips and budget options
- By Kumail Shah -
- Oct 19, 2026
Dell has just launched the newest version of its Dell 14S laptop. Earlier this year, the company released the Dell 14S DS14260 in May, which used Intel Panther Lake processors. In September, Dell introduced the Dell 14S DS14270 with updated Wildcat Lake chips.
Dell originally planned to launch the updated Dell 14S in the fall for the Northern Hemisphere. At that time, the company did not share pricing details. However, it did confirm that the Dell 14S DS14270 would use the same Core 5 320 and Core 7 350 processors found in the more affordable XPS 13, which we reviewed earlier this year (currently $839 on Amazon).
The company has now begun selling its new 14-inch laptop worldwide without any prior announcement. In the US, the DS14270 starts at $649, making it more than 50% cheaper than the DS14260. Prices in other regions are AUD 1,271.60 in Australia, CAD 899.99 in Canada, €821 in the Eurozone, and £721.20 in the UK.
Part of the $750 price difference is because the DS14270 has half the RAM and storage of the DS14260. The Dell 14S DS14270 starts with 256 GB of PCIe Gen 3 storage and 8 GB of LPDDR5x-7467 RAM in single-channel mode.
Dell also offers versions of the laptop with 512 GB or 1 TB PCIe Gen 4 SSDs and 16 GB of RAM, though these still use single-channel mode. You can also choose an 1800p IPS display with a 120 Hz refresh rate and 450 nits of brightness instead of the standard 1200p, 60 Hz, 300-nit screen.
Every version of the laptop comes with a 3-cell, 61.2 Wh battery, which helps keep the weight at 1.15 kg. Reports say the battery can last up to 21 hours when streaming Netflix at 150 nits on a 1200p display. For more information, visit Dell’s website.

title: Marseille, Lille official club stores looted amid unrest in France
text:
Marseille, Lille official club stores looted amid unrest in France
- By Reuters -
- Oct 19, 2026
Olympique de Marseille and fellow French top-flight club Lille said their official stores were looted during weekend unrest in France.
Marseille condemned on Monday the incident at its shop on La Canebiere, the city’s historic main avenue, while Lille thanked everyone who had helped and offered support.
Earlier on Monday, Marseille authorities imposed a ban on public gatherings and demonstrations across the city after violent protests and looting. The ban runs from midday (1000 GMT) until 8 p.m. (1800 GMT).
“Olympique de Marseille condemns in the strongest possible terms the acts of violence and looting targeting its official store on the Canebiere and expresses its solidarity with its partner Puma, which operates the store,” the club said in a statement.
“These events have caused significant property damage, forcing the club to temporarily close this store to the public. Fans may, however, continue to visit OM’s other official stores in Marseille. The club will inform its fans as soon as conditions allow for a reopening …”
Fellow Ligue 1 club Lille said its store on Rue Faidherbe in the downtown area was hit by severe vandalism and looting on Saturday and would remain closed until further notice.
“LOSC would also like to acknowledge and thank everyone who has offered support over the past few hours – first and foremost our store employees, but also the many passersby, fans and non-fans alike, who spontaneously offered their help, a helping hand, and words of comfort,” Lille said on Sunday.
A major cleanup operation took place on Sunday in cities across France, from Lille in the north to Marseille in the south and from Strasbourg in the east to Bordeaux in the southwest, where a masked group invaded the residence of the local prefect.
Marseille are ninth in the league table after seven matches and return to action on Thursday when they visit Austrian side Sturm Graz in the Europa League.
Lille are fourth in Ligue 1 and host Turkish champions Galatasaray in the Champions League on Wednesday.

title: Apple iPhone Duo battery capacity and EU energy label details confirmed
text:
Apple iPhone Duo battery capacity and EU energy label details confirmed
- By Kumail Shah -
- Oct 19, 2026
Back in July, a leaker suggested the Apple iPhone Duo would have a fairly small battery. That prediction from Digital Chat Station turned out to be accurate. Apple has now confirmed through the EU energy label that the foldable iPhone comes with a 4,883 mAh battery.
This means the iPhone Duo’s battery is a bit bigger than the 4,800 mAh battery in the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 ($1,699 on Amazon), even though Samsung’s foldable phone is much thinner and lighter.
The Huawei Pura X Max, which is just as thick as the iPhone Duo, has a bigger 5,300 mAh battery. The iPhone 18 Pro Max also comes with a larger 5,391 mAh battery.
The EU energy label says this battery should last for 51 hours and 30 minutes, which is more than ten hours less than the iPhone 18 Pro Max. However, this kind of battery life usually only happens with light use.
Apple says the battery will last for more than 1,000 charge cycles before its capacity drops to 80 percent. If you fully charge the phone every day, you’ll need to replace the battery in just under three years, which costs $229.
The iPhone Duo is IP68-certified and has the same drop resistance and repairability ratings as the iPhone 18 Pro Max. These ratings come from Apple, not the EU. We’ll only know how durable the iPhone Duo really is once it starts shipping.

title: DG Khan airport to become international facility by January 2028
text:
DG Khan airport to become international facility by January 2028
- By Web Desk -
- Oct 19, 2026
Pakistan has begun a Rs.5.5 billion expansion of Dera Ghazi Khan (DG Khan) airport, with completion expected by January 2028, Federal Energy Minister Sardar Awais Ahmad Khan Leghari has said.
Speaking during a visit to inspect the project, Leghari said Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) teams were working on site, including on plans to extend the runway.
The upgrade follows an announcement by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to develop the airport for international flights.
Awais Leghari said the project would improve travel facilities for residents of Dera Ghazi Khan and create new opportunities for economic development in South Punjab.
The airport expansion is one of four major development projects announced for the city by the prime minister.
The other initiatives include a cancer hospital, a long-term sewerage scheme and the widening and rehabilitation of roads.
According to Leghari, the sewerage project is being designed to meet the region’s needs for the next 50 years. Wider and rehabilitated roads are also expected to improve transport and commuting.
The government says the projects will strengthen public services and support regional development.
During the visit, Leghari also addressed electricity load shedding and efforts to reduce losses across Pakistan’s power distribution network.
He said power cuts were being carried out according to an established schedule, while constraints on gas supplies linked to wider geopolitical tensions had increased the cost of electricity generation.
The government was introducing modern technology to tackle electricity theft and reduce transmission and distribution losses, he said.
The Advanced Power Management System (APMS) is being installed on transformers across the country to identify areas with high levels of electricity theft.
He said the system would allow authorities to disconnect targeted transformers rather than penalize thousands of paying consumers connected to an entire feeder.
He added that load shedding would continue on feeders where AT&C losses reached 30 percent or more.
The minister said the government would take action against electricity theft and persistent non-payment as part of wider efforts to improve the performance of the power distribution system.
Earlier, the Project Director of the Civil Aviation Authority briefed the Federal Minister on the airport expansion project and presented him with a commemorative shield.

title: Man City confirms Semenyo injury as Haaland races to be fit for AEK clash
text:
Man City confirms Semenyo injury as Haaland races to be fit for AEK clash
- By Reuters -
- Oct 19, 2026
Manchester City forward Antoine Semenyo has been sidelined for up to eight weeks after suffering a knee injury at the weekend but striker Erling Haaland could be fit for Tuesday’s Champions League clash at home to AEK Athens, manager Enzo Maresca said.
Ghana international Semenyo limped to the tunnel following Saturday’s 3-2 home win over Ipswich Town, shortly after Haaland took a knock on his foot and ankle in stoppage time.
Maresca said Semenyo’s injury was not as bad as first feared but the 26-year-old, who has two goals and three assists in the Premier League this season, needed time to recover.
“It could be eight weeks. Now the most important thing is recovery. When he is back in December it will be like a new player. Collateral. It’s not muscle,” he told a press conference on Monday ahead of the AEK game.
Semenyo was among the substitutes against Ipswich but came off the bench in the 77th minute at the Etihad Stadium.
“We tried to save him, we tried to keep him fresh, just give him some minutes, he didn’t play a lot but sometimes things happen, we cannot control,” added Maresca.
The manager said there were also some doubts about Norwegian Haaland’s fitness for Tuesday, but he remained hopeful.
“He can be available, we will see, we have a session now. We have some doubts after Saturday’s game. He was quite good yesterday, better. So we will see today,” Maresca added.
Haaland’s double against Ipswich helped City remain perfect in the top flight with seven straight wins. The 26-year-old has netted in his last eight appearances for City, scoring 12 times.
“For sure, to replace Erling it is always difficult but we have some different options,” Maresca said.
“Phil (Foden) can be one of the solutions, not the only one… but now, at the moment the number nine is Erling.”
Maresca is eyeing the AEK match as a chance for City to bounce back from last week’s 4-2 loss at home to European champions Paris St Germain, which left City 17th in the table with three points from two matches.
“I think the response after the PSG game was quite good … It’s a Champions League game, different competition, but the ambition has to be the same, try to win games,” he added.

title: Fire intensifies at garment factory warehouse in Karachi’s SITE Metroville
text:
Karachi factory fire remains uncontrolled after five hours
- By Afzal Khan -
- Oct 19, 2026
KARACHI: A fire that broke out at a factory in Karachi’s SITE area remained uncontrolled even after five hours, as firefighters continued efforts to bring the blaze under control with 11 fire tenders, two snorkels and two water bowsers taking part in the operation.
According to officials, the fire initially broke out on the second floor of the factory before spreading to the third floor. The presence of large quantities of plastic granules, thread and cardboard inside the factory has added to the challenge of controlling the blaze.
Officials said two fire tenders were initially dispatched to the site after the fire was reported. However, as the intensity of the fire increased, additional firefighting vehicles were called in to assist in the operation.
The firefighting operation was continuing five hours after the fire broke out, with 11 fire tenders, two snorkels and two water bowsers engaged in efforts to extinguish the flames.
Officials said the factory staff were immediately evacuated and shifted to a safe location as soon as the fire broke out.
Firefighters continued their efforts to control the blaze and prevent it from spreading further. The fire had already extended from the second to the third floor of the factory, while a large quantity of combustible material remained inside the building.
The cause of the fire and the extent of the damage had not been provided in the information available so far.
Fire brigade officials noted that a fire had also erupted at the same location a few days ago, adding that the factory had converted the third floor into a warehouse. They further mentioned that two water bowsers are assisting the firefighting operation.
The Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KWSC) has declared an emergency at the NIPA and Sakhi Hassan hydrants after the fire brigade requested immediate assistance, a spokesperson for the corporation said.
On the directions of KWSC Chief Executive Officer Ahmed Ali Siddique, an emergency was also imposed at the Crush Plant hydrant.
The spokesperson stated that water tankers have immediately been dispatched to the scene.
He added that the in-charge of the hydrant cell remains in constant contact with fire brigade and rescue officials. Furthermore, the CEO’s focal person for hydrants is personally supervising the operation, and the corporation is extending full cooperation to the rescue teams.

title: ‘We don’t need political lessons from Fazal ur Rehman,’ says Abid Sher Ali
text:
‘We don’t need political lessons from Fazal ur Rehman,’ says Abid Sher Ali
- By Ghulam Awais -
- Oct 19, 2026
PML-N leader Abid Sher Ali has criticised Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, questioning his political stance and recalling the party’s support for former president Pervez Musharraf’s constitutional measures.
Speaking to the media, Abid Sher Ali said Maulana Fazlur Rehman could explain the reasons behind his anger, adding that he was well aware of the history of the Eighth Amendment.
He said his party had opposed the Legal Framework Order (LFO) and the imposition of emergency but alleged that others had supported Musharraf’s actions.
Abid Sher Ali said Musharraf had brought terrorism and instability to the country. He also questioned the past political arrangements under which, he said, a party with 40 seats was given the opposition leadership and the chairmanship of the Kashmir Committee.
“We do not need political lessons from anyone. We stand with the state and its institutions,” he said.
He warned that there would be no compromise with elements involved in attacks on state institutions. He added that efforts were being made to hold meaningful dialogue on all issues.
The PML-N leader said the country was currently fighting a war against terrorism and that security personnel were sacrificing their lives every day. He said the sacrifices of the martyrs conveyed a clear message of peace and security and called for unity among all sections of society to eliminate terrorism and establish lasting peace.
Referring to Maulana Fazlur Rehman, Abid Sher Ali said the JUI-F chief himself could explain whether he was “playing on both sides”.
He also urged people to decide whether they wanted to stand with the nation or alongside terrorists.
Abid Sher Ali on Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s long march
Responding to a journalist’s question about how the government would handle a sit-in or long march by Maulana Fazlur Rehman, Abid Sher Ali said the JUI-F chief had organised marches in the past and that his party had welcomed them.
He said a long march was Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s democratic right and that there was no objection to peaceful protest within the constitutional and legal framework.
Abid Sher Ali also rejected the possibility of a political conspiracy against PML-N President Nawaz Sharif, saying no such conspiracy was currently underway against him.
He added that any conspiracy taking place at present was fundamentally against Pakistan.

title: Ambani's Jio draws about $25 billion in IPO anchor investor bids
text:
Ambani's Jio draws about $25 billion in IPO anchor investor bids
- By Reuters -
- Oct 19, 2026
MUMBAI, Oct 19: Mukesh Ambani’s $3.2 billion Jio Platforms IPO has drawn bids of about $25 billion from institutions including GIC, BlackRock and Fidelity, totaling almost 30 times the quota reserved for anchor investors, two people familiar with the matter said.
The telecoms, cloud and AI group on Monday opened its record initial public offering to institutional investors who can bid for up to 30% of the offering exclusively earmarked for them, before the issue opens for public subscription on Wednesday.
Jio upended India’s telecoms market in 2016 by offering free voice calls and cheap data and soon became the country’s biggest mobile operator. It now has more than 500 million subscribers and competes with Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Its listing is seen as a test of what global investors will pay for that scale and for Jio’s expansion into cloud and AI.
Led by Mukesh Ambani’s son Akash Ambani, Jio operates Reliance Industries’ (RELI.NS), opens new tab telecom and digital businesses, spanning mobile services, fixed broadband, cloud, entertainment, enterprise technology and AI offerings.
Fidelity, Singapore’s GIC, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock were among the investors to place bids for the institutional quota, the two people told Reuters.
Reliance, which is the ultimate owner of Jio Platforms, did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.
ADIA, BlackRock, Fidelity and GIC did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.
Jio’s IPO follows September’s listing of the National Stock Exchange of India, underscoring investor appetite for large offerings in the Indian market. It will be the first offering by Reliance since its listing of Reliance Petroleum in 2006.
Year-to-date Indian IPO proceeds rose 8.3% to $12.65 billion compared with the same period last year, LSEG data shows.
A successful IPO would place Jio Platforms among the top four Indian listed companies by market capitalisation, behind its parent Reliance, its rival Bharti Airtel, and the country’s largest private lender HDFC Bank.
Jio plans to use up to 275 billion Indian rupees ($2.90 billion) of the net proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings of its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm.

title: Emvistegrast pill succeeds in mid-stage bowel disease trial
text:
Emvistegrast pill succeeds in mid-stage bowel disease trial
- By Reuters -
- Oct 19, 2026
Gilead Sciences said on Monday its experimental once-daily pill emvistegrast reduced symptoms of a chronic bowel illness in more patients than placebo in a mid-stage trial.
Emvistegrast met its main goal in a mid-stage study of adults with moderate to severe ulcerative colitis, a chronic condition that causes inflammation and ulcers in the digestive tract.
The oral drug is designed to block the α4β7 integrin pathway, a target already validated in inflammatory bowel disease. After 12 weeks, 66% of patients on the 200 mg dose saw their disease symptoms improve, compared with 37% on placebo. Clinical remission rates were also higher, with 31% of patients on treatment achieving remission versus 8% in the placebo group.
The drug was generally well tolerated, with overall side-effect rates comparable between the treatment and placebo arms and no serious side effects linked to the study medication. BMO Capital Markets analysts called the data “an incremental positive for Gilead’s inflammatory strategy that establishes emvistegrast as a credible oral α4β7 option.” Based on the results, Gilead said it plans to start a late-stage monotherapy study of the pill in 2027.
About Emvistegrast
Emvistegrast (GS-1427) is an investigational oral α4β7 integrin inhibitor being developed for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The α4β7 pathway is a clinically validated target in IBD, and emvistegrast is part of Gilead’s broader effort to advance differentiated therapies for inflammatory diseases. Emvistegrast is not approved anywhere globally, and its safety and efficacy have not been established.
About the SWIFT Study
SWIFT is a Phase 2 randomized, placebo-controlled study evaluating the efficacy, safety and tolerability of emvistegrast in adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis. The study was designed to assess the potential of emvistegrast to improve disease activity and clinically meaningful outcomes for people living with ulcerative colitis, while further characterizing its safety profile.

Dar directs measures to facilitate exports of surplus commodities
- By Web Desk -

ISLAMABAD: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar on Monday directed relevant authorities to take practical measures to address bottlenecks and facilitate the export of surplus commodities while ensuring adequate domestic supplies and price stability.
Dar issued the directives while chairing a meeting to review the domestic supply and demand of essential commodities, prevailing market conditions and opportunities to access international markets.
Participants discussed measures to maintain sufficient availability of essential commodities in the domestic market, ensure price stability and facilitate trade, according to an official statement.
The deputy prime minister directed all concerned authorities to take practical steps to remove constraints and facilitate exports of surplus commodities.
The meeting was attended by the ministers for national food security and research and climate change, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Tariq Bajwa, the secretaries of commerce and national food security and research, and senior officials from federal and provincial departments.

Chairing the first meeting of the Prime Minister’s Subcommittee on Aquaculture and Shrimp Value Chain, the minister stressed the need for coordinated efforts to increase production, improve quality and strengthen Pakistan’s competitiveness in international markets.

title: Pakistan railways police officers booked for kidnapping, torturing KMC city warden

Pakistan railways police officers booked for kidnapping, torturing KMC city warden

title: Gaza teen amputees recount hopes, lost dreams in Jordan centre
text:
Gaza teen amputees recount hopes, lost dreams in Jordan centre
- By AFP -
- Oct 19, 2026
Amman: At 15 years old, Mahmoud Abou Nusair recalls the love he had for football, before Israeli fire in Gaza took his leg and his dreams away.
He is one of more than 450 Palestinian amputees receiving care and prosthetic limbs at a centre in Amman and in Gaza, part of an initiative run by Jordan’s Restoring Hope Society.- Mahmoud, 15 –
On October 31, 2025, during the ongoing Gaza ceasefire agreed that month, Mahmoud Abou Nusair was looking for firewood in Deir al-Balah, in the central Gaza Strip, when a bullet struck his right leg.
With Gaza’s healthcare system decimated after three years of war, he had to undergo an amputation below the knee after his injury worsened.
“The doctor came to see me and told me, ‘We have to amputate your foot’,” he told AFP.
“My mother said, ‘No, doctor, that’s his soul. What will he do if he wants to go out, play football, skate or go to the beach? It’s a sin to cut off his foot’.”
“My first reaction was to scream,” he said. “Then I took a look at the injured people around me in the hospital. They all had amputated arms and legs, so I told myself: my injury is better.
“Then I said, ‘Amputate it, doctor’.”
After his injury, he recalls having to wait half an hour until a horse-drawn cart picked him up and took him to Al-Aqsa hospital.
He was taken to Nasser hospital in Khan Younis in southern Gaza, where he spent two weeks.
He still mourns the loss of his sports equipment and his five balls, all of which he lost when his home was destroyed.
– Zuhdi, 17 –
At the facility in Amman, Zuhdi Abou Shanab, 17, says he lost his entire right leg in a strike that killed nine people and injured 28 others on September 8, 2025.
“I was on my way to buy groceries for my mother and I ran into a friend so we stopped to talk,” he told AFP.
“When they struck the building we were standing next to, I lost consciousness and when I woke up, I found myself wounded and bleeding.
“A week later, the doctors told me that I was suffering from an infection in the artery in my leg and that three veins and three arteries in my leg had been severed,” he continued.
Read Also: ‘They lie to us’: One year on, Gazans don’t believe in ceasefire
“I underwent an operation to reattach the arteries and veins, but it failed, so they decided to amputate my leg.”
“The war has devastated us and torn us away from our friends… there is nothing left,” he added.
But he still holds on to hope that his condition will improve, dreaming of “returning to Gaza”.
“I miss my mother, my brothers and my sisters.”
– Abdulrahman, 16 –
Abdulrahman Rihan lost the use of his legs when his family home in Jabalia, northern Gaza was bombed, the morning of January 12, 2025.
Both he and his father suffered severe wounds. They were taken to multiple hospitals in Gaza, where they “underwent difficult and painful surgeries”, Abdulrahman recounted.
Three of his brothers were also wounded. Their father, Imad Rihan, 42, said he had to “undergo some surgeries without anaesthetic in Gaza”.
“This war was very hard on us,” said the father, who lost his left leg.
“No matter how much we talk about the war, or how much you have seen of it, all of this remains but a drop in the ocean compared to the reality that we witnessed with our own eyes.”

title: Qatar will soon announce local defence production hub
text:
Qatar will soon announce local defence production hub
- By Reuters -
- Oct 19, 2026
The Gulf Arab state of Qatar will soon announce a defence production hub, the minister of state for defence affairs told the Global Security Forum in Doha on Monday.
Against the background of the Middle East conflict, which has drawn Iranian attacks on energy-rich Gulf countries, Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman Al Thani said: “We are partnering with a regional partner, in addition to other partners such as the United States, the United Kingdom, France, to make sure either we do local protection or we are investing in some of these companies.”
When asked about the threats faced by Qatar and the other Gulf countries from ballistic missiles, drones and cyberattacks, Al Thani said: “Soon we are going to announce a new partnership that we will do with the regional partners to establish a new initiative towards building capability into these three elements and others.”
He did not elaborate.
The Iran war has dealt a blow to Qatar. The country was forced to shut down much of its main LNG complex at Ras Laffan shortly after the start of hostilities and it suffered from restrictions on global shipping through the strategic Strait of Hormuz.
Qatar has historically had no large-scale defence production hub because its security model has relied on high-end foreign procurement and external security guarantees rather than building indigenous capacity.

title: Tensions over headscarves, Israel test Ankara-Baku ties
text:
Tensions over headscarves, Israel test Ankara-Baku ties
- By AFP -
- Oct 19, 2026
Istanbul: The normally close ties between Turkey and Azerbaijan have come under strain, fuelled by a dispute over Baku’s restrictions on the Islamic headscarf in schools and disagreements over Israel.
Public tensions have become evident in what has traditionally been a very close relationship between two nations which share a common language and whose bond is characterised by the slogan: One nation, two states.
Although the rhetoric has remained restrained at the top, senior officials have been more outspoken in their reactions.
On Monday, Oktay Saral, chief adviser to President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, shed his normal diplomatic reserve to denounce as “unacceptable” Azerbaijan’s move to change school uniform regulations, banning anything that conflicts with the normal uniform or the secular principles of education.
“Wearing a headscarf … is a requirement of faith!” he wrote on X.
“We expect Azerbaijan to reverse this mistake as soon as possible.”
The following day, the ruling Yeni Azerbaijan Party (YAP) hit back with a sharply worded statement denouncing Saral and MPs from Erdogan’s AKP for their “populist and irresponsible statements”.
“The recent disinformation campaign targeting Azerbaijan has become increasingly aggressive, systematic, and openly slanderous,” it said.
The confrontation reflected sharp differences between Azerbaijan — one of the most secular states in the Muslim world — and the Islamo-conservative leadership in Ankara.
But it also highlighted tensions over the growing rapprochement between Azerbaijan and Israel since Baku’s 2020 Karabakh war with arch-foe Armenia, when the Israelis supplied them with drones and other weaponry.
Turkey’s ties with Israel, by contrast, could hardly be worse, with Erdogan accusing Israel of genocide in Gaza and Ankara regularly releasing images of top-level talks with the leaders of Hamas, the Palestinian Islamist movement whose October 2023 attacks on Israel sparked its war in Gaza.
– Baku more ‘pragmatic’ –
Turkey’s pro-government media has held little back, with the Yeni Safak daily denouncing the headscarf regulations as a gesture towards Israel.
“We firmly reject attempts to deliberately distort Azerbaijani-Israeli relations, portray these ties as supposedly exceptional, and use this as a basis for making political accusations against Azerbaijan,” the country’s ruling party said.
The sharp response underscores Azerbaijan’s emergence as a regional middle power.
It is more willing to push back against Turkey as Ankara seeks to project influence from the Black Sea, increasingly ensnared by the Russia-Ukraine war, and an ever-more volatile Middle East.
“The changing geopolitical order in the greater Eurasia has enabled Azerbaijan to pursue a more pragmatic foreign policy,” said Fuad Shahbazov, an independent political analyst, indicating that meant Baku now “categorically resists the attempts of external actors, even its ally Turkey.”
Azerbaijan offers aid olive branch to Iran after drone attack
But on Friday, Kursad Zorlu, deputy head of Erdogan’s AKP, said the two sides knew how to tackle problems “within the family” in what appeared to be a tacit call for online restraint.
At a regional summit in Baku on Thursday, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan hailed “the unshakable bond … between our leaders” despite being tested “in very difficult times”.
– Too much to lose –
Observers agree the two nations share too much to risk a rupture.
“The sometimes-tense relations with Moscow and the Iran war happening next door mean that Baku cannot afford to alienate an otherwise good partner,” Ivan Klyszcz of the Estonia-based International Centre for Defence and Security (ICDS) told AFP.
“Moreover, energy cooperation, ongoing well before the current spat, is too important for both parties,” he stressed.
“For Turkey, Azerbaijan is an essential gate for Central Asia, a region … seen by Ankara as strategic.”
Paradoxically, Baku seems to hold the cards, despite the fact its population is ten times smaller than that of its ally.
“The litmus test of the Baku-Ankara axis will depend on the latter’s further attitude and commitment to quickly get back on diplomatic tracks to handle this crisis,” Shahbazov told AFP.
“Azerbaijan possesses energy leverage and access to the Central Asian region, giving it leverage over Turkey,” he said.
And this is a crucial asset, given Ankara’s ambition to maintain its role as a transit hub between Europe and Asia.
Even so, points of friction remain.
On Friday, Baku said it had issued an “international arrest warrant” for a Turkish journalist working for the Sanliurfa Olay daily. According to prosecutors, Celal Ciftci called for a “coup d’état” in Azerbaijan and promoted “religious extremism”.

title: Israel announces arrests after West Bank settler attacks on Westerners
text:
Israel announces arrests after West Bank settler attacks on Westerners
- By AFP -
- Oct 19, 2026
JERUSALEM, Undefined: Israeli police said Monday they had arrested 10 people in the West Bank after settler attacks on an American photographer and a French mayor that drew international condemnation but mixed messages from the government.
Police said they raided several locations across the occupied territory and seized cars and potential evidence related to the attacks.
The arrests come as violence increases in the West Bank, with Israeli settlers disrupting the annual olive harvest of Palestinians.
“Following the severe incidents of violence over the past weekend, including the assault of a media worker and the suspected attacks on foreign civilians, an arrest operation was conducted before dawn,” said Major General Moshe Finchi, the Israeli police’s West Bank commander.
“Suspects were arrested on suspicion of involvement in the violent incidents, violating a military commander’s order concerning a closed military zone, and illegal construction,” he said.
Rising numbers of attacks by settlers against Palestinians have drawn international outrage, with Britain describing it as “ethnic cleansing” and imposing sanctions on products from Israeli settlements.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is facing a tight race for a new mandate in October 27 elections, has tried to shore up his right-wing base and has cast doubt on the circumstances behind the recent settler attacks on Westerners.
The opposition meanwhile described the incidents as a stain on Israel’s image and accused Netanyahu of allowing the violence to happen.

title: Pakistan providing all necessary support to Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks: DG ISPR
text:
Pakistan providing all necessary support to Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks: DG ISPR
- By Hamid Ur Rehman -
- Oct 19, 2026
RAWALPINDI: Director General Inter-Services Public Relations (DG ISPR) Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has said Pakistan is providing, and will continue to provide, all necessary support to Saudi Arabia to safeguard its sovereignty, territorial integrity and security amid escalating Houthi threats.
In an interview with Independent Arabia, the DG ISPR said Saudi Arabia’s security and, above all, the protection of Haramain al-Sharifain (the Two Holy Mosques) were paramount and non-negotiable for Pakistan.
Commenting on the Makkah Joint Defence Alliance, he said Pakistan’s commitment to the arrangement was unequivocal, adding that whatever support is needed to do that is being provided and will be provided to Saudi Arabia.
Addressing reports of Houthi escalation, Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said Pakistan had been sending clear signals through its military deployments, official statements and operational measures that the alliance’s collective deterrence mechanism was in effect.
“This collective deterrence will definitely come into play as it is coming into play”, he noted.
“Pakistan is at the same time giving very strong signals that this collective deterrence is at play and has already been actualised, and we will take all necessary steps for the security and integrity of Saudi Arabia,” he said.
Read Also: DG ISPR confirms presence of Pakistani troops in Saudi Arabia under Makkah Agreement
Through our forces, our statements, our acts and our operational employment, Pakistan is giving very strong signals that this collective deterrence is ‘at play’ and has already been actualized”, Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said, adding that the message is going to everyone, whether he is in front or he is behind that.
The DG ISPR stressed that Muslim countries needed unity rather than confrontation, arguing that further escalation would bring no advantage to the countries involved.
“We need to stop attacking each other,” he said, adding that Pakistan’s political and military leadership had been working to encourage de-escalation and a peaceful resolution of regional disputes.
He also highlighted the establishment of the alliance’s General Secretariat and Strategic Political and Defence Committee, noting that its manifestation is also there on the ground.
Responding to a question about the alliance’s potential expansion, he said it was not restricted to the three participating countries and remained open to states committed to collective deterrence, regional peace, stability and security.
He also confirmed reports that Egypt and Syria had expressed interest in joining the Makkah agreement.
Asked whether the alliance was intended to counter specific countries, including Israel or Iran, the DG ISPR said it was not directed against any particular state.
He explained that any actor threatening regional peace, stability or security would automatically come within the scope of the alliance’s collective deterrence mechanism.
He said the alliance’s collective deterrence was intended to send a clear message to any elements threatening regional stability that aggression against any of its participating countries would prompt a collective response.

title: World Food Programme cuts aid to 500,000 Palestinians in Gaza, cites funding shortages
text:
World Food Programme cuts aid to 500,000 Palestinians in Gaza, cites funding shortages
- By Reuters -
- Oct 19, 2026
CAIRO/GAZA: The UN World Food Programme has said funding shortages are forcing major cuts to its aid programme in Gaza, leaving about 500,000 people without monthly food support in a territory where two-thirds of the population struggle to get enough to eat.
The WFP said it was reducing the number of recipients of its monthly assistance to 1.1 million people from 1.6 million.
In addition, food rations have been halved, cash assistance has been cut for 75,000 families, and the number of daily hot meals for those unable to cook has fallen to 150,000 from 250,000, with some families in hard-to-reach areas now receiving a hot meal only every other day.
The WFP said about 1.4 million people, or two-thirds of Gaza’s population, face crisis levels of food insecurity or worse, including roughly 200,000 people in emergency conditions.
Last year’s US-brokered Gaza ceasefire calls for the eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made towards implementing a deal to end the conflict that includes terms for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops.
LIFE IS STILL BRUTAL IN GAZA, SAYS ACTING HEAD OF WFP
“It’s a year into the agreement of this ceasefire. Well, life is still brutal here. There is no proper shelter…There is no basic services. There is no safety, no security,” acting Executive Director of the WFP Carl Skau told Reuters in Gaza.
“These cuts are happening just as we are facing the fourth winter. You know, I’ve been through the winters here, absolutely brutal,” he added.
The WFP said it urgently needs $450 million over the next six months to maintain critical operations in Gaza and the Israeli-occupied West Bank.
“We tell the world now is not the time to look away. This is the time to step up to sustain this support, to protect the progress that has been made, but also to push for early recovery,” said Skau.
Israeli forces still hold more than 60% of the territory and conduct almost daily airstrikes, while Hamas controls most of the area where more than two million Palestinians live, mostly in temporary shelters with what aid agencies call inadequate aid supplies.
The Hamas-run Gaza government media office described the WFP announcement as “catastrophic” and said it might accelerate famine in the enclave, calling for more fund to aid agencies to prevent it.
00:17
“On top of the circumstances and the difficult life, you want to make it even harder on us,” said Palestinian woman Sabrine Kuhail, standing by a tent shelter at a displacement site in Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza Strip.
“You made us hungry for three years with war, destruction, siege, and the bloodshed that is not stopping. What do you want from us? Enough, enough, we are tired.”

title: Cason Wallace agrees to 5-year contract extension with Oklahoma City Thunder
text:
Cason Wallace agrees to 5-year contract extension with Oklahoma City Thunder
- By Reuters -
- Oct 19, 2026
The Oklahoma City Thunder and guard Cason Wallace have agreed to a five-year, $139 million contract extension, according to multiple reports on Sunday night.
ESPN first reported the extension, with attribution to Wallace’s agents at Excel Sports Management.
Cason Wallace, who turns 23 on Nov. 7, made the NBA All-Defensive second team last season, when he led the league in total steals with 150. He will earn $7.42 million for the 2026-27 season before the extension kicks in.
He averaged career highs of 8.6 points, 2.6 assists and 1.9 steals per game and averaged 26.6 minutes in 77 contests (58 starts).
Wallace became a bigger part of the Thunder’s plans after they traded another elite perimeter defender, Lu Dort, to the Atlanta Hawks in the offseason.
“I think the greatest sign of respect we could have shown Cason is moving Lu in that trade,” Thunder president Sam Presti said in September.
“We potentially could have looked at a series of other options, but it’s a bit of a gesture to him to say, ‘We think you can have a great role on this team. We believe in you as a player.’ ”
He entered the league as a first-round pick (10th overall) in the 2023 draft out of Kentucky. The Dallas Mavericks drafted Wallace and traded him and Davis Bertans to Oklahoma City for the rights to Dereck Lively II.
Wallace has averaged 7.9 points, 2.9 rebounds, 2.2 assists, 1.5 steals and 24.7 minutes in 227 regular-season games (114 starts).
He has played in 48 playoff games (five starts) and averaged 6.2 points, 2.7 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.5 steals and 22.7 minutes. The Thunder won the league championship in the 2024-25 season.

title: Woman found dead in Karachi’s Defence Phase 8
text:
Woman found dead in Karachi’s Defence Phase 8
- By Afzal Khan -
- Oct 19, 2026
KARACHI: The body of a woman was found on Monday in a flat located in Defence Phase 8, ARY News reported, citing police.
According to the police, the deceased was identified as 36-year-old Shumaila. Preliminary investigations suggest that she committed suicide by severing her hamstrings.
Police transferred the body to Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC) for an autopsy.
An investigation has been launched to gather further information about the woman, her family, and the circumstances that led to the incident.
Earlier, an elderly couple who had recently returned from Canada were found dead with signs of violence inside their home in North Karachi, prompting police to register a double murder case.
The case was registered at Sir Syed Police Station on the complaint of Muhammad Anwar, the deceased man’s brother, under relevant murder provisions.
The victims were identified as Yameen and his wife, Nafisa Akhtar.
According to the complainant, Yameen had begun renovation work at the house after returning from Canada and had asked his sister to vacate the property.
Anwar told police that he became concerned when the couple stopped answering phone calls.
He visited their residence, opened the door with a duplicate key and found the bodies of his brother and sister-in-law lying in a pool of blood in the TV lounge. He then alerted the police.
The complainant alleged that unidentified assailants had killed the couple for unknown reasons.
Post-mortem examinations were completed at Abbasi Shaheed Hospital. Investigative sources said both victims had sustained severe head injuries, raising suspicion that they may have been attacked with a heavy object.
Police have yet to trace the labourers who had been working at the house. Investigators are questioning workers in the surrounding area as they attempt to establish the circumstances of the killings and identify the suspects.
Earlier, Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar sought details of the incident from SSP Central.
The home minister directed the police to take immediate steps to establish the facts and examine all aspects of the case. He also instructed Central Police to fulfil all legal requirements during the investigation and submit a report detailing the incident and initial findings.

title: 'India should keep Jasprit Bumrah fresh for ODI World Cup 2027'
text:
'India should keep Jasprit Bumrah fresh for ODI World Cup 2027'
- By Reuters -
- Oct 19, 2026
India should keep Jasprit Bumrah fresh for next year’s one-day international World Cup by selecting him mainly for test cricket and using the pace spearhead sparingly in other formats, former coach Ravi Shastri said.
Bumrah was recalled to India’s test squad for their two-match series in New Zealand last week, but will not play in the five ODIs and five Twenty20 internationals that precede the tests.
Bumrah’s career has been disrupted by back injuries, with the 32-year-old having to undergo surgery in 2023.
He was ruled out of a two-test series against Sri Lanka in August due to a left knee injury, but returned to T20 action at the Asian Games and helped India win gold.
“I don’t think he should play all three formats till the ODI World Cup,” Shastri, who coached India from 2017 to 2021, told Indian media on Sunday.
“He should play test cricket and should play sporadically between one-day internationals and T20 cricket. He also shouldn’t be playing the whole lot.
“I would rather preserve him for the test matches. That’s very important. He becomes a key member of that Indian side. Then he should be used sparingly in the other formats.”
Following their tour of New Zealand, India will host Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe in limited-overs series, before hosting Australia in a five-test series which concludes in February.
The 2027 World Cup will be held in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia from October 2 to November 21

title: Mir Raza Case: Family calls for JIT probe and public release of inquiry report
text:
Mir Raza Case: Family calls for JIT probe and public release of inquiry report
KARACHI: The father of slain entrepreneur Mir Raza on Monday demanded the formation of a Joint Investigation Team (JIT) to probe his son’s murder, ARY News reported.
Speaking to the media outside the court alongside his counsel, advocate Jibran Nasir, Mir Hussain stated that the police had shown negligence in investigating his son’s case, adding that their fears were confirmed by the judicial commission’s findings.
He demanded that Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah and Faryal Talpur hand over the judicial commission’s report to the family and make it public following the cabinet meeting.
He also called for action against the police officers found negligent by the judicial commission, noting that the family had repeatedly highlighted through the media the police’s poor performance, shortcomings, and deficiencies in the investigation.
Furthermore, he stated that the judicial commission’s proceedings had validated their concerns, reiterating his demand for strict action against the responsible police officers.
Earlier, the Sindh government has received the judicial commission’s report on the Mir Raza Ali case in a sealed envelope, Additional Secretary Home Javed Abro said on Thursday.
Abro said the government would now decide on the next course of action in the case.
He added that the judicial commission’s proceedings had been conducted in open court, while the final report had been handed over to the government in a sealed envelope.
The report’s receipt marks the next stage in the case, with further decisions now resting with the Sindh government.
The judicial commission headed by SHC Justice Omar Sial contains statements from 49 individuals connected to the case. The commission held 15 hearings and recorded two statements via video link.
The judicial commission was constituted on August 24. Mir Raza Ali’s body was found in the Gulistan-e-Jauhar area on July 29. An initial post-mortem examination was conducted, followed by a second examination after the body was exhumed.
The report covers findings and evidence relating to the police investigation, the medico-legal section and the Health Department. It also examines institutional shortcomings associated with the case.
The report has been prepared in accordance with the terms of reference set by the Sindh government. The Sindh government will decide whether the judicial commission’s report should be made public.
Meanwhile, Mir Raza Ali’s family is demanding the formation of a Joint Investigation Team (JIT) to investigate the incident.

title: National Highway gridlock at Naushahro Feroze jams traffic for hours

title: Iran’s War Is Forcing America to Rethink Warfare?
text:
Iran’s War Is Forcing America to Rethink Warfare?
- By Shargeel Sheikh -
- Oct 19, 2026
When US forces hammered down Iranian cities, little did they know that the Iranian would fight back at this scale. The mighty US firepower and missiles did not stop Iran from punching above its weight.
Uptil now, at least 8 US aircrafts have been destroyed or severely damaged, A number of US radars have been hit and casualties reported. Multiple missiles have hit Israel. The Gulf countries have dealt with fast coming Iranian missiles and drone, many of which they’ve failed to intercept.
The US expected Iran to be left destroyed and empty handed. Instead, the superpower found itself empty of its own 50% patriot missiles and around 50% of its THAAD system missiles. Most of them had been used in intercepting
Iranian drones that were made at a fraction of the missiles cost A domestic Iranian drone can cost as low as $7,000. The missiles intercepting them take millions of dollars to produce. At this rate, the favor heavily lies on Iran’s side,
Iran confidently claimed they are in no short of missiles and drones. If there’s any truth to what Iran mentioned, the US needs to rethink its military strategy and its overall approach to this conflict.
For decades, the US has reigned in as the supreme military power. It’s been hailed as the Mecca of innovation and technology, a place where new ideas breath and come to life.
US triumphed during the Middle East wars, the cold war, and the 2nd World War before that. The secret lied in US high tech innovation, cutting edge weapon technology, and a management structure that made every decision smooth.
But the recent Iran matter had the world discover serious loopholes in the US forces.
If US wants to keep dominating as the military superpower, it has no choice but to reanalyze its entire military buildup and prioritize into emerging technologies and innovation.
Let’s talk about drones first. They have transformed the entire warfare game. They are not expensive. And come with capability of inflating massive damages.
Ukraine used drones as offensive against Russi. Iran has been using them to strike down bases across the Middle East.
The US still needs to invest in massive drone manufacturing infrastructure. The country has procured only 50,000 of modern drones as compared to Ukraine which is manufacturing millions in a year.
During this war, Iran came out with an enormous arsenal of cheap drones. These deadly machines were launched at US basis across the Gulf as well as Israel.
Till now, there has been no permanent solution to tackle these upcoming drones. And it will remain so unless the US military focuses on manufacturing its own at less cost. Currently the US has failed to adopt fast scale manufacturing.
Many of the limited drones being manufactured in US contains Chinese hardware and components. This creates dependence on rivals and exposes weakness.
A viable solution would be to allow large scale and cost-effective production of drones. But that will require harnessing the technology of cheap and fast production.
It’s surprising to know that no such technology has been discovered by the US at scale yet. China dominates the drone market currently. The Chinese DJI company sells more than 70% of civilian’s drones in the world.
The success behind it lies in discovering the tech hobbyist market and optimizing the drone technology and utilizing it in defense.
China’s industrial policies and infrastructure allow it to produce these machines at large scale. The US by far is no good in producing anything cost efficient.
A far greater sweeping change is the implementation of AI in modern warfare. Despite the fact that America is home to the most advance AI companies, other countries have not been far behind in their own pursuit of AI.
Anyone can have access of AI since it’s a product of commercial activity rather than a military one.
The current AI model being introduced by Open AI, Microsoft, Google, and Anthropic are being replicated easily by Chinese firms. American AI models are being used by rivals to train their own native AI technology.
American Ai is still easy to access and manipulate. Recent report showed Yemeni Houthi groups used Claude in navigating drone strikes and guided missiles. This raises questions on AI ‘s credibility.
For the US, it means other nations can have easy access to AI tech and can potentially rival. China has shown remarkable progress in shouldering US in tech. There’s a solid chance it can reach or even surpass US in AI in the next coming years.
But one thing still holding the Dragon back is its inability to create high tech semiconductors and chips. For that very reason, Chinese firms have been desperate in producing home grown semiconductors and high-tech chips for data centers while importing it from the US and the West. Washington alone cannot curb AI’s growth into the market and prevent it from getting it into wrong hands, but it can coordinate with AI firms and work with them into establishing a framework of making it safe.
History has witnessed the rise and fall of every empire. In order to maintain its dominance, the US militarily is in a tough spot. Unless it double down on fast paced tech and manufacturing and create more efficient ways to protect itself from threats.

PM to visit KP this week following governor's rule

text:
Australian lawmaker Helen Haines in critical condition after vehicle attack
- By Reuters -
- Oct 19, 2026
SYDNEY: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines was in a critical condition on Monday after being deliberately struck by a car outside her office in Wangaratta, police and Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said.
Victoria Police said a 43-year-old man had been arrested after the attack on independent MP Haines in Wangaratta, around three hours’ drive northeast of Melbourne.
Haines, 65, was airlifted to hospital, Albanese said.

title: Punjab govt backs consecutive sentences to restore public faith in justice system
text:
Punjab govt backs consecutive sentences to restore public faith in justice system
ISLAMABAD: The Punjab government has supported the imposition of consecutive sentences in grave and heinous crimes, particularly multiple-murder cases, arguing that the practice would help restore public confidence in the criminal justice system.
The provincial government submitted its written response to the Supreme Court in a case concerning whether sentences awarded to convicts involved in multiple murders should run consecutively or concurrently.
Additional Prosecutor General Punjab Tariq Siddique submitted the response, addressing two key questions: whether a sessions court, while convicting and sentencing an accused on multiple counts, is required to direct that the sentences run consecutively or concurrently, and whether the gravity of the offences should also be considered in making that determination.
In its written submissions, the Punjab prosecution argued that courts should not routinely order sentences to run consecutively in every case. Instead, such orders should be passed through reasoned and explicit judicial decisions in exceptional cases involving particularly brutal, inhuman and heinous crimes.
The government maintained that reducing a life sentence to a substantive term of 15 years made it even more important for courts to avoid a mechanical or casual approach when ordering sentences to run concurrently, warning that such a practice could erode public confidence in the criminal justice system.
A convict involved in multiple murders should not be given the benefit of release after serving only 15 years, the response argued.
It further stated that routinely ordering concurrent sentences could send a message that the justice system made little distinction between the killing of one person and multiple victims.
Citing the principle of proportionality, the Punjab government argued that when multiple lives were unlawfully taken, each offence should carry an independent and distinct penal consequence.
Merging all sentences into a single concurrent term in multiple-murder cases would dilute the gravity of additional offences and create an artificial equivalence between taking one life and taking several, the response stated.
The government further argued that allowing all sentences to run concurrently could effectively convey the message that a person convicted of one murder or several murders could be released after the same period in prison.
Referring to the legislative treatment of heinous crimes, the response said lawmakers had recognised that such offences required special measures. It cited restrictions on the grant of remissions to certain convicts under the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, and the Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997, as examples of this approach.
The Punjab government maintained that consecutive sentences in grave and heinous offences would not only strengthen public confidence in the administration of criminal justice but also serve the deterrent and retributive objectives of punishment.
Citing Section 4 of the Punjab Sentencing Act, 2019, the response noted that sentencing aims to punish offenders, reduce crime through deterrence, reform and rehabilitate offenders, and protect the public.
Pakistan offers Bangladesh cooperation on legal reforms and digital justice
It emphasised that consecutive sentences should not be imposed in every routine case but should be ordered through reasoned judicial decisions in exceptional circumstances, particularly where offences have been committed in a brutal, morbid or inhuman manner that shocks the public conscience.
Such cases may include homicide, kidnapping and abduction, sexual abuse and terrorism, the response stated.
The Punjab prosecution added that ordering consecutive sentences in grave, sensational and inhuman crimes, particularly offences against the human body, would help strengthen public faith in the justice system, maintain social equilibrium and fulfil the retributive and deterrent purposes of punishment.

title: Hajj 2027: Ministry issues urgent reminder for second installment payment by Oct 20
text:
Hajj 2027: Ministry issues urgent reminder for second installment payment by Oct 20

title: Oman restores citizenship to 11 people under new royal decree
text:
Oman restores citizenship to 11 people under new royal decree
DUBAI: Oman’s Sultan Haitham bin Tariq has restored Omani citizenship to 11 people under a royal decree published on Sunday, October 18, in the country’s Official Gazette.
Royal Decree No. 89/2026, issued on October 12, reinstates citizenship for the 11 individuals named in an accompanying list published in Issue No. 1670 of the Official Gazette.
The decree’s first article provides for the restoration of nationality to those listed, while its second stipulates that the decree must be published in the Official Gazette and takes effect from the date of its issuance.
The decision was issued after consideration of the Basic Statute of the State and the Omani Citizenship Law introduced under Royal Decree No. 17/2025, and on the grounds of public interest.
What does Oman’s citizenship law say?
Oman’s nationality law, introduced in February 2025, replaced legislation dating from 2014 and sets out the conditions governing the acquisition, loss and restoration of citizenship.
Under Article 7, Omani nationality can be granted, withdrawn, revoked or restored by royal decree following a recommendation from the Minister of Interior.
Article 8 also allows the Sultan to grant or restore citizenship in exceptional circumstances without applying the law’s standard conditions.
The legislation permits Omanis by origin who previously renounced their nationality to acquire another citizenship to apply for its restoration, subject to requirements including residence in Oman or a commitment to return and settle, good conduct and a written declaration of their intention to relinquish their foreign nationality.
The law also provides for the restoration of citizenship to people previously deprived of it when the grounds for its removal no longer apply.
The latest decree does not specify the circumstances under which the 11 individuals previously lost their citizenship or which provisions were applied in their cases.

title: Israeli Ad Firm Accused of Spying Through Online Ads
text:
Israeli agency Discover-Tech spies on internet users through online ads
- By Reuters -
- Oct 19, 2026
WASHINGTON: Israeli digital advertising agency Discover-Tech spied on internet users through a sprawling network of online ads that it used to track targets and help hack their devices, two research groups said.
Its services gave Israel’s Candiru — a spyware company blacklisted by the US government — as well as other Israeli surveillance firms access to advertising platforms run by Google, Comcast, Russia’s Yandex and others, according to separate, reports, from Canadian cyber watchdog group Citizen Lab and New York advertising security firm Confiant.
The reports show how the online advertising business, long a subject of privacy concerns, can also serve as a channel for sweeping espionage campaigns.
“The way online advertising works today is a systemic security threat,” Wolfie Christl, a senior researcher at Citizen Lab, told Reuters. “For states, the private sector, civil society and everyone else alike.”
Discover-Tech’s online ads — often for ordinary products such as phones or earbuds — reached more than 120,000 websites and 75,000 apps through its various partnerships, Citizen Lab said.
Users who visited sites or used apps with the malicious ads could be identified and tracked by Discover-Tech, which would sometimes also try to extract phone numbers from some smartphone users, the researchers said. Ads only needed to load on a website for the spying to occur.
Some ads would be used to help plant spyware from Candiru on users’ devices, both research groups said, though Confiant said that ads it tied to Candiru were a tiny fraction of Discover-Tech’s overall volume.
MALICIOUS ADS SHOWN IN HUNDREDS OF SENSITIVE NETWORKS
Confiant cofounder Jerome Dangu said Discover-Tech was pumping out at least 10 million ads per day all around the world and that data-sharing arrangements — called cookie matching — allowed it to track people even beyond the reach of its advertisements.
“Very likely hundreds of millions of people would have been touched by Discover-Tech,” Dangu said.
Discover-Tech, which was founded in 2020, did not return messages left via its contact form. A LinkedIn message and emails sent to its chief executive, Dekel Boni, were not returned.
Reuters’ attempts to reach Candiru’s owners were similarly unsuccessful. The US Commerce Department blacklisted Candiru in 2021 for allegedly supplying spyware that was used to maliciously target government officials, journalists, activists and academics.
Citizen Lab said a powerful form of Candiru spyware delivered through Discover-Tech’s ads had been used to compromise 45 Windows devices at the Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera between 2024 and 2025, something it said it was able to confirm because the media group had shared its network logs with the group.
Israeli professor indicted over plot to kill hundreds of Arabs and Palestinians
In a statement, Al Jazeera said it “condemns the spyware attacks targeting a number of its staff” and that it was taking steps to protect its employees and its systems. “Those responsible must be held accountable,” it said.
Dangu of Confiant said that the malicious ads had been shown to users in “hundreds of networks in sensitive categories,” including the Pentagon, the International Atomic Energy Agency, and the International Criminal Court. He also said that some regions, like the Palestinian territories, were particularly saturated by the Israeli firm’s ads.
“You go to almost any site in Palestine — any site — you find a Discover-Tech ad. It gives them a very complete visibility on the digital activities of an entire country,” he said.
Citizen Lab also said it had similar evidence showing the malicious ads were shown to people in the United Nations, NATO, the European Commission, and more than a dozen national governments. Other networks the ads appeared in included chip-related firms such as Nvidia, Sandisk, Broadcom, and Micron, as well as several media organizations in Mexico, Israel, and Europe that were not identified.
In addition to identifying Candiru and a couple of other surveillance vendors, Citizen Lab said it was able to glean some details about where Discover-Tech’s users might be based because the firm inadvertently exposed its authentication logs to the internet, showing people logging in from internet protocol addresses in Israel, Europe, and the Gulf.
MEASURES AGAINST DISCOVER-TECH TAKEN
Discover-Tech is now being frozen out of parts of the online ad market.
Google said in a statement that it had collaborated with Citizen Lab and Confiant’s investigation and kicked Discover-Tech off its ad platforms “for systematically violating our policies.”
IAB Europe, the European-level association for the digital marketing and advertising ecosystem, said in an email that Discover-Tech had been suspended from its list of globally approved vendors last week after an audit identified policy violations.
Comcast ad tech subsidiary Beeswax removed Discover-Tech from its platform “following recent activity,” Comcast said in a statement. Yandex did not return Reuters messages seeking comment.
Advertising-driven surveillance is increasingly being seen as a national security threat. Earlier this year, the Pentagon said it had received reports that US forces deployed to war zones had been targeted using location data harvested by ad tech firms and data brokers. Branches of the military have since disabled ad tracking on some devices.
